text_mt: Now, therefore, we shall explain the New and Full Moon sacrifices.

sanskrit_iast: prātar agnihotraṃ hutvānyam āhavanīyaṃ praṇīyāgnīn anvādadhāti
meaning: प्रातर् अग्निहोत्रं हुत्वान्यम् आहवनीयं प्रणीयाग्नीन् अन्वादधाति
text_mt: Having offered the morning agnihotra and brought forward another āhavanīya [fire], he adds fuel to the fires.
For one who has attained prosperity, he does not bring forward another fire.
“O path-finding gods, find the path for the sacrifice!

sanskrit_iast: manasaspatinā devena vātādyajñaḥ prayujyatām iti japitvā mamāgne varco vihaveṣv astv ity āhavanīyam upasaminddhe /
meaning: मनसस्पतिना देवेन वाताद्यज्ञः प्रयुज्यताम् इति जपित्वा ममाग्ने वर्चो विहवेष्व् अस्त्व् इत्य् आहवनीयम् उपसमिन्द्धे /
text_mt: Through the divine lord of the mind, may the sacrifice be applied by the wind!” Having muttered this, with “May my splendor, O Agni, be present in the invocations,” he kindles the āhavanīya.
With the next [verse he kindles] the gārhapatya, [and] with the next the anvāhāryapacana.
He should mutter the last [verse], or put [a stick of firewood] into the āhavanīya.
Some teach adding fuel to the fires with the sacred utterances (vyāhṛtis).

sanskrit_iast: saṃnayataḥ palāśaśākhāṃ śamīśākhāṃ vāharati bahuparṇāṃ bahuśākhām apratiśuṣkāgrāmasuṣirām
meaning: संनयतः पलाशशाखां शमीशाखां वाहरति बहुपर्णां बहुशाखाम् अप्रतिशुष्काग्रामसुषिराम्
text_mt: For one who performs the offering of milk and curds, he fetches a branch of palāśa or a branch of śamī that has many leaves, many twigs, an un-withered tip, and is not hollow.

sanskrit_iast: yaṃ kāmayetāpaśuḥ syād ity aparṇāṃ tasmai śuṣkāgrām āhared apaśur eva bhavati /
meaning: यं कामयेतापशुः स्याद् इत्य् अपर्णां तस्मै शुष्काग्राम् आहरेद् अपशुर् एव भवति /
text_mt: “For one whom he wishes ‘May he be without cattle,’ he should fetch for him [a branch] devoid of leaves and with a withered tip: he indeed becomes without cattle.

sanskrit_iast: yaṃ kāmayeta paśumān syād iti bahuparṇāṃ tasmai bahuśākhām āharet paśumantam evainaṃ karotīti vijñāyate
meaning: यं कामयेत पशुमान् स्याद् इति बहुपर्णां तस्मै बहुशाखाम् आहरेत् पशुमन्तम् एवैनं करोतीति विज्ञायते
text_mt: For one whom he wishes ‘May he possess cattle,’ he should fetch for him [a branch] with many leaves and many twigs: he indeed makes him possess cattle”—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

sanskrit_iast: sā yā prācy udīcī prāgudīcī vā bhavatīṣe tvorje tveti tām ācchinatti
meaning: सा या प्राच्य् उदीची प्रागुदीची वा भवतीषे त्वोर्जे त्वेति ताम् आच्छिनत्ति
text_mt: Whichever [branch] points east, north, or north-east, that one he cuts off with “For sap, for strength thee!”

sanskrit_iast: api veṣe tvety ācchinatty ūrje tveti saṃnamayaty anumārṣṭi vā
meaning: अपि वेषे त्वेत्य् आच्छिनत्त्य् ऊर्जे त्वेति संनमयत्य् अनुमार्ष्टि वा
text_mt: Or, with “For sap thee,” he cuts [it] off; with “For strength thee,” he bends it down or strokes it along.

sanskrit_iast: imāṃ prācīm udīcīm iṣam ūrjam abhisaṃskṛtāṃ bahuparṇāmaśuṣkāgrāṃ harāmi paśupāmaham ity āharati
meaning: इमां प्राचीम् उदीचीम् इषम् ऊर्जम् अभिसंस्कृतां बहुपर्णामशुष्काग्रां हरामि पशुपामहम् इत्य् आहरति
text_mt: With “This [branch] pointing east, pointing north, prepared for food and strength, rich in leaves, with an un-withered tip, the protector of cattle, do I fetch,” he fetches [it].

sanskrit_iast: vāyava sthopāyava stheti tayā ṣaḍavarārdhyān vatsān apākaroti
meaning: वायव स्थोपायव स्थेति तया षडवरार्ध्यान् वत्सान् अपाकरोति
text_mt: With “You are the winds, you are the followers,” he drives away with it at least six calves.
[He does so] with darbha grasses or with darbha tufts.

sanskrit_iast: devo vaḥ savitā prārpayatv iti śākhayā gocarāya gāḥ prasthāpayati
meaning: देवो वः सविता प्रार्पयत्व् इति शाखया गोचराय गाः प्रस्थापयति
text_mt: With “May divine Savitṛ impel you,” he sends the cows forth to the pasture with the branch.

sanskrit_iast: prasthitānām ekāṃ śākhayopaspṛśati darbhair darbhapuñjilair vā
meaning: प्रस्थितानाम् एकां शाखयोपस्पृशति दर्भैर् दर्भपुञ्जिलैर् वा
text_mt: He touches one of those that have set forth with the branch, or with darbha grasses, or with darbha tufts.

sanskrit_iast: āpyāyadhvam aghniyā indrāya devabhāgam ity eke samāmananti /
meaning: आप्यायध्वम् अघ्निया इन्द्राय देवभागम् इत्य् एके समामनन्ति /
text_mt: “Swell, O inviolable ones, for Indra, the gods’ share!”—so some teach.
He should mention Indra in the formulas for one who sacrifices to Indra, [and] Mahendra for one who sacrifices to Mahendra.

sanskrit_iast: śuddhā apaḥ suprapāṇe pibantīḥ śatam indrāya śarado duhānāḥ /
meaning: शुद्धा अपः सुप्रपाणे पिबन्तीः शतम् इन्द्राय शरदो दुहानाः /
text_mt: “Drinking pure waters at a good drinking place, yielding milk for a hundred autumns for Indra,

sanskrit_iast: rudrasya hetiḥ pari vo vṛṇaktv iti prasthitā anumantrayate
meaning: रुद्रस्य हेतिः परि वो वृणक्त्व् इति प्रस्थिता अनुमन्त्रयते
text_mt: may Rudra’s weapon avoid you!”—with this he addresses them as they have set forth.

sanskrit_iast: dhruvā asmin gopatau syāta bahvīr iti yajamānasya gṛhān abhiparyāvartate
meaning: ध्रुवा अस्मिन् गोपतौ स्यात बह्वीर् इति यजमानस्य गृहान् अभिपर्यावर्तते
text_mt: With “Be steadfast and many in this owner of cattle,” he turns toward the house of the sacrificer.

sanskrit_iast: yajamānasya paśūn pāhīty agniṣṭhe 'nasy agnyagāre vā purastātpratīcīṃ śākhām upagūhati paścātprācīṃ vā
meaning: यजमानस्य पशून् पाहीत्य् अग्निष्ठे ऽनस्य् अग्न्यगारे वा पुरस्तात्प्रतीचीं शाखाम् उपगूहति पश्चात्प्राचीं वा
text_mt: With “Protect the cattle of the sacrificer,” he hides the branch in the cart standing by the fire or in the fire-chamber, pointing westward from the east, or eastward from the west.

sanskrit_iast: yo vā adhvaryor gṛhān veda gṛhavān bhavati /
meaning: यो वा अध्वर्योर् गृहान् वेद गृहवान् भवति /
text_mt: “Whoever knows the adhvaryu’s homes becomes possessed of a home.

sanskrit_iast: ā caturthāt karmaṇo 'bhisamīkṣetedaṃ kariṣyāmīdaṃ kariṣyāmīty ete vā adhvaryor gṛhāḥ /
meaning: आ चतुर्थात् कर्मणो ऽभिसमीक्षेतेदं करिष्यामीदं करिष्यामीत्य् एते वा अध्वर्योर् गृहाः /
text_mt: Up to the fourth rite, he should reflect: ‘I shall do this, I shall do that’; these indeed are the adhvaryu’s homes.

sanskrit_iast: ya evaṃ veda gṛhavān bhavatīti vijñāyate
meaning: य एवं वेद गृहवान् भवतीति विज्ञायते
text_mt: He who knows thus becomes possessed of a home”—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

sanskrit_iast: uttareṇa gārhapatyam asido 'śvaparśur anaḍutparśur vā nihitā
meaning: उत्तरेण गार्हपत्यम् असिदो ऽश्वपर्शुर् अनडुत्पर्शुर् वा निहिता
text_mt: North of the gārhapatya, a sickle, a horse’s rib, or an ox’s rib is placed.

sanskrit_iast: devasya tvā savituḥ prasava ity asidam aśvaparśuṃ vādatte tūṣṇīm anaḍutparśum
meaning: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसव इत्य् असिदम् अश्वपर्शुं वादत्ते तूष्णीम् अनडुत्पर्शुम्
text_mt: With “At the impulse of divine Savitṛ,” he takes up the sickle or the horse’s rib; silently [he takes up] the ox’s rib.

sanskrit_iast: yajñasya ghoṣadasīti gārhapatyam abhimantrya pratyuṣṭaṃ rakṣaḥ pratyuṣṭā arātaya ity āhavanīye gārhapatye vāsidaṃ pratitapati
meaning: यज्ञस्य घोषदसीति गार्हपत्यम् अभिमन्त्र्य प्रत्युष्टं रक्षः प्रत्युष्टा अरातय इत्य् आहवनीये गार्हपत्ये वासिदं प्रतितपति
text_mt: Having addressed the gārhapatya with “You are the sound of the sacrifice,” he heats the sickle over the āhavanīya or the gārhapatya with “Burnt is the demon, burnt are the enemies.”

sanskrit_iast: preyam agād ity uktvorvantarikṣamanvihīti prācīm udīcīṃ vā diśam abhipravrajya yataḥ kutaścid darbhamayaṃ barhir āharati
meaning: प्रेयम् अगाद् इत्य् उक्त्वोर्वन्तरिक्षमन्विहीति प्राचीम् उदीचीं वा दिशम् अभिप्रव्रज्य यतः कुतश्चिद् दर्भमयं बर्हिर् आहरति
text_mt: Having said “Forward she went,” he says “Traverse the wide midspace,” goes forward toward the eastern or northern direction, and brings sacrificial grass made of darbha from wherever [he finds it].
With “You are the enclosure of the gods,” he encloses the darbha grasses.

sanskrit_iast: viṣṇo stūpo 'sīty abhipretānām ekaṃ stambam utsṛjati
meaning: विष्णो स्तूपो ऽसीत्य् अभिप्रेतानाम् एकं स्तम्बम् उत्सृजति
text_mt: With “You are Viṣṇu’s tuft,” he leaves aside one clump among those he intended [to cut].

sanskrit_iast: ekaṃ vā stambaṃ pariṣūya taṃ sarvaṃ dāti
meaning: एकं वा स्तम्बं परिषूय तं सर्वं दाति
text_mt: Or having enclosed one clump, he cuts it entirely.

sanskrit_iast: atisṛṣṭo gavāṃ bhāga iti vaikāṃ dve tisro vā nāḍīr utsṛjati
meaning: अतिसृष्टो गवां भाग इति वैकां द्वे तिस्रो वा नाडीर् उत्सृजति
text_mt: Or with “Allowed is the share of the cows,” he leaves aside one, two, or three stalks.
With “This belongs to the gods,” he touches the enclosed ones.
With “This belongs to the cattle,” [he touches] the ones left aside.

sanskrit_iast: devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ barhirdevasadanam ārabha iti viśākheṣu darbhān ārabhate
meaning: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऽश्विनोर् बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्यां बर्हिर्देवसदनम् आरभ इति विशाखेषु दर्भान् आरभते
text_mt: With “At the impulse of divine Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I lay hold of the sacrificial grass, the seat of the gods,” he lays hold of the darbha grasses at the forkings.

sanskrit_iast: devabarhir mā tvānvaṅmā tiryag iti saṃyacchati
meaning: देवबर्हिर् मा त्वान्वङ्मा तिर्यग् इति संयच्छति
text_mt: With “O divine grass, may I not [cut] you following [the grain], nor across,” he holds [it] firmly.
With “May I succeed with your joint,” he puts the sickle down upon [it].

sanskrit_iast: ācchettā te mā riṣam ity ācchinatti
meaning: आच्छेत्ता ते मा रिषम् इत्य् आच्छिनत्ति
text_mt: With “May I, your cutter, not come to harm,” he cuts [it] off.
He cuts a handful up to the fingernails.

sanskrit_iast: kulmimātro 'ratniḥ prādeśa ūrvasthi jānvasthi srugdaṇḍa iti vā tiryakpramāṇāni
meaning: कुल्मिमात्रो ऽरत्निः प्रादेश ऊर्वस्थि जान्वस्थि स्रुग्दण्ड इति वा तिर्यक्प्रमाणानि
text_mt: The size of a fist, a cubit, a span, [the length of] the thigh bone, the knee bone, or the ladle handle—these are the horizontal measurements.
With “Protect from contact with the earth,” he places it not directly on the ground.
“Among them, the grass bunch serves to make the number uneven,” say some.

sanskrit_iast: yadanyat pariṣavaṇād utsarjanāc ca tat sarvatrāvartate
meaning: यदन्यत् परिषवणाद् उत्सर्जनाच् च तत् सर्वत्रावर्तते
text_mt: Whatever is other than the enclosing and the leaving aside is repeated everywhere.

sanskrit_iast: prasataram eva mantreṇa dāti tūṣṇīm itarad iti vājasaneyakam
meaning: प्रसतरम् एव मन्त्रेण दाति तूष्णीम् इतरद् इति वाजसनेयकम्
text_mt: “He cuts only the grass bunch with a formula, the rest silently”—this is the Vājasaneyaka view.

sanskrit_iast: sarvaṃ lutvā devabarhiḥ śatavalśaṃ virohety ālavān abhimṛśati
meaning: सर्वं लुत्वा देवबर्हिः शतवल्शं विरोहेत्य् आलवान् अभिमृशति
text_mt: Having cut all, with “O divine grass, grow up with a hundred shoots,” he touches the stumps.
With “May we grow up with a thousand shoots,” [he touches] himself.

sanskrit_iast: adityai rāsnāsīti tridhātu pañcadhātu vā śulbaṃ karoti
meaning: अदित्यै रास्नासीति त्रिधातु पञ्चधातु वा शुल्बं करोति
text_mt: With “You are the girdle of Aditi,” he makes a cord of three strands or five strands.
With “An unblemished source,” he puts it back.

sanskrit_iast: adityai rāsnāsīty udagagraṃ vitatya susaṃbhṛtā tvā saṃbharāmīti tasminnidhanāni saṃbhṛtyālubhitā yonir ity uttame nidhane prastaram atyādhāyendrāṇyai saṃnahanam iti saṃnahyati
meaning: अदित्यै रास्नासीत्य् उदगग्रं वितत्य सुसंभृता त्वा संभरामीति तस्मिन्निधनानि संभृत्यालुभिता योनिर् इत्य् उत्तमे निधने प्रस्तरम् अत्याधायेन्द्राण्यै संनहनम् इति संनह्यति
text_mt: With “You are the girdle of Aditi,” having stretched [the cord] with its tips pointing north, with “Well gathered, I gather you,” having gathered the bundles upon it, with “An unblemished source,” having placed the grass bunch over the topmost bundle, with “The fastening of Indrāṇī,” he ties [it] up.

sanskrit_iast: pūṣā te granthiṃ grathnātv iti granthiṃ karoti
meaning: पूषा ते ग्रन्थिं ग्रथ्नात्व् इति ग्रन्थिं करोति
text_mt: With “May Pūṣan tie your knot,” he makes a knot.

sanskrit_iast: sa te māsthād iti purastāt pratyañcaṃ granthim upagūhati paścāt prāñcaṃ vā
meaning: स ते मास्थाद् इति पुरस्तात् प्रत्यञ्चं ग्रन्थिम् उपगूहति पश्चात् प्राञ्चं वा
text_mt: With the words: “May it not come undone,” he tucks the knot inside from the east towards the west, or from the west towards the east.
“The waters have wiped you clean, the two Aśvins have wiped you clean, the seven seers have wiped you clean;

sanskrit_iast: barhiḥ sūryasya raśmibhir uṣasāṃ ketumārabha iti barhirārabhate /
meaning: बर्हिः सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिर् उषसां केतुमारभ इति बर्हिरारभते /
text_mt: O sacrificial grass, with the rays of the sun I take hold of the banner of the dawns,” with these words he takes hold of the sacrificial grass.

sanskrit_iast: indrasya tvā bāhubhyām udyaccha ity udyacchate /
meaning: इन्द्रस्य त्वा बाहुभ्याम् उद्यच्छ इत्य् उद्यच्छते /
text_mt: With the words: “With the arms of Indra I raise you up,” he raises it up.
With the words: “With the head of Bṛhaspati I carry [you],” he places it upon his head.
The two verses that are used for going: “May this [goddess] go forth...” and “Traverse the wide midspace...” are used for the return.

meaning: अदित्यास्त्वोपस्थे सादयामीत्य् अन्तर्वेदि परिधिदेशे ऽनधः सादयति
text_mt: With the words: “On the lap of Aditi I set you down,” he sets it down inside the altar ground at the place of the enclosing sticks, not touching the ground.

sanskrit_iast: barhir asi devaṃgamam ity āsannam abhimantrayate
meaning: बर्हिर् असि देवंगमम् इत्य् आसन्नम् अभिमन्त्रयते
text_mt: With the words: “You are sacrificial grass reaching the gods,” he addresses it once it has been set down.
Or, reciting “You are reaching the gods,” he deposits it not touching the ground, in such a way that he sets it facing east.

sanskrit_iast: yā jātā oṣadhayo devebhyas triyugaṃ purā /
meaning: या जाता ओषधयो देवेभ्यस् त्रियुगं पुरा /
text_mt: “The plants that were born for the gods three ages ago,
bringing the strewing grass, may I achieve their knot!

sanskrit_iast: apāṃ medhyaṃ yajñiyaṃ sadevaṃ śivamastu me /
meaning: अपां मेध्यं यज्ञियं सदेवं शिवमस्तु मे /
text_mt: Fit for sacrifice of the waters, belonging to the sacrifice, with the gods, let it be auspicious for me;

sanskrit_iast: ācchettā vo mā riṣaṃ jivāni śaradaḥ śatam //
meaning: आच्छेत्ता वो मा रिषं जिवानि शरदः शतम् //
text_mt: cutter of you, may I not suffer harm; may I live a hundred autumns!
Measured [strands] of unmeasured [plants], I bind [you] for good deed;

sanskrit_iast: eno mā nigāṃ katamccanāhaṃ punarutthāya bahulā bhavantv iti paristaraṇānāmadhinidhānyācchedanī saṃnahanīti yathāliṅgam
meaning: एनो मा निगां कतम्च्चनाहं पुनरुत्थाय बहुला भवन्त्व् इति परिस्तरणानामधिनिधान्याच्छेदनी संनहनीति यथालिङ्गम्
text_mt: may I not fall into any guilt whatsoever! Rising again, let them become abundant,” thus according to their characteristics [are the mantras] for setting down the strewing grass, for cutting it, and for binding it.
He prepares the firewood of twenty-one sticks, made of khadira or made of palāśa.
[they are] of palāśa, kārṣmarya, khadira, udumbara, bilva, rohītaka, or vikaṅkata, or whatever trees are fit for sacrifice;
they may be moist or dry, but with their bark intact.

meaning: स्थविष्ठो मध्यमो ऽणीयान्द्राघीयान्दक्षिणार्ध्यो ऽणिष्ठो ह्रसिष्ठ उत्तरार्ध्यः
text_mt: The middle one is the thickest, the southern one is thinner and longer, and the northern one is the thinnest and shortest.
There are two sticks for the two foundational libations, and the stick for the after-offerings is the twenty-first.

sanskrit_iast: samūlānāmṛtemūlānāṃ vā darbhāṇāṃ pūrvavac chulbaṃ kṛtvodagagraṃ vitatya
meaning: समूलानामृतेमूलानां वा दर्भाणां पूर्ववच् छुल्बं कृत्वोदगग्रं वितत्य
text_mt: Having made a cord as before from darbha grass with roots or without roots, and spreading it out pointing northward,
“When having taken the form of a black deer you entered the trees,
from there I gather you in twenty-one parts, well-gathered;
the three enclosing sticks, the three kindling sticks that course along the life of the sacrifice,

sanskrit_iast: upaveṣaṃ mekṣaṇaṃ dhṛṣṭiṃ saṃbharāmi susaṃbhṛteti śulba idhmaṃ saṃbharati
meaning: उपवेषं मेक्षणं धृष्टिं संभरामि सुसंभृतेति शुल्ब इध्मं संभरति
text_mt: the fire-stirring stick, the stirring stick, the poking stick, I gather well-gathered,” with these words he gathers the firewood upon the cord.

sanskrit_iast: kṛṣṇo 'syākhareṣṭho deva puraścara saghyāsaṃ tveti saṃnahyati /
meaning: कृष्णो ऽस्याखरेष्ठो देव पुरश्चर सघ्यासं त्वेति संनह्यति /
text_mt: With the words: “You are black, resting in the lair, O god, go at the head, may I overcome you,” he ties it;

sanskrit_iast: purastāt pratyañcaṃ granthim upagūhati paścāt prāñcaṃ vā /
meaning: पुरस्तात् प्रत्यञ्चं ग्रन्थिम् उपगूहति पश्चात् प्राञ्चं वा /
text_mt: he tucks the knot inside from the east towards the west, or from the west towards the east;
He sets down the wood-chippings.

sanskrit_iast: tvayā vediṃ vividuḥ pṛthivīṃ tvayā yajño jāyate viśvadāniḥ /
meaning: त्वया वेदिं विविदुः पृथिवीं त्वया यज्ञो जायते विश्वदानिः /
text_mt: “By you they found the altar ground, the earth; through you the sacrifice is born every day;

sanskrit_iast: acchidraṃ yajñam anveṣi vidvāṃs tvayā hotā saṃtanoty ardhamāsān iti darbhāṇāṃ vedaṃ karoti
meaning: अच्छिद्रं यज्ञम् अन्वेषि विद्वांस् त्वया होता संतनोत्य् अर्धमासान् इति दर्भाणां वेदं करोति
text_mt: you follow the flawless sacrifice, wise one; by you the hotṛ extends the half-months,” with these words he makes the veda out of darbha grass:
shaped like a calf’s knee for one who desires cattle; shaped like a woven basket for one who desires food; with a threefold head for one who desires brahminical splendour.
Trimming it at a span’s length from the cord, he sets aside the trimmings of the veda.

sanskrit_iast: antarvedi śākhāyāḥ palāśānyasarvāṇi praśātya mūlataḥ śākhāṃ parivāsyopaveṣaṃ karoty upaveṣo 'si yajñāya tvāṃ pariveṣamadhārayan /
meaning: अन्तर्वेदि शाखायाः पलाशान्यसर्वाणि प्रशात्य मूलतः शाखां परिवास्योपवेषं करोत्य् उपवेषो ऽसि यज्ञाय त्वां परिवेषमधारयन् /
text_mt: Inside the altar ground, having stripped off not all the leaves of a branch and having cut the branch from the base, he makes a fire-stirring stick with the words: “You are the fire-stirring stick; they have maintained you for the service of the sacrifice;

sanskrit_iast: indrāya haviḥ kṛṇvantaḥ śivaḥ śagmo bhavāsi na iti
meaning: इन्द्राय हविः कृण्वन्तः शिवः शग्मो भवासि न इति
text_mt: preparing the oblation for Indra, be auspicious and helpful to us.”
“The soma was brought by the gāyatrī from the third heaven;

sanskrit_iast: somapīthāya saṃnayituṃ vakalamantaramādada iti parivāsanaśakalamādāya prajñātaṃ nidadhāti
meaning: सोमपीथाय संनयितुं वकलमन्तरमादद इति परिवासनशकलमादाय प्रज्ञातं निदधाति
text_mt: to mix for the drinking of soma, I take the inner bark-chip,” with these words, taking a chip cut from the trimming, he deposits it in a known place.

sanskrit_iast: trivṛddarbhamayaṃ pavitraṃ kṛtvā vasūnām pavitram asīti śākhāyāṃ śithilamavasajati mūle mūlānyagre 'grāṇi /
meaning: त्रिवृद्दर्भमयं पवित्रं कृत्वा वसूनाम् पवित्रम् असीति शाखायां शिथिलमवसजति मूले मूलान्यग्रे ऽग्राणि /
text_mt: Having made a threefold strainer of darbha grass, with the words: “You are the strainer of the Vasus,” he hangs it loosely on the branch, the bases at the base, the tips at the tip;
“The threefold darbha grass on the palāśa, of this size, measured by a span;

sanskrit_iast: yajñe pavitraṃ potṛtamaṃ payo havyaṃ karotu me //
meaning: यज्ञे पवित्रं पोतृतमं पयो हव्यं करोतु मे //
text_mt: the purest strainer at the sacrifice, let it make the milk my oblation!
These two, out-breath and in-breath, limbs of the sacrifice on every side,

sanskrit_iast: āpyāyayantau saṃcaratāṃ pavitre havyaśodhane iti kriyamāṇe yajamāno 'numantrayate
meaning: आप्याययन्तौ संचरतां पवित्रे हव्यशोधने इति क्रियमाणे यजमानो ऽनुमन्त्रयते
text_mt: causing it to swell, let the two strainers move about, purifying the oblation,” with these words being recited, the sacrificer accompanies the action with mantras.
They sweep the fire-hall; they plaster the fire-places.
The sacrificer and his wife adorn themselves.
The two pots for the curds-and-milk oblation are new, smeared with cowdung mixed with grit.

sanskrit_iast: amāvāsyāyāṃ yad ahaś candramasaṃ na paśyanti tad ahaḥ piṇḍapitṛyajñaṃ kurute
meaning: अमावास्यायां यद् अहश् चन्द्रमसं न पश्यन्ति तद् अहः पिण्डपितृयज्ञं कुरुते
text_mt: On the new moon day, the day when they do not see the moon, on that day he performs the Piṇḍapitṛyajña.
In the afternoon, or when the sun is over the trees, they perform the Piṇḍapitṛyajña.

sanskrit_iast: apāṃ medhyaṃ yajñiyam iti samūlaṃ sakṛdācchinnaṃ barhir āharati
meaning: अपां मेध्यं यज्ञियम् इति समूलं सकृदाच्छिन्नं बर्हिर् आहरति
text_mt: With the words: “Fit for sacrifice of the waters...”, he brings the sacrificial grass with roots, cut in a single stroke,
or grass-blades cut in a single stroke, clipped near the root.

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇāprāgagrair darbhair dakṣiṇam agniṃ paristīrya dakṣiṇataḥ paścād vā darbhān saṃstīrya dakṣiṇāprāñcyekaikaśaḥ piṇḍapitṛyajñapātrāṇi prayunakti sphyaṃ mekṣaṇaṃ kṛṣṇājinam ulūkhalaṃ musalaṃ śūrpamājyasthālīṃ carusthālīṃ yena cānyenārthī bhavati
meaning: दक्षिणाप्रागग्रैर् दर्भैर् दक्षिणम् अग्निं परिस्तीर्य दक्षिणतः पश्चाद् वा दर्भान् संस्तीर्य दक्षिणाप्राञ्च्येकैकशः पिण्डपितृयज्ञपात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति स्फ्यं मेक्षणं कृष्णाजिनम् उलूखलं मुसलं शूर्पमाज्यस्थालीं चरुस्थालीं येन चान्येनार्थी भवति
text_mt: Having strewn darbha grass around the southern fire with tips pointing southeast, and having spread darbha grass south or west [of it], he sets out the utensils of the Piṇḍapitṛyajña one by one pointing southeast: the wooden sword, the stirring stick, the black antelope skin, the mortar, the pestle, the winnowing basket, the clarified butter pot, the pot for boiled oblation, and whatever else he has need of.
A cart containing rice stands to the south with its pole pointing east.

sanskrit_iast: adhvaryurupavītī sthālīmekapavitreṇāntardhāya tayā dakṣiṇataḥ śakaṭādadhi nirvapaty uttarato vā
meaning: अध्वर्युरुपवीती स्थालीमेकपवित्रेणान्तर्धाय तया दक्षिणतः शकटादधि निर्वपत्य् उत्तरतो वा
text_mt: The adhvaryu, wearing his sacred cord over the left shoulder, having covered the pot with a single strainer, measures out [grain] into it from the cart to the south, or to the north;
having filled it, he wipes it level.

sanskrit_iast: mṛnmaye nirvapati pitṛbhyo vo juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmīti tūṣṇīṃ vā
meaning: मृन्मये निर्वपति पितृभ्यो वो जुष्टं निर्वपामीति तूष्णीं वा
text_mt: He pours it out into an earthenware vessel with the words: “I pour you out agreeable to the ancestors,” or silently.

sanskrit_iast: apareṇānvāhāryapacanaṃ pratyagudaggrīve kṛṣṇājina ulūkhale pratiṣṭhite dakṣiṇāprācī tiṣṭhantī patnyavahanti parāpāvamavivekam
meaning: अपरेणान्वाहार्यपचनं प्रत्यगुदग्ग्रीवे कृष्णाजिन उलूखले प्रतिष्ठिते दक्षिणाप्राची तिष्ठन्ती पत्न्यवहन्ति परापावमविवेकम्
text_mt: Behind the anvāhāryapacana, the mortar being placed on the black antelope skin whose neck points northwest, the wife standing facing southeast unhusks the grain, blowing away the chaff without winnowing it finely;
He cooks unbroken grains on the southern fire.

sanskrit_iast: apahatā asurā rakṣāṃsi piśācā vediṣada ity antarā gārhapatyānvāhāryapacanau dakṣiṇāpūrveṇa vānvāhāryapacanaṃ dakṣiṇāprācīmekasphyāṃ parācīṃ vedimuddhatya śundhantāṃ pitara ity adbhir avokṣyāyantu pitaro manojavasa ity abhimantrya sakṛdācchinnaṃ barhirūrṇāmṛdu syonaṃ pitṛbhyastvā bharāmyaham /
meaning: अपहता असुरा रक्षांसि पिशाचा वेदिषद इत्य् अन्तरा गार्हपत्यान्वाहार्यपचनौ दक्षिणापूर्वेण वान्वाहार्यपचनं दक्षिणाप्राचीमेकस्फ्यां पराचीं वेदिमुद्धत्य शुन्धन्तां पितर इत्य् अद्भिर् अवोक्ष्यायन्तु पितरो मनोजवस इत्य् अभिमन्त्र्य सकृदाच्छिन्नं बर्हिरूर्णामृदु स्योनं पितृभ्यस्त्वा भराम्यहम् /
text_mt: With the words: “The asuras, rakṣases, and piśācas seated on the altar ground are slain,” between the gārhapatya and anvāhāryapacana, or to the southeast of the anvāhāryapacana, having raised an altar ground one wooden sword’s length facing southeast away [from the fires], sprinkling it with water with the words: “Let the ancestors be cleansed,” and addressing it with: “May the ancestors, swift as thought, come hither,” [he strews] the sacrificial grass cut in a single stroke [saying]: “Soft as wool, comfortable, for the ancestors I bring you...”

sanskrit_iast: asminsīdantu me pitaraḥ somyāḥ pitāmahāḥ prapitāmahāścānugaiḥ saheti sakṛdācchinnena barhiṣā vediṃ stṛṇāti
meaning: अस्मिन्सीदन्तु मे पितरः सोम्याः पितामहाः प्रपितामहाश्चानुगैः सहेति सकृदाच्छिन्नेन बर्हिषा वेदिं स्तृणाति
text_mt: With [the words,] 'May my fathers, soma-loving, grandfathers, and great-grandfathers sit on this together with their followers,' he strews the altar ground with the sacrificial grass cut in a single stroke.

sanskrit_iast: utpūtena navanītenānutpūtena vā sarpiṣā sthālīpākamabhighāryaikasphyāyāṃ mekṣaṇamāsādya sthālīpākamāsādayati
meaning: उत्पूतेन नवनीतेनानुत्पूतेन वा सर्पिषा स्थालीपाकमभिघार्यैकस्फ्यायां मेक्षणमासाद्य स्थालीपाकमासादयति
text_mt: Having basted the mess of boiled rice with clarified butter that has been purified, or with unpurified ghee, and having placed the stirring-spoon on the [furrow made with] a single wooden sword, he places the mess of boiled rice [there].
To the south, one by one, he sets down a cushion-mattress, an eye-salve, an unguent, and a water-jar.

sanskrit_iast: adhvaryur upavīto dakṣiṇāṃ jānvācya mekṣaṇa upastīrya tenāvadāyābhighārya somāya pitṛpītāya svadhā nama iti dakṣiṇāgnau juhoti
meaning: अध्वर्युर् उपवीतो दक्षिणां जान्वाच्य मेक्षण उपस्तीर्य तेनावदायाभिघार्य सोमाय पितृपीताय स्वधा नम इति दक्षिणाग्नौ जुहोति
text_mt: The adhvaryu, wearing his sacred cord over the left shoulder, having bent his right knee, having underlaid [an oblation] on the stirring-spoon, having cut an offering with it, and having basted it, offers into the anvāhāryapacana fire with [the words,] 'To Soma, drunk by the fathers, svadhā, homage!'

sanskrit_iast: yamāyāṅgirasvate pitṛmate svadhā nama iti dvitīyām /
meaning: यमायाङ्गिरस्वते पितृमते स्वधा नम इति द्वितीयाम् /
text_mt: [He offers] the second [oblation with the words,] 'To Yama, accompanied by the Aṅgirases, accompanied by the fathers, svadhā, homage!'

sanskrit_iast: agnaye kavyavāhanāya svadhā nama iti tṛtīyām
meaning: अग्नये कव्यवाहनाय स्वधा नम इति तृतीयाम्
text_mt: [He offers] the third [oblation with the words,] 'To Agni Kavyavāhana, svadhā, homage!'

sanskrit_iast: ye mekṣaṇe taṇḍulāstān hutvā tūṣṇīṃ mekṣaṇam ādadhāti
meaning: ये मेक्षणे तण्डुलास्तान् हुत्वा तूष्णीं मेक्षणम् आदधाति
text_mt: Having offered whichever rice grains are on the stirring-spoon, he silently places the stirring-spoon [on the fire].
'May the Asuras go away, having the form of the fathers, who go about putting on various forms;

sanskrit_iast: parāpuro nipuro ye bharanty agniṣṭāṃl lokāt praṇudātyasmāt //
meaning: परापुरो निपुरो ये भरन्त्य् अग्निष्टांल् लोकात् प्रणुदात्यस्मात् //
text_mt: who carry off higher citadels and lower citadels; may Agni expel them from this world.'

sanskrit_iast: ye devāḥ pitaro ye ca mānuṣā ye garbhe mamruruta ye parāstāḥ /
meaning: ये देवाः पितरो ये च मानुषा ये गर्भे मम्रुरुत ये परास्ताः /
text_mt: 'Those who are divine fathers, and those who are human, who died in the womb and who were cast away,

sanskrit_iast: ya ucchatā uta ye nikhātāste samyañca iha mādayantām //
meaning: य उच्छता उत ये निखातास्ते सम्यञ्च इह मादयन्ताम् //
text_mt: who were left above and who were buried—may they together rejoice here.'

sanskrit_iast: ye rūpāṇi pratimuñcamānā asurāḥ santaḥ svadhayā caranti /
meaning: ये रूपाणि प्रतिमुञ्चमाना असुराः सन्तः स्वधया चरन्ति /
text_mt: 'Those who, putting on forms, being Asuras, go about with the svadhā;

sanskrit_iast: parāpuro nipuro ye bharanty agniṣṭāṃl lokāt praṇudāty asmāt //
meaning: परापुरो निपुरो ये भरन्त्य् अग्निष्टांल् लोकात् प्रणुदात्य् अस्मात् //
text_mt: who carry off higher citadels and lower citadels; may Agni expel them from this world.'
'Those who, having the likeness of relatives, being Asuras, have entered among the fathers through magic craft;

sanskrit_iast: parāpuro nipuro ye bharanty agne tānasmātpraṇudasva lokāditi dakṣiṇāgner ekolmukaṃ dhūpāyaddharati
meaning: परापुरो निपुरो ये भरन्त्य् अग्ने तानस्मात्प्रणुदस्व लोकादिति दक्षिणाग्नेर् एकोल्मुकं धूपायद्धरति
text_mt: who carry off higher citadels and lower citadels; O Agni, expel them from this world!'—with these words he takes a smoking firebrand from the anvāhāryapacana fire.

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇāpūrvamavāntaradeśaṃ sakṛtsphyenollikhyodīratāmavara ity adbhir avokṣyollikhitānte nidadhāti
meaning: दक्षिणापूर्वमवान्तरदेशं सकृत्स्फ्येनोल्लिख्योदीरतामवर इत्य् अद्भिर् अवोक्ष्योल्लिखितान्ते निदधाति
text_mt: Having drawn a single line with the wooden sword in the south-eastern intermediate quarter, and having sprinkled it with water with [the verse,] 'May the lower ones arise...', he sets [the firebrand] down at the end of the line.

meaning: यजमानो ऽत ऊर्ध्वं प्राचीनावीती कर्माणि करोति
text_mt: From here onwards, the sacrificer, wearing his sacred cord over the right shoulder, performs the rites.

sanskrit_iast: mārjayantāṃ mama pitaro mārjayantāṃ mama pitāmāhā mārjayantāṃ mama prapitāmahā ity ekasphyāyāṃ trīn udakāñjālīnninayati
meaning: मार्जयन्तां मम पितरो मार्जयन्तां मम पितामाहा मार्जयन्तां मम प्रपितामहा इत्य् एकस्फ्यायां त्रीन् उदकाञ्जालीन्निनयति
text_mt: With [the words,] 'May my fathers cleanse themselves; may my grandfathers cleanse themselves; may my great-grandfathers cleanse themselves,' he pours out three handfuls of water on the [furrow made with] a single wooden sword.
Or he sprinkles round counter-clockwise three times.
The followers of the Vājasaneyi recension prescribe three vessels of water.

sanskrit_iast: savyaṃ jānvācyāvācīnapāṇiḥ sakṛdācchinne barhiṣi dakṣiṇāpavargānpiṇḍāndadāty etatte tatāsau ye ca tvāmanvityetaiḥ pratimantram
meaning: सव्यं जान्वाच्यावाचीनपाणिः सकृदाच्छिन्ने बर्हिषि दक्षिणापवर्गान्पिण्डान्ददात्य् एतत्ते ततासौ ये च त्वामन्वित्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रम्
text_mt: Having bent his left knee, with his hand turned downwards, he presents the rice-balls ending towards the south on the sacrificial grass cut in a single stroke, each with its respective formula: 'This for you, father, N.N., and whoever follow you.'
Or [he presents rice-balls] beginning with the great-grandfather [and going backwards].
[The rice-ball] does not go without a name being uttered.

sanskrit_iast: yadi bandhū na vidyātsvadhā pitṛbhyaḥ pṛthiviṣadbhya iti prathamaṃ piṇḍaṃ dadyāt /
meaning: यदि बन्धू न विद्यात्स्वधा पितृभ्यः पृथिविषद्भ्य इति प्रथमं पिण्डं दद्यात् /
text_mt: If he does not know the relatives, he should present the first rice-ball with [the words,] 'Svadhā to the fathers dwelling on the earth;'
the second with [the words,] 'Svadhā to the fathers dwelling in the midspace;'
the third with [the words,] 'Svadhā to the fathers dwelling in heaven.'

sanskrit_iast: yadi dvipitā syād ekaikasmin piṇḍe dvaudvāv upalakṣayet
meaning: यदि द्विपिता स्याद् एकैकस्मिन् पिण्डे द्वौद्वाव् उपलक्षयेत्
text_mt: If he should have two fathers, he should designate two at each rice-ball.

sanskrit_iast: yadi jīvapitā na dadyādā homātkṛtvā viramet
meaning: यदि जीवपिता न दद्यादा होमात्कृत्वा विरमेत्
text_mt: If his father is living, he should not present [rice-balls]; having performed [the rite] up to the oblation, he should stop.
'What my mother went astray, and what she did without following [proper order],

sanskrit_iast: tan me retaḥ pitā vṛṅktāmābhuranyopapadyataṃ pitṛbhyaḥ svadhāvibhyaḥ svadhā namaḥ pitāmahebhyaḥ svadhāvibhyaḥ svadhā namaḥ prapitāmahebhyaḥ svadhāvibhyaḥ svadhā nama ity upasthāyātra pitaro yathābhāgaṃ mandadhvam ity uktvā parāṅ āvartate
meaning: तन् मे रेतः पिता वृङ्क्तामाभुरन्योपपद्यतं पितृभ्यः स्वधाविभ्यः स्वधा नमः पितामहेभ्यः स्वधाविभ्यः स्वधा नमः प्रपितामहेभ्यः स्वधाविभ्यः स्वधा नम इत्य् उपस्थायात्र पितरो यथाभागं मन्दध्वम् इत्य् उक्त्वा पराङ् आवर्तते
text_mt: that seed of mine may my father receive; another is [born as] an aborted fetus. To the fathers endowed with svadhā, svadhā, homage! To the grandfathers endowed with svadhā, svadhā, homage! To the great-grandfathers endowed with svadhā, svadhā, homage!'—having worshipped with these words, and having said, 'Here, O fathers, revel according to your share,' he turns away.

sanskrit_iast: amīmadanta pitaraḥ somyā iti vyāvṛtta ūṣmaṇy abhiparyāvartate 'vyāvṛtte vā
meaning: अमीमदन्त पितरः सोम्या इति व्यावृत्त ऊष्मण्य् अभिपर्यावर्तते ऽव्यावृत्ते वा
text_mt: When the steam has ceased—or while it has not yet ceased—he turns back towards [the rice-balls] with [the words,] 'The soma-loving fathers have revelled.'

sanskrit_iast: yaḥ sthālyāṃ śeṣastamavajighrati ye samānāḥ samanasaḥ pitaro yamarājye /
meaning: यः स्थाल्यां शेषस्तमवजिघ्रति ये समानाः समनसः पितरो यमराज्ये /
text_mt: He smells what remains in the pot, [saying:] 'The fathers who are united, of like mind, in Yama's realm:

sanskrit_iast: teṣāṃ lokaḥ svadhā namo yajño deveṣu kalpatāṃ vīraṃ dhatta pitara iti
meaning: तेषां लोकः स्वधा नमो यज्ञो देवेषु कल्पतां वीरं धत्त पितर इति
text_mt: theirs is the world, svadhā, homage! May the sacrifice be accomplished among the gods; bestow a hero, O fathers!'

sanskrit_iast: āmayāvinā prāśyo 'nnādyakāmena prāśyo yo 'lamannādyāya sannādyāntena vā prāśyaḥ
meaning: आमयाविना प्राश्यो ऽन्नाद्यकामेन प्राश्यो यो ऽलमन्नाद्याय सन्नाद्यान्तेन वा प्राश्यः
text_mt: It should be eaten by one who is sick, or it should be eaten by one who desires food, or it should be eaten by one who is capable of [eating] food, as the end of his eating.
Having poured three handfuls of water on the [furrow made with] a single wooden sword as before, he presents eye-salve, unguent, and clothing three times next to each rice-ball.
'Anoint your eyes, father, N.N.! Anoint your eyes, grandfather, N.N.! Anoint your eyes, great-grandfather, N.N.!'—[thus he presents] the eye-salve.
In the same manner, [for] the unguent, he adapts the formula: 'Rub yourself...'

sanskrit_iast: yadi nāmāni na vidyād āñjatāṃ mama pitara āñjatāṃ mama pitāmahā āñjatāṃprapitāmahā ity āñjanam /
meaning: यदि नामानि न विद्याद् आञ्जतां मम पितर आञ्जतां मम पितामहा आञ्जतांप्रपितामहा इत्य् आञ्जनम् /
text_mt: If he does not know the names, [he presents] the eye-salve with [the formula:] 'May my fathers anoint their eyes; may my grandfathers anoint their eyes; may my great-grandfathers anoint their eyes.'
In the same manner, [for] the unguent, he adapts the formula: 'May they rub themselves...'

sanskrit_iast: etāni vaḥ pitaro vāsāṃsyato no 'nyatpitaro mā yoṣṭeti vāsaso daśāṃ chittvā nidadhāty ūrṇāstukāṃ vā pūrve vayasi /
meaning: एतानि वः पितरो वासांस्यतो नो ऽन्यत्पितरो मा योष्टेति वाससो दशां छित्त्वा निदधात्य् ऊर्णास्तुकां वा पूर्वे वयसि /
text_mt: With [the words,] 'These are your clothes, O fathers; do not sever from us otherwise, O fathers,' having cut off the fringe of a garment, he places it down, or a tuft of wool, if he is in the earlier stage of life;

sanskrit_iast: vītoṣmasu piṇḍeṣu namo vaḥ pitaro rasāyeti namaskārāñjapati
meaning: वीतोष्मसु पिण्डेषु नमो वः पितरो रसायेति नमस्काराञ्जपति
text_mt: When the rice-balls are devoid of heat, he mutters the salutations: 'Homage to you, O fathers, for the sap...'

sanskrit_iast: gṛhānnaḥ pitaro datta sado vaḥ pitaro deṣmeti pitṝnupatiṣṭhate
meaning: गृहान्नः पितरो दत्त सदो वः पितरो देष्मेति पितॄनुपतिष्ठते
text_mt: He attends upon the fathers with [the words,] 'Give us homes, O fathers; we would give you an abode, O fathers.'

sanskrit_iast: ūrjaṃ vahantīramṛtaṃ ghṛtaṃ payaḥ kīlālaṃ parisrutam /
meaning: ऊर्जं वहन्तीरमृतं घृतं पयः कीलालं परिस्रुतम् /
text_mt: 'Bearing nourishment, ambrosia, ghee, milk, sweet drink, foaming wine:

sanskrit_iast: svadhā stha tarpayata me pitṝn ity udakaṃ ninayati
meaning: स्वधा स्थ तर्पयत मे पितॄन् इत्य् उदकं निनयति
text_mt: you are svadhā; satisfy my fathers!'—with these words he pours out water.
He attends upon [the fires] with the verses containing the word 'manas': 'We invoke the mind...'

sanskrit_iast: uttiṣṭhata pitaraḥ preta śūrā yamasya panthāmanuvetā purāṇam /
meaning: उत्तिष्ठत पितरः प्रेत शूरा यमस्य पन्थामनुवेता पुराणम् /
text_mt: 'Arise, O fathers! Go forth, O heroes, following Yama's ancient path!

sanskrit_iast: dhattādasmāsu draviṇaṃ yac ca bhadraṃ pra ṇo brūtādbhāgadhāṃ devatāsv iti pitṝn utthāpayati
meaning: धत्तादस्मासु द्रविणं यच् च भद्रं प्र णो ब्रूताद्भागधां देवतास्व् इति पितॄन् उत्थापयति
text_mt: Bestow wealth and whatever is auspicious upon us; declare our share among the deities!'—with these words he makes the fathers depart.

sanskrit_iast: pareta pitaraḥ somyā iti pravāhaṇyā pitṝn pravāhayati
meaning: परेत पितरः सोम्या इति प्रवाहण्या पितॄन् प्रवाहयति
text_mt: With the dismissive verse, 'Depart, O soma-loving fathers...', he sends the fathers away.

sanskrit_iast: prajāpate na tvadetānīti yajñopavitī gārhapatyadeśaṃ gacchati
meaning: प्रजापते न त्वदेतानीति यज्ञोपविती गार्हपत्यदेशं गच्छति
text_mt: With [the verse,] 'O Prajāpati, none other than you...', wearing his sacred cord over the left shoulder, he goes to the place of the gārhapatya fire.
He attends upon the gārhapatya fire with the paṅkti verse, 'What [lies in] the midspace...'

sanskrit_iast: apāṃ tvauṣadhīnāṃ rasaṃ prāśayāmi bhūtakṛtaṃ garbhaṃ dhatsveti madhyamaṃ piṇḍaṃ patnyai prayacchati
meaning: अपां त्वौषधीनां रसं प्राशयामि भूतकृतं गर्भं धत्स्वेति मध्यमं पिण्डं पत्न्यै प्रयच्छति
text_mt: With [the words,] 'I make you eat the essence of water and plants; produce an embryo that causes well-being,' he gives the middle rice-ball to his wife.
'Deposit an embryo, O fathers, a boy garlanded with lotuses,

sanskrit_iast: yatheha puruṣo 'sad iti taṃ patnī praśnāti /
meaning: यथेह पुरुषो ऽसद् इति तं पत्नी प्रश्नाति /
text_mt: so that there may be a man here'—with these words the wife eats it.
'She becomes apt to give birth to a male,' so it is known.
'Those kin of mine who are of one mind, living among the living...'

sanskrit_iast: teṣāṃ śrīr mayi kalpatām asmiṃl loke śataṃ samā ity avaśiṣṭānām ekaṃ yajamānaḥ prāśnāti /
meaning: तेषां श्रीर् मयि कल्पताम् अस्मिंल् लोके शतं समा इत्य् अवशिष्टानाम् एकं यजमानः प्राश्नाति /
text_mt: With the words, “May their prosperity belong to me, in this world for a hundred years,” the sacrificer eats one of the remaining [balls].

sanskrit_iast: sthālyāṃ piṇḍān samavadhāya ye samānā iti sakṛdācchinnamagnau praharati
meaning: स्थाल्यां पिण्डान् समवधाय ये समाना इति सकृदाच्छिन्नमग्नौ प्रहरति
text_mt: Putting the balls together in the cooking-pot, he casts [them] onto the fire along with the once-severed [darbha blade], with the words, “Those who are equals...”

sanskrit_iast: abhūnno dūto haviṣo jātavedā avāḍḍhavyāni surabhīṇi kṛtvā /
meaning: अभून्नो दूतो हविषो जातवेदा अवाड्ढव्यानि सुरभीणि कृत्वा /
text_mt: “Jātavedas has become our messenger for the oblation, carrying the offerings after making them fragrant.

sanskrit_iast: prādāḥ pitṛbhyaḥ svadhayā te akṣanprajānannagne punarapyehi devān ity ekolmukaṃ pratyapisṛjya prokṣya pātrāṇi dvandvam abhyudāharati
meaning: प्रादाः पितृभ्यः स्वधया ते अक्षन्प्रजानन्नग्ने पुनरप्येहि देवान् इत्य् एकोल्मुकं प्रत्यपिसृज्य प्रोक्ष्य पात्राणि द्वन्द्वम् अभ्युदाहरति
text_mt: You have given [them] to the ancestors; they have eaten according to the svadhā-call. Knowing [this], O Agni, come back again to the gods”—having pushed back the single brand [into the fire] with these words, and sprinkled the vessels with water, he takes them away in pairs.
The Piṇḍapitṛyajña is concluded.

sanskrit_iast: apaḥ piṇḍān abhyavahared brāhmaṇaṃ vā prāśayet
meaning: अपः पिण्डान् अभ्यवहरेद् ब्राह्मणं वा प्राशयेत्
text_mt: He should throw the balls into water, or he should feed [them] to a brahmin.
This [rite] is prescribed in just the same way for one who has not set up the solemn fires (anāhitāgni).
The cooking rules and the oblation take place in the aupāsana fire.
He should attend upon whichever fire he offers in.
There, the word 'gārhapatya' is omitted, because of the prohibition of the consecration [of that fire].

sanskrit_iast: amāvāsyāyāṃ rātryāṃ svayaṃ yajamāno yavāgvāgnihotraṃ juhoty agnihotroccheṣaṇamātañcanārthaṃ nidadhāti
meaning: अमावास्यायां रात्र्यां स्वयं यजमानो यवाग्वाग्निहोत्रं जुहोत्य् अग्निहोत्रोच्छेषणमातञ्चनार्थं निदधाति
text_mt: On the night of the new moon, the sacrificer himself offers the agnihotra with barley gruel, and sets aside the agnihotra remnant for the purpose of curdling.
On this night, not even children obtain milk from him.
When the evening agnihotra has been offered, he has the evening milking done.

sanskrit_iast: agnīn paristīryāgnimagnī vā sāṃnāyyapātrāṇi prakṣālyottareṇa gārhapatyaṃ darbhān saṃstīrya dvandvaṃ nyañci prayunakti
meaning: अग्नीन् परिस्तीर्याग्निमग्नी वा सांनाय्यपात्राणि प्रक्षाल्योत्तरेण गार्हपत्यं दर्भान् संस्तीर्य द्वन्द्वं न्यञ्चि प्रयुनक्ति
text_mt: Having strewn grass around the fires—or around the fire, or the [two] fires—and washed the sāṃnāyya vessels, he strews darbha grass north of the gārhapatya and arranges [the vessels] downward in pairs:

sanskrit_iast: kumbhīṃ śākhāpavitramabhidhānīṃ nidāne dārupātraṃ dohanamayaspātraṃ dārupātraṃ vāpidhānārtham agnihotrahavaṇīm upaveṣaṃ ca
meaning: कुम्भीं शाखापवित्रमभिधानीं निदाने दारुपात्रं दोहनमयस्पात्रं दारुपात्रं वापिधानार्थम् अग्निहोत्रहवणीम् उपवेषं च
text_mt: the pot, the branch-strainer, the halter, the two hobble-ropes, the wooden vessel, the milking vessel, a metal vessel or a wooden vessel for the purpose of covering, the agnihotra-ladle, and the fire-stirrer.
He makes two strainers out of two darbha blades that are equal, unbroken at the tip, and a span in measure.

sanskrit_iast: pavitre stho vaiṣṇavī vāyurvāṃ manasā punātv iti tṛṇaṃ kāṣṭhaṃ vāntardhāya chinatti
meaning: पवित्रे स्थो वैष्णवी वायुर्वां मनसा पुनात्व् इति तृणं काष्ठं वान्तर्धाय छिनत्ति
text_mt: With the words, “You two are strainers belonging to Viṣṇu; may Vāyu purify you with his mind,” he cuts [them], placing a blade of grass or a piece of wood in between.

sanskrit_iast: viṣṇor manasā pūte stha ity adbhir anumṛjya pavitrāntarhitāyām agnihotrahavaṇyāmapa ānīyodagagrābhyāṃ pavitrābhyāṃ prokṣaṇīrutpunāti devo vaḥ savitotpunātv iti prathamam /
meaning: विष्णोर् मनसा पूते स्थ इत्य् अद्भिर् अनुमृज्य पवित्रान्तर्हितायाम् अग्निहोत्रहवण्यामप आनीयोदगग्राभ्यां पवित्राभ्यां प्रोक्षणीरुत्पुनाति देवो वः सवितोत्पुनात्व् इति प्रथमम् /
text_mt: Wiping them with water with the words, “You two are purified by the mind of Viṣṇu,” and bringing water into the agnihotra-ladle with the two strainers placed inside, he purifies the sprinkling waters upwards with the two strainers pointing north, first with the words, “May god Savitṛ purify you”;
secondly with the words, “With an unbroken strainer”;
thirdly with the words, “With the rays of the good Sun.”

sanskrit_iast: āpo devīragrepuva ity abhimantryottānāni pātrāṇi paryāvartya śundhadhvaṃ daivyāya darmaṇa iti triḥ prokṣya prajñāte pavitre nidadhāti //
meaning: आपो देवीरग्रेपुव इत्य् अभिमन्त्र्योत्तानानि पात्राणि पर्यावर्त्य शुन्धध्वं दैव्याय दर्मण इति त्रिः प्रोक्ष्य प्रज्ञाते पवित्रे निदधाति //
text_mt: Addressing [them] with the words, “O divine waters, purifying first,” and turning the vessels face up, he sprinkles [them] three times with the words, “Be purified for the divine rite,” and deposits the two strainers in a known place.

sanskrit_iast: āpo devīḥ śuddhā sthemā pātrāṇi śundhata /
meaning: आपो देवीः शुद्धा स्थेमा पात्राणि शुन्धत /
text_mt: “O divine waters, you are pure; purify these vessels.
And purify the parṇa-bark for the curdling [material] of the gods.
Purified by god Savitṛ with the rays of the good Sun,

sanskrit_iast: gāṃdohapavitre rajjuṃ sarvā pātrāṇi śundhateti prokṣyamāṇānyabhimantryaitā ācaranti madhumadduhānāḥ prajāvatīryaśaso viśvarūpāḥ /
meaning: गांदोहपवित्रे रज्जुं सर्वा पात्राणि शुन्धतेति प्रोक्ष्यमाणान्यभिमन्त्र्यैता आचरन्ति मधुमद्दुहानाः प्रजावतीर्यशसो विश्वरूपाः /
text_mt: purify the cow-milking strainers, the rope, and all the vessels”—with these words he addresses them while they are being sprinkled; and, with the words: “These come, yielding sweet milk, rich in offspring, glorious, multiform,

sanskrit_iast: bahvīrbhavantīrupajāyamānā iha va indro ramayatu gāva iti gā āyatīḥ pratīkṣate yajamānaḥ
meaning: बह्वीर्भवन्तीरुपजायमाना इह व इन्द्रो रमयतु गाव इति गा आयतीः प्रतीक्षते यजमानः
text_mt: becoming many, multiplying; may Indra delight you cows here,” the sacrificer looks at the cows as they arrive.

sanskrit_iast: niṣṭaptaṃ rakṣo niṣṭapto 'ghaśaṃsa iti gārhapatye sāṃnāyyapātrāṇi pratitapya dhṛṣṭir asi brahma yacchetyupaveṣamādāya nirūḍhaṃ janyaṃ bhayaṃ nirūḍhāḥ senā abhītvarīr iti gārhapatyādudīco 'ṅgārānnirūhya mātariśvano gharmo 'sīti teṣu kumbhīm adhiśrayati
meaning: निष्टप्तं रक्षो निष्टप्तो ऽघशंस इति गार्हपत्ये सांनाय्यपात्राणि प्रतितप्य धृष्टिर् असि ब्रह्म यच्छेत्युपवेषमादाय निरूढं जन्यं भयं निरूढाः सेना अभीत्वरीर् इति गार्हपत्यादुदीचो ऽङ्गारान्निरूह्य मातरिश्वनो घर्मो ऽसीति तेषु कुम्भीम् अधिश्रयति
text_mt: Having heated the sāṃnāyya vessels over the gārhapatya with the words, “Heated away is the demon, heated away the evil-speaker,” and taking the fire-stirrer with the words, “You are the poker; uphold the sacred word,” he pushes aside live coals to the north from the gārhapatya with the words, “Driven away is danger from strangers, driven away are the marching armies,” and sets the pot on them with the words, “You are the caldron of Mātariśvan.”
“For the non-falling of the sacrifice, I set the two pots down.

sanskrit_iast: paśubhiḥ saṃnītaṃ bibhṛtām indrāya śṛtaṃ dadhīti vā
meaning: पशुभिः संनीतं बिभृताम् इन्द्राय शृतं दधीति वा
text_mt: Brought together by the beasts, may they hold boiled milk and curds for Indra”—or [he sets it down with this verse].

sanskrit_iast: bhṛgūṇām aṅgirasāṃ tapasā tapyasveti pradakṣiṇam aṅgāraiḥ paryūhya vasūnāṃ pavitramasīti tasyāṃ prāgagraṃ śākhāpavitramatyādadhāti
meaning: भृगूणाम् अङ्गिरसां तपसा तप्यस्वेति प्रदक्षिणम् अङ्गारैः पर्यूह्य वसूनां पवित्रमसीति तस्यां प्रागग्रं शाखापवित्रमत्यादधाति
text_mt: Having surrounded [the pot] clockwise with coals with the words, “Be heated with the heat of the Bhṛgus and the Aṅgirases,” he places the branch-strainer over it with its tip to the east, with the words, “You are the strainer of the Vasus.”
Touching the pot, he restrains his speech.
Or he sits holding the strainer.
He takes up the halter with the words, “You are the girdle of Aditi.”
“You are the thirty-third of the threads; come together with the strainer.
May this auspicious rope, the halter, serve the inviolable cow”—with these words the sacrificer addresses [the halter] as it is being taken.
He ties up the calf with the words, “You are Pūṣan.”
He issues the call: “Announce to me [the cow] when let loose [to the calf]!”
[The milker] calls out: “I let [her] loose!”

sanskrit_iast: ayakṣmā vaḥ prajayā saṃsṛjāmi rāyaspoṣeṇa bahulā bhavantīr iti vatsamupasṛjati
meaning: अयक्ष्मा वः प्रजया संसृजामि रायस्पोषेण बहुला भवन्तीर् इति वत्समुपसृजति
text_mt: With the words, “Free from disease, I unite you with your offspring; becoming abundant with increase of wealth,” he lets the calf loose.

sanskrit_iast: gāṃ copasṛṣṭāṃ vihāraṃ cāntareṇa mā saṃcāriṣṭeti saṃpreṣyati
meaning: गां चोपसृष्टां विहारं चान्तरेण मा संचारिष्टेति संप्रेष्यति
text_mt: He issues the call: “Do not pass between the cow that has been let loose and the sacrificial ground!”

sanskrit_iast: yady upasṛṣṭāṃ vyaveyātsāṃnāyyaṃ mā vilopīti brūyāt
meaning: यद्य् उपसृष्टां व्यवेयात्सांनाय्यं मा विलोपीति ब्रूयात्
text_mt: If one should cross between [them and] the cow let loose, he should say, “Let not the sāṃnāyya perish!”
[The milker] calls out: “I sit down [to milk]!”

sanskrit_iast: ayakṣmā vaḥ prajayā saṃsṛjāmi rāyaspoṣeṇa bahulā bhavantīḥ /
meaning: अयक्ष्मा वः प्रजया संसृजामि रायस्पोषेण बहुला भवन्तीः /
text_mt: “Free from disease, I unite you with your offspring; becoming abundant with increase of wealth,

sanskrit_iast: ūrjaṃ payaḥ pinvamānā ghṛtaṃ ca jīvā jīvantīr upa vaḥ sadeyam iti dogdhopasīdati
meaning: ऊर्जं पयः पिन्वमाना घृतं च जीवा जीवन्तीर् उप वः सदेयम् इति दोग्धोपसीदति
text_mt: swelling with vigor, milk, and ghee, living, may I sit down by you who are living”—with these words the milker sits down beside [the cow].
A Śūdra should not milk, or he may milk.

meaning: उपसृष्टां दुह्यमानां धाराघोषं च यजमानो ऽनुमन्त्रयते //
text_mt: The sacrificer follows [with mantras] the cow that has been let loose, as she is being milked, and the sound of the stream [of milk].
The one let loose with the words, “Free from disease, I unite you with your offspring.”
“May Heaven and Earth milk this sacrifice together.
May Dhātṛ with Soma, and Vāyu with the wind,
bestow wealth upon the sacrificer”—[with these words he follows] the one being milked.

sanskrit_iast: utsaṃ duhanti kalaśaṃ caturbilamiḍāṃ devīṃ madhumatīṃ suvarvidam /
meaning: उत्सं दुहन्ति कलशं चतुर्बिलमिडां देवीं मधुमतीं सुवर्विदम् /
text_mt: “They milk the spring, the jar with four openings, the divine Iḍā full of sweetness, finding the sun;

sanskrit_iast: tad indrāgnī jinvataṃ sūnṛtāvattadyajamānam amṛtatve dadhātv iti dhārāghoṣam
meaning: तद् इन्द्राग्नी जिन्वतं सूनृतावत्तद्यजमानम् अमृतत्वे दधात्व् इति धाराघोषम्
text_mt: may Indrāgnī quicken it, endowed with truth; may they place the sacrificer in immortality”—[with these words he follows] the sound of the stream [of milk].

sanskrit_iast: taṃ pṛcchati kāmadhukṣaḥ pra ṇo brūhīndrāya havir indriyam iti
meaning: तं पृच्छति कामधुक्षः प्र णो ब्रूहीन्द्राय हविर् इन्द्रियम् इति
text_mt: He asks him: “Which one have you milked? Declare to us the oblation, the power of Indra!”

sanskrit_iast: yasyāṃ devānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ payo hitam iti pratyāha
meaning: यस्यां देवानां मनुष्याणां पयो हितम् इति प्रत्याह
text_mt: [The milker] replies: "In whom the milk of gods and men is deposited."
He addresses [her] with the formula: "She is all-life."

sanskrit_iast: devastvā savitā punātu vasoḥ pavitreṇa śatadhāreṇa supuveti kumbhyāṃ tiraḥ pavitram āsiñcati
meaning: देवस्त्वा सविता पुनातु वसोः पवित्रेण शतधारेण सुपुवेति कुम्भ्यां तिरः पवित्रम् आसिञ्चति
text_mt: He pours [the milk] into the vessel across the strainer with the formula: "May the divine Savitṛ purify you with the faultless strainer of Vasu, possessing a hundred streams."

sanskrit_iast: huta stoko huto drapsa iti vipruṣo 'numantrayate
meaning: हुत स्तोको हुतो द्रप्स इति विप्रुषो ऽनुमन्त्रयते
text_mt: He addresses the drops with the formula: "The drop is offered, the drop is sacrificed."
In the same manner, he causes the second and the third [cow] to be milked.
He addresses the second with: "She is all-embracing."
[He addresses] the third with: "She is all-creating."

sanskrit_iast: tisro dohayitvā bahu dugdhīndrāya devebhyo havyamāpyāyataṃ punaḥ /
meaning: तिस्रो दोहयित्वा बहु दुग्धीन्द्राय देवेभ्यो हव्यमाप्यायतं पुनः /
text_mt: Having caused three to be milked, [he recites:] "Yield abundantly for Indra; may the offering swell again for the gods;

sanskrit_iast: vatsebhyo manuṣyebhyaḥ punardohāya kalpatām iti trir vācaṃ visṛjyānanvārabhya tūṣṇīm uttarā dohayitvā dohane 'pa ānīya saṃpṛcyadhvamṛtāvarīr iti dumbhyāṃ saṃkṣālanamānīyāviṣyandayansuśṛtaṃ karoti
meaning: वत्सेभ्यो मनुष्येभ्यः पुनर्दोहाय कल्पताम् इति त्रिर् वाचं विसृज्यानन्वारभ्य तूष्णीम् उत्तरा दोहयित्वा दोहने ऽप आनीय संपृच्यध्वमृतावरीर् इति दुम्भ्यां संक्षालनमानीयाविष्यन्दयन्सुशृतं करोति
text_mt: may it be fit for the calves, for men, for milking again." Having released speech three times, without holding on [to the vessel], he causes the remaining [cows] to be milked silently. Pouring water into the milk-pail, and pouring the wash-water into the vessel with: "Mix, O you true to the cosmic order," he boils it thoroughly without letting it overflow.

sanskrit_iast: dṛṃha gā dṛmha gopatiṃ mā vo yajñpatī riṣaditi vartma kurvan prāgudvāsayaty udak prāgudagvā
meaning: दृंह गा दृम्ह गोपतिं मा वो यज्ञ्पती रिषदिति वर्त्म कुर्वन् प्रागुद्वासयत्य् उदक् प्रागुदग्वा
text_mt: With the formula: "Make the cows firm, make the lord of cows firm; may your master of sacrifice not come to harm," he moves [the vessel] off [the fire], making a path, towards the east, towards the north, or towards the northeast.

sanskrit_iast: ekasyā dvayostisṛṇāṃ vaikāhe dvyāhe tryahe vā purastād upavasathād ātañcanārthaṃ dohayitvā saṃtatamabhiduhantyopavasathāt
meaning: एकस्या द्वयोस्तिसृणां वैकाहे द्व्याहे त्र्यहे वा पुरस्ताद् उपवसथाद् आतञ्चनार्थं दोहयित्वा संततमभिदुहन्त्योपवसथात्
text_mt: Having caused one, two, or three cows to be milked for the sake of curdling-agent one day, two days, or three days before the upavasatha day, they milk continuously [each day] until the upavasatha day.
With that he curdles [the milk], its bottom having cooled.
With curd, [he curdles it] with the formula: "With soma I curdle you, curd for Indra."

sanskrit_iast: yajñasya saṃtatir asi yajñasya tvā saṃtatimanusaṃtanomītyagnihotroccheṣaṇamanvavadhāyāyaṃ payaḥ somaṃ kṛtvā svāṃ yonim apigacchatu /
meaning: यज्ञस्य संततिर् असि यज्ञस्य त्वा संततिमनुसंतनोमीत्यग्निहोत्रोच्छेषणमन्ववधायायं पयः सोमं कृत्वा स्वां योनिम् अपिगच्छतु /
text_mt: Having put in the remainder of the agnihotra with: "You are the continuity of the sacrifice; I continue you following the continuity of the sacrifice," [and with:] "Having made this milk soma, let it go to its own source;

sanskrit_iast: parṇavalkaḥ pavitraṃ saumyaḥ somāddhi nirmita iti parivāsanaśakalamanvavadadhāti
meaning: पर्णवल्कः पवित्रं सौम्यः सोमाद्धि निर्मित इति परिवासनशकलमन्ववदधाति
text_mt: the parṇa bark is the strainer, soma-natured, for it is produced from soma," he puts in a wood-chip cut off [from the parṇa branch].

sanskrit_iast: oṣadhayaḥ pūtikāḥ kvalāstaṇḍulāḥ parṇavalkā ity ātañcanavikalpāḥ
meaning: ओषधयः पूतिकाः क्वलास्तण्डुलाः पर्णवल्का इत्य् आतञ्चनविकल्पाः
text_mt: Plants, pūtikā plants, bark of badarī, grains of rice, [and] parṇa bark are the alternatives for the curdling-agent.
In the absence of the agnihotra remainder, he should curdle with rice grains; in the absence of rice grains, with plants.

sanskrit_iast: āpo haivḥṣu jāgṛta yathā deveṣu jāgratha /
meaning: आपो हैव्ःषु जागृत यथा देवेषु जाग्रथ /
text_mt: "O waters, keep watch over the offerings, just as you keep watch among the gods;

sanskrit_iast: evam asminyajñe yajamānāya jāgṛtetyayaspātre dārupātre vāpa ānīyādastamasi viṣṇave tvā yajñāyāpi dadhāmy aham /
meaning: एवम् अस्मिन्यज्ञे यजमानाय जागृतेत्ययस्पात्रे दारुपात्रे वाप आनीयादस्तमसि विष्णवे त्वा यज्ञायापि दधाम्य् अहम् /
text_mt: even so, keep watch for the sacrificer in this sacrifice." Having poured water into an iron vessel or a wooden vessel, with: "You are the non-eaten; I cover you for the sacrifice to Viṣṇu;

sanskrit_iast: adbhirariktena pātreṇa yāḥ pūtāḥ pariśerata iti tenāpidadhāti //
meaning: अद्भिररिक्तेन पात्रेण याः पूताः परिशेरत इति तेनापिदधाति //
text_mt: which purified ones lie around with a vessel not empty of waters," with that he covers [the milk].
"May the divine vessel not made of clay be employed for the life of the sacrifice;

sanskrit_iast: tiraḥ pavitramatinītā āpo dhāraya mātiguriti yajamāno japati
meaning: तिरः पवित्रमतिनीता आपो धारय मातिगुरिति यजमानो जपति
text_mt: O waters carried across the strainer, hold fast; do not pass through," the sacrificer mutters.
If he should cover [it] with an earthen vessel, he should push in a blade of grass or a piece of wood under the lid.
With: "O Viṣṇu, guard the offering," he sets it down beneath [the cart].

sanskrit_iast: imau parṇaṃ ca darbhaṃ ca devānāṃ havyaśodhanau /
meaning: इमौ पर्णं च दर्भं च देवानां हव्यशोधनौ /
text_mt: "These two, the parṇa and the darbha grass, are the cleansers of the offering for the gods;

sanskrit_iast: prātarveṣāya gopāya viṣṇo havyaṃ hi rakṣasīti prajñātaṃ śākhāpavitraṃ nidadhāti
meaning: प्रातर्वेषाय गोपाय विष्णो हव्यं हि रक्षसीति प्रज्ञातं शाखापवित्रं निदधाति
text_mt: guard [the milk] for the morning service, for, O Viṣṇu, you guard the offering," he deposits the branch-strainer in a known place.

sanskrit_iast: tayaiva śākhayā darbhair vā sāyaṃdohavatprātardohāya vatsān apākaroti
meaning: तयैव शाखया दर्भैर् वा सायंदोहवत्प्रातर्दोहाय वत्सान् अपाकरोति
text_mt: With that same branch or with darbha grasses, he drives away the calves for the morning milking, in the same way as for the evening milking.
Having set down the potsherds, he causes the morning milk to be milked in the same way as the evening milking.
The curdling, the covering [with water], and the setting down [beneath the cart] are omitted.
One who has not performed a Soma sacrifice should not offer the saṃnāyya, or he may offer it.
One who has not attained prosperity should not sacrifice to Mahendra.
"Three, indeed, are those who have attained prosperity," it is said.

sanskrit_iast: aurvo gautamo bhāradvājaste 'nantaraṃ somejyāyā mahendraṃ yajeran
meaning: और्वो गौतमो भारद्वाजस्ते ऽनन्तरं सोमेज्याया महेन्द्रं यजेरन्
text_mt: An Aurva, a Gautama, and a Bhāradvāja: these should sacrifice to Mahendra immediately after their Soma sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast: tataḥ saṃpreṣyati paristṛṇīta paridhattāgniṃ parihito 'gnir yajamānaṃ bhunaktu /
meaning: ततः संप्रेष्यति परिस्तृणीत परिधत्ताग्निं परिहितो ऽग्निर् यजमानं भुनक्तु /
text_mt: Then he gives the ritual call: "Strew around, enclose the fire; may the enclosed fire benefit the sacrificer;

sanskrit_iast: apāṃ rasa oṣadhīṇāṃ suvarṇo niṣkā ime yajamānasya santu kāmadughā amutrāmuṣmiṃl loka iti
meaning: अपां रस ओषधीणां सुवर्णो निष्का इमे यजमानस्य सन्तु कामदुघा अमुत्रामुष्मिंल् लोक इति
text_mt: may the sap of the waters, the gold ornament of the plants, be wish-granting cows over there in yonder world for the sacrificer."
Some teach that this [mantra] is used while strewing around [the fires].

sanskrit_iast: udagagraiḥ prāgagraiś ca darbhair agnīn paristṛṇāti
meaning: उदगग्रैः प्रागग्रैश् च दर्भैर् अग्नीन् परिस्तृणाति
text_mt: He strews around the fires with darbha grasses having their tips pointing north and their tips pointing east.
Those on the west and on the east have their tips pointing north.
The adding fuel to the fires, the driving away of the calves, the firewood and sacrificial grass, the veda, the altar ground:
having done [all this] prior to the second tracing [of the altar ground], on the following day, having poured out the water-ointment, he should perform the second tracing.
And the strewing around [is done] on the preceding day at the new moon; but at the full moon, [there are only] the adding fuel to the fires, the strewing around, and the fasting.
Or, on the occasion of a single-day rite, everything is performed on the same day.
When the sun has risen, he begins the procedure of the full-moon sacrifice; before sunrise, that of the new-moon sacrifice.
He strews around the fires as before, if they are not already strewn around.

sanskrit_iast: karmaṇe vāṃ devebhyaḥ śakeyam iti hastāvavanijya yajñasya saṃtatirasi yajñasya tvā saṃtatyai stṛṇāmi saṃtatyai tvā yajñasyeti gārhapatyātprakramya saṃtatāmulaparājīṃ stṛṇātyāhavanīyāttūṣṇīṃ dakṣiṇāmuttarāṃ ca
meaning: कर्मणे वां देवेभ्यः शकेयम् इति हस्ताववनिज्य यज्ञस्य संततिरसि यज्ञस्य त्वा संतत्यै स्तृणामि संतत्यै त्वा यज्ञस्येति गार्हपत्यात्प्रक्रम्य संततामुलपराजीं स्तृणात्याहवनीयात्तूष्णीं दक्षिणामुत्तरां च
text_mt: With the formula: "May I be able to perform work for you two, the gods," having washed his hands, beginning from the gārhapatya up to the āhavanīya, he strews a continuous line of grass blades with: "You are the continuity of the sacrifice; I strew you for the continuity of the sacrifice, for the continuity of you, the sacrifice"; silently [he strews] the southern and the northern [lines].

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇenāhavanīyaṃ brahmayajamānayorāsane prakalpayati pūrvaṃ brahmaṇo 'paraṃ yajamānasya
meaning: दक्षिणेनाहवनीयं ब्रह्मयजमानयोरासने प्रकल्पयति पूर्वं ब्रह्मणो ऽपरं यजमानस्य
text_mt: To the south of the āhavanīya, he arranges the seats of the brahman and the sacrificer: the eastern one for the brahman, the western one for the sacrificer.

sanskrit_iast: uttareṇa gārhapatyāhavanīyau darbhān saṃstīrya dvandvaṃ nyañci pātrāṇi prayunakti daśāparāṇi daśa pūrvāṇi
meaning: उत्तरेण गार्हपत्याहवनीयौ दर्भान् संस्तीर्य द्वन्द्वं न्यञ्चि पात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति दशापराणि दश पूर्वाणि
text_mt: To the north of the gārhapatya and āhavanīya, having spread darbha grasses, he sets out the utensils in pairs facing downward: ten western and ten eastern.

sanskrit_iast: sphyaś ca kapālāni ceti yathāsamāmnātamaparāṇi prayujya sruvaṃ juhūmupabhṛtaṃ dhruvāṃ vedaṃ pātrīmājyasthālīṃ prāśitraharaṇamiḍāpātraṃ praṇītāpraṇayanam iti pūrvāṇi
meaning: स्फ्यश् च कपालानि चेति यथासमाम्नातमपराणि प्रयुज्य स्रुवं जुहूमुपभृतं ध्रुवां वेदं पात्रीमाज्यस्थालीं प्राशित्रहरणमिडापात्रं प्रणीताप्रणयनम् इति पूर्वाणि
text_mt: Having set out the western ones as handed down in tradition—the wooden sword and the potsherds—[he sets out] the eastern ones: the dipping-spoon, the juhū, the upabhṛt, the dhruvā, the veda, the vessel, the clarified-butter pot, the vessel for taking the prāśitra portion, the iḍā-vessel, [and] the vessel for bringing forward the praṇītā waters.
To the north of these, the remaining ones:
the pot for the anvāhārya cooked rice, the stone, the fire-stirrer, [and] the utensils for the morning milking.
Some teach that the bringing forward of the praṇītā waters takes place before the setting out of the utensils.
The sruva is made of khadira wood; the juhū is made of parṇa wood; the upabhṛt is made of aśvattha wood; the dhruvā is made of vikaṅkata wood.

sanskrit_iast: eteṣāṃ vā vṛkṣāṇām ekasya srucaḥ kārayet
meaning: एतेषां वा वृक्षाणाम् एकस्य स्रुचः कारयेत्
text_mt: Or he should cause the offering-ladles to be made from one of these trees.
They are a cubit in length or a forearm in length, having their tips at the top, their hollows on the bark side, and their mouths shaped like a swan's beak.
The wooden sword, the yoke-pin, [and] the prāśitra-vessel are made of khadira wood.
[Utensils] not meant for offering are made of varaṇa wood.

sanskrit_iast: atra pūrvavatpavitre karoti yadi na saṃnayati
meaning: अत्र पूर्ववत्पवित्रे करोति यदि न संनयति
text_mt: At this point he prepares the two strainers as before, if he does not offer the saṃnāyya.
For one who performs the Saṃnāyya, however, those [two strainers] are sufficient.

sanskrit_iast: vānaspatyo 'si devebhyaḥ śundhasveti praṇītāpraṇayanaṃ camasamadbhiḥ parikṣālayati tūṣṇīṃ kaṃsaṃ mṛnmayaṃ ca /
meaning: वानस्पत्यो ऽसि देवेभ्यः शुन्धस्वेति प्रणीताप्रणयनं चमसमद्भिः परिक्षालयति तूष्णीं कंसं मृन्मयं च /
text_mt: With 'You are of wood; cleanse yourself for the gods,' he rinses the cup for the Praṇītā water with water; silently [he rinses] a bronze vessel and an earthen one.

sanskrit_iast: kaṃsena praṇayedbrahmavarcasakāmasya mṛnmayena pratiṣṭhākāmasya godohanena paśukāmasya /
meaning: कंसेन प्रणयेद्ब्रह्मवर्चसकामस्य मृन्मयेन प्रतिष्ठाकामस्य गोदोहनेन पशुकामस्य /
text_mt: He should bring forward [the waters] with a bronze vessel for one who desires spiritual luster, with an earthen one for one who desires a firm foundation, [and] with a milking-pail for one who desires cattle.

sanskrit_iast: apareṇa gārhapatyaṃ pavitrāntarhitaṃ camasaṃ nidhāya tasminko vo gṛhṇāti sa vo gṛhṇātu kasmai vo gṛhṇāmi tasmai vo gṛhṇāmi poṣāya va ity apa ānayati
meaning: अपरेण गार्हपत्यं पवित्रान्तर्हितं चमसं निधाय तस्मिन्को वो गृह्णाति स वो गृह्णातु कस्मै वो गृह्णामि तस्मै वो गृह्णामि पोषाय व इत्य् अप आनयति
text_mt: Having placed the cup behind the gārhapatya, interposed by the two strainers, he pours in the water with 'Who draws you? Let him draw you! For whom do I draw you? For him I draw you! For your nourishment!'

sanskrit_iast: apo gṛhṇangrahīṣyaṃś ca pṛthivīṃ manasā dhyāyati
meaning: अपो गृह्णन्ग्रहीष्यंश् च पृथिवीं मनसा ध्यायति
text_mt: While drawing the water and when about to draw it, he meditates mentally on the earth.

sanskrit_iast: upabilaṃ camasaṃ pūrayitvā prokṣaṇīvadutpūyābhimantrya brahmannapaḥ praṇeṣyāmi yajamāna vācaṃ yaccheti saṃpreṣyati
meaning: उपबिलं चमसं पूरयित्वा प्रोक्षणीवदुत्पूयाभिमन्त्र्य ब्रह्मन्नपः प्रणेष्यामि यजमान वाचं यच्छेति संप्रेष्यति
text_mt: Having filled the cup up to the brim, purified it like the sprinkling water, and consecrated it, he gives the ritual call: 'O Brahman, I will bring forward the water; O sacrificer, restrain speech!'
Everywhere, he acts when the impulsion has been spoken.
While the waters are being brought forward, the adhvaryu and the sacrificer restrain speech until the [call to the] preparer of the oblation (haviṣkṛt).

sanskrit_iast: ko vaḥ praṇayati sa vaḥ praṇayatvapo devīḥ praṇayāni yajñaṃ saṃsādayantu naḥ /
meaning: को वः प्रणयति स वः प्रणयत्वपो देवीः प्रणयानि यज्ञं संसादयन्तु नः /
text_mt: 'Who brings you forward? Let him bring you forward! May I bring forward the divine waters; let them set our sacrifice in order! /'

sanskrit_iast: iraṃ madantīrghṛtapṛṣṭhā udākuḥ sahasrapoṣaṃ yajamāne nyañcatīr iti samaṃ prāṇair dhārayamāṇaḥ sphyenopasaṃgṛhyāviṣiñcanharati
meaning: इरं मदन्तीर्घृतपृष्ठा उदाकुः सहस्रपोषं यजमाने न्यञ्चतीर् इति समं प्राणैर् धारयमाणः स्फ्येनोपसंगृह्याविषिञ्चन्हरति
text_mt: 'Exhilarating with refreshing drink, having ghee on their backs, the water serpents, conferring thousandfold nourishment upon the sacrificer'—holding [the cup] level with his breath, supporting it from below with the wooden sword, he carries it without spilling.
And he meditates mentally on the earth.

sanskrit_iast: ko vo yunakti sa vo yunaktv ity uttareṇāhavanīyamasaṃspṛṣṭā darbheṣu sādayati
meaning: को वो युनक्ति स वो युनक्त्व् इत्य् उत्तरेणाहवनीयमसंस्पृष्टा दर्भेषु सादयति
text_mt: With 'Who yokes you? Let him yoke you,' he sets it down to the north of the āhavanīya on darbha blades, untouched [by anything else].
Having covered it with darbha blades, they do not shake it and do not move it until the completion [of the sacrifice].

sanskrit_iast: saṃviśantāṃ daivīrviśaḥ pātrāṇi devayajyāyā iti sapavitreṇa pāṇinā pātrāṇi saṃmṛśya
meaning: संविशन्तां दैवीर्विशः पात्राणि देवयज्याया इति सपवित्रेण पाणिना पात्राणि संमृश्य
text_mt: Touching the vessels with a hand bearing the strainers with 'Let the divine folk settle down, the vessels for the worship of the gods!'
He takes the agnihotrahavaṇī ladle with 'You are of wood, for skill [I take] you!'

sanskrit_iast: pratyuṣṭaṃ rakṣaḥ pratyuṣṭā arātaya ityāhavanīye gārhapatye vā pratitapya yajamāna havirnirvapsyāmīty āmantrayate
meaning: प्रत्युष्टं रक्षः प्रत्युष्टा अरातय इत्याहवनीये गार्हपत्ये वा प्रतितप्य यजमान हविर्निर्वप्स्यामीत्य् आमन्त्रयते
text_mt: Having heated them over the āhavanīya or the gārhapatya with 'Scorched is the demon, scorched are the enemies,' he addresses [the sacrificer]: 'O sacrificer, I will pour out the oblation!'
If [the sacrificer] is away from home, [he addresses the fire]: 'O Agni, I will pour out the oblation!'
With 'Go along the wide atmosphere,' he walks forward toward the cart.

sanskrit_iast: apareṇa gārhapatyaṃ prāgīṣamudagīṣaṃ vā naddhayugaṃ śakaṭamavasthitaṃ bhavati vrīhimad yavamad vā
meaning: अपरेण गार्हपत्यं प्रागीषमुदगीषं वा नद्धयुगं शकटमवस्थितं भवति व्रीहिमद् यवमद् वा
text_mt: To the west of the gārhapatya, a cart with its yoke tied, containing rice or barley, stands with its shaft pointing east or north.
With 'You are the yoke-pin,' he touches the southern yoke-pin or the northern one.

sanskrit_iast: tvaṃ devānāmasi sasnitamamity uttarāmīṣām ālabhya japati
meaning: त्वं देवानामसि सस्नितममित्य् उत्तरामीषाम् आलभ्य जपति
text_mt: Touching the northern shaft, he mutters: 'You are the most gainful of the gods.'

sanskrit_iast: viṣṇustvākraṃsteti savye cakre dakṣiṇaṃ pādam atyādhāyāhrutam asi havirdhānam ity ārohati
meaning: विष्णुस्त्वाक्रंस्तेति सव्ये चक्रे दक्षिणं पादम् अत्याधायाह्रुतम् असि हविर्धानम् इत्य् आरोहति
text_mt: Placing his right foot on the left wheel with 'Viṣṇu strode over you,' he climbs up with 'You are the uncrooked cart for oblation (havirdhāna).'

sanskrit_iast: uru vātāyeti parīṇāhamapacchādya mitrasya tvā cakṣuṣā prekṣā iti puroḍāśīyān prekṣate
meaning: उरु वातायेति परीणाहमपच्छाद्य मित्रस्य त्वा चक्षुषा प्रेक्षा इति पुरोडाशीयान् प्रेक्षते
text_mt: Uncovering the cover with 'Wide for the wind,' he looks at the oblation materials with 'I look at you with the eye of Mitra.'

sanskrit_iast: nirastaṃ rakṣo nirasto 'ghaśaṃsa iti yadanyatpuroḍāśīyebhyas tannirasyorjāya vaḥ payo mayi dhehīty abhimantrya daśahotāraṃ vyākhyāya śūrpe pavitre nidhāya tasminnagnihotrahavaṇyā havīṃṣi nirvapati tayā vā pavitravatyā
meaning: निरस्तं रक्षो निरस्तो ऽघशंस इति यदन्यत्पुरोडाशीयेभ्यस् तन्निरस्योर्जाय वः पयो मयि धेहीत्य् अभिमन्त्र्य दशहोतारं व्याख्याय शूर्पे पवित्रे निधाय तस्मिन्नग्निहोत्रहवण्या हवींषि निर्वपति तया वा पवित्रवत्या
text_mt: With 'Cast out is the demon, cast out is the speaker of evil,' he casts away whatever is other than the oblation materials; having consecrated [the grains] with 'For vigor; place milk in me,' recited the Daśahotṛ formula, and placed the two strainers into the winnowing basket, he measures out the oblations into it with the agnihotrahavaṇī ladle, or with that [ladle] holding the strainers:

sanskrit_iast: yacchantāṃ pañceti muṣṭiṃ gṛhītvā sruci muṣṭim opya devasya tvety anudrutyāgnaye juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmīti trir yajuṣā tūṣṇīṃ caturtham
meaning: यच्छन्तां पञ्चेति मुष्टिं गृहीत्वा स्रुचि मुष्टिम् ओप्य देवस्य त्वेत्य् अनुद्रुत्याग्नये जुष्टं निर्वपामीति त्रिर् यजुषा तूष्णीं चतुर्थम्
text_mt: Having taken a handful with 'Let the five hold,' and poured the handful into the ladle, reciting after 'At the impulse of the god...': 'I pour you out agreeable to Agni,' three times with the formula, the fourth time silently.
Likewise the subsequent [oblation] according to the deity: with 'For Agni-Soma' at full moon;
'For Indra-Agni' at new moon.

sanskrit_iast: caturo muṣṭīnnirupya nirupteṣvanvopyedaṃ devānām iti niruptānabhimṛśati /
meaning: चतुरो मुष्टीन्निरुप्य निरुप्तेष्वन्वोप्येदं देवानाम् इति निरुप्तानभिमृशति /
text_mt: Having poured out four handfuls, and poured further upon the poured portions, he touches the poured-out grains with 'This of the gods!'
[He touches] the remaining [grains] with 'This is ours together!'

sanskrit_iast: sphātyai tvā nārātyā iti niruptānevābhimantryedam ahaṃ nirvaruṇasya pāśād ity upaniṣkramya svarabhivyakhyam iti prāṅ prekṣate
meaning: स्फात्यै त्वा नारात्या इति निरुप्तानेवाभिमन्त्र्येदम् अहं निर्वरुणस्य पाशाद् इत्य् उपनिष्क्रम्य स्वरभिव्यख्यम् इति प्राङ् प्रेक्षते
text_mt: Having consecrated the poured-out grains with 'For prosperity [I take] you, not for misfortune,' and stepped out with 'Here have I been freed from Varuṇa’s noose,' he looks toward the east with 'I have perceived the heavenly light!'
With 'May I behold the heavenly light,' he looks around at the entire sacrificial ground.

sanskrit_iast: vaiśvānaraṃ jyotirity āhavanīyaṃ svāhā dyāvāpṛthivībhyām iti skannānabhimantrya dṛṃhantāṃ duryā dyāvāpṛthivyor iti pratyavarohyorvantarikṣamanvihīti harati
meaning: वैश्वानरं ज्योतिरित्य् आहवनीयं स्वाहा द्यावापृथिवीभ्याम् इति स्कन्नानभिमन्त्र्य दृंहन्तां दुर्या द्यावापृथिव्योर् इति प्रत्यवरोह्योर्वन्तरिक्षमन्विहीति हरति
text_mt: Touching the āhavanīya with 'The light belonging to all men,' and the spilled grains with 'Svāhā to Heaven and Earth!', he climbs down with 'May the doors of Heaven and Earth be firm,' and carries [the grains] with 'Go along the wide atmosphere!'
With 'We set you in the lap of Aditi,' he sets them down behind the gārhapatya, according to their deities;
or behind the āhavanīya, if he cooks on the āhavanīya.

sanskrit_iast: yadi pātryā nirvaped dakṣiṇataḥ sphyamupadhāya tasyāṃ sarvāñchakaṭamantrāñjapet
meaning: यदि पात्र्या निर्वपेद् दक्षिणतः स्फ्यमुपधाय तस्यां सर्वाञ्छकटमन्त्राञ्जपेत्
text_mt: If he should pour out [the oblation] from a trough, having placed the wooden sword to the south, he should mutter all the cart formulas over that [trough].

sanskrit_iast: saśūkāyāmagnihotrahavaṇyām apa ānīya pūrvavadutpūyābhimantrya brahmanprokṣiṣyāmīti brahmāṇamāmantrya devasya tvety anudrutyāgnaye vo juṣṭaṃ prokṣāmīti yathādevataṃ havistriḥ prokṣannāgnimabhiprokṣet
meaning: सशूकायामग्निहोत्रहवण्याम् अप आनीय पूर्ववदुत्पूयाभिमन्त्र्य ब्रह्मन्प्रोक्षिष्यामीति ब्रह्माणमामन्त्र्य देवस्य त्वेत्य् अनुद्रुत्याग्नये वो जुष्टं प्रोक्षामीति यथादेवतं हविस्त्रिः प्रोक्षन्नाग्निमभिप्रोक्षेत्
text_mt: Having drawn water into the agnihotrahavaṇī ladle together with the awns, purified it as before, consecrated it, addressed the Brahman with 'Brahman, I will sprinkle,' and recited after 'At the impulse of the god...': 'I sprinkle you agreeable to Agni,' sprinkling the oblation three times according to the deity, he should not sprinkle toward the fire.
He should sprinkle toward the fire in the case of one whom he hates.

sanskrit_iast: uttānāni pātrāṇi paryāvartya śundhadhvaṃ daivyāya karmaṇa iti triḥ prokṣya prokṣaṇīśeṣamagreṇa gārhapatyaṃ nidhāya devasya tvā savituḥ prasava iti kṛṣṇājinam ādāyāvadhūtaṃ rakṣo 'vadhūtā arātaya ity utkare trir avadhūnotyūrdhvagrīvaṃ bahiṣṭādviśasanam
meaning: उत्तानानि पात्राणि पर्यावर्त्य शुन्धध्वं दैव्याय कर्मण इति त्रिः प्रोक्ष्य प्रोक्षणीशेषमग्रेण गार्हपत्यं निधाय देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसव इति कृष्णाजिनम् आदायावधूतं रक्षो ऽवधूता अरातय इत्य् उत्करे त्रिर् अवधूनोत्यूर्ध्वग्रीवं बहिष्टाद्विशसनम्
text_mt: Having turned the vessels face up, sprinkled them three times with 'Be clean for the divine rite,' placed the remnant of the sprinkling water in front of the gārhapatya, and taken the black antelope skin with 'At the impulse of the god Savitṛ...', he shakes it three times over the rubbish heap with 'Shaken off is the demon, shaken off are the enemies,' with its neck pointing upward and the slit outside.

sanskrit_iast: adityāstvagasīty uttareṇa gārhapatyamutkaradeśe vā pratīcīnagrīvam uttaralomopastṛṇāti
meaning: अदित्यास्त्वगसीत्य् उत्तरेण गार्हपत्यमुत्करदेशे वा प्रतीचीनग्रीवम् उत्तरलोमोपस्तृणाति
text_mt: With 'You are the skin of Aditi,' he spreads it out to the north of the gārhapatya, or in the place of the rubbish heap, with its neck pointing to the west and the hairy side turned up.
He turns the rear part from the east toward the west.

sanskrit_iast: anutsṛjan kṛṣṇājinam adhiṣavaṇam asīti tasminn ulūkhalam adhivartayati
meaning: अनुत्सृजन् कृष्णाजिनम् अधिषवणम् असीति तस्मिन्न् उलूखलम् अधिवर्तयति
text_mt: Without letting go of the black antelope skin, he rolls the mortar onto it with 'You are the pressing board.'

sanskrit_iast: anutsṛjann ulūkhalam agnes tanūrasīti tasmin havirāvapati trir yajuṣā tūṣṇīm caturtham
meaning: अनुत्सृजन्न् उलूखलम् अग्नेस् तनूरसीति तस्मिन् हविरावपति त्रिर् यजुषा तूष्णीम् चतुर्थम्
text_mt: Without letting go of the mortar, he throws the oblation material into it with 'You are the body of Agni,' three times with the formula, the fourth time silently.

sanskrit_iast: adrir asi vānaspatya iti musalam ādāya haviṣkṛdehīti triravahanti /
meaning: अद्रिर् असि वानस्पत्य इति मुसलम् आदाय हविष्कृदेहीति त्रिरवहन्ति /
text_mt: Taking the pestle with 'You are a stone, made of wood,' he pounds three times with 'Preparer of the oblation, come!'
Or without striking, he calls the preparer of the oblation.

sanskrit_iast: haviṣkṛdehīti brāhmaṇasya haviṣkṛdāgahīti rājanyasya haviṣkṛdādraveti vaiśyasya haviṣkṛdādhāveti śūdrasya
meaning: हविष्कृदेहीति ब्राह्मणस्य हविष्कृदागहीति राजन्यस्य हविष्कृदाद्रवेति वैश्यस्य हविष्कृदाधावेति शूद्रस्य
text_mt: 'Preparer of the oblation, come (ehi)!' for a Brāhmaṇa; 'Preparer of the oblation, come hither (āgahi)!' for a Rājanya; 'Preparer of the oblation, run hither (ādrava)!' for a Vaiśya; 'Preparer of the oblation, hurry hither (ādhāva)!' for a Śūdra.
He pounds with 'May I strike down the demon, the rival, from heaven.'
He gives the ritual call: 'To be struck together loudly!'

sanskrit_iast: kuṭarur asi madhujihva ity āgnīdhro 'śmānamādāyeṣamāvadorjamāvadeti dṛṣadupale samāhanti
meaning: कुटरुर् असि मधुजिह्व इत्य् आग्नीध्रो ऽश्मानमादायेषमावदोर्जमावदेति दृषदुपले समाहन्ति
text_mt: Taking a stone with 'You are a cock with a sweet tongue,' the āgnīdhra strikes the lower and upper millstones together with 'Proclaim food, proclaim vigor!'
Striking twice on the lower millstone and once on the upper millstone, repeating this three times, he completes nine times.
Or taking the yoke-pin with the Sāvitra formula, he strikes with it.
With 'You are rain-grown,' he pushes the winnowing basket beneath from the east or from the north.

sanskrit_iast: varṣavṛddhā sthetyabhimantrya prati tvā varṣavṛddhaṃ vettv ity udvapati
meaning: वर्षवृद्धा स्थेत्यभिमन्त्र्य प्रति त्वा वर्षवृद्धं वेत्त्व् इत्य् उद्वपति
text_mt: Having consecrated [the grains] with 'You are rain-grown,' he pours them out into it with 'May the rain-grown recognize you!'

sanskrit_iast: parāpūtaṃ rakṣaḥ parāpūtā arātaya ity utkare parāpunāti
meaning: परापूतं रक्षः परापूता अरातय इत्य् उत्करे परापुनाति
text_mt: With 'Winnowed away is the demon, winnowed away are the enemies,' he winnows them over the rubbish heap.

sanskrit_iast: praviddhaṃ rakṣaḥ parādhmātā amitrā iti tuṣān praskandato 'numantrayate
meaning: प्रविद्धं रक्षः पराध्माता अमित्रा इति तुषान् प्रस्कन्दतो ऽनुमन्त्रयते
text_mt: Over the fallen husks he mutters: 'Cast away is the demon, blown away are the enemies.'

sanskrit_iast: madhyame puroḍāśakapāle tuṣānopya rakṣasāṃ bhāgo 'sīty adhastāt kṛṣṇājinasyopavapaty uttaramaparamavāntaradeśam
meaning: मध्यमे पुरोडाशकपाले तुषानोप्य रक्षसां भागो ऽसीत्य् अधस्तात् कृष्णाजिनस्योपवपत्य् उत्तरमपरमवान्तरदेशम्
text_mt: Having poured the husks into the central potsherd for the cake, he pours them beneath the black antelope skin with 'You are the share of the demons,' into the north-western intermediate direction.
'He pours them in with the hand,' says the Brāhmaṇa of the Rigvedins.

sanskrit_iast: adbhiḥ kapālaṃ saṃsparśya prajñātaṃ nidhāyāpa upaspṛśya vāyur vo vi vinaktv iti vivicya devo vaḥ savitā hiraṇyapānīḥ pratigṛhṇātv iti pātryāṃ taṇḍulān praskandayitvādabdhena vaścakṣuṣāvapaśyāmi rāyaspodṣāya varcase suprajāstvāya cakṣuṣo gopīthāyāśiṣamāśāsa ity avekṣya triṣphalīkartavā iti saṃpreṣyat
meaning: अद्भिः कपालं संस्पर्श्य प्रज्ञातं निधायाप उपस्पृश्य वायुर् वो वि विनक्त्व् इति विविच्य देवो वः सविता हिरण्यपानीः प्रतिगृह्णात्व् इति पात्र्यां तण्डुलान् प्रस्कन्दयित्वादब्धेन वश्चक्षुषावपश्यामि रायस्पोद्षाय वर्चसे सुप्रजास्त्वाय चक्षुषो गोपीथायाशिषमाशास इत्य् अवेक्ष्य त्रिष्फलीकर्तवा इति संप्रेष्यत्
text_mt: Having touched the potsherd with water, having placed it in a known place, and having touched water, he separates [the grains] with: 'May Vāyu winnow you apart!' Having caused the rice grains to fall into the vessel with: 'May the divine Savitṛ of golden hands receive you!', and having looked [at them] with: 'With an unblinking eye I look down upon you for the increase of wealth, for brilliance, for good offspring; I pray for the blessing of protection for the eye,' he gives the ritual call: 'Pound [the grains] so as to dehusk them thrice!'
She who is the sacrificer's wife runs up and pounds.
Or anyone, if she is absent.

sanskrit_iast: devebhyaḥ śundhadhvaṃ devebhyaḥ śundhyadhvaṃ devebhyaḥ śumbhadhvam iti suphalīkṛtān karoti /
meaning: देवेभ्यः शुन्धध्वं देवेभ्यः शुन्ध्यध्वं देवेभ्यः शुम्भध्वम् इति सुफलीकृतान् करोति /
text_mt: With: 'Purify yourselves for the gods! Purify yourselves for the gods! Adorn yourselves for the gods!', he makes them well-dehusked.

sanskrit_iast: prakṣālya tuṇḍulāṃs triṣphalīkriyamāṇānāṃ yo nyaṅgo avaśiṣyate /
meaning: प्रक्षाल्य तुण्डुलांस् त्रिष्फलीक्रियमाणानां यो न्यङ्गो अवशिष्यते /
text_mt: Having washed the rice grains, whatever residue remains of those being dehusked thrice—
with: 'The portion of the Rakṣases; O waters, carry it away from here!'—he pours out thrice on the rubbish heap.

sanskrit_iast: atra kṛṣṇājinasyādānādi prāgadhivartanātkṛtvā diva skambhanirasīti kṛṣṇājina udīcīnakumbāṃ śmyāṃ nidhāya dhiṣaṇāsi parvatyeti śamyāyāṃ dṛṣadamatyādhāya dhiṣaṇāsi pārvateyīti dṛṣadyupalāmatyādadhāti
