he adapts the formula: "I hope..."

sanskrit_iast: paridhīnprahṛtya saṃsrāvāntaṃ kṛtvā vājinapātra upastīryāntarvedi barhiranuviṣiñcanvājinaṃ gṛhṇāti
meaning: परिधीन्प्रहृत्य संस्रावान्तं कृत्वा वाजिनपात्र उपस्तीर्यान्तर्वेदि बर्हिरनुविषिञ्चन्वाजिनं गृह्णाति
text_mt: Having cast the enclosing sticks [into the fire] and concluded with the scrapings, having spread an under-layer [of butter] in the whey-vessel, he takes the whey, continuously sprinkling the sacrificial grass inside the altar ground.
"Recite for the Vājins," "Offer to the Vājins," are the two ritual calls;
at the vaṣaṭ-call he offers with the goblet,
or with the ladling spoon that is being continuously sprinkled, and also at the secondary vaṣaṭ-call.
Kneeling with knees raised, the hotṛ offers without drawing breath.
He offers the after-oblation with: "O Agni, enjoy the whey."

sanskrit_iast: trayāṇāṃ ha vai haviṣāṃ sviṣṭakṛtena samavadyati somasya vājinasya gharmasyeti
meaning: त्रयाणां ह वै हविषां स्विष्टकृतेन समवद्यति सोमस्य वाजिनस्य घर्मस्येति
text_mt: Indeed, of three oblations he cuts portions together for the Sviṣṭakṛt: of soma, of whey, and of the gharma.

sanskrit_iast: udrekeṇa paśubandhavaddiśaḥ pratījyāntarvedi śeṣaṃ sarve samupahūya bhakṣayanti
meaning: उद्रेकेण पशुबन्धवद्दिशः प्रतीज्यान्तर्वेदि शेषं सर्वे समुपहूय भक्षयन्ति
text_mt: Having offered to the quarters with the residue as in the animal sacrifice, all, having invited one another inside the altar ground, partake of the remainder.
He addresses him by his ritual title: 'So-and-so, do invite [me]!'
The reply is: "Invited!"
The hotṛ partakes first, the sacrificer last.
The sacrificer is both first and last, say some.

sanskrit_iast: vājināṃ bhakṣo avatu vājo asmām̐ retaḥ siktamamṛtaṃ balāya /
meaning: वाजिनां भक्षो अवतु वाजो अस्माम्̐ रेतः सिक्तममृतं बलाय /
text_mt: "May the partaking of the whey protect [us], may vigor [protect] us, the seed that is poured out, immortal, for strength.

sanskrit_iast: sa na indriyaṃ draviṇaṃ dadhātu mā riṣāma vājinaṃ bhakṣayantaḥ /
meaning: स न इन्द्रियं द्रविणं दधातु मा रिषाम वाजिनं भक्षयन्तः /
text_mt: May it bestow on us power and wealth; may we not come to harm while partaking of the whey.

sanskrit_iast: tasya te vājibhirbhakṣaṃkṛtasya vājibhiḥ sutasya vājipītasya vājinasyopahūtasyopahūto bhakṣayāmīti bhakṣayati
meaning: तस्य ते वाजिभिर्भक्षंकृतस्य वाजिभिः सुतस्य वाजिपीतस्य वाजिनस्योपहूतस्योपहूतो भक्षयामीति भक्षयति
text_mt: From that [portion] of yours, prepared as food by the spirited, pressed by the spirited, drunk by the spirited, invited from the invited whey, I partake"—with this he partakes.
The samiṣṭayajus formulas are as in the animal sacrifice.
The offering is concluded in the established manner.

sanskrit_iast: śvobhūte paurṇamāsyeṣṭvā prasūtā devena savitrā daivyā āpa undantu te tanuṃ dīrghāyutvāya varcasa ityupodya tryeṇyā śalalyekṣukāṇḍenekṣuśalākayā vā lauhena ca kṣureṇaudumbareṇa ni keśānvartayate vāpayate śmaśrūṇi
meaning: श्वोभूते पौर्णमास्येष्ट्वा प्रसूता देवेन सवित्रा दैव्या आप उन्दन्तु ते तनुं दीर्घायुत्वाय वर्चस इत्युपोद्य त्र्येण्या शलल्येक्षुकाण्डेनेक्षुशलाकया वा लौहेन च क्षुरेणौदुम्बरेण नि केशान्वर्तयते वापयते श्मश्रूणि
text_mt: On the following day, having performed the Full Moon sacrifice, with the words: "Impelled by the god Savitṛ, may the divine waters moisten your body for long life and splendor," having moistened [his hair], he trims his hair and has his beard shaved with a porcupine quill having three white rings, a piece of reed or a reed splint, an iron razor, and [an implement] made of udumbara wood.
"Truth alone is the Highest, nothing goes beyond truth.

sanskrit_iast: ṛte samudra āhita ṛte bhumiriyaṃ śritā //
meaning: ऋते समुद्र आहित ऋते भुमिरियं श्रिता //
text_mt: In truth the ocean is placed; on truth this earth rests.
Agni, with his sharp flame, has overcome the heat [with his] neck;
the head is placed in heat by the splendor of Vaiśvānara.
With truth I turn it around; with reality I turn it around;
with austerity I turn it along; with what is auspicious I turn it toward; with what is pleasant I turn it toward"—with this formula he turns it around.

sanskrit_iast: tadṛtaṃ tatsatyaṃ tadvrataṃ tacchakeyaṃ tena śakeyaṃ tena rādhyāsamiti yajamāno japati /
meaning: तदृतं तत्सत्यं तद्व्रतं तच्छकेयं तेन शकेयं तेन राध्यासमिति यजमानो जपति /
text_mt: "That is truth, that is reality, that is the vow; may I be capable of it, may I be capable through it, may I succeed through it"—thus the sacrificer mutters.
And he mutters the anuvāka [beginning with]: "The brāhmaṇa is the single hotṛ..."
His intermediate vows [continue] during the seasonal junctures.
He does not eat meat; he does not approach a woman;
Eating honey should be [his food], is one view.
It is for flavoring, is another view.
One who sacrifices at the seasons is indeed one [kind of sacrificer], and one who sacrifices with the Cāturmāsya sacrifices is another.

meaning: यो वसन्तो ऽभूत्प्रावृडभूच्छरदभूदिति यजते स ऋतुयाजी /
text_mt: He who sacrifices thinking, "Spring has come," "The rainy season has come," "Autumn has come," is one who sacrifices at the seasons.
Now he who [sacrifices] every four [months] is one who sacrifices with the Cāturmāsya sacrifices.
In spring he sacrifices with the Vaiśvadeva; in the rainy season with the Varuṇapraghāsa sacrifices;
in autumn with the Sākamedha sacrifices—thus it is known [from the scriptures].
Then, after four months, on the full moon day of Āṣāḍha or of Śravaṇā, having set out, he sacrifices with the Varuṇapraghāsa sacrifices.
"One should sacrifice when the brush has grown up"—so states a Brāhmaṇa of the Rigvedins.
Its procedure is like that of the Vaiśvadeva.

sanskrit_iast: vedau kṛtvāgreṇa gārhapatyaṃ same prācī vedī bhavataḥ
meaning: वेदौ कृत्वाग्रेण गार्हपत्यं समे प्राची वेदी भवतः
text_mt: Having made two altar grounds in front of the gārhapatya, they are equal and facing east.
The adhvaryu makes the northern one; the pratiprasthātṛ makes the southern one.
The adhvaryu operates in the northern sacrificial enclosure; the pratiprasthātṛ in the southern.
In both places the entire procedure is performed.
The brahman gives assent in the dual.

sanskrit_iast: dvyaṅgulaṃ tryaṅgulaṃ caturaṅgulaṃ pṛthamātraṃ rathavartmamātraṃ sītāmātraṃ prādeśamātreṇa vā tiryagasaṃbhinne vedī bhavataḥ
meaning: द्व्यङ्गुलं त्र्यङ्गुलं चतुरङ्गुलं पृथमात्रं रथवर्त्ममात्रं सीतामात्रं प्रादेशमात्रेण वा तिर्यगसंभिन्ने वेदी भवतः
text_mt: The two altar grounds are separated crosswise by two finger-breadths, three finger-breadths, four finger-breadths, the width of a palm, the width of a chariot rut, the width of a furrow, or by the measure of a span.
Between the two altar grounds is the movement path for the pratiprasthātṛ.
Carrying the stambayajus to the west of the northern altar ground, he does not pass around the adhvaryu.
Whatever the adhvaryu does, that the pratiprasthātṛ also does.
Whatever is to be done by speech, only the adhvaryu should do that,
or the recitations whose timing is simultaneous,
and the consecrations of common substances.
Having made [the trenches] before the northern enclosing line, he connects the two altar grounds by the single stroke of the wooden sword:
stepping forward from the northern hip of the southern [altar ground] to the southern shoulder of the northern [altar ground].
On the northern altar ground he strews the high altar as in the animal sacrifice.
At the proper time, they both carry forward the two fires from the gārhapatya, as in the animal sacrifice.
Between the two altar grounds the pratiprasthātṛ steps forward;
to the north of the northern altar ground, the adhvaryu.
First the adhvaryu establishes the fire on the high altar;
last, the pratiprasthātṛ on the southern [altar ground].
Having added fuel to the fires, the two [adhvaryu and pratiprasthātṛ] bring two separate branches.
The pratiprasthātṛ drives away the calves of the herd for the Maruts;
The dipping spoons are made of śamī wood or of gold.
According to their deities, the two [adhvaryu and pratiprasthātṛ] milk the evening milkings.
Or the Varuṇapraghāsa rites may take place on a single day.
If so, the curd preparation would be made with ordinary curd.
Some state that the curd and milk offering is a modification of the morning milking.
At the time of apportioning, he measures out the nine subsequent oblations, beginning with 'To Agni on eight potsherds'.

sanskrit_iast: api vā pauṣṇaḥ karambhapātrāṇi meṣāviti yavānāṃ vrīhīṇāmitarāṇi
meaning: अपि वा पौष्णः करम्भपात्राणि मेषाविति यवानां व्रीहीणामितराणि
text_mt: Alternatively, the oblation to Pūṣan, the karambha pots, and the two rams are of barley, while the others are of rice.
At this time, the pratiprasthātṛ silently measures out the barley meant for the karambha pots.
The adhvaryu measures out with a yajus formula [the barley] meant for the ram;
the pratiprasthātṛ [measures out that] meant for the ewe.
The deity of these two corresponds to that of the curds.
The wife makes the karambha pots out of unbaked dough.
There are as many as there are members of the sacrificer's household, including the women, with one extra.
The two effigies of the rams are made of unbaked dough.
The adhvaryu makes the ram; the pratiprasthātṛ the ewe.
To the female he gives female characteristics;

sanskrit_iast: api vā purvedyuranvāhāryapacane vituṣāniva yavānkṛtvā teṣāmīṣadupataptānāṃ patnī karambhapātrāṇi karoti
meaning: अपि वा पुर्वेद्युरन्वाहार्यपचने वितुषानिव यवान्कृत्वा तेषामीषदुपतप्तानां पत्नी करम्भपात्राणि करोति
text_mt: Or, on the previous day, having made the barley as if dehusked on the anvāhāryapacana, the wife makes the karambha pots out of them after they are slightly roasted.

sanskrit_iast: atrāpi meṣaṃ meṣīṃ ca karotīti vājasaneyakam
meaning: अत्रापि मेषं मेषीं च करोतीति वाजसनेयकम्
text_mt: Here too, she makes the ram and the ewe; thus the Vājasaneyaka says.
Having placed [the oblations] up to that for Indra-Agni on the fire, he places the ewe on eleven potsherds;
Or the two are cooked in an earthen pot.
Having placed the oblation for Ka on one potsherd on the fire and poured out [water] for the Āpyas, they carry forward the fires; thus the Vājasaneyaka says.

meaning: महीनां पयो ऽसीति पृषदाज्यधान्यां सकृदाज्यं गृह्णाति /
text_mt: with the verse 'You are the milk of the great ones,' he takes butter once into the vessel for speckled butter;
Or indeed, he may take it after mixing it in a shallow cup.
At the time of taking down, the two make the two effigies of the rams hairy with non-sheep wool.
In the absence of that, having affixed kuśa fibres, he places the ram in the [curd portion] for the Maruts;
Then upon the two he scatters śamī leaves and karīra fruits, more than a hundred or more than a thousand.
And having scattered them also into the karambha pots, he sets down the eight oblations on the northern altar ground.

sanskrit_iast: ekāṃ mārutīṃ pratiprasthātā dakṣiṇasyāṃ karambhapātrāṇi ca
meaning: एकां मारुतीं प्रतिप्रस्थाता दक्षिणस्यां करम्भपात्राणि च
text_mt: The pratiprasthātṛ sets down the single [oblation] for the Maruts and the karambha pots on the southern [altar ground].
Here the two exchange the effigies of the two rams:
he places the ewe in that for the Maruts;
As in the animal sacrifice, there are the two churning-sticks, the firewood-kindling verses, and nine fore-offerings and after-offerings.
With the verse 'We summon the gluttonous ones,' the pratiprasthātṛ leads forward the wife and makes her recite this [mantra].

sanskrit_iast: tāṃ pṛcchati patni kati te jārā iti
meaning: तां पृच्छति पत्नि कति ते जारा इति
text_mt: He asks her: 'Wife, how many paramours do you have?'
Whomever she declares, he designates [saying]: 'May Varuṇa seize them!'

sanskrit_iast: yajjāraṃ santaṃ na prabrūyātpriyaṃ jñātiṃ rundhyāt /
meaning: यज्जारं सन्तं न प्रब्रूयात्प्रियं ज्ञातिं रुन्ध्यात् /
text_mt: If she does not declare one who is a paramour, she would harm a dear kinsman.
She should declare: 'So-and-so is my paramour.'
'Having designated him alone, she causes Varuṇa's noose to seize him,' so it is known.
The northern fire is swept clean, the southern is unswept.

sanskrit_iast: athāntarā vedī gatvā yajamānaḥ patnī cottareṇa vottarāṃ vedimaiṣīke śūrpe karambhapātrāṇyopya śīrṣannadhinidhāya purastātpratyañcau tiṣṭhantau dakṣiṇe 'gnau śūrpeṇa juhutaḥ
meaning: अथान्तरा वेदी गत्वा यजमानः पत्नी चोत्तरेण वोत्तरां वेदिमैषीके शूर्पे करम्भपात्राण्योप्य शीर्षन्नधिनिधाय पुरस्तात्प्रत्यञ्चौ तिष्ठन्तौ दक्षिणे ऽग्नौ शूर्पेण जुहुतः
text_mt: Then, having gone between the two altar grounds or along the north of the northern altar ground, having poured the karambha pots into a winnowing basket made of reed and placed it upon their heads, standing in front facing west, the sacrificer and his wife offer with the winnowing basket into the southern fire.

sanskrit_iast: mo ṣū ṇa indreti yajamānaḥ puro 'nuvākyāmanvāha /
meaning: मो षू ण इन्द्रेति यजमानः पुरो ऽनुवाक्यामन्वाह /
text_mt: With 'Do not, O Indra,' the sacrificer recites the invitatory verse;
with 'What in the village,' both recite the consecratory verse.
Turning away, they whisper: 'The work-doers have done the work.'
Alternatively, the adhvaryu or the pratiprasthātṛ may make the offering;
the other two should touch along.
At this point, he sweeps the southern fire clean.
Having proceeded with [the offerings] ending with the one to Indra-Agni, the adhvaryu pauses.

sanskrit_iast: atha pratiprasthātā pūrveṇa sahāvadānena mārutyāḥ sarvāṃ meṣīm avadyati /
meaning: अथ प्रतिप्रस्थाता पूर्वेण सहावदानेन मारुत्याः सर्वां मेषीम् अवद्यति /
text_mt: Then the pratiprasthātṛ cuts off the whole ewe from the [curds] for the Maruts along with the first portion;
with the subsequent portion, the śamī leaves and karīra fruits.

sanskrit_iast: athādhvaryuḥ pūrveṇa sahāvadānena vāruṇyāḥ sarvaṃ meṣamavadyati /
meaning: अथाध्वर्युः पूर्वेण सहावदानेन वारुण्याः सर्वं मेषमवद्यति /
text_mt: Then the adhvaryu cuts off the whole ram from the [curds] for Varuṇa along with the first portion;
with the subsequent portion, the śamī leaves and karīra fruits.
"Recite for Ka," [and] "Sacrifice to Ka," are the two ritual calls for the [cake] on one potsherd.
He offers over the [cake] on one potsherd with the names of the four months: "Nabhas and Nabhasya..."
Now some cut off separate iḍās.
Cutting off together from the seven oblations, the adhvaryu hands [it] to the pratiprasthātṛ.
Upon it, the pratiprasthātṛ places along [the portion] of the Mārutyā oblation.
A bull that is past its prime, as it were, is the sacrificial gift.
He may, however, give more than that if he wishes.
"He hopes for the wellbeing of the full year."
"He hopes for the divine abode": the hotṛ adds [this] in the blessings of the Sūktavāka.
He adapts the formula: "I hope..."
Both proceed with the two portions of vājina.

sanskrit_iast: śesau samavanīyottare vihāre pūrvavadbhaksayantyā mā viśantvindava ā galgā dhavanīnāṃ rasena me rasaṃ pṛṇa /
meaning: शेसौ समवनीयोत्तरे विहारे पूर्ववद्भक्सयन्त्या मा विशन्त्विन्दव आ गल्गा धवनीनां रसेन मे रसं पृण /
text_mt: Pouring together the two remainders in the northern vedi, they consume it as before, [with]: "May the drops enter me; rushing forth from the shaking vessels, fill my essence with essence."
[The rest,] "Of you who have been made a drink by the swift ones...", is the same.
Excluding the full-vessel gift, he concludes the sacrifice as before.
In place of the full-vessel gift, there is the purificatory bath of the Soma sacrifice.
With the scrapings of the oblation to Varuṇa and with the husks, they perform the purificatory bath.
The husks acquire the ritual status of the soma dregs.
Some teach [a cake] on one potsherd for Varuṇa.
He does not [recite] the "life-giving" verse, nor the formula for stepping forth, nor does he sing a sāman.
Going to any direction for the purificatory bath is handed down in the texts.
They should not go down towards the north, say some.
In whichever direction they go, facing that way they should perform the ritual, say some.
They should go down into standing [pools] of flowing [waters].

sanskrit_iast: udakānte staraṇāntāṃ vediṃ kṛtvā tasyāṃ havīṃṣi sādayati
meaning: उदकान्ते स्तरणान्तां वेदिं कृत्वा तस्यां हवींषि सादयति
text_mt: At the water's edge, having made an altar ground extending up to the strewing, he places the oblations upon it.

sanskrit_iast: śataṃ te rājanbhiṣajaḥ sahasramityapo dṛṣṭvā japati
meaning: शतं ते राजन्भिषजः सहस्रमित्यपो दृष्ट्वा जपति
text_mt: Having looked at the water, he mutters: "A hundred are your medicines, O King, a thousand..."
They step upon the edge of the water with: "Trodden down is the fetter of Varuṇa."
Having plunged into the water, standing, they perform the purificatory bath.
Having thrown in a blade of grass, he makes the continuous libation with the dipping-spoon.
Or, if there should be grass there beforehand, he should offer on it.
He summons: "Agnīdh, wipe the waters three times."

sanskrit_iast: āpo vājajito vājaṃ vaḥ sariṣyantīrvājaṃ jeṣyantīrvājinīrvājajito vājajityāyai saṃmārjmyapo annādā annādyāyeti mantraṃ saṃnamati
meaning: आपो वाजजितो वाजं वः सरिष्यन्तीर्वाजं जेष्यन्तीर्वाजिनीर्वाजजितो वाजजित्यायै संमार्ज्म्यपो अन्नादा अन्नाद्यायेति मन्त्रं संनमति
text_mt: He adapts the formula: "O waters, winning the prize, about to run for your prize, about to win the prize, rich in prizes, winning the prize, I wipe you for winning the prize, eating food, for the eating of food."
He makes the continuous libation with the offering ladle with: "The face of Agni has entered into the waters."
The sacrificer recites over it: "You are speech belonging to Agni."
Having offered the fore-offerings without the barhis, he offers the two butter portions containing [verses on] water.
"Soma told me that within the waters are all medicines, / and Agni who brings good fortune to all, and the waters containing all medicines"—these are the two containing [verses on] water.
[The two verses are] the ones containing [words for] water.

sanskrit_iast: niṣkāsasyāvadāya varuṇamiṣṭvā kṛtsnaṃ niṣkāsamavadāyāgnīvaruṇau sviṣṭakṛdarthe yajati
meaning: निष्कासस्यावदाय वरुणमिष्ट्वा कृत्स्नं निष्कासमवदायाग्नीवरुणौ स्विष्टकृदर्थे यजति
text_mt: Cutting off from the scraping, having sacrificed to Varuṇa, cutting off the entire scraping, he sacrifices to Agni and Varuṇa in place of the Sviṣṭakṛt.
Or, bringing the butter from the upabhṛt into the juhū, he offers the two after-offerings without the barhis.
"Sacrifice to the two gods," he summons for the first.

sanskrit_iast: tuṣāṇāṃ sthālīṃ pūrayitvāpsūpamārayati samudre te hṛdayamapsvantariti
meaning: तुषाणां स्थालीं पूरयित्वाप्सूपमारयति समुद्रे ते हृदयमप्स्वन्तरिति
text_mt: Having filled a pot with the husks, he lets it sink in the water with: "Your heart is in the ocean, inside the waters."
Or rather, there is no purificatory bath belonging to a Soma sacrifice.
Silently, he should scatter the husks and scrapings into the water.
The wife unfastens the loop of the yoke-halter with: "Here I unloosen..."

sanskrit_iast: devīrāpa ityavabhṛthaṃ yajamāno 'bhimantrya sumitrā na āpa oṣadhaya ityapaḥ pragāhya saśiraskāvanupamakṣantau snātaḥ patnī yajamānaśca
meaning: देवीराप इत्यवभृथं यजमानो ऽभिमन्त्र्य सुमित्रा न आप ओषधय इत्यपः प्रगाह्य सशिरस्कावनुपमक्षन्तौ स्नातः पत्नी यजमानश्च
text_mt: The sacrificer addresses the purificatory bath with: "O divine waters..."; having plunged into the water with: "Friendly to us be the waters and the herbs...", the wife and the sacrificer bathe, including their heads, without dipping themselves under.
They rub each other's back.

sanskrit_iast: kāmamete vāsasī yasmai kāmayeyātaṃ tasmai dadyātām /
meaning: काममेते वाससी यस्मै कामयेयातं तस्मै दद्याताम् /
text_mt: They may give these two garments to whomsoever they wish.
"For they are not the garments of the consecrated," says the Vājasaneyaka.

sanskrit_iast: udvayaṃ tamasasparītyādityamupasthāya pratiyuto varuṇasya paśa ityudakāntaṃ pratyasitvā samidhaḥ kṛtvāpratīkṣāstūṣṇīmetyaidho 'syedhiṣīmahītyāhavanīye samidha ādhāyāpo anvacāriṣamityupatiṣṭhante
meaning: उद्वयं तमसस्परीत्यादित्यमुपस्थाय प्रतियुतो वरुणस्य पश इत्युदकान्तं प्रत्यसित्वा समिधः कृत्वाप्रतीक्षास्तूष्णीमेत्यैधो ऽस्येधिषीमहीत्याहवनीये समिध आधायापो अन्वचारिषमित्युपतिष्ठन्ते
text_mt: Having paid reverence to the sun with: "Rising out of the darkness...", having thrown [a grass-blade] back into the water's edge with: "Averted is the fetter of Varuṇa", having made fuel-sticks, having returned silently without looking back, having placed the fuel-sticks on the āhavanīya with: "You are kindling; may we be kindled", they revere [the fire] with: "I have followed the waters..."
Here, having sacrificed with the Full Moon sacrifice, the moistening and other acts [of tonsure] are repeated as before.
“Since the caldron revolved around the ends of the earth and the sky,
Agni, ruling with might, Varuṇa with thoughts,
Indra with the Maruts as comrades.”
The part starting with “Agni with the sharp...” is identical.

sanskrit_iast: api vā snātvoptvā keśaśmaśrūṇyaraṇyoragnīnsamāropyodavasāya nirmathya paurṇamāsena yajate
meaning: अपि वा स्नात्वोप्त्वा केशश्मश्रूण्यरण्योरग्नीन्समारोप्योदवसाय निर्मथ्य पौर्णमासेन यजते
text_mt: Or, having bathed, shaved hair and beard, mounted the fires upon the two kindling sticks, moved away [from the place of sacrifice], and churned out [fire], he sacrifices with the Full Moon sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast: yajño ha vā eṣa yadvaruṇaparaghāsā nahyavakalpate yaduttaravedyāmagnihotraṃ juhuyāditi vājasaneyakam
meaning: यज्ञो ह वा एष यद्वरुणपरघासा नह्यवकल्पते यदुत्तरवेद्यामग्निहोत्रं जुहुयादिति वाजसनेयकम्
text_mt: “This is indeed a [soma] sacrifice, namely the Varuṇapraghāsa rites; for it is not fitting that one should offer the agnihotra on the high altar ground,” says a Vājasaneyaka passage.
Then, after four months, having begun on the first junction day, he sacrifices for two days with the Sākamedha rites.

meaning: अग्नये ऽनीकवते पुरोडाशमष्टाकपालं निर्वपति साकं सूर्येणोद्यता
text_mt: He pours out [grains for] a sacrificial cake on eight potsherds for Agni Anīkavat, together with the rising sun.
Or they proceed along with the rays.
The sacrifice concludes in the established manner.
At midday, [he offers] a pap to the Maruts Sāṃtapanas.
He does not throw the barhis after [into the fire].
The sacrifice concludes in the established manner.

sanskrit_iast: marudbhyo gṛhamedhibhyaḥ sarvāsāṃ dugdhe sāyaṃ carum
meaning: मरुद्भ्यो गृहमेधिभ्यः सर्वासां दुग्धे सायं चरुम्
text_mt: In the evening, [he offers] a pap in the milk of all [the cows] to the Maruts Gṛhamedhins.
What was the barhis of the Sāṃtapana [rite] is that of the Gṛhamedhīya.
Or there is no firewood and barhis.
No fore-offerings are offered, nor after-offerings.
Having driven away the calves without a yajus, he causes the cows to be milked without a strainer.

sanskrit_iast: sa vai khalu parṇaśākhayā vatsānapākṛtya pavitrayati saṃdohya yathaitadamāvāsyāyāṃ kriyate taṃ caruṃ śrapayatītyeke
meaning: स वै खलु पर्णशाखया वत्सानपाकृत्य पवित्रयति संदोह्य यथैतदमावास्यायां क्रियते तं चरुं श्रपयतीत्येके
text_mt: “Indeed, having driven away the calves with a branch of the parṇa tree, he purifies [the milk] with a strainer, milks them together just as is done on the New Moon day, and cooks that pap,” say some.

sanskrit_iast: agnīnanvādhāya vedaṃ kṛtvāgnīnparistīrya pāṇiprakṣālanādi karma pratipadyate /
meaning: अग्नीनन्वाधाय वेदं कृत्वाग्नीन्परिस्तीर्य पाणिप्रक्षालनादि कर्म प्रतिपद्यते /
text_mt: Having added fuel to the fires, made the veda, and strewn grass around the fires, he proceeds to the rite beginning with the washing of the hands.
He sets out the utensils according to purpose.
[He places] a cooking pot in place of the potsherds.
having poured out four handfuls, he adds much [grain] more.
At the time of placing the potsherds, he places the cooking pot with the first potsherd mantra.
He adapts the mantra to: “Firm are you...”
At the time of purifying the flour, he purifies the rice grains.

sanskrit_iast: adhiśrayaṇakāle prātardohavatsarvā yajamānasya gā dohayitvā tasmiñchrapayati
meaning: अधिश्रयणकाले प्रातर्दोहवत्सर्वा यजमानस्य गा दोहयित्वा तस्मिञ्छ्रपयति
text_mt: At the time of placing [the pot] on the fire, having had all the cows of the sacrificer milked as in the morning milking, he cooks [the pap] in that [milk].
At the time of the ritual call, he calls for whatever is other than the firewood and barhis.
At the time of ladling the clarified butter, he takes it in the dhruvā ladle alone.

sanskrit_iast: prokṣaṇīrabhimantrya brahmāṇamāmantrya vediṃ prokṣya prokṣaṇīśeṣaṃ ninīya pavitre apisṛjyāntarvedi vidhṛtī nidhāya dhruvāṃ ca sādayati
meaning: प्रोक्षणीरभिमन्त्र्य ब्रह्माणमामन्त्र्य वेदिं प्रोक्ष्य प्रोक्षणीशेषं निनीय पवित्रे अपिसृज्यान्तर्वेदि विधृती निधाय ध्रुवां च सादयति
text_mt: Having consecrated the sprinkling waters, called upon the brahman priest, sprinkled the altar ground, poured out the residue of the sprinkling waters, inserted the two strainers, and placed the two separating blades inside the altar ground, he also places the dhruvā ladle down.
He adapts the mantra to: “May these two sit down...”

sanskrit_iast: udvāsanakāle śaraṃ nidhāya yāvanto yajamānasyāmātyāstāvata odanānuddharati
meaning: उद्वासनकाले शरं निधाय यावन्तो यजमानस्यामात्यास्तावत ओदनानुद्धरति
text_mt: At the time of taking down [the cooked food], having laid down a shallow bowl, he ladles out as many portions of boiled rice as there are members of the sacrificer’s household.
More than that, if there is abundant boiled rice.
He places them down, ladled out, purified, adorned, and besprinkled with clarified butter.
On the dakṣiṇāgni he cooks a neighboring portion of boiled rice for the wife.
The Vājasaneyins prescribe the ladling out of two [dishes]:
From the southern one he sacrifices to the Maruts Gṛhamedhins;
from the northern one, to [Agni] Sviṣṭakṛt.

sanskrit_iast: odanayornimne kṛtvā tatrājyamānīya tata ājyārthānkuruta ājyasthālyā veti vājasaneyakam
meaning: ओदनयोर्निम्ने कृत्वा तत्राज्यमानीय तत आज्यार्थान्कुरुत आज्यस्थाल्या वेति वाजसनेयकम्
text_mt: “Having made depressions in the two portions of boiled rice and poured clarified butter into them, from there he performs the actions requiring clarified butter, or from the pot of clarified butter,” says a Vājasaneyaka passage.
Doing so, he should not take it into the dhruvā ladle.

sanskrit_iast: ājyabhāgābhyāṃ pracarya juhvāmupastīrya sarvataḥ samavadāya maruto gṛhamedhino yajati
meaning: आज्यभागाभ्यां प्रचर्य जुह्वामुपस्तीर्य सर्वतः समवदाय मरुतो गृहमेधिनो यजति
text_mt: Having proceeded with the two clarified butter portions and made an underlayer in the juhū ladle, having cut off [portions] from every side, he sacrifices to the Maruts Gṛhamedhins.
Having cut off once from the northern half of all of them, [he sacrifices] to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt.
There is no prāśitra portion, nor the sacrificer’s portion.
Those dependents of the sacrificer who eat the remnants of the sacrificial food consume the remainders of the boiled rice.
Or the officiating priests or other brahmins [consume it].
Brahmins consume the boiled rice that is in the cooking pot.

sanskrit_iast: suhitā etāṃ rātriṃ vasanti pratītā anavartimukhinaḥ
meaning: सुहिता एतां रात्रिं वसन्ति प्रतीता अनवर्तिमुखिनः
text_mt: Satiated, trusting, with faces free from distress, they pass this night.
He sets down the pot without scraping it out.
He lays alongside it the stirring ladle and the spoon, unwiped.

meaning: पराचीनरात्रे ऽभिवान्याया अग्निहोत्र्यै च वत्सौ बध्नाति
text_mt: In the latter part of the night, he ties the two calves to the foster cow and to the agnihotra cow.
At daybreak, before the agnihotra, they perform the rite with the full ladle;

sanskrit_iast: śaraniṣkāsasya darvīṃ pūrayitvarṣabhamāhūya tasya ravate pūrṇā darvi parāpatetyanudrutyottarayā gārhapatye juhuyāt
meaning: शरनिष्कासस्य दर्वीं पूरयित्वर्षभमाहूय तस्य रवते पूर्णा दर्वि परापतेत्यनुद्रुत्योत्तरया गार्हपत्ये जुहुयात्
text_mt: Having filled the ladle with the scraper-remnants of the boiled mess and having called a bull, when he roars, he should run along [with the ladle] and offer into the gārhapatya with the next verse: 'O full ladle, fly away...'.
If the bull does not roar, the brahman should say, 'Offer!'

sanskrit_iast: yasya ravate juhoti tāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dadāti
meaning: यस्य रवते जुहोति तां दक्षिणां ददाति
text_mt: At whose roaring he offers, that [bull] he gives as the sacrificial gift.

sanskrit_iast: marudbhyaḥ krīḍibhyaḥ svatavadbhyo vā puroḍāśaṃ saptakapālaṃ nirvapati /
meaning: मरुद्भ्यः क्रीडिभ्यः स्वतवद्भ्यो वा पुरोडाशं सप्तकपालं निर्वपति /
text_mt: He parcels out a sacrificial cake on seven potsherds for the playful Maruts, or for the mighty Maruts.

sanskrit_iast: sākaṃ sūryeṇodyatā sākaṃ vā raśmibhiḥ pracaranti /
meaning: साकं सूर्येणोद्यता साकं वा रश्मिभिः प्रचरन्ति /
text_mt: They proceed [with the offering] along with the rising sun, or along with its rays.
The sacrifice is concluded in the established manner.
Then he initiates the framework of the Mahāhavis.
Its procedure is explained by the northern fire-enclosure of the Vāruṇapraghāsa rites.
At the time of parceling out, he parcels out the eight subsequent oblations, beginning with 'the cake on eight potsherds for Agni'.

sanskrit_iast: aindrasya caroḥ sthāna indrāya vṛtraghne carumeke samāmananti //
meaning: ऐन्द्रस्य चरोः स्थान इन्द्राय वृत्रघ्ने चरुमेके समामनन्ति //
text_mt: In place of the boiled mess for Indra, some prescribe a boiled mess for Indra the slayer of Vṛtra.
He performs the continuous pouring of the ghee with the ladle, saying: 'Agni has enjoyed the office of hotṛ, he has enjoyed the message; he has stood erect at the sacrifice;

sanskrit_iast: avatāṃ tvā dyāvāpṛthivī ava taṃ dyāvāpṛthivī /
meaning: अवतां त्वा द्यावापृथिवी अव तं द्यावापृथिवी /
text_mt: may Heaven and Earth protect you; may Heaven and Earth protect him;

sanskrit_iast: sviṣṭakṛdindrāya devebhyo bhava juṣāṇo asya haviṣo ghṛtasya vīhi svāheti srucyamāghārayati //
meaning: स्विष्टकृदिन्द्राय देवेभ्यो भव जुषाणो अस्य हविषो घृतस्य वीहि स्वाहेति स्रुच्यमाघारयति //
text_mt: be the maker of good offerings to Indra and to the gods; enjoying this oblation of ghee, partake of it, svāhā!'
The sacrificer addresses [the offering] with: 'You are Speech related to Agni...'.
He offers upon the single potsherd with four names of the months, beginning with 'Sahas and Sahasya' [etc.].
The sacrificial gift is a milch cow, or an old bull.
He hopes for the well-being of the Idāvatsara year.
Among the blessings of the sūktavāka recitation, the hotṛ continues with: 'He hopes for the divine abode.'
he modifies the mantra as: 'I hope...'
He consigns the chaff of the cake for Indra and Agni to the waters.
The sacrifice is concluded in the established manner.
At that very time, he initiates the framework of the Pitṛyajña.

sanskrit_iast: vedaṃ kṛtvāgreṇānvāhāryapacanaṃ yajamānamātrīṃ catuḥsraktiṃ vediṃ karoti
meaning: वेदं कृत्वाग्रेणान्वाहार्यपचनं यजमानमात्रीं चतुःस्रक्तिं वेदिं करोति
text_mt: Having made the broom-bunch, he makes in front of the anvāhāryapacana a four-cornered altar ground measuring the sacrificer's size.
The corners face the cardinal directions, the middles face the intermediate directions.
The altar ground should not be excavated eastward,
it should be excavated in between both directions;

sanskrit_iast: ubhaye hi devāśca pitaraścejyanta iti vijñāyate
meaning: उभये हि देवाश्च पितरश्चेज्यन्त इति विज्ञायते
text_mt: for it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa]: 'Both gods and ancestors are sacrificed to.'

sanskrit_iast: ye ke ca devasaṃyuktā mantrā devebhyaḥ pitṛbhya iti tānsaṃnamati /
meaning: ये के च देवसंयुक्ता मन्त्रा देवेभ्यः पितृभ्य इति तान्संनमति /
text_mt: And whatever mantras contain the word 'gods', he modifies them to 'gods and ancestors',
as in: 'O earth, place of sacrifice to gods and ancestors!'
Or there is no modification, because of the hearing of the other text.
Having acted [up to the step] before the second enclosing line, he brings fire from the dakṣiṇāgni and sets it up in the middle of the altar ground.
In this Pitṛyajña, the duties of the āhavanīya are performed [in that fire].
Having added fuel to the fires, he brings the firewood and the sacrificial grass.
The firewood is larger and longer in proportion to its purpose.
Having strewn grass around the fires, he proceeds to the rite beginning with the washing of hands.
The setting out of the vessels is according to the purpose.

sanskrit_iast: nirvapaṇakāle sarvato vediṃ pariśrityottareṇa dvāraṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇataḥ prācīnāvītī havīṃṣi nirvapati /
meaning: निर्वपणकाले सर्वतो वेदिं परिश्रित्योत्तरेण द्वारं कृत्वा दक्षिणतः प्राचीनावीती हवींषि निर्वपति /
text_mt: At the time of parceling out, having screened the altar ground on all sides and having made an entrance to the north, he parcels out the oblations from the south, wearing his sacred cord over the right shoulder;
wearing the sacred cord over the left shoulder, for 'Soma accompanied by the ancestors,' as handed down in the text.

sanskrit_iast: somāya pitṛmata ājyaṃ pitṛbhyo barhiṣadbhyaḥ ṣaṭkapālaṃ pitṛbhyo 'gniṣvāttebhyo dhānā agnaye kavyavāhanāya yamāya vā manthaṃ yamāyāṅgirasvate pitṛmate
meaning: सोमाय पितृमत आज्यं पितृभ्यो बर्हिषद्भ्यः षट्कपालं पितृभ्यो ऽग्निष्वात्तेभ्यो धाना अग्नये कव्यवाहनाय यमाय वा मन्थं यमायाङ्गिरस्वते पितृमते
text_mt: Clarified butter for Soma accompanied by the ancestors, a cake on six potsherds for the ancestors seated on the grass, parched grains for the ancestors consumed by fire, and a mixed beverage for Agni bearer of the funeral offering or for Yama, [or] for Yama accompanied by the Aṅgirases and accompanied by the ancestors.
A water-jar serves as the vessel for the sprinkling water.

sanskrit_iast: prokṣaṇyudrekeṇa yavānsaṃyutya triṣphalīkṛtāṃstaṇḍulānvibhāgamantreṇa vibhajya dhānārthānnidhāyetarānpiṣṭāni kṛtvā dakṣiṇārdhe gārhapatyasya ṣaṭkapālānyupadhāya dakṣiṇāgnau prathamena kapālamantreṇa dhānārthaṃ kapālamadhiśrayati
meaning: प्रोक्षण्युद्रेकेण यवान्संयुत्य त्रिष्फलीकृतांस्तण्डुलान्विभागमन्त्रेण विभज्य धानार्थान्निधायेतरान्पिष्टानि कृत्वा दक्षिणार्धे गार्हपत्यस्य षट्कपालान्युपधाय दक्षिणाग्नौ प्रथमेन कपालमन्त्रेण धानार्थं कपालमधिश्रयति
text_mt: Having mixed barley with the remainder of the sprinkling water, having divided the husked rice that has been husked three times with the division mantra, having set aside [the grains] intended for the parched grains, having made the others into flour, and having arranged six potsherds in the southern half of the gārhapatya, he puts a potsherd for the parched grains onto the dakṣiṇāgni with the first potsherd mantra.

meaning: अधिश्रयणकाले ऽधिश्रयणमनत्रेण तण्डुलानोप्य बहुरूपा धानाः करोति
text_mt: At the time of setting [them] over [the fire], having poured the rice grains with the mantra for setting over [the fire], he makes variegated parched grains.
For it is known: 'Being slightly scorched, they lie about.'
At the time of the ritual calls, he issues the ritual calls excluding the wife.
At the time of taking the clarified butter, he takes four portions of clarified butter to the north of the gārhapatya.
He proceeds to the rite beginning with the consecration of the sprinkling water.

sanskrit_iast: sataraṇakāle barhiṣā triḥ prasavyaṃ vediṃ stṛṇanparyeti
meaning: सतरणकाले बर्हिषा त्रिः प्रसव्यं वेदिं स्तृणन्पर्येति
text_mt: At the time of strewing, he walks around three times counter-clockwise, strewing the altar ground with sacrificial grass;
holding raised [grass bunches], he walks around three times in the opposite direction without strewing.
The taking and placing of the grass bunch are done silently.
He puts around two enclosing sticks,

sanskrit_iast: yadi sarvānāvāhanakāle paridhīm̐raporṇviti vābhijñāya dakṣiṇaṃ madhyame paridhāvupasamasyet
meaning: यदि सर्वानावाहनकाले परिधीम्̐रपोर्ण्विति वाभिज्ञाय दक्षिणं मध्यमे परिधावुपसमस्येत्
text_mt: If all, then at the time of summoning, recognising [the moment] or upon the words 'Uncover the enclosing sticks', he should push the southern one alongside the middle enclosing stick.

sanskrit_iast: udvāsanakāle dhānā udvāsya vibhāgamantreṇa vibhajyārdhā ājyena saṃyauti
meaning: उद्वासनकाले धाना उद्वास्य विभागमन्त्रेण विभज्यार्धा आज्येन संयौति
text_mt: At the time of taking off [the offerings], having taken off the parched barley grains and having divided them with the formula for division, he mixes half with clarified butter.

sanskrit_iast: ardhāḥ piṣṭānāmāvṛtā saktūnkṛtvābhivānthāyai dugdhasyārdhaśarāve saktūnopyaikayekṣuśalākayekṣukāṇḍena vā dakṣiṇāmukhastriḥ prasavyamanārabhyopamanthati
meaning: अर्धाः पिष्टानामावृता सक्तून्कृत्वाभिवान्थायै दुग्धस्यार्धशरावे सक्तूनोप्यैकयेक्षुशलाकयेक्षुकाण्डेन वा दक्षिणामुखस्त्रिः प्रसव्यमनारभ्योपमन्थति
text_mt: Having ground half into groats according to the procedure for flour, pouring the groats into half a bowl of milk from a cow that mates with a bull while pregnant, he stirs [them] three times counterclockwise with a single stalk of reed or a piece of sugarcane, facing south, without touching [the bowl with his hand].
Having placed the stir-stick in the beverage, he sets down the sacrificial offerings one by one.

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇataḥ kaśipūpabarhaṇamāñjanamabhyañjanamudakumbhamityekaikaśa āsādya vedaṃ nidhāya sāmidhenībhyaḥ pratipadyate
meaning: दक्षिणतः कशिपूपबर्हणमाञ्जनमभ्यञ्जनमुदकुम्भमित्येकैकश आसाद्य वेदं निधाय सामिधेनीभ्यः प्रतिपद्यते
text_mt: Having set down one by one to the south the grass mat and cushion, collyrium, unguent, and a water-pot, and having laid down the veda-broom, he proceeds to the kindling verses.
He issues the ritual call: 'Recite for Agni, for the gods, for the Ancestors, as he is being kindled.'
He recites one kindling verse three times,
namely, 'Desiring you, we summon...'.

sanskrit_iast: ekāmanūyājasamidhamavaśiṣya samaśa idhmaṃ traidhaṃ vibhajya trirādadhāti
meaning: एकामनूयाजसमिधमवशिष्य समश इध्मं त्रैधं विभज्य त्रिरादधाति
text_mt: Leaving aside one stick of kindling for the after-offerings, having divided the firewood equally into three parts, he puts [them] on three times.
He does not choose the ancestral seers, nor the hotṛ.
Having called for recitation, he says: 'Sit down, hotṛ.'
Having offered the fore-offerings without the barhis, he offers the two butter portions containing the word 'alive':

sanskrit_iast: ā no agne suketunā rayiṃ viśvāyupoṣasam /
meaning: आ नो अग्ने सुकेतुना रयिं विश्वायुपोषसम् /
text_mt: 'Agni, with good guidance, grant us wealth, nourishment of a full lifespan

sanskrit_iast: tvaṃ soma mahe bhagaṃ tvaṃ yūna ṛtāyate /
meaning: त्वं सोम महे भगं त्वं यून ऋतायते /
text_mt: 'You, Soma, bestow great fortune; you bestow skill
upon the youth who observes truth, so that he may live'—these are the two containing the word 'alive'.
Here some teach the enclosing of the altar ground with screens:
'Having untied their sacred threads, they make them hang over the right shoulder;
the priests walk about in reverse;
they transpose the ladles, the offerings, and the screens.'
He places the upabhṛt to the south of the juhū;

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇenopabhrtaṃ dhruvāṃ dakṣiṇena puroḍāśaṃ dhānāstā dakṣiṇena mantham
meaning: दक्षिणेनोपभ्र्तं ध्रुवां दक्षिणेन पुरोडाशं धानास्ता दक्षिणेन मन्थम्
text_mt: the dhruvā to the south of the upabhṛt; the parched barley grains to the south of the sacrificial cake; and the stir-beverage to the south of them.
The juhū and the cake on six potsherds are placed in the same spot.
Some say the Brahman and the sacrificer [also change places].
There are six cuttings for those who make five cuttings, and five cuttings for those who make four cuttings.
Breaking through the sacrificial cake, he cuts [portions].
For one who makes five cuttings, he should cut twice from the first [offering].

meaning: जुह्वामुपस्तीर्य सोमाय पितृमते ऽनु स्वधेति संप्रेष्यति
text_mt: Having spread under [clarified butter] in the juhū, he issues the ritual call: 'Svadha for Soma accompanied by the Ancestors!'
He takes a cutting once from the sacrificial cake, once from the parched barley grains, and once from the stir-beverage.
Having taken cuttings from the south side and having basted them, stepping across toward the north and standing facing south, he calls for recitation with: 'Bring svadhā!'
[The agnīdh] responds with: 'Let there be svadhā.'
He issues the ritual call: 'Offer svadhā to Soma accompanied by the Ancestors.'
With: 'We who make svadhā...', he offers.
He pronounces the vaṣaṭ-call with: 'Svadhā, reverence!'
However, rejecting the svadhā-call, he prescribes the calls and responses of the Bahvṛcas and Vājasaneyins.
He recites two invitatory verses.

sanskrit_iast: tvaṃ soma pracikita ityetā āmnātā bhavanti
meaning: त्वं सोम प्रचिकित इत्येता आम्नाता भवन्ति
text_mt: 'You, Soma, understand...'—these are handed down by tradition.
it is 'The Agniṣvātta Ancestors...':

sanskrit_iast: ye agniṣvāttā ye 'nagniṣvāttā aṃhomucaḥ pitaraḥ somyāsaḥ /
meaning: ये अग्निष्वात्ता ये ऽनग्निष्वात्ता अंहोमुचः पितरः सोम्यासः /
text_mt: 'The Ancestors who are consumed by fire, and who are not consumed by fire, deliverers from distress, worthy of Soma,

meaning: परे ऽवरे मृतासो भवन्तो ऽधिब्रुवन्तु ते अवन्त्वस्मान् //
text_mt: whether far or near, being departed, let them speak for us, let them aid us.'

sanskrit_iast: vānyāyai dugdhe juṣamāṇāḥ karambhamudīrāṇā avare pare ca /
meaning: वान्यायै दुग्धे जुषमाणाः करम्भमुदीराणा अवरे परे च /
text_mt: 'Enjoying the porridge made with the milk of a cow mating while pregnant, rising up, those who are lower and those who are higher,

sanskrit_iast: agniṣvāttā ṛtubhiḥ saṃvidānā indravanto haviridaṃ juṣantāmiti pitṛbhyo 'gniṣvāttebhyaḥ
meaning: अग्निष्वात्ता ऋतुभिः संविदाना इन्द्रवन्तो हविरिदं जुषन्तामिति पितृभ्यो ऽग्निष्वात्तेभ्यः
text_mt: the Agniṣvāttas, being in accord with the seasons, accompanied by Indra, let them enjoy this oblation'—[these are] for the Agniṣvātta Ancestors.
They perform the Ancestor sacrifice in a low voice within the screened [enclosure].
According to this very procedure, he sacrifices to the Barhiṣad Ancestors and to the Agniṣvāttas.
He sacrifices to Agni Kavyavāhana in place of the Sviṣṭakṛt.
To whichever deity he sacrifices, he takes the first cutting from that [deity's] oblation.
He cuts the iḍā into the stir-beverage, or [takes] the stir-beverage itself [as the iḍā].
He places the stir-beverage into the hands of the hotṛ.
Likewise the brahman, the adhvaryu, the agnīdh, and the sacrificer.

sanskrit_iast: samaśo vā prativibhajyāvaghreṇa bhakṣayitvā barhiṣi lepānnimṛjante
meaning: समशो वा प्रतिविभज्यावघ्रेण भक्षयित्वा बर्हिषि लेपान्निमृजन्ते
text_mt: Or having divided it into equal parts and consumed [their shares] by smelling, they wipe off the remnants upon the barhis.

sanskrit_iast: udakumbhamādāya yajamānaḥ śundhantāṃ pitara iti triḥ prasavyaṃ vediṃ pariṣiñcanparyeti
meaning: उदकुम्भमादाय यजमानः शुन्धन्तां पितर इति त्रिः प्रसव्यं वेदिं परिषिञ्चन्पर्येति
text_mt: Taking a jar of water, the sacrificer goes around the altar ground three times from right to left, sprinkling it with the formula: 'May the ancestors be purified.'

sanskrit_iast: nidhāya kumbhamayā viṣṭhā janayan karvarāṇīti trirapariṣiñcanpratiparyeti
meaning: निधाय कुम्भमया विष्ठा जनयन् कर्वराणीति त्रिरपरिषिञ्चन्प्रतिपर्येति
text_mt: Setting down the jar, he goes back around three times without sprinkling, with the formula: 'Generating various forms, may these become adorned.'

sanskrit_iast: haviḥśeṣānsaṃplomnāya piṇḍānkṛtvā tisṛṣu sraktiṣu nidadhāti pūrvasyāṃ dakṣiṇasyāmaparasyāmiti /
meaning: हविःशेषान्संप्लोम्नाय पिण्डान्कृत्वा तिसृषु स्रक्तिषु निदधाति पूर्वस्यां दक्षिणस्यामपरस्यामिति /
text_mt: Having collected the remnants of the oblation and formed them into rice-balls, he places them at three corners: at the eastern, at the southern, and at the western;

sanskrit_iast: etatte tatāsau ye ca tvāmanvityetaiḥ pratimantram
meaning: एतत्ते ततासौ ये च त्वामन्वित्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रम्
text_mt: with these respective formulas: 'This is yours, father N.N., and of those who follow you.'
He mentions three remote ancestors:
the sixth on the first rice-ball,

sanskrit_iast: uttarasyāṃ sraktyāṃ riptalepaṃ nimṛjyātra pitaro yathābhāgaṃ mandadhvamityuktvodañco niṣkramya susaṃdṛśaṃ tvā vayamityaindryarcāhavanīyamupatiṣṭhanta aindrībhyāṃ vā
meaning: उत्तरस्यां स्रक्त्यां रिप्तलेपं निमृज्यात्र पितरो यथाभागं मन्दध्वमित्युक्त्वोदञ्चो निष्क्रम्य सुसंदृशं त्वा वयमित्यैन्द्र्यर्चाहवनीयमुपतिष्ठन्त ऐन्द्रीभ्यां वा
text_mt: Having wiped off the smeared remnant on the northern corner, saying, 'Here, O ancestors, take delight according to your shares,' and stepping out towards the north, they worship the āhavanīya with the Indra verse, 'You of fair appearance we...', or with two Indra verses.
Having worshipped until they lose their breath, they worship the gārhapatya with the paṅkti verse: 'They have eaten, they have rejoiced...'
With that very verse they enter the enclosed area.
Here some prescribe the consuming and the sprinkling.
All consumptions are by smelling.
The rites from the application of collyrium up to the paṅkti verse are as in the Piṇḍapitṛyajña.
He returns with the paṅkti verse: 'What [we have done] in the intermediate space...'
Undoing their garments worn over the right shoulder (prācīnāvīta), they make them worn over the left shoulder (yajñopavīta).
The priests step around in reverse.
They remove the enclosing screens.
Having poured the ghee from the upabhṛt into the juhū, he offers the two after-offerings (anuyājas) without the barhis.
He issues the first call: 'Sacrifice to the two gods.'
At the time of the sūktavāka recitation, they wear their garments suspended around the neck (nivīta).
They do not perform the offerings to the wives of the gods (patnīsaṃyājas).
He does not offer the samiṣṭayajus.
The Pitṛyajña is concluded.
He portions out one-pot potsherd cakes for each individual: as many as there are members of the sacrificer's household together with the women, and one more in addition.

sanskrit_iast: yāvanto gṛhyāḥ smastebhyaḥ kamakaramiti nirupyamāṇeṣu yajamāno japati
meaning: यावन्तो गृह्याः स्मस्तेभ्यः कमकरमिति निरुप्यमाणेषु यजमानो जपति
text_mt: While they are being portioned out, the sacrificer murmurs: 'As many as we are household members, for them I have made ease.'
They are prepared silently.
He places them on the northern half of the gārhapatya.

sanskrit_iast: tānabhighāryānabhighārya vodvāsyāntarvedyāsādya paśūnaṃ śrmāsīti mūte samāvapati
meaning: तानभिघार्यानभिघार्य वोद्वास्यान्तर्वेद्यासाद्य पशूनं श्र्मासीति मूते समावपति
text_mt: Having basted them or without basting them, having taken them down and set them inside the altar ground, he pours them into a woven basket with the formula: 'You are the protection of cattle.'
According to some, they carry them out with the cover of a chest.

sanskrit_iast: eka eva rudro na dvitīyāya tastha iti dakṣiṇāgnerekolmukaṃ dhūpāyaddharati
meaning: एक एव रुद्रो न द्वितीयाय तस्थ इति दक्षिणाग्नेरेकोल्मुकं धूपायद्धरति
text_mt: With the formula, 'Rudra alone is one, he did not stand for a second,' he carries a smoking firebrand from the southern fire (dakṣiṇāgni).

sanskrit_iast: uttarapūrvamavāntaradeśaṃ gatvākhuste urdra paśurityākhūtkara ekaṃ puroḍāśamupavapati
meaning: उत्तरपूर्वमवान्तरदेशं गत्वाखुस्ते उर्द्र पशुरित्याखूत्कर एकं पुरोडाशमुपवपति
text_mt: Having gone to the north-eastern intermediate direction, he places one sacrificial cake on a molehill with the formula: 'This is your beast, O Rudra: the mole.'

sanskrit_iast: asau te paśuriti vā dveṣyaṃ manasā dhyāyan
meaning: असौ ते पशुरिति वा द्वेष्यं मनसा ध्यायन्
text_mt: Or meditating in his mind upon an enemy: 'That one is your beast.'
If he does not hate anyone, he should say: 'The mole is your beast.'

sanskrit_iast: catuṣpatha ekolmukamupasamādhāya saṃparistīrya sarveṣāṃ puroḍāśānāmuttarārdhātsakṛtsakṛdavadāya madhyamenāntamenā vā palāśaparṇena juhoti
meaning: चतुष्पथ एकोल्मुकमुपसमाधाय संपरिस्तीर्य सर्वेषां पुरोडाशानामुत्तरार्धात्सकृत्सकृदवदाय मध्यमेनान्तमेना वा पलाशपर्णेन जुहोति
text_mt: Having laid down the single firebrand at a crossroads and strewn around it, having cut off once from the northern half of each of all the sacrificial cakes, he offers with the middle or the terminal leaf of a palāśa leaf.

sanskrit_iast: eṣa te rudra bhāgaḥ saha svasrāmbikayā taṃ juṣasva svāheti bheṣajaṃ gava ityetābhyāṃ cātuṣpathamagniṃ pariṣiñcati /
meaning: एष ते रुद्र भागः सह स्वस्राम्बिकया तं जुषस्व स्वाहेति भेषजं गव इत्येताभ्यां चातुष्पथमग्निं परिषिञ्चति /
text_mt: With the formula, 'This is your share, O Rudra, along with your sister Ambikā; enjoy it, svāhā,' and with the verse, 'Medicine for the cow...', he sprinkles the fire at the crossroads.
The sacrificer murmurs: 'We have appeased Rudra, the mother.'

sanskrit_iast: tryambakaṃ yajāmaha iti triḥ pradakṣiṇamagniṃ pariyanti
meaning: त्र्यम्बकं यजामह इति त्रिः प्रदक्षिणमग्निं परियन्ति
text_mt: They go around the fire three times from left to right with the formula: 'We worship Tryambaka...'
'We worship Tryambaka, the fragrant one who procures a husband.

sanskrit_iast: urvārukamiva bandhanādito mukṣīya mā pateriti yajamānasya patikāmā parīyāt
meaning: उर्वारुकमिव बन्धनादितो मुक्षीय मा पतेरिति यजमानस्य पतिकामा परीयात्
text_mt: Like a cucumber from its stem, from here may I be freed, not from a husband'—a woman of the sacrificer's household who desires a husband should go around [with this verse].

sanskrit_iast: ūrdhvānpuroḍāśānudasya pratilabhya tryambakaṃ yajāmaha iti yajamānasyāñjalau samopya bhaga stha bhagasya vo lapsīyetyapādāyaitenaiva kalpena triḥ samāvapeyuḥ
meaning: ऊर्ध्वान्पुरोडाशानुदस्य प्रतिलभ्य त्र्यम्बकं यजामह इति यजमानस्याञ्जलौ समोप्य भग स्थ भगस्य वो लप्सीयेत्यपादायैतेनैव कल्पेन त्रिः समावपेयुः
text_mt: Having tossed the sacrificial cakes upwards and caught them, having poured them together into the folded hands of the sacrificer with the formula 'We worship Tryambaka...', and taking them back with the formula 'You are fortune; may I obtain your fortune,' they should pour them together three times in this same manner.
And they should pour them together in this way for a woman desiring a husband, modifying the formula accordingly.
According to some, they pour them together after each round of going around.
He pours them into a woven basket, or into two woven baskets, or into several woven baskets.

sanskrit_iast: eṣa te rudra bhāga iti vṛkṣa āsajati vṛkṣayorvṛkṣeṣu vā
meaning: एष ते रुद्र भाग इति वृक्ष आसजति वृक्षयोर्वृक्षेषु वा
text_mt: With the formula, 'This is your share, O Rudra,' he hangs it on a tree, or on two trees, or on several trees.

sanskrit_iast: api vā mūtayoḥ samopya vivadhaṃ kṛtvā śuṣke sthāṇau valmīkavapāyāṃ vāvadhāyāvatatadhanvā pinākahastaḥ kṛttivāsomiti triravatāmyanti
meaning: अपि वा मूतयोः समोप्य विवधं कृत्वा शुष्के स्थाणौ वल्मीकवपायां वावधायावततधन्वा पिनाकहस्तः कृत्तिवासोमिति त्रिरवताम्यन्ति
text_mt: Or having poured them into two woven baskets, having made a carrying-pole, and having placed them on a dry stump or on the crest of an anthill, they hold their breath three times with the formula: 'With unstrung bow, holding the pināka bow in hand, clad in a hide...'

meaning: अपः परिषिच्याप्रतीक्षास्तूष्णीमेत्यैधो ऽस्येधिषीमहीत्याहवनीये समिध आधायापो अन्वचारिषमित्युपतिष्ठन्ते
text_mt: Having sprinkled water around, returning silently without looking back, and having placed kindling on the āhavanīya with the formula 'You are kindling; may we kindle,' they worship with the formula 'I have followed the waters.'
He portions out a mess of boiled rice (caru) in ghee for the Ādityas as before.
Or a white bull, or one with white lower marks.
The sacrifice is concluded according to the established procedure.

sanskrit_iast: āgnāvaiṣṇavamekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapeccakṣuṣkāmo bārhaspatyaṃ caruṃ brahmavarcasakāma aindraṃ paśukāmaḥ sārsavataṃ prajākāmaḥ pauṣṇaṃ pratiṣṭhākāmaḥ
meaning: आग्नावैष्णवमेकादशकपालं निर्वपेच्चक्षुष्कामो बार्हस्पत्यं चरुं ब्रह्मवर्चसकाम ऐन्द्रं पशुकामः सार्सवतं प्रजाकामः पौष्णं प्रतिष्ठाकामः
text_mt: One who desires sight should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Agni-and-Viṣṇu; one who desires spiritual luster, a caru to Bṛhaspati; one who desires cattle, [a cake] to Indra; one who desires offspring, [a caru] to Sarasvatī; one who desires stability, [a caru] to Pūṣan.
Whichever of these he might desire, that one he should offer additionally.
The offering is completed in the established manner.
The Sākamedha offerings are concluded.
Here, having sacrificed on the full-moon day, the moistening and the rest, up to the shaving, are performed as before,
“He who makes the plants turn back upon the skin of this earth,
Agni the ruler through might, Varuṇa along with thoughts,
Indra together with the Maruts as comrades.”
“Agni with sharp [weapon]…” is the same.

sanskrit_iast: tato dvyahe tryahe caturahe 'rdhamāse māsi caturṣu vā māseṣu śunāsīrīyeṇa yajate
meaning: ततो द्व्यहे त्र्यहे चतुरहे ऽर्धमासे मासि चतुर्षु वा मासेषु शुनासीरीयेण यजते
text_mt: Then after two days, after three days, after four days, after half a month, after a month, or after four months, he sacrifices with the Śunāsīrīya.
Its procedure is like that of the Vaiśvadeva.
At the time of the apportioning, he parcels out the ten subsequent sacrificial substances beginning with the eight-pot-sherd cake for Agni.
The milk for Vāyu is prepared according to the rule of the morning milking.

sanskrit_iast: pañca saṃcarāṇi nirupya vāyavyā yavāgūḥ pratidhugvendrāya śunāsīrāya puroḍāśo dvādaśakapālaḥ //
meaning: पञ्च संचराणि निरुप्य वायव्या यवागूः प्रतिधुग्वेन्द्राय शुनासीराय पुरोडाशो द्वादशकपालः //
text_mt: Having apportioned the five common offerings, there is barley gruel or fresh warm milk for Vāyu, and a twelve-pot-sherd sacrificial cake for Indra Śunāsīra.

sanskrit_iast: indrāya śunāsīrāya srucā uhuta no haviḥ /
meaning: इन्द्राय शुनासीराय स्रुचा उहुत नो हविः /
text_mt: “For Indra Śunāsīra our sacrificial substance has been offered with the ladle;
let the wise one accept it!”

sanskrit_iast: pra havyāni ghṛtavantyasmai haryaśvāya bharatā sajoṣāḥ /
meaning: प्र हव्यानि घृतवन्त्यस्मै हर्यश्वाय भरता सजोषाः /
text_mt: “Offer the ghee-rich sacrificial substances to this driver of bay steeds, united in mind!

sanskrit_iast: indrartubhirbrahmaṇā vāvṛdhānaḥ śunāsīrī haviridaṃ juṣasveti śunāsīrīyasya yājyānuvākye //
meaning: इन्द्रर्तुभिर्ब्रह्मणा वावृधानः शुनासीरी हविरिदं जुषस्वेति शुनासीरीयस्य याज्यानुवाक्ये //
text_mt: O Indra, grown great through the seasons by sacred speech, O Śunāsīrī, enjoy this offering!”—these are the yājyā and anuvākyā verses for the Śunāsīrīya offering.
It has five fore-offerings and three after-offerings, say some.
With the month-name, “Thou art Saṃsarpa; for Aṃhaspatya thee,” he makes an offering over the one-pot-sherd cake.
A plow with a team of twelve oxen is the sacrificial gift,
a white horse, or a white cow for the one-pot-sherd cake.
“He prays for well-being for the coming year;
he prays for the heavenly realm,” thus the hotṛ inserts into the blessings of the sūktavāka recitation.
He adapts the mantra: “I pray…”
The offering is completed in the established manner.
The Seasonal Sacrifices (Cāturmāsya) are concluded.
Here, having sacrificed on the full-moon day, the moistening and the rest, up to the shaving, are performed as before,
“Parameṣṭhin released one month for living beings;
thereby he brought great immortality to mortals.
After offspring thou art born; that indeed is thine immortality, O mortal.
Whereby the months, the half-months, the seasons, the full years [are ordered],

sanskrit_iast: yena te te prajāpata ījānasya nyavartayan /
meaning: येन ते ते प्रजापत ईजानस्य न्यवर्तयन् /
text_mt: whereby they shaved thine [hair], O Prajāpati, when thou didst sacrifice,
thereby, by his sacred word, I shave this one for life.”
“Agni with sharp [weapon]…” is the same.
Having sacrificed with the Seasonal Sacrifices, he sacrifices with soma or with an animal sacrifice.
When the Phālguna full moon becomes visible, he undergoes initiation for soma.
After that, another Phālguna full moon should not pass by him without having sacrificed.
This is indeed for one who is concluding [the cycle].
Now for one who is undertaking it again: having sacrificed with the Śunāsīrīya on the fourteenth day of the Phālguna [fortnight],
he sacrifices with the Vaiśvadeva on the fifteenth.

sanskrit_iast: etenaiva paśukāmo yajeta yasminnasyartau bhuyiṣṭhaṃ goṣu payaḥ syāt
meaning: एतेनैव पशुकामो यजेत यस्मिन्नस्यर्तौ भुयिष्ठं गोषु पयः स्यात्
text_mt: One desiring cattle should sacrifice with this very [rite] in whichever season the milk in his cows would be most abundant.
One desiring offspring or desiring cattle should sacrifice with this very [rite].

sanskrit_iast: vaiśvadevenetareṣāṃ parvaṇāṃ sthāne paśukāmo yajeta yāvatsahasraṃ paśūnprāpnuyāt /
meaning: वैश्वदेवेनेतरेषां पर्वणां स्थाने पशुकामो यजेत यावत्सहस्रं पशून्प्राप्नुयात् /
text_mt: One desiring cattle should sacrifice with the Vaiśvadeva in place of the other seasonal offerings until he attains a thousand cattle;
then he should sacrifice with the other [rites] at their prescribed times.
One desiring a village should sacrifice with the Śunāsīrīya using rainwater.
Having collected rainwater, he performs the water-duties with it.

sanskrit_iast: etenaiva prajākāmaḥ paśukāmaḥ puṣṭikāmo brahmavarcasakāmo 'nnādyakāmo vā yajeta
meaning: एतेनैव प्रजाकामः पशुकामः पुष्टिकामो ब्रह्मवर्चसकामो ऽन्नाद्यकामो वा यजेत
text_mt: One desiring offspring, desiring cattle, desiring prosperity, desiring spiritual lustre, or desiring food should sacrifice with this very [rite].
Through the seasonal offerings, he counts the months in the Seasonal Sacrifices.
We shall explain the five-year rituals.
Having sacrificed for three seasonal years, he does not sacrifice for a month;
having sacrificed for the subsequent two, he desists.

sanskrit_iast: caitryāṃ tūpakramya dvāviṣṭvā māsamaniṣṭvā trīnparāniṣṭvā viramati
meaning: चैत्र्यां तूपक्रम्य द्वाविष्ट्वा मासमनिष्ट्वा त्रीन्परानिष्ट्वा विरमति
text_mt: Having begun, however, on the full moon of Caitra, having sacrificed for two [years], not having sacrificed for a month, and having sacrificed for the subsequent three, he desists.
Now the fifteen-year rituals:
or he should repeat them thrice, or indefinitely.

sanskrit_iast: vijñāyate ca sa triṣutriṣu saṃvatsareṣu māsaṃ na yajata ityetadvacano 'bhyāsaḥ
meaning: विज्ञायते च स त्रिषुत्रिषु संवत्सरेषु मासं न यजत इत्येतद्वचनो ऽभ्यासः
text_mt: And it is learned [in the Brāhmaṇa]: 'He does not sacrifice for a month every three years'—such a text indicates repetition.
In the five-year rituals, the offering to Vaiśvānara and Parjanya and the Pañcahotṛ formula should not recur,
just like the Anvārambhaṇīyā sacrifice, just like the Anvārambhaṇīyā sacrifice.

title: praśnaḥ 09
text_mt: An expiation having scripture as its authority is prescribed upon a transgression of a rule.
When multiple expiations are taught for a single flaw, they should be combined, because they serve distinct purposes.
these serve to eliminate the flaw.
They are to be performed immediately after the flaw.
Once the flaw is eliminated, the entire rite [is performed] again.
There is no repetition of it without an explicit injunction.
One who has added fuel to his fires, when about to set out on a journey, should offer [a libation] with: 'To thee, O greatest of the Aṅgirases…'
Having mounted the fires separately onto churning sticks, he sets out.
Where he resides, there he should conclude that sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast: yadyanvāhitāgnerāhavanīyo 'nugacchedanvagniruṣasāmagramakhyadityanyaṃ praṇīya bhūrityupasthāya yo agniṃ devavītaye haviṣmām̐ āvivāsati /
meaning: यद्यन्वाहिताग्नेराहवनीयो ऽनुगच्छेदन्वग्निरुषसामग्रमख्यदित्यन्यं प्रणीय भूरित्युपस्थाय यो अग्निं देववीतये हविष्माम्̐ आविवासति /
text_mt: If the āhavanīya fire of one who has added fuel to the fires should go out, having brought forward another with: 'Agni has followed the morning glows…', having attended upon it with: 'Bhūḥ', [and with]: 'He who strives to serve Agni for the feast of the gods with an oblation,
to him, O Purifier, be gracious, svāhā!'—

sanskrit_iast: pūrṇaṃ sruvaṃ sarvaprāyaścittaṃ hutvedaṃ viṣṇurvicakrama ity āhutiṃ juhuyāt
meaning: पूर्णं स्रुवं सर्वप्रायश्चित्तं हुत्वेदं विष्णुर्विचक्रम इत्य् आहुतिं जुहुयात्
text_mt: having offered a full dipping-spoon as a universal expiation, he should offer an oblation with: 'Viṣṇu strode across this…'
He should mutter the yajus formula for undertaking the vow mentally.
Whichever fire should go out, this same [procedure] should be repeated, with the exception of bringing forward [the fire].
[The fire to be churned or brought for the anvāhāryapacana is] whatever is the origin of the southern fire.

sanskrit_iast: yadyāhitāgneragnirapakṣāyedā śamyāparāsātpari vājapatiḥ kaviragniriti triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ parikramya taṃ saṃbharedidaṃ ta ekaṃ para uta ekaṃ tṛtīyena jyotiṣā saṃviśasva /
meaning: यद्याहिताग्नेरग्निरपक्षायेदा शम्यापरासात्परि वाजपतिः कविरग्निरिति त्रिः प्रदक्षिणं परिक्रम्य तं संभरेदिदं त एकं पर उत एकं तृतीयेन ज्योतिषा संविशस्व /
text_mt: If the fire of one who has set up his fires should burn beyond [its hearth] up to a yoke-pin's throw, having walked thrice around it clockwise with: 'Agni, the ruler of spoils, the sage…', he should gather it with: 'This is one of yours, and that other is one; enter together with the third light!

sanskrit_iast: saṃveśanastanuvai cāruredhi priye devānāṃ parame janitra iti
meaning: संवेशनस्तनुवै चारुरेधि प्रिये देवानां परमे जनित्र इति
text_mt: As a gatherer of bodies, be lovely in the dear, highest birthplace of the gods!'
If it should burn beyond further than that, he should pursue it and pitch camp.
There he should set apart an eight-potsherd cake for Agni the Path-Maker.
He should fetch sacrificial grass from near the path.
The sacrifice concludes in the established manner.
Then, on the next day, he moves back home.

sanskrit_iast: yasya haviṣe vatsā apākṛtā dhayeyustatsthāne vāyavyāṃ yavāgūṃ nirvapet
meaning: यस्य हविषे वत्सा अपाकृता धयेयुस्तत्स्थाने वायव्यां यवागूं निर्वपेत्
text_mt: If calves separated for the oblation should suckle [their mothers], in their place he should set apart barley gruel for Vāyu.
Then, having separated the calves for the subsequent oblation, he should observe the fast.
For whom the oblation milked in the evening meets with mishap, having set apart rice grains for Indra, he should observe the fast.
Whatever [milk] there is in the morning, he should cook it.
Then the other [offering] should be a cake for Indra.
Cutting portions from it together with the morning milking, he should proceed.
This very same is the expiation when the morning milking meets with mishap.
Cutting portions from it together with the evening milking, he should proceed.
If both milkings of his should meet with mishap, he should set apart an eight-potsherd [cake] for Agni and a five-cup mess of cooked rice for Indra.
He should worship Agni with the cake
Or he should worship both deities with the five-cup mess.
Then, having separated the calves for the subsequent oblation, he should observe the fast.
Whose wife should be menstruating on the day of the vow, he should sacrifice having secluded her.
Behind the altar ground or inside the altar ground, he should spread out her girdle with its cord pointing north.

sanskrit_iast: yadā trirātrīṇā syādathaināmupahvayetāmūhamasmi sā tvaṃ dyaurahaṃ pṛthivī tvaṃ sāmāhamṛktvaṃ tāvehi saṃbhavāva saha reto dadhāvahai puṃse putrāya vettavai rāyaspoṣāya suprajāstvāya suvīryāyeti
meaning: यदा त्रिरात्रीणा स्यादथैनामुपह्वयेतामूहमस्मि सा त्वं द्यौरहं पृथिवी त्वं सामाहमृक्त्वं तावेहि संभवाव सह रेतो दधावहै पुंसे पुत्राय वेत्तवै रायस्पोषाय सुप्रजास्त्वाय सुवीर्यायेति
text_mt: When three nights have passed for her, he should then summon her: 'I am he, you are she; I am the sky, you are the earth; I am the Sāman, you are the Ṛc. Come, let us unite, let us place our seed together, for a male child to be born, for wealth and prosperity, for good offspring, for heroic strength.'

sanskrit_iast: yasyāgnihotraṃ sāmnāyyaṃ vā viṣyandetodaṅparetya valmīkavapāmuddhṛtya prajāpate na tvadetānīti prājāpatyayarcā valmīkavapāyāmavanīya bhūrityupasthāyānyāṃ dugdhvā punarjuhuyāt /
meaning: यस्याग्निहोत्रं साम्नाय्यं वा विष्यन्देतोदङ्परेत्य वल्मीकवपामुद्धृत्य प्रजापते न त्वदेतानीति प्राजापत्ययर्चा वल्मीकवपायामवनीय भूरित्युपस्थायान्यां दुग्ध्वा पुनर्जुहुयात् /
text_mt: If his agnihotra or curd-and-milk oblation should overflow, having gone away to the north, having extracted the interior of an ant-hill, having poured [the spilled liquid] into the ant-hill interior with the verse addressed to Prajāpati: 'O Prajāpati, none other than you…', having attended upon it with 'Bhūḥ', and having milked another [cow], he should offer again.
If it is the curd-and-milk oblation, he should bring another [portion].

sanskrit_iast: yadi kīṭo 'vapadyeta madhyamenāntamena vā palāśaparṇena mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca na iti dyāvāpṛthivyayarcāntaḥparidhi ninīyānyāṃ dugdhvā punarjuhuyāt /
meaning: यदि कीटो ऽवपद्येत मध्यमेनान्तमेन वा पलाशपर्णेन मही द्यौः पृथिवी च न इति द्यावापृथिव्ययर्चान्तःपरिधि निनीयान्यां दुग्ध्वा पुनर्जुहुयात् /
text_mt: If an insect should fall into it, having poured it out inside the enclosing sticks with the middle or outer leaf of a palāśa tree, accompanied by the verse addressed to Heaven and Earth: 'May the great Heaven and Earth for us…', and having milked another [cow], he should offer again.
If [the milk intended for] the sāṃnāyya [is spoiled], he should fetch another.

sanskrit_iast: yasyāgnihotramavavarṣenmitro janānkalpayati prajānanmitro dādhāra pṛthivīmuta dyām /
meaning: यस्याग्निहोत्रमववर्षेन्मित्रो जनान्कल्पयति प्रजानन्मित्रो दाधार पृथिवीमुत द्याम् /
text_mt: If rain falls upon a sacrificer's agnihotra [offering, with the verses]: "Mitra arranges the peoples, knowing well; Mitra sustains the earth and also heaven;

sanskrit_iast: mitraḥ kṛṣṭīranimiṣābhicaṣṭe satyāya havyaṃ ghṛtavajjuhoteti tatkṛtvānyāṃ dugdhvā punarjuhuyāt
meaning: मित्रः कृष्टीरनिमिषाभिचष्टे सत्याय हव्यं घृतवज्जुहोतेति तत्कृत्वान्यां दुग्ध्वा पुनर्जुहुयात्
text_mt: Mitra looks upon the communities with unwinking eye; offer the oblation rich in clarified butter to Truth"—having performed that [rite] and milked another [cow], he should offer again.

sanskrit_iast: yadi pūrvasyāmāhutyāṃ hutāyāmuttarāhutiḥ skandedyadi vottarayā pūrvāmabhijuhuyādyatra vettha vanaspate devānāṃ guhyā nāmāni /
meaning: यदि पूर्वस्यामाहुत्यां हुतायामुत्तराहुतिः स्कन्देद्यदि वोत्तरया पूर्वामभिजुहुयाद्यत्र वेत्थ वनस्पते देवानां गुह्या नामानि /
text_mt: If, after the first offering is offered, the subsequent offering spills, or if he offers over the first with the subsequent one, with [the verse]: "Where thou knowest, O lord of the forest, the secret names of the gods,

sanskrit_iast: tatra havyāni gāmayoṃta vānaspatyayarcā samidhamādhāya tata eva tūṣṇīṃ hutvānyāṃ dugdhvā punarjuhuyāt
meaning: तत्र हव्यानि गामयोंत वानस्पत्ययर्चा समिधमाधाय तत एव तूष्णीं हुत्वान्यां दुग्ध्वा पुनर्जुहुयात्
text_mt: There send the oblations," with this verse addressed to the lord of the forest, having placed a piece of firewood [on the fire], having offered silently right from there, and having milked another [cow], he should offer again.

sanskrit_iast: yadi pūrvasyāmāhutyāṃ hutāyāmāhavanīyo 'nugacchedagnirdārau dārāvagniriti vadannanantare śakale hiraṇye vā juhuyāt
meaning: यदि पूर्वस्यामाहुत्यां हुतायामाहवनीयो ऽनुगच्छेदग्निर्दारौ दारावग्निरिति वदन्ननन्तरे शकले हिरण्ये वा जुहुयात्
text_mt: If, after the first offering has been offered, the āhavanīya goes out, he should offer upon an unbroken chip of wood or upon gold, reciting: "Agni is in the wood, in the wood is Agni."

sanskrit_iast: yadi purā prayājebhyo bahiḥparidhyaṅgāraḥ skandettaṃ sruvasya budhnenābhinidadhyānmā tamo mā yajñastamanmā yajamānasyamannamaste astvāyate namo rudra parāyate namo yatra niṣīdasi /
meaning: यदि पुरा प्रयाजेभ्यो बहिःपरिध्यङ्गारः स्कन्देत्तं स्रुवस्य बुध्नेनाभिनिदध्यान्मा तमो मा यज्ञस्तमन्मा यजमानस्यमन्नमस्ते अस्त्वायते नमो रुद्र परायते नमो यत्र निषीदसि /
text_mt: If before the preliminary offerings an ember falls outside the enclosing sticks, he should press it down with the bottom of the sruva, [saying]: "May darkness not [fall upon us], may the sacrifice not faint, may the sacrificer's food not fail; homage be to thee as thou comest, homage, O Rudra, as thou goest away, homage to where thou sittest!

sanskrit_iast: adhvaryuṃ mā hiṃsīryajamānaṃ mā hiṃsīriti yadi purastāt /
meaning: अध्वर्युं मा हिंसीर्यजमानं मा हिंसीरिति यदि पुरस्तात् /
text_mt: Do not harm the adhvaryu; do not harm the sacrificer!" if it is to the east.

sanskrit_iast: brahmāṇaṃ mā hiṃsīryajamānaṃ mā hiṃsīriti yadi dakṣiṇataḥ /
meaning: ब्रह्माणं मा हिंसीर्यजमानं मा हिंसीरिति यदि दक्षिणतः /
text_mt: "Do not harm the brahman; do not harm the sacrificer!" if it is to the south.

sanskrit_iast: hotāraṃ mā hiṃsīḥ patnīṃ mā hiṃsīryajamānaṃ mā hiṃsīriti yadi paścāt /
meaning: होतारं मा हिंसीः पत्नीं मा हिंसीर्यजमानं मा हिंसीरिति यदि पश्चात् /
text_mt: "Do not harm the hotṛ; do not harm the wife; do not harm the sacrificer!" if it is to the west.

sanskrit_iast: āgnīdhraṃ mā hiṃṣīḥ paśūnmā hiṃsīryajamānaṃ mā hiṃsīriti yadyuttarataḥ
meaning: आग्नीध्रं मा हिंषीः पशून्मा हिंसीर्यजमानं मा हिंसीरिति यद्युत्तरतः
text_mt: "Do not harm the agnīdh; do not harm the cattle; do not harm the sacrificer!" if it is to the north.

sanskrit_iast: āhaṃ yajñaṃ dadhe nirṛterupasthāttaṃ devebhyaḥ paridadāmītyenamādāya
meaning: आहं यज्ञं दधे निरृतेरुपस्थात्तं देवेभ्यः परिददामीत्येनमादाय
text_mt: Having taken it with [the verse]: "I take up the sacrifice from the lap of Nirṛti; I deliver it to the gods,"
With [the verse]: "The thousand-horned bull, Jātavedas, chant-backed, rich in clarified butter, fair-faced;

sanskrit_iast: mā no hāsīnmetthito nettvā jahāma gopoṣaṃ no vīrapoṣaṃ ca yacchetyenamagnau praharati
meaning: मा नो हासीन्मेत्थितो नेत्त्वा जहाम गोपोषं नो वीरपोषं च यच्छेत्येनमग्नौ प्रहरति
text_mt: May he not forsake us, nor may we, united, forsake thee; grant us abundance in cattle and abundance in men," he casts it into the fire.
Or, having cast it [into the fire], he may offer [an oblation] upon it.

sanskrit_iast: yadi kālasaṃnikarṣe 'gnirmathyamāno na jāyeta yatrānyaṃ paśyettata āhṛtya juhuyāt
meaning: यदि कालसंनिकर्षे ऽग्निर्मथ्यमानो न जायेत यत्रान्यं पश्येत्तत आहृत्य जुहुयात्
text_mt: If at the arrival of the time [of offering], fire being churned is not produced, he should bring [fire] from wherever he sees another and offer.
Then, not hurrying, he should churn again.

sanskrit_iast: yadyanyaṃ na vindedajāyai dakṣiṇe karṇe hotavyam
meaning: यद्यन्यं न विन्देदजायै दक्षिणे कर्णे होतव्यम्
text_mt: If he cannot find another [fire], the offering should be made in the right ear of a she-goat.
Thereafter, however, he should not eat [the meat] of a goat.

sanskrit_iast: yadyajāṃ na vindedbrāhmaṇasya dakṣiṇe haste hotavyam
meaning: यद्यजां न विन्देद्ब्राह्मणस्य दक्षिणे हस्ते होतव्यम्
text_mt: If he does not find a she-goat, the offering should be made in the right hand of a brāhmaṇa.
However, he should not deny shelter to a brāhmaṇa.
If he does not find a brāhmaṇa, the offering should be made on a clump of darbha grass.
However, he should not sit upon darbha grass.
If he does not find darbha grass, the offering should be made in water.

sanskrit_iast: āpastu na paricakṣītemā bhojanīyā imā abhojanīyā iti
meaning: आपस्तु न परिचक्षीतेमा भोजनीया इमा अभोजनीया इति
text_mt: However, he should not disparage waters, saying: "These are fit for consumption, these are unfit for consumption."
Even [from someone] whose [food] is unfit for consumption, he must accept waters throughout this year.
However, he should not wash his feet with water.
"These observances are for one year," says Āśmarathya;
"For life," says Ālekhana.
After a year, he should offer a sacrificial cake on eight potsherds to Agni Vratapati.

sanskrit_iast: agnaye kṣamavate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ yeṣāṃ pūrvāparā anvañcaḥ pramīyeran /
meaning: अग्नये क्षमवते ऽष्टाकपालं येषां पूर्वापरा अन्वञ्चः प्रमीयेरन् /
text_mt: To Agni Kṣāmavat [he offers] a cake on eight potsherds, if those related senior or junior to him should die in succession,

meaning: अग्नये विविचये ऽष्टाकपालं यस्याहिताग्नेरन्यैरग्निभिरग्नयः संसृजेरन्मिथो वा
text_mt: To Agni Vivici [he offers] a cake on eight potsherds, if the fires of an āhitāgni should become commingled with other fires, or with each other.
To Agni Vipṛc [he offers] a cake on eight potsherds, if the gārhapatya and the āhavanīya [become commingled].

sanskrit_iast: agninā vipṛcā vayaṃ gīrbhiḥ stomaṃ manāmahe /
meaning: अग्निना विपृचा वयं गीर्भिः स्तोमं मनामहे /
text_mt: "With Agni the separator, we think of a chant with hymns;
"Agni the sage is kindled, the wise accomplisher of the sacrifice;
Separating, grant us wealth"—these are the invitatory and consecratory verses.

sanskrit_iast: agnaye vītaye 'ṣṭākapālaṃ yadi gārhapatyadakṣiṇāgnī dakṣiṇāgnyāhavanīyau vā
meaning: अग्नये वीतये ऽष्टाकपालं यदि गार्हपत्यदक्षिणाग्नी दक्षिणाग्न्याहवनीयौ वा
text_mt: To Agni Vīti [he offers] a cake on eight potsherds, if the gārhapatya and the dakṣiṇāgni, or the dakṣiṇāgni and the āhavanīya [become commingled].

sanskrit_iast: agnaye śucaye 'ṣṭakapālaṃ yadi pradāvyenābhyādāhyena śavāgninā vā //
meaning: अग्नये शुचये ऽष्टकपालं यदि प्रदाव्येनाभ्यादाह्येन शवाग्निना वा //
text_mt: To Agni Śuci [he offers] a cake on eight potsherds, if [a fire becomes commingled] with a conflagration, with a cremation fire, or with a corpse fire.
To Agni Saṃkusuka [he offers] a cake on eight potsherds, if [it becomes commingled] with the fire of a lying-in room.
"Saṃkusuka, who scatters and who disperses;
With beans and clarified butter, with reed firewood, we appease the flesh-consuming fire.
In this Saṃkusuka fire we wipe away our impurities;

sanskrit_iast: abhūma yajñiyāḥ śuddhāḥ pra ṇa āyūṃṣi tāriṣāditi yājyānuvākye //
meaning: अभूम यज्ञियाः शुद्धाः प्र ण आयूंषि तारिषादिति याज्यानुवाक्ये //
text_mt: We have become worthy of sacrifice, purified; may he prolong our spans of life"—these are the invitatory and consecratory verses.
To Agni Apsumat [he offers] a cake on eight potsherds, if [it becomes commingled] with fire from lightning.

sanskrit_iast: yadi sarvāḥ saṃnipateranvivicaye nirupya śucaye nirvapedvrātabhṛtīṃ tṛtīyāmapsumatīṃ caturthīṃ kṣāmavatīmantaṃ parikramayet
meaning: यदि सर्वाः संनिपतेरन्विविचये निरुप्य शुचये निर्वपेद्व्रातभृतीं तृतीयामप्सुमतीं चतुर्थीं क्षामवतीमन्तं परिक्रमयेत्
text_mt: If all [types of fires] meet together, having offered to [Agni] Vivici, he should offer to [Agni] Śuci, the [offering] to [Agni] Vrātabhṛt as the third, the [offering] to [Agni] Apsumat as the fourth, and conclude with the [offering] to [Agni] Kṣāmavat.
Some hand down the offering to [Agni] Vrātabhṛt as the second,
"Agni, Indra, Tvaṣṭṛ, and Bṛhaspati have cured the leaking womb;

sanskrit_iast: pṛthivyāmavacuścotaitannābhiprāpnoti nirṛtiṃ parācairityagnihotrasthālīṃ sravantīmabhimantrya vidhuṃ dadrāṇamiti saṃdadhyāt
meaning: पृथिव्यामवचुश्चोतैतन्नाभिप्राप्नोति निरृतिं पराचैरित्यग्निहोत्रस्थालीं स्रवन्तीमभिमन्त्र्य विधुं दद्राणमिति संदध्यात्
text_mt: What has dripped upon the earth does not reach Nirṛti below"—addressing the leaking agnihotra pot with this verse, he should join [the crack] with [the formula]: "The moon wandering...."
It has been stated: "He who offers the New and Full Moon sacrifices should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Pathikṛt."
Or, [this offering] should be made as the principal rite within the same ritual procedure.

sanskrit_iast: vi vā etasya yajñaśchidyate yasya yajñe pratate 'ntaretāmiṣṭiṃ nirvapanti /
meaning: वि वा एतस्य यज्ञश्छिद्यते यस्य यज्ञे प्रतते ऽन्तरेतामिष्टिं निर्वपन्ति /
text_mt: "The sacrifice of him in whose extended sacrifice they offer this intermediate offering is indeed severed;

sanskrit_iast: ya evāsāvāgneyo 'ṣṭākapālaḥ paurṇamāsyāṃ yo 'māvāsyāyāṃ tamagnaye pathikṛte kuryāt /
meaning: य एवासावाग्नेयो ऽष्टाकपालः पौर्णमास्यां यो ऽमावास्यायां तमग्नये पथिकृते कुर्यात् /
text_mt: That cake on eight potsherds for Agni which belongs to the Full Moon, or that which belongs to the New Moon, he should make that one for Agni Pathikṛt;

sanskrit_iast: tenaiva punaḥ panthāmavaiti na yajñaṃ vicchinattīti vijñāyate
meaning: तेनैव पुनः पन्थामवैति न यज्ञं विच्छिनत्तीति विज्ञायते
text_mt: By that very means he finds the path again and does not sever the sacrifice"—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].
Another [view] is that the two saṃyājyā verses should be those addressed to Agni Pathikṛt.
It has been stated: "If the moon rises in the east over one whose oblation has been set apart..."
"If [the moon] rises when it has not yet been set apart, he should set apart [the oblations] for the regular deities," says Āśmarathya.
When they have become husked rice grains, he should lead [the calves] away.
'For the deities whose portions have become altered,' says Ālekhana.
If [the moon] rises when [the oblation] has been portioned out, the remainder is for the original [deities].
When they have become husked rice grains, he should lead [the calves] away.
If [the moon] should rise when his oblation has not yet been taken, or if he should intend the performance of the vow,
[he should divide] the rice grains into three parts, as before.
Then, having driven away the calves for the subsequent oblation, he should observe the fast.

sanskrit_iast: atha yasya gṛhītaṃ havirabhyudiyātsaiva prāyaścittiḥ sā vratacaryā
meaning: अथ यस्य गृहीतं हविरभ्युदियात्सैव प्रायश्चित्तिः सा व्रतचर्या
text_mt: Then, if [the moon] should rise when his oblation has been taken, that very expiation [applies], that [same] performance of the vow.

sanskrit_iast: vatsānmātṛbhiḥ saṃsṛjya punarapākṛtya pūrvedyurdugdhaṃ dadhi havirātañcanārthaṃ nidadhyāt
meaning: वत्सान्मातृभिः संसृज्य पुनरपाकृत्य पूर्वेद्युर्दुग्धं दधि हविरातञ्चनार्थं निदध्यात्
text_mt: Having united the calves with their mothers and driven them away again, he should set aside the curd milked on the previous day for the sake of curdling the oblation.

sanskrit_iast: agnaye vratapataye puroḍāśamaṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapedya āhitāgniḥ sannavratyamiva caretpravasedvā vratye 'hani māṃsaṃ vāśnāti striyaṃ vopaiti
meaning: अग्नये व्रतपतये पुरोडाशमष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद्य आहिताग्निः सन्नव्रत्यमिव चरेत्प्रवसेद्वा व्रत्ये ऽहनि मांसं वाश्नाति स्त्रियं वोपैति
text_mt: He should portion out an eight-pot-sherd cake to Agni Vratapati if he, being an āhitāgni, should act as if breaking a vow, or if he should go on a journey, or if on the day of a vow he eats meat or approaches a woman.
[He should portion out] an eight-pot-sherd cake to Agni Vratabhṛt if he should shed tears born of distress.
'You, O pure Agni, bearer of vows, seat the gods here,

sanskrit_iast: vratānubibhradvratapā adābhyo yajā no devām̐ ajaraḥ suvīraḥ /
meaning: व्रतानुबिभ्रद्व्रतपा अदाभ्यो यजा नो देवाम्̐ अजरः सुवीरः /
text_mt: 'Bearing the vows, protector of vows, undeceived, sacrifice to the gods for us, ageless, rich in heroic sons;

sanskrit_iast: dadhadratnāni suvidāno agne gopāya no jīvase jātaveda iti yājyānuvākye //
meaning: दधद्रत्नानि सुविदानो अग्ने गोपाय नो जीवसे जातवेद इति याज्यानुवाक्ये //
text_mt: bestowing treasures, well-knowing, O Agni Jātavedas, protect us so that we may live'—these are the invitatory and consecratory verses.
Some prescribe the [cake] to Vratabhṛt in case of a journey, and the [cake] to Vratapati in the act of shedding tears.

sanskrit_iast: yadyagnihotryupasṛṣṭā vāśyeta yasmādbhīṣāvāśiṣṭhāstato no abhayaṃ kṛdhi /
meaning: यद्यग्निहोत्र्युपसृष्टा वाश्येत यस्माद्भीषावाशिष्ठास्ततो नो अभयं कृधि /
text_mt: If the agnihotra-cow, having been brought near, should low: 'From whatever terror you have lowed, make fearlessness for us therefrom;

sanskrit_iast: abhayaṃ naḥ paśubhyo namo rudrāya mīḍhuṣa iti juhuyādabhi vā mantrayeta
meaning: अभयं नः पशुभ्यो नमो रुद्राय मीढुष इति जुहुयादभि वा मन्त्रयेत
