meaning: मा यः सोममिमं पिबात्संसृष्टमुभयं कृतमिति भक्षयति
text_mt: Let not him who drinks this soma, mixed and made into both [suffer]!”—with this [formula] he partakes.

sanskrit_iast: mā no dhvāriṣuḥ pitaro mota vīrā mā naḥ sabandhuruta vānyabandhuḥ /
meaning: मा नो ध्वारिषुः पितरो मोत वीरा मा नः सबन्धुरुत वान्यबन्धुः /
text_mt: “Let not the fathers injure us, nor the heroes, nor our kinsman, nor one who is no kin;

sanskrit_iast: mā no duścakṣā aghaśaṃsa īśatāhuto 'yaṃ yajñamapyetu devāniti bhakṣayantamabhimantrayate
meaning: मा नो दुश्चक्षा अघशंस ईशताहुतो ऽयं यज्ञमप्येतु देवानिति भक्षयन्तमभिमन्त्रयते
text_mt: Let not an evil-eyed speaker of wickedness have power! May this unoffered [soma] attain the sacrifice, the gods!”—with this [formula] he consecrates the one partaking.

sanskrit_iast: saptartvijaḥ sapta sadāṃsyeṣāṃ daśa kṣipo aśvinā pañca vājāḥ /
meaning: सप्तर्त्विजः सप्त सदांस्येषां दश क्षिपो अश्विना पञ्च वाजाः /
text_mt: “Seven are the priests, seven are their halls, ten the fingers, the two Aśvins, five the strengths;

sanskrit_iast: prāṇo vyāno 'pāno mana ākūtamagniḥ svāhākṛtaṃ haviradantu devā iti bhakṣaṃ vyāpannamabhimantryedaṃ viṣṇurvicakrama iti dakṣiṇapūrva uparave 'vanayet
meaning: प्राणो व्यानो ऽपानो मन आकूतमग्निः स्वाहाकृतं हविरदन्तु देवा इति भक्षं व्यापन्नमभिमन्त्र्येदं विष्णुर्विचक्रम इति दक्षिणपूर्व उपरवे ऽवनयेत्
text_mt: Prāṇa, vyāna, apāna, mind, intention, Agni: let the gods eat the oblation made with Svāhā!”—having addressed a spoiled portion for partaking with this [formula], he should pour it into the southeastern uparava with: “This Viṣṇu strode…”

sanskrit_iast: yaḥ somavāmī syāttasmā etaṃ somendraṃ śyāmākaṃ caruṃ nirvapet
meaning: यः सोमवामी स्यात्तस्मा एतं सोमेन्द्रं श्यामाकं चरुं निर्वपेत्
text_mt: For one who vomits soma, he should offer this śyāmāka caru to Somā-Indra.

sanskrit_iast: yadi sadohavirdhānāni kṛṣṇaśakuniruparyuparyatipatetpakṣābhyāmādhūnvāna ivābhiniṣīdedvedaṃ viṣṇurvicakrama ityāhutiṃ juhuyāt /
meaning: यदि सदोहविर्धानानि कृष्णशकुनिरुपर्युपर्यतिपतेत्पक्षाभ्यामाधून्वान इवाभिनिषीदेद्वेदं विष्णुर्विचक्रम इत्याहुतिं जुहुयात् /
text_mt: If a black bird should fly right over the sadas or the havirdhāna [sheds], or settle down as if flapping its wings, he should offer an oblation with: “This Viṣṇu strode…”
If it should fly high above, he should pay no regard to it.

sanskrit_iast: yadyano ratho vāntarāgnī sadohavirdhāne vā vīyātpāthikṛtīṃ pūrvavannirvapet
meaning: यद्यनो रथो वान्तराग्नी सदोहविर्धाने वा वीयात्पाथिकृतीं पूर्ववन्निर्वपेत्
text_mt: If a cart or a chariot should pass between the two fires, or between the sadas and the havirdhāna [sheds], he should offer the oblation to Pathikṛt as before.

sanskrit_iast: yadi havirdhānaṃ padyetodastāmpsītsavitā mitro aryamā sarvānamitrānavadhīdyugena /
meaning: यदि हविर्धानं पद्येतोदस्ताम्प्सीत्सविता मित्रो अर्यमा सर्वानमित्रानवधीद्युगेन /
text_mt: If the havirdhāna [shed] should collapse, with: “Savitṛ, Mitra, Aryaman have raised it up; he has slain all enemies with the yoke;

sanskrit_iast: bṛhantaṃ māmakaradvīravantaṃ rathaṃtare śrayasva svāhetyāhavanīye juhuyāt
meaning: बृहन्तं मामकरद्वीरवन्तं रथंतरे श्रयस्व स्वाहेत्याहवनीये जुहुयात्
text_mt: He has made me great, possessing heroes; rest in the Rathantara, svāhā!”—he should make an offering in the āhavanīya.

sanskrit_iast: etenaiva pṛthivyāṃ vāmadevye śrayasva svāheti hotrīye yadi sadaḥ
meaning: एतेनैव पृथिव्यां वामदेव्ये श्रयस्व स्वाहेति होत्रीये यदि सदः
text_mt: If [it is] the sadas, [he offers] in the hotṛ’s hearth with the very same [formula, substituting]: “Upon the earth, rest in the Vāmadevya, svāhā!”
If [it is] the āgnīdhra [shed], [he offers] in the āgnīdhra fire with: “In the atmosphere, rest in the Bṛhat, svāhā!”
If [it is] the prāgvaṃśa [hall], he should offer in the śālāmukhīya fire with all [the formulas].
The propping up of all [the sheds] is common [to each], with: “I prop you up in heaven with the Bṛhat!”

sanskrit_iast: yadyenamārtvijyādvṛtaṃ santaṃ narharerannāgnīdhre juhuyādanu mā sarvo yajño 'yametu viśve devā marutaḥ sāmārkaḥ /
meaning: यद्येनमार्त्विज्याद्वृतं सन्तं नर्हरेरन्नाग्नीध्रे जुहुयादनु मा सर्वो यज्ञो ऽयमेतु विश्वे देवा मरुतः सामार्कः /
text_mt: If they should not bring [food] to him when he has been chosen for the office of priest, he should offer in the āgnīdhra fire with: “May this entire sacrifice follow me, the All-gods, the Maruts, the Sāman, the Arka;
The Āprī verses, the metres, the nivids, the yajuses, whatever belongs to sacrifice on this earth!”
Having partaken of soma at another’s sacrifice, he should offer an oblation of ghee in the āhavanīya for the fires, around the partaking:

sanskrit_iast: apāṃ puṣpamasyoṣadhīnāṃ rasaḥ somasya priyaṃ dhāmāgneḥ priyatamaṃ haviḥ svāhā /
meaning: अपां पुष्पमस्योषधीनां रसः सोमस्य प्रियं धामाग्नेः प्रियतमं हविः स्वाहा /
text_mt: “You are the flower of the waters, the sap of the plants, the dear abode of Soma, the dearest oblation of Agni, svāhā!

sanskrit_iast: apāṃ puṣpamasyoṣadhīnāṃ rasaḥ somasya priyaṃ dhāmendrasya priyatamaṃ haviḥ svāhā /
meaning: अपां पुष्पमस्योषधीनां रसः सोमस्य प्रियं धामेन्द्रस्य प्रियतमं हविः स्वाहा /
text_mt: You are the flower of the waters, the sap of the plants, the dear abode of Soma, the dearest oblation of Indra, svāhā!

sanskrit_iast: apāṃ puṣpamasyoṣadhīnāṃ rasaḥ somasya priyaṃ dhāma viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ priyatamaṃ haviḥ svāheti
meaning: अपां पुष्पमस्योषधीनां रसः सोमस्य प्रियं धाम विश्वेषां देवानां प्रियतमं हविः स्वाहेति
text_mt: You are the flower of the waters, the sap of the plants, the dear abode of Soma, the dearest oblation of the All-gods, svāhā!”

sanskrit_iast: vayaṃ soma vrate tava manastanūṣu piprataḥ /
meaning: वयं सोम व्रते तव मनस्तनूषु पिप्रतः /
text_mt: “We, O Soma, in your observance, filling our minds in our bodies,

sanskrit_iast: prajāvanto aśīmahīti śeṣaṃ bhakṣayitvā devebhyaḥ pitṛbhyaḥ svāhā somyebhyaḥ pitṛbhyaḥ svāhā kavyebhyaḥ pitṛbhyaḥ svāheti dakṣiṇāgnau pratimantraṃ juhoti
meaning: प्रजावन्तो अशीमहीति शेषं भक्षयित्वा देवेभ्यः पितृभ्यः स्वाहा सोम्येभ्यः पितृभ्यः स्वाहा कव्येभ्यः पितृभ्यः स्वाहेति दक्षिणाग्नौ प्रतिमन्त्रं जुहोति
text_mt: May we attain [life] rich in offspring!”—having partaken of the remainder, he offers into the dakṣiṇāgni, verse by verse, with: “To the divine fathers, svāhā! To the soma-loving fathers, svāhā! To the kavya-eating fathers, svāhā!”

sanskrit_iast: taṃ jaghanena dakṣiṇāprāgagrāndarbhānsaṃstīrya dadhi dadāti devāsa iha mādayadhvaṃ somyāsa iha mādayadhvaṃ kavyāsa iha mādayadhvamiti
meaning: तं जघनेन दक्षिणाप्रागग्रान्दर्भान्संस्तीर्य दधि ददाति देवास इह मादयध्वं सोम्यास इह मादयध्वं कव्यास इह मादयध्वमिति
text_mt: Having strewn darbha grass behind it with its points to the south and east, he gives curds with: “O divine ones, exhilarate yourselves here! O soma-loving ones, exhilarate yourselves here! O kavya-eating ones, exhilarate yourselves here!”
He reverences [it] with: “The soma-loving fathers have not been excluded from drinking the soma!”

sanskrit_iast: bhaye jāte 'śakye yaṣṭuṃ sarvebhyo havirbhyaḥ somebhyaśca droṇakalaśe samavadhāya ye devā yeṣāmidaṃ bhāgadheyaṃ babhūva yeṣāṃ prayājā utānūyājāḥ /
meaning: भये जाते ऽशक्ये यष्टुं सर्वेभ्यो हविर्भ्यः सोमेभ्यश्च द्रोणकलशे समवधाय ये देवा येषामिदं भागधेयं बभूव येषां प्रयाजा उतानूयाजाः /
text_mt: If fear arises so that it is impossible to sacrifice, having placed [portions] from all the oblations and the somas together into the droṇakalaśa, with: “Which gods, whose share this has become, whose are the fore-offerings and the after-offerings,

sanskrit_iast: indrajyeṣṭhebhyo varuṇarājabhyo 'gnihotṛbhyo devebhyaḥ svāheti droṇakalaśena hutvābhaye punaryajeta
meaning: इन्द्रज्येष्ठेभ्यो वरुणराजभ्यो ऽग्निहोतृभ्यो देवेभ्यः स्वाहेति द्रोणकलशेन हुत्वाभये पुनर्यजेत
text_mt: To the gods whose chief is Indra, whose king is Varuṇa, who have Agni as hotṛ, svāhā!”—having offered with the droṇakalaśa, he should sacrifice again when fear has passed.
If a half-verse should be omitted, or if he should give a response over [another’s recitation], [he offers with]: “You, O Agni, [deliver us]…”;
“O Prajāpati…”—he should offer these four oblations,

sanskrit_iast: yadyṛkto yajñaṃ bhreṣa āgacchedbhūriti gārhapatye juhuyāt /
meaning: यद्यृक्तो यज्ञं भ्रेष आगच्छेद्भूरिति गार्हपत्ये जुहुयात् /
text_mt: If a fault should come to the sacrifice through an ṛc, he should offer in the gārhapatya with: “Bhūḥ!”
If through a yajus, in the dakṣiṇāgni with: “Bhuvaḥ!”
If through a sāman, in the āhavanīya with: “Suvaḥ!”
If through all of them, he should offer them all.
Or the brahman should sit, meditating in his mind.

sanskrit_iast: yadyaudumbarī naśyedanyāṃ pracchidyorgasyarjaṃ mayi dhehi śriyāṃ tiṣṭha pratiṣṭhitā /
meaning: यद्यौदुम्बरी नश्येदन्यां प्रच्छिद्योर्गस्यर्जं मयि धेहि श्रियां तिष्ठ प्रतिष्ठिता /
text_mt: If the post of udumbara wood should be ruined, having cut another, with: “You are vigor, place vigor in me; stand established in glory!

sanskrit_iast: divaṃ stabdhvāntarikṣaṃ ca pṛthivyāṃ ca dṛḍhā bhava /
meaning: दिवं स्तब्ध्वान्तरिक्षं च पृथिव्यां च दृढा भव /
text_mt: Having propped up the sky and the atmosphere, be firm on the earth!
Upholder, supporter, mother, restrainer!”—the adhvaryu, the udgātṛ, and the sacrificer erect it.
When it is measured, he touches it with the regular yajus formula.
If the two havirdhāna carts should fall down, the adhvaryu should lift up the southern one, and the pratiprasthātṛ should prop it up;
the pratiprasthātṛ should lift up the northern one, and the adhvaryu should prop it up.
They two prop them up with a verse to Viṣṇu.
With the three [verses beginning]: “O Agni, of strength rich in cows…”:

sanskrit_iast: bhadro no agnirāhuto bhadrā rātiḥ subhaga bhadro adhvaraḥ /
meaning: भद्रो नो अग्निराहुतो भद्रा रातिः सुभग भद्रो अध्वरः /
text_mt: “Auspicious for us is Agni when invoked, auspicious the gift, O fortunate one, auspicious the sacrifice,

sanskrit_iast: bhadrā uta praśastayo bhadraṃ manaḥ kṛṇuṣva vṛtratūrye /
meaning: भद्रा उत प्रशस्तयो भद्रं मनः कृणुष्व वृत्रतूर्ये /
text_mt: And auspicious the praises, make our mind auspicious in the slaying of Vṛtra,
With which you may conquer in battles, cast down the firm [defenses] of the many who are insolent;

sanskrit_iast: yenā samatsu sāsaho 'va sthirā tanuhi bhūri śardhatām /
meaning: येना समत्सु सासहो ऽव स्थिरा तनुहि भूरि शर्धताम् /

text_mt: May we win through your assistances!”—with these six uṣṇih-kakubh verses they two offer into the āgnīdhra fire.
The adhvaryu [offers] with the first uṣṇih verses.
The pratiprasthātṛ [offers] with the subsequent kakubh verses.
“May the head of the sacrifice be put back, immortal, consisting of the deities.

sanskrit_iast: vaiṣṇavyā kriyatāṃ śira āśvinyā pratidhīyatāmiti pañcagṛhītena samānau homau juhutaḥ
meaning: वैष्णव्या क्रियतां शिर आश्विन्या प्रतिधीयतामिति पञ्चगृहीतेन समानौ होमौ जुहुतः
text_mt: May the head be made with the [mantra] to Viṣṇu, may it be put back with the [mantra] to the Aśvins”—with [ghee] taken five times, both make identical offerings.
If the clay pan for the fire should break while raw, he should grind it together and make it anew.

sanskrit_iast: yadi pakvā saṃpiṣyānayayā mṛdā saṃsṛjyokhāṃ kārayet
meaning: यदि पक्वा संपिष्यानयया मृदा संसृज्योखां कारयेत्
text_mt: If baked, he should crush it, mix it with other clay, and have the pan made.
If the fire in the pan should go out for someone, he should carry another forth from the gārhapatya.
“He generates him from his own womb,” so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

sanskrit_iast: kṛṣṇaṃ vāsaḥ kṛṣṇā dhenuḥ kṛṣṇo vā gauḥ śatamānaṃ ca hiraṇyaṃ dakṣiṇā
meaning: कृष्णं वासः कृष्णा धेनुः कृष्णो वा गौः शतमानं च हिरण्यं दक्षिणा
text_mt: A black garment, a black milch-cow or a black bull, and a piece of gold of one hundred mānas are the sacrificial gift.
By that which is done on the previous day for the subsequent day, he connects the day.

sanskrit_iast: yatpūrvasminnahanyuttarasmā ahne vasatīvarīryajñāyajñiyaṃ prati gṛhṇāti tenāharabhyāsajati /
meaning: यत्पूर्वस्मिन्नहन्युत्तरस्मा अह्ने वसतीवरीर्यज्ञायज्ञियं प्रति गृह्णाति तेनाहरभ्यासजति /
text_mt: When on the previous day he receives the vasatīvarī waters for the subsequent day at the time of the Yajñāyajñīya [sāman], he connects the day thereby;
When on the previous day he orders the milks for the subsequent day, he connects the day thereby;
When he makes an anticipatory ritual call, he connects the day thereby;

sanskrit_iast: eteṣāmekasminnapyakriyamāṇe namo brahmaṇe namo astvagnaye namaḥ pṛthivyai nama oṣadhībhyaḥ /
meaning: एतेषामेकस्मिन्नप्यक्रियमाणे नमो ब्रह्मणे नमो अस्त्वग्नये नमः पृथिव्यै नम ओषधीभ्यः /
text_mt: If even one of these is not performed, having offered the oblation with: “Homage to the Brahman! Homage be to Agni! Homage to the earth! Homage to the plants!

sanskrit_iast: namo vāce namo vācaspataye namo viṣṇave bṛhate karomi svāhetyāhutiṃ hutvā sarvaprāyaścittaṃ juhuyājjuhuyāt
meaning: नमो वाचे नमो वाचस्पतये नमो विष्णवे बृहते करोमि स्वाहेत्याहुतिं हुत्वा सर्वप्रायश्चित्तं जुहुयाज्जुहुयात्
text_mt: Homage to Speech! Homage to the Lord of Speech! Homage to the great Viṣṇu I make, svāhā!”, he should offer the general expiation, he should offer [it].

sanskrit_iast: pravargyaṃ saṃbhariṣyannamāvāsyāyāṃ paurṇamāsyāmāpūryamāṇapakṣasya vā puṇye nakṣatre tūṣṇīṃ kāṇṭakīṃ samidhamādhāya yuñjate mana iti caturgṛhītaṃ juhoti
meaning: प्रवर्ग्यं संभरिष्यन्नमावास्यायां पौर्णमास्यामापूर्यमाणपक्षस्य वा पुण्ये नक्षत्रे तूष्णीं काण्टकीं समिधमाधाय युञ्जते मन इति चतुर्गृहीतं जुहोति
title: praśnaḥ 15
text_mt: Intending to gather the materials for the Pravargya, on the new moon day, the full moon day, or under an auspicious constellation of the waxing fortnight, having placed a thorny kindling stick silently, he offers four ladlings [of ghee] with: “They yoke their mind...”
Now, if he is consecrated, he should place just a thorny kindling stick with this [mantra].

sanskrit_iast: devasya tvā savituḥ prasava ityabhrimādāyābhrirasi nārirasītyabhimantrayate
meaning: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसव इत्यभ्रिमादायाभ्रिरसि नारिरसीत्यभिमन्त्रयते
text_mt: Having taken up the spade with: “At the impulse of the divine Savitṛ...”, he consecrates it with: “You are a spade, you are a woman.”
He addresses the brahman with: “Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati!”
Both murmur the subsequent half-verse.
They lead along a she-goat that has borne male young, and an uncastrated horse.

sanskrit_iast: praitu brahmaṇaspatiriti prāñco 'śvaprathamā abhipravrajanti yatra mṛdaṃ khaniṣyantaḥ syuḥ
meaning: प्रैतु ब्रह्मणस्पतिरिति प्राञ्चो ऽश्वप्रथमा अभिप्रव्रजन्ति यत्र मृदं खनिष्यन्तः स्युः
text_mt: With: “May Brahmaṇaspati go forth,” they proceed eastward, with the horse foremost, to where they will dig the clay.

meaning: अपि वास्यैते संभाराः परिश्रिते ऽभ्युदाहृता भवन्ति
text_mt: Or else, these materials of his have already been brought near within the enclosure.
In front of the āhavanīya is the clay pit;

sanskrit_iast: uttareṇa mṛtkhanaṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ prācīnagrīvamuttaralomāstīrya devī dyāvāpṛthivī iti mṛtkhanamabhimantrayate /
meaning: उत्तरेण मृत्खनं कृष्णाजिनं प्राचीनग्रीवमुत्तरलोमास्तीर्य देवी द्यावापृथिवी इति मृत्खनमभिमन्त्रयते /
text_mt: North of the clay pit, having spread out the black antelope skin with its neck to the east and its hairy side turned upward, he addresses the clay pit with: “O divine Heaven and Earth!”

sanskrit_iast: ṛdhyāsamadyeti mṛtkhane 'bhriyā prahṛtya makhasya śira ityapādāya makhāya tveti harati /
meaning: ऋध्यासमद्येति मृत्खने ऽभ्रिया प्रहृत्य मखस्य शिर इत्यपादाय मखाय त्वेति हरति /
text_mt: Having struck into the clay pit with the spade with: “May I prosper today,” [and] taking [clay] with: “The head of Makha,” he carries it with: “For Makha thee!”

sanskrit_iast: makhasya tvā śīrṣṇa iti kṛṣṇājine nivapati
meaning: मखस्य त्वा शीर्ष्ण इति कृष्णाजिने निवपति
text_mt: He pours it out onto the black antelope skin with: “For the head of Makha thee!”
In this manner he carries [clay] a second and a third time.

sanskrit_iast: tūṣṇīṃ caturthaṃ yāvatīṃ vṛdaṃ pravargyapātrebhya āptāṃ manyate
meaning: तूष्णीं चतुर्थं यावतीं वृदं प्रवर्ग्यपात्रेभ्य आप्तां मन्यते
text_mt: Silently a fourth time, as much clay as he deems sufficient for the Pravargya vessels.
[earth] torn up by a boar with: “So large wert thou formerly...”;
an ant-hill mound with: “O divine ants...”;

sanskrit_iast: indrasyaujo 'sīti pūtīkānajalomāni kṛṣṇājinalomāni ca saṃsṛjyāgnijā asi prajāpate reta iti
meaning: इन्द्रस्यौजो ऽसीति पूतीकानजलोमानि कृष्णाजिनलोमानि च संसृज्याग्निजा असि प्रजापते रेत इति
text_mt: with: “Thou art Indra's might,” pūtīka plants; and having mixed goat's hair and black antelope hairs, with: “Born of fire art thou, the seed of Prajāpati.”

sanskrit_iast: āyurdhehi prāṇaṃ dhehītyaśvenāvaghrāpya madhu tvā madhulā karotvityajayābhidohayati
meaning: आयुर्धेहि प्राणं धेहीत्यश्वेनावघ्राप्य मधु त्वा मधुला करोत्वित्यजयाभिदोहयति
text_mt: Having made the horse sniff it with: “Bestow life, bestow breath,” he causes it to be milked over by a she-goat with: “May the honey-sweet one make thee sweet.”
Some teach that the milking over precedes the sniffing.
Several Āryas take hold of it and carry it.

meaning: उत्तरेण विहारमुद्धते ऽवोक्षिते सिकतोपाप्ते परिश्रिते निदधति
text_mt: North of the sacrificial enclosure, on a raised, sprinkled, sand-covered, enclosed [ground], they set it down.
He pours on hot water with: “May the honey-sweet one make thee sweet.”

sanskrit_iast: ye cokhāsaṃsarjanāḥ saṃbhārā yaccānyaddṛḍhārtha upārdhaṃ manyate
meaning: ये चोखासंसर्जनाः संभारा यच्चान्यद्दृढार्थ उपार्धं मन्यते
text_mt: And whatever materials belong to the mixing of the pan, and whatever else he considers suitable for the purpose of strengthening.
Whatever action involving water is done in the Pravargya, that is done only with hot water.
Neither a woman nor a Śūdra looks upon it.
While making it, he does not breathe over it.
Turning his face away, not breathing over it, he fashions it with a bamboo [knife].
One should not pass between the Pravargya and the sun.

sanskrit_iast: yatra kvaca viprakrānte pravargya ādityo 'stamiyāt kṛtāntādeva viramet /
meaning: यत्र क्वच विप्रक्रान्ते प्रवर्ग्य आदित्यो ऽस्तमियात् कृतान्तादेव विरमेत् /
text_mt: Wherever the sun should set when the Pravargya has been commenced, he should stop right at a finished stage;
on the next day he should complete the remainder.

sanskrit_iast: saṃprakliśya mṛdaṃ makhasya śiro 'sīti piṇḍaṃ kṛtvā yajñasya pade stha ityaṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ nigṛhya mahāvīraṃ karoti tryuddhitaṃ pañcoddhimaparimitoddhiṃ vā prādeśamātramūrdhvasānumupariṣṭādāsecanavantaṃ madhye saṃnataṃ vāyavyaprakāram
meaning: संप्रक्लिश्य मृदं मखस्य शिरो ऽसीति पिण्डं कृत्वा यज्ञस्य पदे स्थ इत्यङ्गुष्ठाभ्यां निगृह्य महावीरं करोति त्र्युद्धितं पञ्चोद्धिमपरिमितोद्धिं वा प्रादेशमात्रमूर्ध्वसानुमुपरिष्टादासेचनवन्तं मध्ये संनतं वायव्यप्रकारम्
text_mt: Having thoroughly kneaded the clay, made a lump with: “Thou art the head of Makha,” and held it with both thumbs with: “Ye are in the step of the sacrifice,” he makes the Mahāvīra pot with three elevations, or with five elevations, or with an indefinite number of elevations, one span high, with a raised collar, having a pouring lip at the top, narrowed in the middle, in the shape of a Vāyu vessel.
[He fashions] the first [third] with: “I make thee with the gāyatrī metre”;
the second with: “...with the traiṣṭubha”;
With: "Thou art the collar of Makha," he makes the collar around the rim.

sanskrit_iast: aditiste bilaṃ gṛhṇātviti veṇuparvaṇā bilaṃ karoti
meaning: अदितिस्ते बिलं गृह्णात्विति वेणुपर्वणा बिलं करोति
text_mt: With: "May Aditi seize thy cavity," he makes the cavity by means of a bamboo joint.
He carries it beyond the third mark.
"As much as he thinks sufficient for the divinity, for the sviṣṭakṛt, for the agnihotra, and for the consuming"—this is another [view].

sanskrit_iast: sūryasya harasā śrāyetyuttarataḥ sikatāsu pratiṣṭhāpya makho 'sītyanuvīkṣate
meaning: सूर्यस्य हरसा श्रायेत्युत्तरतः सिकतासु प्रतिष्ठाप्य मखो ऽसीत्यनुवीक्षते
text_mt: Having placed it upon the sands to the north with: "Be cooked by the heat of the sun," he gazes after it with: "Thou art Makha."
Thus he makes the second and the third.

sanskrit_iast: etasyā eva mṛdo dogdhre karoti hastyoṣṭhye prasecanavatī yathā srugadaṇḍaivam
meaning: एतस्या एव मृदो दोग्ध्रे करोति हस्त्योष्ठ्ये प्रसेचनवती यथा स्रुगदण्डैवम्
text_mt: Out of this very clay he makes two milking vessels, with handles and lips, having spouts, like ladles without handles.
The one belonging to the adhvaryu is larger than the one belonging to the pratiprasthātṛ.
[He makes] the clarified butter-pot, and two circular potsherds for the rauhiṇa [cake] in the shape of a horse's hoof.
The gharma-brick and the kulāyinī [brick], if [the sacrifice] is accompanied by the piling of the fire-altar.
"They should not exist where there is no pravargya"—this is another [view].
They polish [them] with polishing materials,
with unwashed caṇḍātaka garments, with gavīdhukā grains, with klītaka roots, with bamboo joints, [and] with clarified butter.

sanskrit_iast: vṛṣṇo 'śvasya śakṛdgārhapatye pradīpya prathamakṛtaṃ mahāvīraṃ śaphābhyāṃ parigṛhya dhūpayati vṛṣṇo aśvasya niṣpadasīti
meaning: वृष्णो ऽश्वस्य शकृद्गार्हपत्ये प्रदीप्य प्रथमकृतं महावीरं शफाभ्यां परिगृह्य धूपयति वृष्णो अश्वस्य निष्पदसीति
text_mt: Having kindled the dung of a stallion in the gārhapatya fire, having seized the first-made mahāvīra with two tongs, he fumigates it with: "Thou art the stepping out of the stallion."
Thus he fumigates the second and the third.
From then on, he handles the mahāvīras only with the two tongs.

sanskrit_iast: agreṇa gārhapatyamavaṭaṃ khātvā lohitapacanīyaiḥ saṃbhārairavastīrya teṣu mahāvīrānupāvaharati
meaning: अग्रेण गार्हपत्यमवटं खात्वा लोहितपचनीयैः संभारैरवस्तीर्य तेषु महावीरानुपावहरति
text_mt: Having dug a pit in front of the gārhapatya, having strewn it with materials for baking red, he deposits the mahāvīras in them.
With: "Thou art the light; thou art the heat," the third.

sanskrit_iast: tūṣṇīmitarāṇyanvavadhāya lohitapacanīyaiḥ saṃbhāraiḥ pracchādya gārhapatye muñjānādīpyopoṣatyarciṣe tvetyetaiḥ pratimantraṃ pratidiśam
meaning: तूष्णीमितराण्यन्ववधाय लोहितपचनीयैः संभारैः प्रच्छाद्य गार्हपत्ये मुञ्जानादीप्योपोषत्यर्चिषे त्वेत्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रं प्रतिदिशम्
text_mt: Having deposited the other [vessels] silently, having covered [them] with the materials for baking red, having kindled muñja grass in the gārhapatya, he sets [them] on fire in each direction, formula by formula, with these [words]: "To the flame thee..."
Or on all sides with all [formulas].
While they are being baked, he attends upon them with the verse addressed to Mitra: "This one with greatness heaven..."

sanskrit_iast: pakveṣu siddhyai tveti dhṛṣṭī ādāya bhasmāpohya prathamakṛtaṃ mahāvīraṃ śaphābhyāṃ parigṛhyodvāsayati
meaning: पक्वेषु सिद्ध्यै त्वेति धृष्टी आदाय भस्मापोह्य प्रथमकृतं महावीरं शफाभ्यां परिगृह्योद्वासयति
text_mt: When they are baked, having taken two fire-shovels with: "To accomplishment thee," having brushed away the ashes, and having seized the first-made mahāvīra with the two tongs, he removes it.

sanskrit_iast: devastvā savitodvapatvityudvāsyāpadyamānaḥ pṛthivyāmāśā diśa āpṛṇetyuttarataḥ sikatāsu pratiṣṭhāpya sūryasya tvā cakṣuṣānvīkṣa ityanuvīkṣate
meaning: देवस्त्वा सवितोद्वपत्वित्युद्वास्यापद्यमानः पृथिव्यामाशा दिश आपृणेत्युत्तरतः सिकतासु प्रतिष्ठाप्य सूर्यस्य त्वा चक्षुषान्वीक्ष इत्यनुवीक्षते
text_mt: Having removed it with: "May god Savitṛ remove thee," having set it down upon the sands to the north with: "Falling down on the earth, fill the quarters and directions," he gazes after it with: "With the eye of the sun I gaze after thee."
Thus he removes the second and the third.

sanskrit_iast: athainānpradakṣiṇaṃ sikatābhiḥ paryūhatīdamahamamumāmuṣyāyaṇaṃ viśā paśubhirbrahmavarcasena paryūhāmīti /
meaning: अथैनान्प्रदक्षिणं सिकताभिः पर्यूहतीदमहममुमामुष्यायणं विशा पशुभिर्ब्रह्मवर्चसेन पर्यूहामीति /
text_mt: Then he heaps sands clockwise around them with: "Here I enclose NN, descendant of NN, with the people, with cattle, with spiritual lustre."
"With cattle," in the case of a vaiśya.
Then he drenches them with abundant goat's milk.
With: "With the gāyatrī meter I drench thee," [and so forth], each one with these three [formulas], three by three.
Then, having tied them up in a black antelope skin, he suspends them with: "O god, going in front, may I endure thee."
"This formula belongs to a later time"—this is another [view].
When about to perform the pravargya, they close the doors.
To the south the brahman, the sacrificer, and the prastotṛ.
To the north the pratiprasthātṛ and the agnīdhra.

sanskrit_iast: madantīrupaspṛśya prathamenānuvākena śāntiṃ kṛtvāgreṇa gārhapatyaṃ darbhānsaṃstīrya teṣu mahāvīrānupāvaharati deva puraścara saghyāsaṃ tveti
meaning: मदन्तीरुपस्पृश्य प्रथमेनानुवाकेन शान्तिं कृत्वाग्रेण गार्हपत्यं दर्भान्संस्तीर्य तेषु महावीरानुपावहरति देव पुरश्चर सघ्यासं त्वेति
text_mt: Having touched the madantī waters, having performed the appeasement rite with the first section, having strewn darbha grass in front of the gārhapatya, he deposits the mahāvīras on them with: "O god, going in front, may I endure thee."
"This formula belongs to a later time"—this is another [view].
Here itself are all the utensils belonging to the gharma.
The samrāj-chair, very low.
Some teach [it to be] taller than the king's chair.
Woven with single-strand cords of muñja grass.
Between the two with handles, the larger [is] the under-holding ladle for the sprinkling-water vessel.

sanskrit_iast: sruvau śaphau mahāvīrasaṃmitāvraskyau dhṛṣṭī methīṃ mayūkhānṣaṭ śakalānkāṇṭakīṃ ca samidhaṃ trayodaśa vaikaṅkatānparidhīnvaikaṅkatāni gharmendhanāni /
meaning: स्रुवौ शफौ महावीरसंमिताव्रस्क्यौ धृष्टी मेथीं मयूखान्षट् शकलान्काण्टकीं च समिधं त्रयोदश वैकङ्कतान्परिधीन्वैकङ्कतानि घर्मेन्धनानि /
text_mt: Two dipping spoons; two pairs of tongs; two cutting knives matching the mahāvīra pots; two fire-pokers; a peg; six pegs; splinters; a thorny fuel-stick; thirteen enclosing sticks of vikankata wood; [and] fuel-sticks of vikankata wood for the gharma.

sanskrit_iast: khādirāṇi pālāśānyaudumbarāṇyarkamayāṇi kārṣmaryamayāṇi vaiṇavāni śamīmayāni vā
meaning: खादिराणि पालाशान्यौदुम्बराण्यर्कमयाणि कार्ष्मर्यमयाणि वैणवानि शमीमयानि वा
text_mt: Or [they are] of khadira wood, of palāśa wood, of udumbara wood, of arka wood, of kākṣmarya wood, of bamboo, or of śamī wood.
Three fans made of black-antelope skin, with white and black hair.

sanskrit_iast: teṣāṃ vaiṇavā daṇḍā bāhumātrā bhavantīti vijñāyate
meaning: तेषां वैणवा दण्डा बाहुमात्रा भवन्तीति विज्ञायते
text_mt: Their handles are of bamboo, one cubit in length—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].
Having handles of udumbara wood, says another [view].
Two gold plates, [one of] silver and [one of] gold.
One of the two is trimmed around.
A halter; two hobble cords; three branching tethers; [and] abundant tufts of muñja grass.
Flour of unhusked [grains] for the two rauhiṇa cakes.
Having prepared the sprinkling waters according to the rite of sprinkling waters, he addresses the brahman:
"O brahman, we shall proceed with the Pravargya.
O hotṛ, praise the gharma.
O agnīdh, set the two rauhiṇa cakes on [the fire].
O pratiprasthātṛ, spread [the fires].
O prastotṛ, sing the sāmans."
Having murmured, "Yoked by the yajus, anointed with sāmans, the space [is made]," [the brahman] loudly authorizes with: "Om! Possessed of Indra, proceed!"

sanskrit_iast: yamāya tvā makhāya tveti sarvaṃ parigharmyamabhipūrvaṃ triḥ prokṣati
meaning: यमाय त्वा मखाय त्वेति सर्वं परिघर्म्यमभिपूर्वं त्रिः प्रोक्षति
text_mt: With: "For Yama, you! For Makha, you!" he sprinkles everything belonging to the gharma three times in succession.
He sets apart the sprinkled items.
The āgnīdhra puts the two rauhiṇa cakes on [the fire], served silently.
At this time the pratiprasthātṛ prepares the ghee according to the preparation of a ladle-offering.
There is no preparation for this, says another [view].
Here he puts the curd on [the fire].
Then, taking this sovereign-seat and carrying it along the front of the āhavanīya, he sets it down in front of the king's seat.

sanskrit_iast: tasyāṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ prācīnagrīvamuttaralomāstīrya tasminnapracaraṇīyau mahāvīrāvupāvaharati deva puraścara saghyāsaṃ tveti
meaning: तस्यां कृष्णाजिनं प्राचीनग्रीवमुत्तरलोमास्तीर्य तस्मिन्नप्रचरणीयौ महावीरावुपावहरति देव पुरश्चर सघ्यासं त्वेति
text_mt: Having spread a black-antelope skin upon it with the neck pointing east and the hair facing up, he brings down the two mahāvīra pots not used for the proceeding upon it with: "O god, going in front, may I be equal to you!"
This mantra is [used] at a later time, says another [view].

sanskrit_iast: athaitāṃ methīṃ mayūkhānviśākhadāmānītyādāyāgreṇa hotāraṃ jaghanena gārhapatyaṃ dakṣiṇayā dvāropanirhṛtya dakṣiṇena dakṣiṇaṃ dvāraṃ methīṃ nihanti hotuḥ samīkṣāyai
meaning: अथैतां मेथीं मयूखान्विशाखदामानीत्यादायाग्रेण होतारं जघनेन गार्हपत्यं दक्षिणया द्वारोपनिर्हृत्य दक्षिणेन दक्षिणं द्वारं मेथीं निहन्ति होतुः समीक्षायै
text_mt: Then, taking this peg, the pegs, and the branching tethers, having carried [them] out in front of the hotṛ, behind the gārhapatya, by the southern door, he drives in the peg south of the southern door for the hotṛ's view.

sanskrit_iast: etasyaiva dvārasya pūrvasyai dvāryāyai dakṣiṇato vatsāya śaṅkum
meaning: एतस्यैव द्वारस्य पूर्वस्यै द्वार्यायै दक्षिणतो वत्साय शङ्कुम्
text_mt: To the south of the eastern door-post of this very door, a peg for the calf.
To the south of the western door-post of this very [door], [a peg] on the inside for the goat.
He fastens the branching tethers to them.
They remain fastened until the final disposal.
With them they tie these [animals] at the proper time.
Then he scatters the mounds [of sand]:
One to the north of the gārhapatya;
One to the north of the āhavanīya.

sanskrit_iast: uttarapūrvaṃ dvāraṃ pratyucchiṣṭakharaṃ karoti bāhyato niḥṣecanavantam
meaning: उत्तरपूर्वं द्वारं प्रत्युच्छिष्टखरं करोति बाह्यतो निःषेचनवन्तम्
text_mt: Facing the north-eastern door, he makes the remnant-mound with an outlet on the outside.
To the north of the āhavanīya he places the heated curd,
The splinters, and the thorny fuel-stick.

sanskrit_iast: athaitaṃ pracaraṇīyaṃ mahāvīraṃ śaphābhyāṃ parigṛhyāpracchinnāgreṇa vedenopariṣṭātsaṃmārṣṭi deva puraścara saghyāsaṃ tveti
meaning: अथैतं प्रचरणीयं महावीरं शफाभ्यां परिगृह्याप्रच्छिन्नाग्रेण वेदेनोपरिष्टात्संमार्ष्टि देव पुरश्चर सघ्यासं त्वेति
text_mt: Then, grasping this mahāvīra [pot] to be used for the proceeding with the two pairs of tongs, he wipes it from above with the grass broom whose tips are uncut, with: "O god, going in front, may I be equal to you!"

sanskrit_iast: prāṇāya svāha vyānāya svāheti sruveṇāhavanīye saptaikādaśa vā prāṇāhutīrhutvā devastvā savitā madhvānaktviti sruveṇoparyāhavanīye mahāvīramaktvā pṛthivīṃ tapasastrāyasvetyaparasminkhare rājataṃ rukmaṃ nidhāya pratiṣṭhāpya mahāvīramanyasmai vā pradāya dvayānmuñjapralavānādāya dakṣiṇeṣāmagrāṇi gārhapatye pradīpayatyarciṣe tveti /
meaning: प्राणाय स्वाह व्यानाय स्वाहेति स्रुवेणाहवनीये सप्तैकादश वा प्राणाहुतीर्हुत्वा देवस्त्वा सविता मध्वानक्त्विति स्रुवेणोपर्याहवनीये महावीरमक्त्वा पृथिवीं तपसस्त्रायस्वेत्यपरस्मिन्खरे राजतं रुक्मं निधाय प्रतिष्ठाप्य महावीरमन्यस्मै वा प्रदाय द्वयान्मुञ्जप्रलवानादाय दक्षिणेषामग्राणि गार्हपत्ये प्रदीपयत्यर्चिषे त्वेति /
text_mt: Having offered seven or eleven life-breath offerings in the āhavanīya with the dipping spoon, with: "To the out-breath, svāhā! To the all-pervading breath, svāhā!" and having anointed the mahāvīra over the āhavanīya with the dipping spoon, with: "May god Savitṛ anoint you with honey!", having laid down the silver plate on the western mound with: "Protect the earth from heat!", having firmly set the mahāvīra [there] or handed [it] over to someone else, having taken two tufts of muñja grass, he sets alight the tips of the southern ones in the gārhapatya with: "To the flame, you!";
With their tips, the bases of the northern ones with: "To the blaze, you!";
With their bases, the bases of the southern ones with: "To the light, you!";
With their bases, the tips of the northern ones with: "To the heat, you!"

sanskrit_iast: tānvyatyastānupari rukme nidadhātyarcirasi śocirasi jyotirasi tapo 'sīti
meaning: तान्व्यत्यस्तानुपरि रुक्मे निदधात्यर्चिरसि शोचिरसि ज्योतिरसि तपो ऽसीति
text_mt: He places them crosswise upon the gold plate with: "Flame you are, blaze you are, light you are, heat you are!"

sanskrit_iast: saṃsīdasva mahām̐ asīti teṣu mahāvīraṃ pratiṣṭhāpyāñjanti yaṃ prathayanta iti sruveṇa mahāvīramanakti /
meaning: संसीदस्व महाम्̐ असीति तेषु महावीरं प्रतिष्ठाप्याञ्जन्ति यं प्रथयन्त इति स्रुवेण महावीरमनक्ति /
text_mt: Having firmly placed the mahāvīra pot upon them with: "Sit down, great are you!", he anoints the mahāvīra pot with the dipping spoon with: "They anoint [the steed], whom they spread out...";

sanskrit_iast: adhyadhi mahāvīramasaṃspṛśanyajamānaḥ prāñcaṃ prādeśaṃ dhārayamāṇo japatyanādhṛṣyā purastādityetairyathāliṅgam
meaning: अध्यधि महावीरमसंस्पृशन्यजमानः प्राञ्चं प्रादेशं धारयमाणो जपत्यनाधृष्या पुरस्तादित्येतैर्यथालिङ्गम्
text_mt: Above the mahāvīra, without touching it, holding his span pointing east, the sacrificer mutters according to their characteristic markers with these [formulas]: "Unassailable from the east...".
With: "You are Manu's mare, rich in offspring," he touches the earth to the north.

sanskrit_iast: siddhyai tveti dhṛṣṭī ādatto 'dhvaryuḥ pratiprasthātā ca
meaning: सिद्ध्यै त्वेति धृष्टी आदत्तो ऽध्वर्युः प्रतिप्रस्थाता च
text_mt: With: "For accomplishment, you!" the adhvaryu and the pratiprasthātṛ take up the two fire-pokers.

sanskrit_iast: tapo ṣvagne antarām̐ amitrāniti gārhapatyādudīco 'ṅgārānnirūhya citaḥ stha paricita iti pradakṣiṇamaṅgāraiḥ paryūhya
meaning: तपो ष्वग्ने अन्तराम्̐ अमित्रानिति गार्हपत्यादुदीचो ऽङ्गारान्निरूह्य चितः स्थ परिचित इति प्रदक्षिणमङ्गारैः पर्यूह्य
text_mt: Having scraped out embers from the gārhapatya towards the north with: "Burn down, O Agni, the enemies within!", having surrounded [the mahāvīra] with embers clockwise with: "Piled up are you, piled around [are you]!",
They enclose [it] with the enclosing sticks of vikankata wood.
The adhvaryu lays down two pointing east with: "Measure you are!"
The pratiprasthātṛ [sets down] two towards the north with: "Thou art the measure."
Thus, of the remaining [spoons], the adhvaryu [sets down each] with the preceding formula;
the pratiprasthātṛ with the following.
The adhvaryu alone puts down the thirteenth to the south with: "Thou art the concealment of the midspace."

sanskrit_iast: divaṃ tapasastrāyasveti sauvarṇena rukmeṇāpidhāyābhirgīrbhiriti tisṛbhirabhimantrya dhavitrāṇyādatte /
meaning: दिवं तपसस्त्रायस्वेति सौवर्णेन रुक्मेणापिधायाभिर्गीर्भिरिति तिसृभिरभिमन्त्र्य धवित्राण्यादत्ते /
text_mt: Having covered [the mahāvīra] with the golden plate with [the formula], "Protect the sky from heat," and having consecrated it with the three [verses], "With these songs...", he takes the fans.
[He takes] the first [fan] with, "You are of the gāyatrī."
The second with, "You are of the triṣṭubh."
With them he fans it upwards three times with, "Sweet, sweet!"
He hands one of them to the pratiprasthātṛ,
With the agnīdh first, fanning upwards, they go around clockwise three times.
Facing it, they sit around it:
the pratiprasthātṛ to the south,

sanskrit_iast: avyatiṣaṅgamūrdhvaṃ dhūnvantaḥ praṇavaiḥ saṃrādhayanta indhānāḥ samañjanto vāgyatā āsate
meaning: अव्यतिषङ्गमूर्ध्वं धून्वन्तः प्रणवैः संराधयन्त इन्धानाः समञ्जन्तो वाग्यता आसते
text_mt: Fanning upwards without intercrossing, propitiating with om-calls, kindling [the fire], anointing [it with clarified butter], they sit, restraining their speech.
It is known [from the Brāhmaṇa]: "When it is blazing up, he removes the plate."

sanskrit_iast: yatrābhijānāti yābhir vartikāṃ grasitām amuñcatam iti tad adhvaryur mahāvīram abhimantrayate daśa prācīr daśa bhāsi dakṣiṇety anuvākena
meaning: यत्राभिजानाति याभिर् वर्तिकां ग्रसिताम् अमुञ्चतम् इति तद् अध्वर्युर् महावीरम् अभिमन्त्रयते दश प्राचीर् दश भासि दक्षिणेत्य् अनुवाकेन
text_mt: When he recognises [the verse], "With which you released the swallowed quail...", then the adhvaryu consecrates the mahāvīra with the section, "Ten eastward, ten you shine to the south..."

sanskrit_iast: yatrābhijānāty apnasvatīm aśvinā vācam asme iti tad upottiṣṭhann adhvaryur āha rucito gharma iti
meaning: यत्राभिजानात्य् अप्नस्वतीम् अश्विना वाचम् अस्मे इति तद् उपोत्तिष्ठन्न् अध्वर्युर् आह रुचितो घर्म इति
text_mt: When he recognises [the verse], "Bestowing property, Aśvins, [may] speech [be] in us...", then rising up, the adhvaryu says: "The gharma has shone!"
With the adhvaryu first, not fanning it, they go around it three times in reverse.
Taking the fans, the adhvaryu gives them to the pratiprasthātṛ.
Bringing them around in front of the āhavanīya, the pratiprasthātṛ places them on the sovereign's throne.

sanskrit_iast: yathālokamavasthāya sarva ṛtvijo yajamānaścādhīyanto mahāvīramavekṣante 'paśyaṃ gopāmiti
meaning: यथालोकमवस्थाय सर्व ऋत्विजो यजमानश्चाधीयन्तो महावीरमवेक्षन्ते ऽपश्यं गोपामिति
text_mt: Standing in their respective places, all the officiating priests and the sacrificer, reciting, look at the mahāvīra with, "I saw the herdsman..."

sanskrit_iast: anuvākaśeṣaṃ tu pariśrite pratiprasthātā patnīṃ vācayati tvaṣṭīmatī te sapeyeti
meaning: अनुवाकशेषं तु परिश्रिते प्रतिप्रस्थाता पत्नीं वाचयति त्वष्टीमती ते सपेयेति
text_mt: With the remainder of the section, however, inside the enclosed space, the pratiprasthātṛ makes the wife recite, "Accompanied by Tvaṣṭṛ, may I serve you..."
Then he issues the call: "Agnīdh, set down the two rauhiṇa cakes!"
On two ladles that are not tied, he sets down the two cakes after spreading [clarified butter beneath] and pouring [clarified butter over them]:
one along the southern junction of the enclosing sticks,
the other along the northern junction of the enclosing sticks.

sanskrit_iast: sāvitreṇa raśanāmādāyādityai rāsnāsītyabhimantrya pūrvayā dvāropaniṣkramya trirupāṃśu gharmadughamāhvayatīḍa ehyadita ehi sarasvatyehīti
meaning: सावित्रेण रशनामादायादित्यै रास्नासीत्यभिमन्त्र्य पूर्वया द्वारोपनिष्क्रम्य त्रिरुपांशु घर्मदुघमाह्वयतीड एह्यदित एहि सरस्वत्येहीति
text_mt: Taking the cord with [the verse addressed] to Savitṛ, consecrating it with, "You are the girdle of Aditi," and stepping out by the eastern door, he calls the gharma-cow three times in a low voice: "Iḍā, come! Aditi, come! Sarasvatī, come!"

sanskrit_iast: pratyetya dogdhre nidāne ityādāya dakṣiṇayā dvāropaniṣkramya triruccairasāvehyasāvehīti yathānāmā bhavati
meaning: प्रत्येत्य दोग्ध्रे निदाने इत्यादाय दक्षिणया द्वारोपनिष्क्रम्य त्रिरुच्चैरसावेह्यसावेहीति यथानामा भवति
text_mt: Returning and taking the milking pail and the tether, and stepping out by the southern door, he calls three times aloud, "N.N., come! N.N., come!", using whatever name she has.
With the cord, he ties the gharma-cow with, "You are the turban of Aditi,"
and the calf with, "You are Vāyu, offspring of Iḍā."

sanskrit_iast: pūṣā tvopāvasṛjatvityupāvasṛjya yaste stanaḥ śaśaya iti gharmadughamabhimantrayate
meaning: पूषा त्वोपावसृजत्वित्युपावसृज्य यस्ते स्तनः शशय इति घर्मदुघमभिमन्त्रयते
text_mt: Having released [the calf] with, "May Pūṣan release you to [her]!", he addresses the gharma-cow with, "That teat of yours which is swelling..."

sanskrit_iast: usra gharmaṃ śiṃṣosra gharmaṃ pāhi gharmāya śiṃṣeti nidāya vatsaṃ bṛhaspatistvopasīdatvityupasīdati
meaning: उस्र घर्मं शिंषोस्र घर्मं पाहि घर्माय शिंषेति निदाय वत्सं बृहस्पतिस्त्वोपसीदत्वित्युपसीदति
text_mt: Tethering the calf with, "O bright cow, leave a remainder for the gharma; O bright cow, protect the gharma; leave a remainder for the gharma!", he sits down by her with, "May Bṛhaspati sit beside you!"

sanskrit_iast: dānavaḥ stha perava iti stanānasaṃmṛśyāśvibhyāṃ pinvasva sarasvatyai pinvasva pūṣṇe pinvasva bṛhaspataye pinvasvendrāya pinvasvendrāya pinvasveti varṣīyasi dogdhre dogdhi
meaning: दानवः स्थ पेरव इति स्तनानसंमृश्याश्विभ्यां पिन्वस्व सरस्वत्यै पिन्वस्व पूष्णे पिन्वस्व बृहस्पतये पिन्वस्वेन्द्राय पिन्वस्वेन्द्राय पिन्वस्वेति वर्षीयसि दोग्ध्रे दोग्धि
text_mt: Without rubbing the teats, with, "You are liberal, swelling," he milks into the larger milking pail with, "Swell for the two Aśvins! Swell for Sarasvatī! Swell for Pūṣan! Swell for Bṛhaspati! Swell for Indra! Swell for Indra!"
Silently the pratiprasthātṛ [milks] the goat into the smaller [milking vessel].

sanskrit_iast: yatrābhijānātyuttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspata iti tadupottiṣṭhantāvagnīdhe payasī pradāya pūrvāvatidutya śaphopayamānādadāte /
meaning: यत्राभिजानात्युत्तिष्ठ ब्रह्मणस्पत इति तदुपोत्तिष्ठन्तावग्नीधे पयसी प्रदाय पूर्वावतिदुत्य शफोपयमानाददाते /
text_mt: When he recognises [the verse], "Arise, Brahmaṇaspati!", then the two, rising up and handing the two milks to the agnīdh, having run past as before, take the tongs and the supportive ladle.
[The adhvaryu takes] the first [tong] with, "You are of the gāyatrī."
The second with, "You are of the triṣṭubh."
The pratiprasthātṛ [takes] the supportive ladle with, "You are of the jagatī."
When he recognises [the verse], "Run forward with the milk, cow-milker!", then the agnīdh enters.

sanskrit_iast: sahorjo bhāgenopa mehīti paya āhriyamāṇaṃ pratīkṣate
meaning: सहोर्जो भागेनोप मेहीति पय आह्रियमाणं प्रतीक्षते
text_mt: He looks at the milk as it is being brought with, "Come near to me with a share of vigor and strength!"

sanskrit_iast: indrāśvinā madhunaḥ sāraghasyeti mahāvīre gopaya ānayati
meaning: इन्द्राश्विना मधुनः सारघस्येति महावीरे गोपय आनयति
text_mt: With, "Indra and the two Aśvins, of the sweet bee-honey...", he pours the cow's milk into the mahāvīra.

sanskrit_iast: svāhā tvā sūryasya raśmaye vṛṣṭivanaye juhomītyudyantamūṣmāṇamanumantrayate
meaning: स्वाहा त्वा सूर्यस्य रश्मये वृष्टिवनये जुहोमीत्युद्यन्तमूष्माणमनुमन्त्रयते
text_mt: He addresses the rising vapor with, "Svāhā! I sacrifice you to the ray of the sun, the winner of rain!"
[He pours in] the goat's milk with, "You are the sweet oblation."
Some teach the pouring in of the goat's milk first.
[He addresses] the vapor with, "Burn with the heat of the sun!"

sanskrit_iast: dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ tvā parigṛhṇāmīti śaphābhyāṃ mahāvīraṃ parigṛhya pracchinnāgreṇa vedena bhasma pramṛjyāntarikṣeṇa tvopayacchāmītyupayamanena pratiprasthātopayacchati
meaning: द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां त्वा परिगृह्णामीति शफाभ्यां महावीरं परिगृह्य प्रच्छिन्नाग्रेण वेदेन भस्म प्रमृज्यान्तरिक्षेण त्वोपयच्छामीत्युपयमनेन प्रतिप्रस्थातोपयच्छति
text_mt: Grasping the mahāvīra with the two tongs with, "I grasp you with heaven and earth," and brushing off the ashes with the brush having trimmed ends, the pratiprasthātṛ supports it with the supportive ladle with, "I support you with the intermediate space."

sanskrit_iast: devānāṃ tvā pitṝṇāmanumato bhartuṃ śakeyamityādāyotthāya tejo 'si tejo 'nuprehīti harati
meaning: देवानां त्वा पितॄणामनुमतो भर्तुं शकेयमित्यादायोत्थाय तेजो ऽसि तेजो ऽनुप्रेहीति हरति
text_mt: Lifting it with, "Permitted by the gods and ancestors, may I be able to bear you," and having risen, he carries it with, "You are splendor; go along with splendor!"

sanskrit_iast: vrajannanavānaṃ pañca vātanāmāni vyācaṣṭe samudrāya tvā vātāya svāheti
meaning: व्रजन्ननवानं पञ्च वातनामानि व्याचष्टे समुद्राय त्वा वाताय स्वाहेति
text_mt: Walking without taking a breath, he pronounces the five names of the wind: "Svāhā to you, the ocean-wind!"
Having exhaled, [he pronounces] the five subsequent ones: "Svāhā to you, Agni accompanied by the Vasus!"

sanskrit_iast: etasminkāle pratiprasthātā dakṣiṇaṃ rauhiṇaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ juhotyaharjyotiḥ ketunā juṣatāṃ sujyotirjyotiṣāṃ svāheti
meaning: एतस्मिन्काले प्रतिप्रस्थाता दक्षिणं रौहिणं प्रतिष्ठितं जुहोत्यहर्ज्योतिः केतुना जुषतां सुज्योतिर्ज्योतिषां स्वाहेति
text_mt: At this time the pratiprasthātṛ offers the southern rauhiṇa [cake] while it rests [in the ladle], with, "May the day-light enjoy with its banner, well-light of lights, svāhā!"
Stepping across to the south behind the āhavanīya, he looks at the brahman with, "All the quarters, sitting to the south..."
He looks at the hotṛ with, "He has sacrificed to all the gods here."

sanskrit_iast: svāhākṛtasya gharmasyeti gharmamabhimantryāśrāvya pratyāśrāvite saṃpreṣyati gharmasya yajeti /
meaning: स्वाहाकृतस्य घर्मस्येति घर्ममभिमन्त्र्याश्राव्य प्रत्याश्राविते संप्रेष्यति घर्मस्य यजेति /
text_mt: Addressing the gharma with, "Of the gharma consecrated with svāhā...", calling for recitation and when the response has been made, he issues the call: "Recite the consecratory verse for the gharma!"
When the vaṣaṭ-call is uttered, he offers with, "Aśvins, drink the gharma!"
When the secondary vaṣaṭ-call is uttered, [he offers] with, "Svāhā! To Indra vaṭ!"
Having paid reverence with the remainder of the section, "You two drank the gharma, Aśvins...", while it is held above the āhavanīya, the pratiprasthātṛ fills it up with boiled curds.
He addresses it as it overflows with, "Swell for food, swell for strength!"

sanskrit_iast: athainaṃ diśo 'nu prahāvayati tviṣyai tvā dyumnāya tvendriyāya tvā bhūtyai tveti
meaning: अथैनं दिशो ऽनु प्रहावयति त्विष्यै त्वा द्युम्नाय त्वेन्द्रियाय त्वा भूत्यै त्वेति
text_mt: Then he makes it move along toward the directions with, "For splendor to you, for glory to you, for vigor to you, for prosperity to you!"

sanskrit_iast: pratyākramyopayamane śeṣamānīyāntarvedyupayamanaṃ nidhāya pūrvasminkhare rājataṃ rukmaṃ nidhāya tasminmahāvīraṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati dharmāsi sudharmāmenyasme brahmāṇi dhārayeti /
meaning: प्रत्याक्रम्योपयमने शेषमानीयान्तर्वेद्युपयमनं निधाय पूर्वस्मिन्खरे राजतं रुक्मं निधाय तस्मिन्महावीरं प्रतिष्ठापयति धर्मासि सुधर्मामेन्यस्मे ब्रह्माणि धारयेति /
text_mt: Having stepped back and poured the remainder into the supportive ladle, having set down the supportive ladle inside the altar ground, and having placed the silver plate on the eastern mound, he sets down the mahāvīra firmly on it with, "You are order, possessing good order; hold firmly in us priestly powers!"
"Hold firmly royal powers!" for a nobleman.
"Hold firmly the common people!" for a vaiśya.
with: 'Lest the wind spill thee.'
If he would practice sorcery, he should set it down with: 'I set thee down upon the breath of so-and-so.'
Thereupon the pratiprasthātṛ offers the second rauhiṇa [cake] as before.

meaning: अथैताञ्छकलानुपयमने ऽञ्जञ्जुहोति पूष्णे शरसे स्वाहेत्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रम्
text_mt: Then, anointing these chips on the upayamana, he offers them, each with its respective mantra, with: 'To Pūṣan of the cream, svāhā!'

sanskrit_iast: ṣaṣṭhaṃ śakalaṃ sarveṣu lepeṣvaktvānanvīkṣamāṇa udañcaṃ nirasyati rudrāya rudrahotre svāheti
meaning: षष्ठं शकलं सर्वेषु लेपेष्वक्त्वानन्वीक्षमाण उदञ्चं निरस्यति रुद्राय रुद्रहोत्रे स्वाहेति
text_mt: Having anointed the sixth chip in all the remainders, not looking back, he casts it to the north with: 'To Rudra, the Rudra-hotṛ, svāhā!'
Some teach [the offering of] the chips before the rauhiṇa offering.

sanskrit_iast: athāpa upaspṛśya tūṣṇīṃ kāṇṭakīṃ samidhamādhāyaitasmādeva śeṣādupayamanenāgnihotraṃ juhoti bhūḥ svāheti /
meaning: अथाप उपस्पृश्य तूष्णीं काण्टकीं समिधमाधायैतस्मादेव शेषादुपयमनेनाग्निहोत्रं जुहोति भूः स्वाहेति /
text_mt: Then, having touched water and silently put on a thorny kindling-stick, he offers the agnihotra with the upayamana from this very remainder with: 'Bhūḥ svāhā!'
Having brought together the remainder on the upayamana, they all partake of it.
He addresses each with their liturgical title: 'So-and-so, do thou invite!'
The reply is: 'Invited!'
The hotṛ, the adhvaryu, the brahman, the pratiprasthātṛ, the agnīdh, and the sacrificer.
Or rather, only the sacrificer [partakes] visibly,

sanskrit_iast: hutaṃ havirmadhu haviriti bhakṣayitvopayamanaṃ pratiprasthātre prayacchati
meaning: हुतं हविर्मधु हविरिति भक्षयित्वोपयमनं प्रतिप्रस्थात्रे प्रयच्छति
text_mt: Having partaken with: 'The oblation is offered, the oblation is honey,' he hands over the upayamana to the pratiprasthātṛ.

sanskrit_iast: taducchiṣṭakhare prakṣālyāntarvedyupayamanaṃ nidhāya tasminrukmāvavadhāya madnatīrānīyāpohiṣṭhīyābhirmārjayitvā ninīyāpo 'traiva sarvaṃ parigharmyaṃ samavadhāya
meaning: तदुच्छिष्टखरे प्रक्षाल्यान्तर्वेद्युपयमनं निधाय तस्मिन्रुक्माववधाय मद्नतीरानीयापोहिष्ठीयाभिर्मार्जयित्वा निनीयापो ऽत्रैव सर्वं परिघर्म्यं समवधाय
text_mt: Having washed it on the mound for remnants, placed the upayamana inside the altar ground, put the two gold plates upon it, poured boiling water over it, wiped [the utensils] with the Apo-hiṣṭhā verses, poured out the water, and put together all the accessories of the pravargya right there,
he issues the ritual call: 'Recite for the gharma being set down!'
or: 'Recite for the one being set down!'

sanskrit_iast: ā yasminsapta vāsavā ityabhijñāyāgreṇāhavanīyaṃ paryāhṛtya samrāḍāsandyāṃ sādayati svāhā tvā sūryasya raśmibhya iti prātaḥ /
meaning: आ यस्मिन्सप्त वासवा इत्यभिज्ञायाग्रेणाहवनीयं पर्याहृत्य सम्राडासन्द्यां सादयति स्वाहा त्वा सूर्यस्य रश्मिभ्य इति प्रातः /
text_mt: Having recognized [the beginning of the verse]: 'In whom the seven Vasus...', he carries it around to the east of the āhavanīya and sets it down on the sovereign's throne with: 'Svāhā to thee, to the rays of the sun!' in the morning,
with: 'Svāhā to thee, to the constellations!' in the evening.

sanskrit_iast: yatrābhijānātyaddhi tṛṇamaghnye viśvadānīmiti tadgāmavasṛjya madantīrupaspṛśyottamenānuvākena śāntiṃ kurvanti
meaning: यत्राभिजानात्यद्धि तृणमघ्न्ये विश्वदानीमिति तद्गामवसृज्य मदन्तीरुपस्पृश्योत्तमेनानुवाकेन शान्तिं कुर्वन्ति
text_mt: When he recognizes [the words]: 'Eat the grass, O unslayable cow, at all times,' having let the cow loose at that point and touched boiling water, they perform the expiation with the last anuvāka.
Thus they perform the Pravargya and the Upasad in the evening and in the morning.
At a rite with three Upasads, six times;
at one with six Upasads, twelve times;
at one with twelve Upasads, twenty-four times.
In the evening he offers the rauhiṇa [cake] with the subsequent mantra.
'Thou hast brought me across the day; protect me from the night.
This is thy kindling-stick, O Agni; blaze up therewith.

sanskrit_iast: āyurme dā varcasā māñjīriti sāyaṃ samidhamādadhāti /
meaning: आयुर्मे दा वर्चसा माञ्जीरिति सायं समिधमादधाति /
text_mt: Grant me life; anoint me with splendour!'—with this he puts on a kindling-stick in the evening.

sanskrit_iast: apīparo mā rātriyā ahno mā pāhīti prātaḥ
meaning: अपीपरो मा रात्रिया अह्नो मा पाहीति प्रातः
text_mt: 'Thou hast brought me across the night; protect me from the day'—in the morning.
He offers the agnihotra in the evening with: 'Agni is light, light is Agni, svāhā!'
In the morning with: 'Sūrya is light, light is Sūrya, svāhā!'
He performs the Pravargya at a Viśvajit with all the Pṛṣṭhas.
Having performed the Pravargya with it, he should not eat meat for a year;
a Śūdra should not drink his leftover.
'It is fiery splendour indeed that he thereby whets'—so it is known.
About to conclude the Pravargya, he gives a she-goat to the agnīdh,

sanskrit_iast: aparaṃ kharaṃ pūrvasminkhare nyupyocchiṣṭakharaṃ saṃkṛṣyottareṇāhavanīyaṃ samrāḍāsandīṃ pratiṣṭhāpya tasyāṃ sarvaṃ parigharmyaṃ samavadhāyaudumbaryāṃ sruci caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā gharma yā te divi śugityetairyathāliṅgaṃ juhoti
meaning: अपरं खरं पूर्वस्मिन्खरे न्युप्योच्छिष्टखरं संकृष्योत्तरेणाहवनीयं सम्राडासन्दीं प्रतिष्ठाप्य तस्यां सर्वं परिघर्म्यं समवधायौदुम्बर्यां स्रुचि चतुर्गृहीतं गृहीत्वा घर्म या ते दिवि शुगित्येतैर्यथालिङ्गं जुहोति
text_mt: Having poured the western mound onto the eastern mound, scraped up the mound for remnants, set up the sovereign's throne to the north of the āhavanīya, placed all the accessories of the pravargya upon it, and taken four ladlings of clarified butter in the spoon of udumbara wood, he offers them according to their characteristics with: 'O Gharma, whatever heat of thine is in heaven...'

sanskrit_iast: api vā pratiprasthātā trīnsaṃnakhāñchalākāmuṣṭīnādāya teṣāmekamāhavanīye pradīpyāsyadaghne dhārayati /
meaning: अपि वा प्रतिप्रस्थाता त्रीन्संनखाञ्छलाकामुष्टीनादाय तेषामेकमाहवनीये प्रदीप्यास्यदघ्ने धारयति /
text_mt: Or rather, the pratiprasthātṛ, having taken three fistfuls of splints trimmed even to the nails and ignited one of them in the āhavanīya, holds it at mouth-level.

sanskrit_iast: tamadhvaryurabhijuhoti gharma yā te divi śugiti /
meaning: तमध्वर्युरभिजुहोति घर्म या ते दिवि शुगिति /
text_mt: Over it the adhvaryu makes an offering with: 'O Gharma, whatever heat of thine is in heaven...'

sanskrit_iast: tasminnaparaṃ pradīpyāhavanīye pūrvaṃ prahṛtya nābhidaghne dhārayati /
meaning: तस्मिन्नपरं प्रदीप्याहवनीये पूर्वं प्रहृत्य नाभिदघ्ने धारयति /
text_mt: Having ignited another upon it and cast the first into the āhavanīya, he holds it at navel-level.

meaning: तमध्वर्युरभिजुहोति घर्म या ते ऽन्तरिक्षे शुगिति /
text_mt: Over it the adhvaryu makes an offering with: 'O Gharma, whatever heat of thine is in the intermediate space...'

sanskrit_iast: tasminnaparaṃ pradīpyāhavanīye pūrvaṃ prahṛtya jānudaghne dhārayati /
meaning: तस्मिन्नपरं प्रदीप्याहवनीये पूर्वं प्रहृत्य जानुदघ्ने धारयति /
text_mt: Having ignited another upon it and cast the first into the āhavanīya, he holds it at knee-level.

sanskrit_iast: tamadhvaryurabhijuhoti gharma yā te pṛthivyāṃ śugiti
meaning: तमध्वर्युरभिजुहोति घर्म या ते पृथिव्यां शुगिति
text_mt: Over it the adhvaryu makes an offering with: 'O Gharma, whatever heat of thine is on earth...'
He throws it along into the āhavanīya itself.

meaning: अनु नो ऽद्यानुमतिरिति परिश्रिते प्रतिप्रस्थाता पत्नीमुदानयति
text_mt: With: 'May Anumati [approve] us today,' the pratiprasthātṛ leads the wife out into the enclosed space.
They step out after with: 'Followed by Anumati...'
They carry after [them]: the post, the shovel, the pegs, the branching pegs, the cords, and the two mounds.
He carries the mound for remnants around to the south.

sanskrit_iast: samrāḍāsandyā dvāvantarvedi pādau dvau bahirvedi pratiṣṭhāpya saṃpreṣyati prastotaḥ sāma gāyeti
meaning: सम्राडासन्द्या द्वावन्तर्वेदि पादौ द्वौ बहिर्वेदि प्रतिष्ठाप्य संप्रेष्यति प्रस्तोतः साम गायेति
text_mt: Having set up two feet of the sovereign's throne inside the altar ground and two outside the altar ground, he issues the ritual call: 'O prastotṛ, sing the saman!'
All, together with the wife [of the sacrificer], join in the finale of the sāman three times.
Having arrived to the west of the high altar, a third time.
With "From the sky, as far-protector..." they step forward at the first [call];
with "From the sacred word, as far-protector..." at the second;
with "From the breath, as far-protector..." at the third.

sanskrit_iast: uttareṇottaravediṃ samrāḍāsandīṃ pratiṣṭhāpya saṃpreṣyati prastotarvārṣāharaṃ sāma gāyeṣṭāhotrīyaṃ sāma gāyeti /
meaning: उत्तरेणोत्तरवेदिं सम्राडासन्दीं प्रतिष्ठाप्य संप्रेष्यति प्रस्तोतर्वार्षाहरं साम गायेष्टाहोत्रीयं साम गायेति /
text_mt: Having set down the emperor-stool north of the high altar, he gives the call: "Prastotṛ, sing the Vārṣāhara sāman; sing the Iṣṭāhotrīya sāman!"
They join in the finale of the Iṣṭāhotrīya sāman;
If he sprinkles water afterwards, then he should enjoin the Vārṣāhara.

sanskrit_iast: udakumbhamādāyādhvaryurvalgurasi śaṃyudhāyā iti triḥ pradakṣiṇamuttaravediṃ pariṣiñcanparyeti /
meaning: उदकुम्भमादायाध्वर्युर्वल्गुरसि शंयुधाया इति त्रिः प्रदक्षिणमुत्तरवेदिं परिषिञ्चन्पर्येति /
text_mt: Taking a water jar, the adhvaryu circumambulates the high altar sunwise three times, sprinkling [water] with "Pleasing art thou, for well-being..."

sanskrit_iast: nidhāya kumbhaṃ śaṃ ca vakṣi pari ca vakṣīti trirapariṣiñcanpratiparyeti
meaning: निधाय कुम्भं शं च वक्षि परि च वक्षीति त्रिरपरिषिञ्चन्प्रतिपर्येति
text_mt: Having set down the jar, he circumambulates [it] counter-sunwise three times without sprinkling, with "Mayest thou bring well-being, mayest thou carry [it] all around..."
Having touched the high altar with "Four-cornered is the navel of the cosmic order...", he scatters and spreads two mounds north of the high navel with "A seat of all life..."

sanskrit_iast: apa dveṣo apa hṛra iti mārjālīyadeś ucchiṣṭakharam
meaning: अप द्वेषो अप हृर इति मार्जालीयदेश् उच्छिष्टखरम्
text_mt: With "Away hatred, away crookedness!" [he scatters] the mound for the remnants in the place of the mārjālīya.

sanskrit_iast: uttareṇottaranābhiṃ khare hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya tasmin pracaraṇīyaṃ mahāvīramupāvaharati
meaning: उत्तरेणोत्तरनाभिं खरे हिरण्यं निधाय तस्मिन् प्रचरणीयं महावीरमुपावहरति
text_mt: Having placed gold upon the mound north of the high navel, he brings down upon it the Mahāvīra used in the rite.
Right here [he places] the other two, east and west, or south and north.

sanskrit_iast: atraiva sarvaṃ parigharmyaṃ sarvataḥ parimaṇḍalamādityasya rūpaṃ karoti
meaning: अत्रैव सर्वं परिघर्म्यं सर्वतः परिमण्डलमादित्यस्य रूपं करोति
text_mt: Right here he forms everything belonging to the cauldron circular on all sides, as the form of the sun.

meaning: महीनां पयो ऽसीति महावीरे गोपय आनयति /
text_mt: With "Thou art the milk of the great ones," he pours cow's milk into the Mahāvīra;

sanskrit_iast: jyotirbhā asi vanaspatīnāmoṣadhīnāṃ rasa iti madhu /
meaning: ज्योतिर्भा असि वनस्पतीनामोषधीनां रस इति मधु /
text_mt: with "Thou art the light, thou art the sap of trees and plants," honey;

meaning: वाजिनं त्वा वाजिनो ऽवनयाम इति दधि
text_mt: with "Speedy one, we pour thee down, who art vigorous," curds.
In this way he fills the second and the third [vessels].
Or he should pour clarified butter into the first;

sanskrit_iast: gharmaitatte 'nnametatpurīṣamiti dadhnā madhumiśreṇa pātrāṇi pūrayati yānyāsecanavanti /
meaning: घर्मैतत्ते ऽन्नमेतत्पुरीषमिति दध्ना मधुमिश्रेण पात्राणि पूरयति यान्यासेचनवन्ति /
text_mt: With "O cauldron, this is thy food, this thy rubble," he fills with curds mixed with honey whichever vessels are meant to receive poured liquid;
"For non-emptiness," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].
Now if he should intend to make [it] in the shape of a man, the procedure is the same up to bringing down the first [Mahāvīra].
Having brought down the other two right here, he forms the shape of the head.
He places a veda with unbroken ends on top, as the form of the topknot;
on both sides, the two milking-pails as the form of the ears;
on both sides, two gold pieces, or the two butter spoons, as the form of the eyes;
on both sides, the two sruva spoons as the form of the nostrils;
the vessel for sprinkling water as the form of the mouth;
the pot for clarified butter as the form of the neck;
on both sides, the two tongs as the form of the collarbones;
on both sides, the two pincers as the form of the shoulders;
on both sides, the two Rauhiṇa offering ladles as the form of the arms;
pointing east, the peg as the form of the spine;
on both sides, the two fanning-fans as the form of the ribs;
in the middle, the third [fan] as the form of the chest;
in the middle, the support shovel as the form of the belly;
into it he places all the cord material, as the form of the entrails;
pointing north, the wooden shovel as the form of the hips;
on both sides, the two pegs as the form of the thighs;
in the middle, a third [peg] as the form of the penis;
on both sides, the two potsherds for the Rauhiṇa cakes as the form of the heels;
with the remainder of the Rauhiṇa flour he scatters [it], as the form of the marrow;
having untied the veda, he strews it along, as the form of the sinews;
he covers [it] with avakā plants and scented grass, as the form of the flesh;
he sprinkles [it] with curds mixed with honey, as the form of the blood;
he covers [it] with a black antelope skin with the hair turned upward, as the form of the skin and hair;
having dismantled the emperor-stool, he places it on top, as the form of sovereignty.
He should dispose of [the Pravargya equipment] on the high altar for one who desires splendor;
on the high altar for one who desires proper nourishment.
Or he should dispose of it in front, or behind;
If he disposes of it on an island in a river, he should not sprinkle [water] all around.

sanskrit_iast: yaṃ dviṣyādyatra sa syāttasyāṃ diśyaudumbaryāṃ śākhāyāmudvāsayet /
meaning: यं द्विष्याद्यत्र स स्यात्तस्यां दिश्यौदुम्बर्यां शाखायामुद्वासयेत् /
text_mt: Whomever he hates, in whichever direction he may be, in that direction he should set it out upon an udumbara branch.
The udumbara is indeed sap, food is breath, [and] the gharma is pain.
With the formula, 'Here do I close up the breath of so-and-so, descendant of so-and-so, with pain,' he closes up his breath with pain.
'Instantly he meets with ruin,' so it is taught.
Where darbha grass is swarming with termites, there he should set it out for one desiring rain.
They declare the constant rule [to be] on the uttaravedī.
Birds should not alight around it once it is set out until the carrying forward of the fire.
Here some prescribe pouring water around [it].
Then they revere it with, 'Ranti by name are you, the heavenly Gandharva...'

sanskrit_iast: etattvaṃ deva gharma devo devānupāgā ityabhimantryedamahaṃ namuṣyo manuṣyāniti pradakṣiṇamāvṛtya sumitrā na āpa oṣadhaya iti mārjālīyadeśa ucchiṣṭakhare mārjayitvodvayaṃ tamasasparītyādityamupasthāyodu tyaṃ citramiti dvābhyāṃ gārhapatye juhoti /
meaning: एतत्त्वं देव घर्म देवो देवानुपागा इत्यभिमन्त्र्येदमहं नमुष्यो मनुष्यानिति प्रदक्षिणमावृत्य सुमित्रा न आप ओषधय इति मार्जालीयदेश उच्छिष्टखरे मार्जयित्वोद्वयं तमसस्परीत्यादित्यमुपस्थायोदु त्यं चित्रमिति द्वाभ्यां गार्हपत्ये जुहोति /
text_mt: Having addressed it with, 'Thus, O divine gharma, a god, have you approached the gods,' [and then saying,] 'Here do I, a man, [approach] men,' having turned clockwise, having cleansed themselves with 'Friendly to us be waters and plants' in the place of the mārjālīya on the refuse-mound, having revered the sun with 'Looking upon the higher light beyond darkness,' he offers into the gārhapatya with the two [verses], 'Up that All-knower...' and 'The brilliant front of the gods...'
He offers into the āhavanīya with, 'This very [drink] for us...'
If the gharma spills, he should address it with the two [verses], 'The earth has leaped...'

sanskrit_iast: yadi ghrameṇa caratsu vidyudāpatedyā purastādvidyudāpatadityetairyathāliṅgaṃ juhuyāt
meaning: यदि घ्रमेण चरत्सु विद्युदापतेद्या पुरस्ताद्विद्युदापतदित्येतैर्यथालिङ्गं जुहुयात्
text_mt: If lightning strikes while they are proceeding with the gharma, he should make an offering with these verses according to their characteristic marks: 'The lightning which struck from the east...'
If from all sides, he should offer all [of them].
The two sections, 'To Prāṇa svāhā, to Pūṣan svāhā,' are the expiations for the gharma.
He places the gharma-brick with the section, 'Its light did not perish from its heat...'

sanskrit_iast: kulāyinīṃ yāste agna ārdrā yonaya ityanuvākena /
meaning: कुलायिनीं यास्ते अग्न आर्द्रा योनय इत्यनुवाकेन /
text_mt: [He places] the nest-like [brick] with the section, 'Those moist wombs of yours, O Agni...'
The adhvaryu touches the fire with the iḍā-piling with the section, 'You are Agni, you are Vaiśvānara...'
'Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar' are the universal expiations.

sanskrit_iast: yadi mahāvīraḥ padyetordhva ū ṣu ṇa ūtaya iti dvābhyāmenamucchrayīta
meaning: यदि महावीरः पद्येतोर्ध्व ऊ षु ण ऊतय इति द्वाभ्यामेनमुच्छ्रयीत
text_mt: If the mahāvīra falls over, he should set it upright with the two verses, 'Upright for our aid...'
If it breaks, he should join it together with 'The solitary runner...'

sanskrit_iast: tato yāni dṛḍhārthe saṃśleṣaṇāni syustairenamabhidihyādyadanyanmāṃsānmāṣebhyaśca yadṛte cidabhiśriṣa iti
meaning: ततो यानि दृढार्थे संश्लेषणानि स्युस्तैरेनमभिदिह्याद्यदन्यन्मांसान्माषेभ्यश्च यदृते चिदभिश्रिष इति
text_mt: Then, whatever binding substances there may be for making it firm, with those he should smear it over, other than meat and māṣa beans, with 'Even without bindings...'

sanskrit_iast: yadi ghramamatiparīyurna vā pratiparīyuḥ punarūrjā saha rayyetyetābhyāmenaṃ pratiparīyuḥ
meaning: यदि घ्रममतिपरीयुर्न वा प्रतिपरीयुः पुनरूर्जा सह रय्येत्येताभ्यामेनं प्रतिपरीयुः
text_mt: If they bypass the gharma or do not walk around it in return, they should walk back around it with these two verses, 'Again with sap, together with wealth...'

sanskrit_iast: mā no gharma vyathita ityaṣṭau gharme vyathite prāyaścittāni
meaning: मा नो घर्म व्यथित इत्यष्टौ घर्मे व्यथिते प्रायश्चित्तानि
text_mt: The eight [formulas], 'May the gharma not be troubled for us,' are the expiations when the gharma is troubled.
Or he should address the troubled gharma itself with four of these [verses].

sanskrit_iast: yadi gharmeṇa caratsvādityo 'stamiyādaparasyāṃ dvāri darbheṇa hiraṇyaṃ prabadhyodvayaṃ tamasasparītyupasthāyodu tyaṃ citramiti dvābhyāṃ gārhapatye hutvā pravṛjya śvobhūte vayaḥ suparṇā ityādityamupatiṣṭhante
meaning: यदि घर्मेण चरत्स्वादित्यो ऽस्तमियादपरस्यां द्वारि दर्भेण हिरण्यं प्रबध्योद्वयं तमसस्परीत्युपस्थायोदु त्यं चित्रमिति द्वाभ्यां गार्हपत्ये हुत्वा प्रवृज्य श्वोभूते वयः सुपर्णा इत्यादित्यमुपतिष्ठन्ते
text_mt: If the sun sets while they are proceeding with the gharma, having tied gold at the western door with a blade of darbha grass, having revered [the sun] with 'Looking upon the higher light beyond darkness,' having offered into the gārhapatya with the two verses, 'Up that All-knower...' and 'The brilliant front of the gods...', having performed the heating, on the next day they revere the sun with 'The fair-winged birds...'

sanskrit_iast: yadi gharmadhugdohakāle nāgacchedanyāṃ dugdhvā pravṛjya tāṃ sutyāyāṃ brāhmaṇāya dadyādyamanabhyāgamiṣyansyāt
meaning: यदि घर्मधुग्दोहकाले नागच्छेदन्यां दुग्ध्वा प्रवृज्य तां सुत्यायां ब्राह्मणाय दद्याद्यमनभ्यागमिष्यन्स्यात्
text_mt: If the gharma-milch-cow does not come at the time of milking, having milked another and having performed the heating, he should give her on the soma-pressing day to a brahmin whom he will not visit again.

sanskrit_iast: yadi gharmadhugi payo na syāddṛteścaturthaṃ pādaṃ stanaṃ kṛtvā pinvayet
meaning: यदि घर्मधुगि पयो न स्याद्दृतेश्चतुर्थं पादं स्तनं कृत्वा पिन्वयेत्
text_mt: If there is no milk in the gharma-milch-cow, having made the fourth foot of a leather bag into a teat, he should make it flow.
If she yields curds, he should recite [a verse] to Bṛhaspati.
If milk, [a verse] to the Aśvins with a conclusion.

sanskrit_iast: yadyu vai lohitaṃ duhīta raudryarcā juhuyāt
meaning: यद्यु वै लोहितं दुहीत रौद्र्यर्चा जुहुयात्
text_mt: And if she yields blood, he should offer with a verse to Rudra.
If she is lost, he should offer with two verses to Dhātṛ.
If her calf [is lost], he should offer with a verse to Vāyu with team.
If she sits down upon something unholy or unfit for sacrifice, he should offer with a verse to Agni.
If a bird flies against her, he should offer with a verse to the Aśvins.

sanskrit_iast: yadyudvā patetsaṃ vā vijeta śārdūlo vā hanyādarkakṣīramajākṣīra āścotya tena precaret
meaning: यद्युद्वा पतेत्सं वा विजेत शार्दूलो वा हन्यादर्कक्षीरमजाक्षीर आश्चोत्य तेन प्रेचरेत्
text_mt: If she bolts, or trembles, or a tiger strikes her down, having dripped calotropis milk into goat's milk, he should proceed with that.
Some prescribe the heating [of the gharma] on the soma-pressing day.
When it becomes reddish in the east, then it is to be heated;

sanskrit_iast: upakāśa upavyuṣaṃ samayāviṣita uditānudita udite vā /
meaning: उपकाश उपव्युषं समयाविषित उदितानुदित उदिते वा /
text_mt: at dawn, at daybreak, when the sun is half-risen, when it has risen or not risen;

sanskrit_iast: prātaḥ saṃgave mādhyaṃdine vā pavamāne stute
meaning: प्रातः संगवे माध्यंदिने वा पवमाने स्तुते
text_mt: in the morning at grazing time, or at midday when the pavamāna chant has been sung.
It is to be heated in the house of the agnīdh.
'It is to be heated only once,' so it is taught.
These options are to be alternated with the heatings belonging to the upasads.
They partake of the curd-gharma with the section, 'Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar.'

meaning: व्याख्याता घोरास्तन्वो ऽरण्येऽनुवाक्यो गण उत्तरौ चानुवाकौ
text_mt: The terrifying bodies, the group to be recited in the forest, and the two subsequent sections have been explained.

sanskrit_iast: yadi gharmeṇa caratsvekasṛka uttiṣṭhedvi gā indra vicaranspāśayasvetyetamabhimantryobhayata ādīpyolmukamasmai pratyasyedagne agninā saṃvadasveti
meaning: यदि घर्मेण चरत्स्वेकसृक उत्तिष्ठेद्वि गा इन्द्र विचरन्स्पाशयस्वेत्येतमभिमन्त्र्योभयत आदीप्योल्मुकमस्मै प्रत्यस्येदग्ने अग्निना संवदस्वेति
text_mt: If a jackal rises while they are proceeding with the gharma, having addressed it with 'O Indra, roaming about, discover the cows,' having ignited a firebrand at both ends, he should throw it towards it with, 'O Agni, speak with Agni.'
Then they revere it with the remainder of the section, 'Once, O Agni, homage to you...'

sanskrit_iast: atha yadi gṛdhraḥ salāvṛkī bhayeḍako dīrghamukhyulūko bhūtopasṛṣṭaḥ śakunirvā vadedasṛṅmukhaḥ /
meaning: अथ यदि गृध्रः सलावृकी भयेडको दीर्घमुख्युलूको भूतोपसृष्टः शकुनिर्वा वदेदसृङ्मुखः /
text_mt: Now if a vulture, a she-jackal, an omen-ram, a long-snouted animal, an owl, an animal possessed by an evil spirit, or a bird with a bloody mouth should cry out,
'What is this, having entered beings...',
[and] 'Spreading both thighs...', having addressed it with these according to the characteristic marks, the throwing of the firebrand and the subsequent rites are the same.

sanskrit_iast: yadi gharmadhukkrimiṇā syādatriṇā tvā krime hanmītyanuvākenāsyāḥ krimīnhanyāt
meaning: यदि घर्मधुक्क्रिमिणा स्यादत्रिणा त्वा क्रिमे हन्मीत्यनुवाकेनास्याः क्रिमीन्हन्यात्
text_mt: If the gharma-milch-cow has worms, he should kill her worms with the section, 'With Atri I slay you, O worm.'
Or this expiation may be performed on all occasions.
If he practices sorcery against someone, he should make a portion out of his blood and offer it with the section: 'Bring out [the portion] cut off from the cooked [offering]...'

sanskrit_iast: yamabhivyāhariṣyansyāttrirātrāvaraṃ brahmacaryaṃ caritvā gatvainamabhivyāharedbrahmaṇā tvā śapāmītyanuvākena
meaning: यमभिव्याहरिष्यन्स्यात्त्रिरात्रावरं ब्रह्मचर्यं चरित्वा गत्वैनमभिव्याहरेद्ब्रह्मणा त्वा शपामीत्यनुवाकेन
text_mt: If he intends to curse someone, he should observe celibacy for at least three nights, go up to him, and curse him with the section: 'By the brahman I curse you...'

sanskrit_iast: yaṃ dviṣyāttasy goṣṭhe svajamoṣadhīṃ nikhaneduttuda śimijāvarītyanuvākena
meaning: यं द्विष्यात्तस्य् गोष्ठे स्वजमोषधीं निखनेदुत्तुद शिमिजावरीत्यनुवाकेन
text_mt: Against whom he feels hatred, he should bury a svajā-snake [or plant] in his cattle-pen with the section: 'Stir up, O Śimijāvarī...'

sanskrit_iast: api vā goṣṭhasyaiva dakṣiṇāṃ dvārbāhumetenaiva vicālayet
meaning: अपि वा गोष्ठस्यैव दक्षिणां द्वार्बाहुमेतेनैव विचालयेत्
text_mt: Or he may simply displace the right doorpost of his cattle-pen with this very [section].

sanskrit_iast: yadyudgātā puruṣasāma na gāyedadhvaryurevaitena sāmnodgāyedbhurbhuvaḥ suvarityanuvākena
meaning: यद्युद्गाता पुरुषसाम न गायेदध्वर्युरेवैतेन साम्नोद्गायेद्भुर्भुवः सुवरित्यनुवाकेन
text_mt: If the udgātṛ does not sing the Puruṣasāman, the adhvaryu himself should sing with that sāman by means of the section: 'Bhūḥ bhuvaḥ suvaḥ...'
Now we shall explain the intermediate initiation (avāntaradīkṣā).

sanskrit_iast: parvaṇyudagayana āpūryamāṇapakṣasya vā puṇye nakṣatre keśaśmaśru vāpayitvāparāhṇe prācīmudīcīṃ vā diśamupaniṣkramya khile 'cchadirdarśe 'gnimupasamādhāya saṃparistīrya pūrvavadupākṛtya madantīrupaspṛśya prathamenānuvākena śāntiṃ kṛtvā catasra audumbarīḥ samidho ghṛtānvaktā abhyādadhāti pṛthivī samidityetairmantraiḥ
meaning: पर्वण्युदगयन आपूर्यमाणपक्षस्य वा पुण्ये नक्षत्रे केशश्मश्रु वापयित्वापराह्णे प्राचीमुदीचीं वा दिशमुपनिष्क्रम्य खिले ऽच्छदिर्दर्शे ऽग्निमुपसमाधाय संपरिस्तीर्य पूर्ववदुपाकृत्य मदन्तीरुपस्पृश्य प्रथमेनानुवाकेन शान्तिं कृत्वा चतस्र औदुम्बरीः समिधो घृतान्वक्ता अभ्यादधाति पृथिवी समिदित्येतैर्मन्त्रैः
text_mt: On a junction-day during the northern course of the sun, or during the waxing fortnight under an auspicious lunar mansion, having had his hair and beard shaved, having gone out in the afternoon toward the east or north, having set up the fire in an uncultivated plot where roofs are out of sight, having strewn around it, having brought [the ritual] into commencement as before, having touched hot water, and having performed the pacification rite with the first section, he puts on four firesticks of udumbara wood smeared with ghee with the mantras: 'Earth is the firestick...'

sanskrit_iast: atha devatā upatiṣṭhate 'gne vratapate vrataṃ cariṣyāmīti
meaning: अथ देवता उपतिष्ठते ऽग्ने व्रतपते व्रतं चरिष्यामीति
text_mt: Then he attends upon the deities with: 'O Agni, lord of vows, I will observe the vow...'
Then he makes him recite the beginnings of all the sections;

sanskrit_iast: uttamenānuvākena śāntiṃ kṛtvā tataḥ saṃmīlayati vācaṃ ca yacchati
meaning: उत्तमेनानुवाकेन शान्तिं कृत्वा ततः संमीलयति वाचं च यच्छति
text_mt: Having performed the pacification rite with the last section, he closes his eyes and restrains his speech.

sanskrit_iast: athāsyāhatena vāsasā pradakṣiṇaṃ saṃmukhaṃ śiro veṣṭayitvāstamite grāmaṃ prapādayati
meaning: अथास्याहतेन वाससा प्रदक्षिणं संमुखं शिरो वेष्टयित्वास्तमिते ग्रामं प्रपादयति
text_mt: Then, having wrapped his head around from left to right in front with an unwashed cloth, he brings him into the village after sunset.
With restrained speech, he stands or sits through this night.

meaning: श्वोभूते खिले ऽच्छदिर्दर्शे ऽग्निमुपसमाधाय संपरिस्तीर्याथास्य षट्तयमभिविदर्शयति /
text_mt: On the next day, having set up the fire in an uncultivated plot where roofs are out of sight and having strewn around it, he causes him to look upon a group of six objects;
fire, the sun, a water-pot, a stone, a calf, and a naked woman;
Or, having shown the first three, [he shows] the others as they happen to be available.

sanskrit_iast: atraitadvāso gurave dattvā vayaḥ suparṇā ityādityamupatiṣṭhate
meaning: अत्रैतद्वासो गुरवे दत्त्वा वयः सुपर्णा इत्यादित्यमुपतिष्ठते
text_mt: At this point, having given this garment to his teacher, he attends upon the sun with: 'The winged birds...'
Now, with respect to his celibacy, [these rules are] permanent:
If he does eat, [it should be] while a fire is blazing.
He should not drink directly from an earthen vessel.
He should not converse with a woman or with a śūdra.
He should fast on eighth days and junction-days, with restrained speech.
He should observe this vow for a year;
he should study only during this year.
If he does not study within this year, he should observe this vow as long as the study lasts.

sanskrit_iast: saṃvatsare paryavete khile 'cchadirdarśe 'gnimupasamādhāya saṃparistīrya pūrvavadvisṛjya madantīrupaspṛśya prathamenānuvākena śāntiṃ kṛtvāvṛttairmantraiḥ samidha ādhāyāvṛttairdevatā upasthāyottamenānuvākena śāntiṃ kṛtvā gurave varaṃ dattvā keśaśmaśru vāpayate
meaning: संवत्सरे पर्यवेते खिले ऽच्छदिर्दर्शे ऽग्निमुपसमाधाय संपरिस्तीर्य पूर्ववद्विसृज्य मदन्तीरुपस्पृश्य प्रथमेनानुवाकेन शान्तिं कृत्वावृत्तैर्मन्त्रैः समिध आधायावृत्तैर्देवता उपस्थायोत्तमेनानुवाकेन शान्तिं कृत्वा गुरवे वरं दत्त्वा केशश्मश्रु वापयते
text_mt: When the year has elapsed, having set up the fire in an uncultivated plot where roofs are out of sight, having strewn around it, having released [the vow] as before, having touched hot water, having performed the pacification rite with the first section, having placed the firesticks with the mantras repeated, having attended upon the deities with [the mantras] repeated, having performed the pacification rite with the last section, and having given a choice gift to the teacher, he has his hair and beard shaved.
Now, with respect to his private recitation (svādhyāya), [these rules are] permanent:
He should not study if the study period has not been opened.

sanskrit_iast: nātidoṣamabrahmacaryamāpadya na māṃsaṃ khāditvā na keśaśmaśrulomanakhāni vāpayitvā na keśānprasādhya na dataḥ prāksālya
meaning: नातिदोषमब्रह्मचर्यमापद्य न मांसं खादित्वा न केशश्मश्रुलोमनखानि वापयित्वा न केशान्प्रसाध्य न दतः प्राक्साल्य
text_mt: not having transgressed celibacy too late [into the morning], not after eating meat, not after having hair, beard, body-hair, or nails shaved, not after combing his hair, not without having cleaned his teeth;

sanskrit_iast: nākto nābhyakto nārdro nārdre nānavavṛṣṭe nābhre na chāyāyāṃ na paryāvṛtta āditye na haritayavānprekṣamāṇo na grāmyasya paśorante nāraṇyasya nāpāmante
meaning: नाक्तो नाभ्यक्तो नार्द्रो नार्द्रे नानववृष्टे नाभ्रे न छायायां न पर्यावृत्त आदित्ये न हरितयवान्प्रेक्षमाणो न ग्राम्यस्य पशोरन्ते नारण्यस्य नापामन्ते
text_mt: not anointed, not smeared, not wet, not in wet clothes, not when it has not rained [during clear sky?], not under clouds, not in shade, not after the sun has turned, not looking at green barley, not near a domestic animal, not near a wild animal, not near water;
not after seeing something uncooked that has burst open, nor after seeing blood;

sanskrit_iast: na harmyāṇi na śarīrāṇi na śavaṃ nāpapātram
meaning: न हर्म्याणि न शरीराणि न शवं नापपात्रम्
text_mt: not [near] mansions, nor [unburied] bodies, nor a corpse, nor an outcaste.

sanskrit_iast: adhyeṣyamāṇaḥ prācīmudīcīṃ vā diśamupaniṣkramya khile 'cchadirdarśe 'gnimupasamādhāya saṃparistīrya madantīrupaspṛśya prathamenānuvākena śāntiṃ kṛtvāpareṇāgniṃ darbheṣvāsīno darbhāndūrvā vā dhārayamāṇaḥ parācīnamadhīyīta
meaning: अध्येष्यमाणः प्राचीमुदीचीं वा दिशमुपनिष्क्रम्य खिले ऽच्छदिर्दर्शे ऽग्निमुपसमाधाय संपरिस्तीर्य मदन्तीरुपस्पृश्य प्रथमेनानुवाकेन शान्तिं कृत्वापरेणाग्निं दर्भेष्वासीनो दर्भान्दूर्वा वा धारयमाणः पराचीनमधीयीत
text_mt: When about to study, having gone out toward the east or north, having set up the fire in an uncultivated plot where roofs are out of sight, having strewn around it, having touched hot water, having performed the pacification rite with the first section, seated to the west of the fire upon darbha grass, holding darbha grass or dūrvā grass, he should study the subsequent text.
When about to study, he should not utter other words.
Wherever he sees something unpacified, he should study only after performing the pacification rite again.
Having gone out for the Pravargya, he should not study anything else without having returned [to the village]; he should not study anything else.

meaning: अग्निं चेष्यमाणो ऽमावास्यायां पौर्णमास्यामेकाष्टकायां वोखां संभरति
title: praśnaḥ 16
text_mt: Intending to pile the fire altar, he procures the materials for the boiler-pan (ukhā) on a new moon day, on a full moon day, or on the Ekāṣṭakā.
Some teach [this] with reference to the aṣāḍhā brick.

sanskrit_iast: bṛhaspatipurohitā devā devānāṃ devā devāḥ prathamajā devā deveṣu parākramadhvaṃ prathamā dvitīyeṣu dvitīyāstṛtīyeṣu trirekādaśāstristrayastriṃśā anu va ārabha idaṃ śakeyaṃ yadidaṃ karomi te māvata te mā jinvatāsminbrahamannasminkṣatre 'syāmāśiṣyasyāṃ purodhāyāmasminkarmannasyāṃ devahūtyāmiti caturgṛhītaṃ juhoti
meaning: बृहस्पतिपुरोहिता देवा देवानां देवा देवाः प्रथमजा देवा देवेषु पराक्रमध्वं प्रथमा द्वितीयेषु द्वितीयास्तृतीयेषु त्रिरेकादशास्त्रिस्त्रयस्त्रिंशा अनु व आरभ इदं शकेयं यदिदं करोमि ते मावत ते मा जिन्वतास्मिन्ब्रहमन्नस्मिन्क्षत्रे ऽस्यामाशिष्यस्यां पुरोधायामस्मिन्कर्मन्नस्यां देवहूत्यामिति चतुर्गृहीतं जुहोति
text_mt: With: 'The gods who have Bṛhaspati as their domestic priest, the gods of the gods, the first-born gods, make your effort among the gods, the first among the second, the second among the third, the thrice-eleven, the thrice-thirty-three; I take hold of you from behind; may I be able to do this which I do; protect me, invigorate me, in this sacred lore, in this royal power, in this wish, in this priestly office, in this work, in this invocation of the gods!'—he offers a fourfold ladleful.

sanskrit_iast: juhūṃ sruvaṃ ca saṃmṛjya juhvāmaṣṭagṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā yuñjānaḥ prathamaṃ mana iti yajuraṣṭamābhirṛgbhirekāmāhutiṃ juhotyantarvedyūrdhvastiṣṭhan
