meaning: जुहूं स्रुवं च संमृज्य जुह्वामष्टगृहीतं गृहीत्वा युञ्जानः प्रथमं मन इति यजुरष्टमाभिरृग्भिरेकामाहुतिं जुहोत्यन्तर्वेद्यूर्ध्वस्तिष्ठन्
text_mt: Having wiped the juhū and the sruva, having taken eight ladlefuls in the juhū, he offers a single oblation standing upright inside the altar ground with the eight verses [beginning with] the yajus: 'Yoking first the mind...'
One whom he desires should become worse off, for him he should offer each [verse] standing crooked.
If he desires: 'May I invest the meters with the sacrificial glory,' [the rule] has been stated.

sanskrit_iast: ṛcā stomaṃ samardhayetyaparaṃ caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā devasya tvā savituḥ prasava iti caturbhirabhrimādatte vaiṇavīṃ kalmāṣīṃ suṣirāmasuṣirāṃ vobhayataḥkṣṇūmanyatarataḥkṣṇūṃ vā prādeśamātrīmaratnimātrīṃ vyāyāmamātrīmaparimitāṃ vā /
meaning: ऋचा स्तोमं समर्धयेत्यपरं चतुर्गृहीतं गृहीत्वा देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसव इति चतुर्भिरभ्रिमादत्ते वैणवीं कल्माषीं सुषिरामसुषिरां वोभयतःक्ष्णूमन्यतरतःक्ष्णूं वा प्रादेशमात्रीमरत्निमात्रीं व्यायाममात्रीमपरिमितां वा /
text_mt: Having taken another fourfold ladleful with: 'Swell the stoma with the ṛc...', he takes up the spade with the four [mantras beginning with]: 'At the impulse of the divine Savitṛ...'—[a spade] of bamboo, speckled, hollow or not hollow, sharpened at both ends or sharpened at one end, a span long, a cubit long, a fathom long, or of unlimited size;

sanskrit_iast: khādirīṃ pālāśīmaudumbarīmarkamayīṃ kārṣmaryamayīṃ vaikaṅkatīṃ śamīmayīṃ vā yo vā yajñiyo vṛkṣaḥ phalagrahiḥ
meaning: खादिरीं पालाशीमौदुम्बरीमर्कमयीं कार्ष्मर्यमयीं वैकङ्कतीं शमीमयीं वा यो वा यज्ञियो वृक्षः फलग्रहिः
text_mt: or made of khadira, of palāśa, of udumbara, of arka, of kārṣmarya, of vikankata, or of śamī, or whatever sacrificial tree bears fruit.
Taking the horse's halter with: 'They have grasped this halter of cosmic order...', he bridles the horse with: 'Run swiftly, O courser...'

sanskrit_iast: tūṣṇīṃ gardabhasyādāya yuñjāthāṃ rāsabhaṃ yuvamiti gardabham
meaning: तूष्णीं गर्दभस्यादाय युञ्जाथां रासभं युवमिति गर्दभम्
text_mt: Silently taking that of the donkey, [he bridles] the donkey with: 'Yoke the donkey, you two...'

sanskrit_iast: yogeyoge tavastaramiti tisṛbhiraśvaprathamā abhipravrajanti yatra mṛdaṃ khaniṣyantaḥ syuḥ
meaning: योगेयोगे तवस्तरमिति तिसृभिरश्वप्रथमा अभिप्रव्रजन्ति यत्र मृदं खनिष्यन्तः स्युः
text_mt: With the three [verses beginning with]: 'In every venture the most mighty...', they set out, with the horse first, to where they will dig the clay.

sanskrit_iast: yadi kāmayeta pāpavasyasaṃ syāditi gardabhaprathamā gaccheyuḥ
meaning: यदि कामयेत पापवस्यसं स्यादिति गर्दभप्रथमा गच्छेयुः
text_mt: If he should desire that things become worse instead of better, they should go with the donkey first.
He murmurs, 'Go to the earthly Agni as did the Aṅgirases.'

sanskrit_iast: agniṃ purīṣyamaṅgirasvadacchema iti yena dveṣyeṇa saṃgacchate tamabhimantrayate /
meaning: अग्निं पुरीष्यमङ्गिरस्वदच्छेम इति येन द्वेष्येण संगच्छते तमभिमन्त्रयते /
text_mt: With 'We go to the earthly Agni as did the Aṅgirases,' he addresses any hateful person he encounters;
With 'We will bear the earthly Agni as did the Aṅgirases,' [he addresses] an anthill's crest.
Having dug it up, he attends upon it until the rising of the sun.
With 'Agni has looked after the front of the dawns,' he steps forth from the anthill's crest.

sanskrit_iast: āgatya vājyadhvana ākramya vājinpṛthivīmiti dvābhyāṃ mṛtkhanamaśvamākramayya dyauste pṛṣṭhamityaśvasya pṛṣṭhaṃ saṃmārṣṭi
meaning: आगत्य वाज्यध्वन आक्रम्य वाजिन्पृथिवीमिति द्वाभ्यां मृत्खनमश्वमाक्रमय्य द्यौस्ते पृष्ठमित्यश्वस्य पृष्ठं संमार्ष्टि
text_mt: Having made the horse step upon the clay-pit with the two [formulas], 'The courser having arrived from the road' and 'Stepping, O courser, upon the earth,' he strokes the back of the horse with 'The sky is your back.'

meaning: अभि तिष्ठ पृतन्यतो ऽधरे सन्तु शत्रवः /
text_mt: 'Tread upon those who fight [against us]; let the enemies be below!

sanskrit_iast: indra iva vṛtrahā tiṣṭhāpaḥ kṣetrāṇi saṃjayan /
meaning: इन्द्र इव वृत्रहा तिष्ठापः क्षेत्राणि संजयन् /
text_mt: Stand like Indra the slayer of Vṛtra, conquering the waters and the fields!'

sanskrit_iast: abhiṣṭhito 'sīti yaṃ dveṣṭi tamadhaspadamaśvasya manasā dhyāyati
meaning: अभिष्ठितो ऽसीति यं द्वेष्टि तमधस्पदमश्वस्य मनसा ध्यायति
text_mt: With 'You are stepped upon,' he mentally focuses on whomever he hates under the horse's foot.

sanskrit_iast: utkrāmodakrāmīditi dvābhyāṃ mṛtkhanādudañcamaśvamutkramayyāpo devīrupasṛjetyaśvasya pade 'pa upasṛjya pade hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya
meaning: उत्क्रामोदक्रामीदिति द्वाभ्यां मृत्खनादुदञ्चमश्वमुत्क्रमय्यापो देवीरुपसृजेत्यश्वस्य पदे ऽप उपसृज्य पदे हिरण्यं निधाय
text_mt: Having made the horse step northward out of the clay-pit with the two [formulas], 'Step out' and 'It has stepped out,' having poured water into the horse's footprint with 'Divine waters, flow forth,' and having placed gold in the footprint,

sanskrit_iast: jigharmy agnim ā tvā jigharmīti manasvatībhyām ekām āhutiṃ hiraṇye hutvāpādāya hiraṇyaṃ pari vājapatiḥ kavir agniriti tisṛbhirabhriyā mṛtkhanaṃ parilikhati /
meaning: जिघर्म्य् अग्निम् आ त्वा जिघर्मीति मनस्वतीभ्याम् एकाम् आहुतिं हिरण्ये हुत्वापादाय हिरण्यं परि वाजपतिः कविर् अग्निरिति तिसृभिरभ्रिया मृत्खनं परिलिखति /
text_mt: having offered a single oblation upon the gold with the two mind-formulas, 'I moisten Agni' and 'I moisten you,' and having taken up the gold, he traces around the clay-pit with the spade with the three [verses], 'Around, the lord of prize, the seer Agni…'
each outer [line] being larger.

sanskrit_iast: devasya tvā savituḥ prasava iti dvābhyāṃ khanati
meaning: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसव इति द्वाभ्यां खनति
text_mt: With the two [formulas], 'At the instigation of divine Savitṛ,' he digs.

sanskrit_iast: apāṃ pṛṣṭham asīti puṣkaraparṇam āhṛtyaitayaiva viveṣṭya śarma ca stho varma ca stha iti dvābhyām uttareṇa mṛtkhanaṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ prācīnagrīvam uttaralomāstṛṇāti /
meaning: अपां पृष्ठम् असीति पुष्करपर्णम् आहृत्यैतयैव विवेष्ट्य शर्म च स्थो वर्म च स्थ इति द्वाभ्याम् उत्तरेण मृत्खनं कृष्णाजिनं प्राचीनग्रीवम् उत्तरलोमास्तृणाति /
text_mt: Having fetched a lotus-leaf with 'You are the back of the waters,' and having wrapped it with this very [formula], he spreads a black antelope skin north of the clay-pit, with its neck pointing east and its hair facing upward, with the two [formulas], 'You two are protection, and you two are armour.'
Above it [he places] the lotus-leaf face upward.

sanskrit_iast: purīṣyo 'si viśvabharā iti mṛtkhanam abhimantrya tvām agne puṣkarād adhīti kṛṣṇājine puṣkaraparṇe ca saṃbharati catasṛbhis tisṛbhir vā /
meaning: पुरीष्यो ऽसि विश्वभरा इति मृत्खनम् अभिमन्त्र्य त्वाम् अग्ने पुष्कराद् अधीति कृष्णाजिने पुष्करपर्णे च संभरति चतसृभिस् तिसृभिर् वा /
text_mt: Having addressed the clay-pit with 'You are earthly, all-bearing,' he collects [the clay] onto the black antelope skin and the lotus-leaf with 'You, O Agni, from the lotus…' using four or three [verses]:
with gāyatrī verses for a brāhmaṇa;
with triṣṭubh verses for a rājanya;

sanskrit_iast: yaṃ kāmayeta vasīyān syād ity ubhayībhis tasya saṃbharet
meaning: यं कामयेत वसीयान् स्याद् इत्य् उभयीभिस् तस्य संभरेत्
text_mt: For one whom he wishes to become wealthier, he should collect with both.

sanskrit_iast: janiṣvā hi jenya iti mṛdam abhimṛśya mṛtkhanaṃ saṃlobhya saṃ te vāyur iti mṛtkhane 'pa ānīya samudyamya kṛṣṇājinasyāntānsujāto jyotiṣā saheti kṣaumeṇa mauñjenārkamayeṇa vā dāmnopanahyati
meaning: जनिष्वा हि जेन्य इति मृदम् अभिमृश्य मृत्खनं संलोभ्य सं ते वायुर् इति मृत्खने ऽप आनीय समुद्यम्य कृष्णाजिनस्यान्तान्सुजातो ज्योतिषा सहेति क्षौमेण मौञ्जेनार्कमयेण वा दाम्नोपनह्यति
text_mt: Having touched the clay with 'Be born, noble one,' having smoothed the clay-pit, having poured water into the clay-pit with 'May Vāyu unite you,' and having lifted the corners of the black antelope skin, he ties it up with 'Well-born with light' using a cord of linen, of muñja grass, or made of arka.

sanskrit_iast: udu tiṣṭha svadhvarordhva ū ṣu ṇa ūtaya iti sāvitrībhyāmuttiṣṭhati
meaning: उदु तिष्ठ स्वध्वरोर्ध्व ऊ षु ण ऊतय इति सावित्रीभ्यामुत्तिष्ठति
text_mt: He stands up with the two Savitṛ verses, 'Rise up, of good sacrifice' and 'Upright unto us for help.'
He carries [it] with 'Born, you are the embryo.'

sanskrit_iast: sthiro bhava vīḍvaṅga iti gardabhasya pṛṣṭha ādadaḥti
meaning: स्थिरो भव वीड्वङ्ग इति गर्दभस्य पृष्ठ आददःति
text_mt: With 'Be firm, strong-limbed,' he places it on the back of the donkey.
He addresses it once placed with 'Be for the welfare of creatures tomorrow.'
They return without haste with the three [verses], 'Let the courser advance neighing.'

sanskrit_iast: agniṃ purīṣyamaṅgirasvadbharāma iti yena dveṣyeṇa saṃgacchate tamabhimantrayate /
meaning: अग्निं पुरीष्यमङ्गिरस्वद्भराम इति येन द्वेष्येण संगच्छते तमभिमन्त्रयते /
text_mt: With 'We bear the earthly Agni as did the Aṅgirases,' he addresses any hateful person he encounters;

sanskrit_iast: uttareṇa vihāraṃ pariśrita oṣadhayaḥ prati gṛhṇītāgnimetamiti dvābhyāmoṣadhīṣu puṣpavatīṣu phalavatīṣūpāvaharati
meaning: उत्तरेण विहारं परिश्रित ओषधयः प्रति गृह्णीताग्निमेतमिति द्वाभ्यामोषधीषु पुष्पवतीषु फलवतीषूपावहरति
text_mt: To the north of the sacrificial ground, inside an enclosure, he sets it down among flowering and fruit-bearing plants with the two [verses], 'O plants, receive this Agni.'

sanskrit_iast: vi pājaseti visrasyāpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuva iti tisṛbhirapa upasṛjya mitraḥ saṃsṛjya pṛthivīmiti dvābhyāṃ saṃsarjanīyaiḥ saṃsṛjati /
meaning: वि पाजसेति विस्रस्यापो हि ष्ठा मयोभुव इति तिसृभिरप उपसृज्य मित्रः संसृज्य पृथिवीमिति द्वाभ्यां संसर्जनीयैः संसृजति /
text_mt: Having untied [it] with 'With wide light,' having poured water with the three [verses], 'You, waters, are indeed refreshing,' he mixes it with the mixing ingredients with the two [formulas], 'Mitra, having united the earth…'—

sanskrit_iast: armakapālaiḥ piṣṭairveṇvaṅgārairvrīhituṣaiḥ palāśakaṣāyeṇa śarkarābhiḥ piṣṭābhiḥ kṛṣṇājinalomabhirajalomabhiriti
meaning: अर्मकपालैः पिष्टैर्वेण्वङ्गारैर्व्रीहितुषैः पलाशकषायेण शर्कराभिः पिष्टाभिः कृष्णाजिनलोमभिरजलोमभिरिति
text_mt: with crushed potsherds from an abandoned site, bamboo embers, rice husks, a decoction of palāśa bark, crushed gravel, hair of a black antelope, and hair of a goat—
and whatever else he considers useful for the purpose of making it firm.

sanskrit_iast: rudrāḥ saṃbhṛtya pṛthivīmiti mṛdaṃ saṃkṣipya saṃsṛṣṭāṃ vasubhiriti tisṛbhiḥ kartre prayacchati
meaning: रुद्राः संभृत्य पृथिवीमिति मृदं संक्षिप्य संसृष्टां वसुभिरिति तिसृभिः कर्त्रे प्रयच्छति
text_mt: Having gathered the clay with 'The Rudras, having assembled the earth,' he hands it over to the maker with the three [formulas], 'Mixed by the Vasus…'

sanskrit_iast: makhasya śiro 'sīti piṇḍaṃ kṛtvā yajñasya pade stha iti kṛṣṇājinaṃ puṣkaraparṇaṃ cābhivṛśati mṛdi vāṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ nigṛhṇāti
meaning: मखस्य शिरो ऽसीति पिण्डं कृत्वा यज्ञस्य पदे स्थ इति कृष्णाजिनं पुष्करपर्णं चाभिवृशति मृदि वाङ्गुष्ठाभ्यां निगृह्णाति
text_mt: Having made a lump with 'You are the head of Makha,' he touches the black antelope skin and the lotus-leaf with 'You two are the footprints of the sacrifice,' or presses down into the clay with his two thumbs.

sanskrit_iast: vasavastvā kṛṇvantu gāyatreṇa cchandaseti caturbhirmahiṣyukhāṃ karoti bahubhāryasya /
meaning: वसवस्त्वा कृण्वन्तु गायत्रेण च्छन्दसेति चतुर्भिर्महिष्युखां करोति बहुभार्यस्य /
text_mt: With the four [formulas], 'May the Vasus make you with the gāyatrī metre,' the chief queen makes the ukhā-pot for one who has many wives;
the adhvaryu, for one who has one wife.
While it is being made, the sacrificer follows it with these same [formulas].
[It has] three layers, five layers, or an unmeasured number of layers;
four-cornered or circular;
a span in height, a cubit in width, a fathom in circumference;

sanskrit_iast: pañcaprādeśāmiṣumātrīṃ vā yadi pañca paśvo bhavantīti vājasaneyakam
meaning: पञ्चप्रादेशामिषुमात्रीं वा यदि पञ्च पश्वो भवन्तीति वाजसनेयकम्
text_mt: Five spans or an arrow-length [in size] if there are five sacrificial animals: so says the Vājasaneyaka.
In making it, he raises four corners towards the cardinal directions;
For one practicing sorcery, he should make it nine-cornered.
Two finger-breadths below the rim,
he makes a girdle with 'You are Aditi's girdle.'

sanskrit_iast: aśrīṇāṃ rāsnāyāśca saṃdhau dvau caturaḥ ṣaḍaṣṭau vā stanānkaroti
meaning: अश्रीणां रास्नायाश्च संधौ द्वौ चतुरः षडष्टौ वा स्तनान्करोति
text_mt: At the junction of the corners and the girdle, he makes two, four, six, or eight nipples.
Having fashioned the rim with 'May Aditi take your rim,'

sanskrit_iast: ya ukhāṃ karoti so 'ṣāḍhāmetasyā eva mṛdastūṣṇīṃ caturaśrāṃ tryālikhitāmiṣṭakām
meaning: य उखां करोति सो ऽषाढामेतस्या एव मृदस्तूष्णीं चतुरश्रां त्र्यालिखितामिष्टकाम्
text_mt: whoever makes the ukhā-pot makes the aṣāḍhā brick silently from this very clay, four-cornered, with three lines drawn upon it.

sanskrit_iast: vasavastvā dhūpayantu gāyatreṇa cchandaseti saptabhiraśvaśakenokhāṃ dhūpayati
meaning: वसवस्त्वा धूपयन्तु गायत्रेण च्छन्दसेति सप्तभिरश्वशकेनोखां धूपयति
text_mt: With the seven [formulas], 'May the Vasus fumigate you with the gāyatrī metre,' he fumigates the ukhā-pot with horse dung;
with the dung of a stallion, say some.
The fumigation and the baking are done with [fire] from the gārhapatya.

sanskrit_iast: aditistvā devītyagreṇa gārhapatyamavaṭaṃ khātvā lohitapacanīyaiḥ saṃbhārairavastīrya devānāṃ tvā patnīriti tasminnukhāmavadadhāti
meaning: अदितिस्त्वा देवीत्यग्रेण गार्हपत्यमवटं खात्वा लोहितपचनीयैः संभारैरवस्तीर्य देवानां त्वा पत्नीरिति तस्मिन्नुखामवदधाति
text_mt: Having dug a pit in front of the gārhapatya with 'You, the goddess Aditi,' and having strewn it with materials for baking red, he places the ukhā-pot down into it with 'You, the wives of the gods.'

sanskrit_iast: tūṣṇīmaṣāḍhāmanvavadhāya lohitapacanīyaiḥ saṃbhāraiḥ pracchādya dhiṣaṇāstvā devīriti caturbhirukhāyāmagnimabhyādadhāti
meaning: तूष्णीमषाढामन्ववधाय लोहितपचनीयैः संभारैः प्रच्छाद्य धिषणास्त्वा देवीरिति चतुर्भिरुखायामग्निमभ्यादधाति
text_mt: Silently putting in the aṣāḍhā [brick], covering [the whole] with materials for baking red, he places fire into the pan with the four [verses], 'May the divine Dhiṣaṇās...'
While it is being baked, he attends to it with the three [verses] addressed to Mitra, 'O Mitra, bake this pan...'

sanskrit_iast: pakvāṃ devastvā savitodvapatvityudvāsyāpadyamānā pṛthivyāśā diśa ā pṛṇetyuttarataḥ sikatāsu pratiṣṭhāpya mitraitāṃ ta ukhāṃ paridadāmyabhitryā eṣā mā bhedīti mitrāya paridadāti
meaning: पक्वां देवस्त्वा सवितोद्वपत्वित्युद्वास्यापद्यमाना पृथिव्याशा दिश आ पृणेत्युत्तरतः सिकतासु प्रतिष्ठाप्य मित्रैतां त उखां परिददाम्यभित्र्या एषा मा भेदीति मित्राय परिददाति
text_mt: When it is baked, he lifts it off with 'May divine Savitṛ lift you off...', places it to the north on sand with 'Not falling to earth, fill the quarters and directions!', and commits it to Mitra with 'O Mitra, I commit this pan to you for non-destruction, lest it break.'
Having silently lifted off the aṣāḍhā [brick],
he pours goat's milk into the pan with the four [formulas], 'May the Vasus unclose you with the Gāyatrī metre...'

sanskrit_iast: saptaikaviṃśatiṃ vā māsānādāya puruṣaśiro 'cchaiti vaiśyasya rājanyasya veṣuhatasyāśanihatasya vā
meaning: सप्तैकविंशतिं वा मासानादाय पुरुषशिरो ऽच्छैति वैश्यस्य राजन्यस्य वेषुहतस्याशनिहतस्य वा
text_mt: Having taken seven or twenty-one beans, he goes to fetch the head of a man—of a Vaiśya or a Rājanya, killed by an arrow or killed by lightning.

sanskrit_iast: māṣānupanyupyāyaṃ yo 'si yasya ta idaṃ śira iti puruṣaśiraḥ pracchidyaitena tvamatra śīrṣaṇvānedhīti saptadhā vitṛṇāṃ valmīkavapāṃ śirasaḥ sthāne pratinidadhāti
meaning: माषानुपन्युप्यायं यो ऽसि यस्य त इदं शिर इति पुरुषशिरः प्रच्छिद्यैतेन त्वमत्र शीर्षण्वानेधीति सप्तधा वितृणां वल्मीकवपां शिरसः स्थाने प्रतिनिदधाति
text_mt: Having scattered the beans, he severs the head of the man with 'This one who you are, whose head this is...', and in place of the head deposits an anthill mound pierced seven ways, with 'By means of this, be endowed with a head here!'

meaning: यो ऽस्य कौष्ठ्य जगतः पार्थिवस्यैक इद्वशी /
text_mt: 'Who, dwelling in the storehouse of this earthly world, is the sole ruler,
Sing of Yama, O Bhaṅgyaśravas, who is the unopposable king!
Sing of Yama, O Bhaṅgyaśravas, who is the unopposable king,

sanskrit_iast: yenāpo nadyo dhanvāni yena dyauḥ pṛthivī dṛḍhā //
meaning: येनापो नद्यो धन्वानि येन द्यौः पृथिवी दृढा //
text_mt: by whom the waters, the rivers, the deserts, by whom heaven and earth are made firm!
Golden-girthed, easy to harness, golden-eyed, iron-hoofed,

sanskrit_iast: aśvānanaśyato dānaṃ yamo rājābhitiṣṭhatīti tisṛbhiryamagāthābhiḥ parigāyati
meaning: अश्वाननश्यतो दानं यमो राजाभितिष्ठतीति तिसृभिर्यमगाथाभिः परिगायति
text_mt: undecaying horses—king Yama mounts this gift.' With these three Yama-gāthās he sings around [the head].

sanskrit_iast: idamasmākaṃ bhuje bhogāya bhūyāditi puruṣaśira ādāyodehyagne adhi mātuḥ pṛthivyā ityāharati
meaning: इदमस्माकं भुजे भोगाय भूयादिति पुरुषशिर आदायोदेह्यग्ने अधि मातुः पृथिव्या इत्याहरति
text_mt: Taking the head of the man with 'May this be for our enjoyment, for our pleasure!', he brings it with 'Rise up, O Agni, from mother earth!'
'Agni goes round the sacrifice three times like a charioteer,
This [second verse is]: 'Round about, the lord of prize, the seer...'
'The divine Agni has gone round, killer of rakṣases, expeller of sickness,

sanskrit_iast: sedhanviśvā apa dviṣo dhanrakṣāṃsi viśvaheti tisṛbhiḥ paryagnikṛtvā mṛdā pralipya nidadhāti
meaning: सेधन्विश्वा अप द्विषो धन्रक्षांसि विश्वहेति तिसृभिः पर्यग्निकृत्वा मृदा प्रलिप्य निदधाति
text_mt: driving away all foes, burning the rakṣases forever.' Having carried fire around [the head] with these three [verses], and having smeared it with clay, he deposits it.
He seizes uncastrated animals for the Agnis according to desire:
having assigned a hornless he-goat for Prajāpati, a horse, a bull, a ram, and a he-goat.
He recites twenty-one or twenty-four continuous sāmidhenī verses:
ten verses belonging to the fire ritual, [beginning with] 'May the years, O Agni...'

sanskrit_iast: rāyo agne mahe tvā dānāya samidhīmahi /
meaning: रायो अग्ने महे त्वा दानाय समिधीमहि /
text_mt: 'For great wealth to be given, O Agni, we would kindle you;

sanskrit_iast: īḍiṣvā hi mahī vṛṣandyāvā hotrāya pṛthivīmiti yadyekaviṃśatiḥ
meaning: ईडिष्वा हि मही वृषन्द्यावा होत्राय पृथिवीमिति यद्येकविंशतिः
text_mt: implore, O bull, the great heaven and earth for the hotṛ's office'—[these are added] if there are twenty-one.

sanskrit_iast: upemasṛkṣi vājayurvacasyāṃ cano dadhīta nādyo giro me /
meaning: उपेमसृक्षि वाजयुर्वचस्यां चनो दधीत नाद्यो गिरो मे /
text_mt: 'Desiring a prize, I have sent forth this well-spoken speech; may the river-god accept my hymns;
swiftly moving Apāṃ Napāt, may he make them well adorned, for he will be pleased.'

sanskrit_iast: apāṃ napādā hyasthādupasthaṃ jihmānāmūrdhvaḥ svayaśā upasthe /
meaning: अपां नपादा ह्यस्थादुपस्थं जिह्मानामूर्ध्वः स्वयशा उपस्थे /
text_mt: 'Apāṃ Napāt has mounted the lap of the crooked [waters], upright, glorious in their lap;

sanskrit_iast: ubhe abhi priyatame sadhasthe ā ca parā ca carati prajānanniti tisro 'psumatīryadi caturviṃśatiḥ
meaning: उभे अभि प्रियतमे सधस्थे आ च परा च चरति प्रजानन्निति तिस्रो ऽप्सुमतीर्यदि चतुर्विंशतिः
text_mt: knowing well, he moves between both dearest common homes'—these three water-verses [are added] if there are twenty-four.
For a sick [sacrificer], he should say: 'May he be in that world.'
For one who is not sick: 'O Bṛhaspati, O Savitṛ, awaken him.'
They conclude with the verse containing 'light', 'Up from darkness...'
He performs the continuous offering from the ladle with 'The golden embryo evolved in the beginning...'

sanskrit_iast: ūrdhvā asya samidho bhavantīti prayājānāmāpriyo bhavanti
meaning: ऊर्ध्वा अस्य समिधो भवन्तीति प्रयाजानामाप्रियो भवन्ति
text_mt: The āprī verses of the fore-offerings are those beginning with 'Upward are his firebrands...'
Triṣṭubh verses addressed to Agni are the invitatory and consecratory verses for those [offerings] addressed to Agni.

sanskrit_iast: yaḥ prāṇato ya ātmadā iti prājāpatyasya
meaning: यः प्राणतो य आत्मदा इति प्राजापत्यस्य
text_mt: The two verses 'Who is the giver of breath, who is the giver of soul...' are for the [offering] dedicated to Prajāpati.

sanskrit_iast: api vā saṃjñaptānāṃ śirāṃsi pracchidya mṛdā pralipya nidadhāti
meaning: अपि वा संज्ञप्तानां शिरांसि प्रच्छिद्य मृदा प्रलिप्य निदधाति
text_mt: Or, having severed the heads of the suffocated [animals] and smeared them with clay, he deposits them.
They carry the headless trunks down to the water.
It is known [from the Brāhmaṇa]: 'He concludes [the rite] with the one dedicated to Prajāpati.'

sanskrit_iast: api vā sarveṣāmeteṣāṃ sthāne vāyave niyutvate śvetamajaṃ tūparamālabhate
meaning: अपि वा सर्वेषामेतेषां स्थाने वायवे नियुत्वते श्वेतमजं तूपरमालभते
text_mt: Or rather, in place of all these, he seizes a white hornless he-goat for Vāyu accompanied by the Niyuts.
The invitatory and consecratory verses for the omentum contain the words 'vāyu' and 'śveta';
those for the offering of animal flesh contain the words 'vāyu' and 'niyut'.

sanskrit_iast: tasya śiraḥ pracchidya mṛdā pralipya nidadhāti
meaning: तस्य शिरः प्रच्छिद्य मृदा प्रलिप्य निदधाति
text_mt: Having severed its head and smeared it with clay, he deposits it.
It has been said: 'The actions relating to Vāyu should be performed.'
For it, he pours out a sacrificial animal-cake on twelve potsherds for Agni Vaiśvānara.

sanskrit_iast: yaḥ kaścanāgnau paśurālabhyate vaiśvānara evāsya dvādaśakapālaḥ paśupuroḍāśo bhavatītyeke
meaning: यः कश्चनाग्नौ पशुरालभ्यते वैश्वानर एवास्य द्वादशकपालः पशुपुरोडाशो भवतीत्येके
text_mt: Some say: 'Whatever animal is seized at the fire, its animal-cake is on twelve potsherds for Vaiśvānara alone.'

sanskrit_iast: teneṣṭvā saṃvatsaraṃ na māṃsamaśnīyānna striyamupeyānnopari śyīta
meaning: तेनेष्ट्वा संवत्सरं न मांसमश्नीयान्न स्त्रियमुपेयान्नोपरि श्यीत
text_mt: Having sacrificed with it, he should not eat meat, nor approach a woman, nor sleep on a raised couch for a year.

sanskrit_iast: api vā māṃsamaśnīyādupari śayīta striyaṃ tveva nopeyāditi vājasneyakam
meaning: अपि वा मांसमश्नीयादुपरि शयीत स्त्रियं त्वेव नोपेयादिति वाजस्नेयकम्
text_mt: Or rather, he may eat meat and sleep on a raised couch, but he should certainly not approach a woman: thus the Vājasaneyaka.
Having performed whatever comes prior to the consecration offering, he pours out the consecration offering consisting of three oblations.
For one who has not borne [the fire in the pan] for a year, the third is for Vaiśvānara on twelve potsherds, [offered] beforehand.

meaning: यत्प्राग्दीक्षाहुतीभ्यस्तत्कृत्वाकूत्यै प्रयुजे ऽग्नये स्वाहेति पञ्चाध्वरिकीर्हुत्वाकूतिमग्निमिति षडाग्निकीः /
text_mt: Having performed whatever comes prior to the consecration oblations, having offered the five oblations belonging to the basic sacrifice with 'To intention, to impulse, to Agni, svāhā!', and the six belonging to the fire ritual with 'Intention, Agni...';
he offers the seventh, the full oblation, with 'Of the divine guide, all...'

sanskrit_iast: yaṃ kāmayeta pramāyukaḥ syāditi tasya sakṛdanudrutya juhuyāt /
meaning: यं कामयेत प्रमायुकः स्यादिति तस्य सकृदनुद्रुत्य जुहुयात् /
text_mt: For one whom he would wish 'May he be liable to die!', he should offer by reciting continuously at one stretch;
he pierces his vital breaths;
he indeed becomes deaf, so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].
The consecrated one carries the fire in the pan for a year,
or for three days, or for six days, or for twelve days.
'Whoever [piles the fire] inside of a year, he is only a builder of pain,' say some.
It has already been said: 'By Agni's initiation indeed…'

sanskrit_iast: yatprāṅmuṣṭikarmaṇastatkṛtvā śaṇakulāyane vokhāṃ pracchādya mā su bhitthā iti dvābhyāmāhavanīye pravṛṇakti
meaning: यत्प्राङ्मुष्टिकर्मणस्तत्कृत्वा शणकुलायने वोखां प्रच्छाद्य मा सु भित्था इति द्वाभ्यामाहवनीये प्रवृणक्ति
text_mt: Having performed whatever precedes the closing of the fists, or having covered the ukhā-pot with a nest of hemp, he places it upside down on the āhavanīya with the two [formulas], 'Do not break!'
With 'O Mitra, heat this ukhā-pot,' he surrounds it clockwise with burning embers.

sanskrit_iast: dvarannaḥ sarpirāsutiriti tasyāṃ krumukamullikhitaṃ ghṛtenāktvāvadadhāti muñjāṃśca
meaning: द्वरन्नः सर्पिरासुतिरिति तस्यां क्रुमुकमुल्लिखितं घृतेनाक्त्वावदधाति मुञ्जांश्च
text_mt: With the verse, 'Having ghee as drink, butter as food…' he puts into it a scraped piece of krumuka wood, having anointed it with ghee, and muñja grass.
The case of one who has attained prosperity has been stated.

sanskrit_iast: pradāvyādāharedyaṃ kāmayeta prasyandinayāmasya rāṣṭraṃ jāyukaṃ syāditi /
meaning: प्रदाव्यादाहरेद्यं कामयेत प्रस्यन्दिनयामस्य राष्ट्रं जायुकं स्यादिति /
text_mt: He should bring it from a forest fire for him of whom he desires, 'May his realm become flowing with wealth.'
From the burning top of a tree for one who desires spiritual lustre;
from a parching pan for one who desires food.
When performing the fire for a specific wish, he should not turn [the pot] over on the āhavanīya.
When [the fire] is born in the pot, he allows the āhavanīya to expire.

sanskrit_iast: parasyā adhi saṃvata iti vaikaṅkatīṃ samidhamādadhāti
meaning: परस्या अधि संवत इति वैकङ्कतीं समिधमादधाति
text_mt: With the verse, 'From the further reach…' he puts on a firewood stick of vikankaṭa wood.
With the verse, 'From the farthest distance…' [he puts on] one made of śamī wood.

sanskrit_iast: sīda tvaṃ mātur asyā upastha iti tisṛbhir jātamukhyam upatiṣṭhate
meaning: सीद त्वं मातुर् अस्या उपस्थ इति तिसृभिर् जातमुख्यम् उपतिष्ठते
text_mt: With three verses beginning with 'Sit thou in the lap of this mother…' he attends upon the [fire] born in the pot.

sanskrit_iast: yadagne yāni kāni ceti pañcabhiraudumbaramaparaśuvṛkṇamukhya idhmamabhyādadhāti
meaning: यदग्ने यानि कानि चेति पञ्चभिरौदुम्बरमपरशुवृक्णमुख्य इध्ममभ्यादधाति
text_mt: With five verses beginning with 'Whatever, O Agni, whatsoever…' he places onto the [fire] in the pot firewood of udumbara wood, not cut down with an axe.
One of tilvaka wood for one practicing sorcery.
With the verse, 'With both fangs the robbers…' he puts on a firewood stick of aśvattha wood.
With 'Those thieves who are among people…' one of vikankaṭa wood.
With 'Whosoever would act with hostility against us…' one made of śamī wood.

sanskrit_iast: tasmādagnicitaḥ pāpaṃ na kīrtayenno agniṃ bibhrato no agnividaḥ
meaning: तस्मादग्निचितः पापं न कीर्तयेन्नो अग्निं बिभ्रतो नो अग्निविदः
text_mt: Therefore, one should not utter evil of one who has piled the fire, nor of one bearing the fire, nor of one who knows the fire.

sanskrit_iast: saṃśitaṃ me brahmodeṣāṃ bāhū atiramityuttame yajamānaṃ vācayaṃstūṣṇīmaudumbaryau samidhāvādadhāti
meaning: संशितं मे ब्रह्मोदेषां बाहू अतिरमित्युत्तमे यजमानं वाचयंस्तूष्णीमौदुम्बर्यौ समिधावादधाति
text_mt: Making the sacrificer recite the two verses, 'Sharpened is my prayer…' and 'I have raised their arms…', he silently puts on two firewood sticks of udumbara wood.

sanskrit_iast: māteva putraṃ pṛthivī purīṣyamagniṃ sve yonau bhariṣyatyukhā /
meaning: मातेव पुत्रं पृथिवी पुरीष्यमग्निं स्वे योनौ भरिष्यत्युखा /
text_mt: 'Like a mother her son, the earth [shall bear] the fire belonging to the soil; the pot shall bear it in its own birthplace.

sanskrit_iast: tāṃ viśvairdevairṛtubhiḥ saṃvidānaḥ prajāpatirviśvakarmā yunaktviti mauñje śikye ṣaḍudyāme dvādaśodyāme vokhāmavadadhāti
meaning: तां विश्वैर्देवैरृतुभिः संविदानः प्रजापतिर्विश्वकर्मा युनक्त्विति मौञ्जे शिक्ये षडुद्यामे द्वादशोद्यामे वोखामवदधाति
text_mt: Agreement made with all the gods and the seasons, let Prajāpati Viśvakarman yoke it'—with this verse he places the pot into a sling made of muñja grass, six spans long or twelve spans long.

sanskrit_iast: ekaviṃśatinirbodho yo rukmaḥ sūtroto dṛśāno rukma iti tamāsīno yajamāno 'ntarnirbādhaṃ pratimucya bahirnirbādhānkurute
meaning: एकविंशतिनिर्बोधो यो रुक्मः सूत्रोतो दृशानो रुक्म इति तमासीनो यजमानो ऽन्तर्निर्बाधं प्रतिमुच्य बहिर्निर्बाधान्कुरुते
text_mt: A gold plate having twenty-one knobs, strung on a cord: with 'The visible gold plate…' the sacrificer, sitting down, fastens it on so that the knobs face inward, and makes the knobs face outward.
With 'All forms…' he fastens the noose of the sling [about his neck].
With 'Night and Dawn…' [he fastens] the black antelope skin above.

sanskrit_iast: suparṇo 'si garutmānityukhyamavekṣya suparṇo 'si garutmānityādāyotthāyopari nābherdhārayamāṇo viṣṇoḥ kramo 'sīti caturo viṣṇukramānprācaḥ krāmati
meaning: सुपर्णो ऽसि गरुत्मानित्युख्यमवेक्ष्य सुपर्णो ऽसि गरुत्मानित्यादायोत्थायोपरि नाभेर्धारयमाणो विष्णोः क्रमो ऽसीति चतुरो विष्णुक्रमान्प्राचः क्रामति
text_mt: Looking at the fire in the pot with 'A fair-winged eagle art thou…', taking it up with 'A fair-winged eagle art thou…', rising, and holding it above the navel, he steps the four Viṣṇu strides toward the east with 'Thou art the stride of Viṣṇu.'
Having recited the verse, 'Agni has cried out…', he turns around clockwise with the four verses beginning with 'O Agni, turn back…'.

meaning: उदुत्तममिति शिक्यपाशमुन्मुच्या त्वाहार्षमित्याहृत्योपतिष्ठते ऽग्रे बृहन्नुषसामूर्ध्वो अस्थादिति
text_mt: With 'The highest…' he unfastens the noose of the sling; having brought it forward with 'I have brought thee…', he attends upon it with 'High, upright in front of the dawns, he has stood…'.

sanskrit_iast: yaṃ kāmayeta rāṣṭraṃ syāditi taṃ manasā dhyāyet
meaning: यं कामयेत राष्ट्रं स्यादिति तं मनसा ध्यायेत्
text_mt: Him of whom he desires that he may obtain a realm, he should contemplate in mind.

sanskrit_iast: audumbaryāsandyaratnimātraśīrṣaṇyānūcyā prādeśamātrapādā mauñjavivānā phalakāstīrṇā vā mṛḍā pradigdhā
meaning: औदुम्बर्यासन्द्यरत्निमात्रशीर्षण्यानूच्या प्रादेशमात्रपादा मौञ्जविवाना फलकास्तीर्णा वा मृडा प्रदिग्धा
text_mt: There is a stool of udumbara wood, an aratni long in its head-pieces and side-pieces, a span high in its feet, woven with muñja grass or spread over with planks, smeared with clay.

sanskrit_iast: sīda tvaṃ māturasyā upastha iti tasyāṃ catasṛbhirukhyaṃ sādayati
meaning: सीद त्वं मातुरस्या उपस्थ इति तस्यां चतसृभिरुख्यं सादयति
text_mt: On it, with four verses beginning with 'Sit thou in the lap of this mother…', he sets down the [fire] in the pot.
Or he sets it down on gravel with three verses.
He attends upon it with the Haṃsavatī verse, say some.

sanskrit_iast: yena devā jyotiṣordhvā udāyanniti prādeśamātraiḥ kāṣṭhairukhyamupasaminddhe
meaning: येन देवा ज्योतिषोर्ध्वा उदायन्निति प्रादेशमात्रैः काष्ठैरुख्यमुपसमिन्द्धे
text_mt: With 'By which light the gods rose upward…' he fuels the [fire] in the pot with pieces of firewood a span long.

meaning: व्रतकाले ऽन्नपते ऽन्नस्य नो देहीत्यौदुम्बरीं समिधं व्रते ऽक्त्वाभ्यादधाति
text_mt: At the time of the fast-food, with 'O lord of food, give us food…' he puts on a firewood stick of udumbara wood, having anointed it in the fast-food.

sanskrit_iast: devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinorbāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ gāyatreṇa cchandasā rātrimiṣṭakāmupadadhe tayā devatayāṅgirasvaddhruvā sīdeti sāyaṃ samidhamādadhāti
meaning: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऽश्विनोर्बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्यां गायत्रेण च्छन्दसा रात्रिमिष्टकामुपदधे तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद्ध्रुवा सीदेति सायं समिधमादधाति
text_mt: With 'At the impulse of divine Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, with the gāyatrī metre I place the night-brick; with that deity sit firmly like Aṅgiras,' he puts on a firewood stick in the evening.
With this very formula [substituting] 'with the triṣṭubh metre I place the day-brick' in the morning.
With eleven, twelve, or thirteen verses beginning with 'From the sky…' he attends upon it with the Vātsapra hymn.
On the previous day he steps the Viṣṇu strides;
on the following day he attends upon [the fire].
On the day he purchases the soma, on that day he should combine both:
he should step [the Viṣṇu strides] and attend upon [the fire].
He undertakes the rite beginning with the clenching of the fists.

sanskrit_iast: yadyukhye bhriyamāṇe 'yaṃ devaḥ prajā abhimanyetāgneyībhirbhiṣagvatībhistisṛbhistisraḥ samidha ādadhyāt //
meaning: यद्युख्ये भ्रियमाणे ऽयं देवः प्रजा अभिमन्येताग्नेयीभिर्भिषग्वतीभिस्तिसृभिस्तिस्रः समिध आदध्यात् //
text_mt: If while [the fire] is being carried in the pot, this god should rage against creatures, he should put on three firewood sticks with three verses addressed to Agni containing the word 'physician':
'Bring us your own form as a physician, O Agni of black course;

sanskrit_iast: tvaṃ no agne bhiṣagbhava deveṣu havyavāhanaḥ /
meaning: त्वं नो अग्ने भिषग्भव देवेषु हव्यवाहनः /
text_mt: Be thou our physician, O Agni, carrying the oblation among the gods;
We invoke thee as physician, as physician may we kindle thee;
be a physician for us among the gods.'

sanskrit_iast: yadi kāmayeta varṣediti yāḥ saurī raśmivatīstābhistisṛbhistisraḥ samidha ādadhyāt //
meaning: यदि कामयेत वर्षेदिति याः सौरी रश्मिवतीस्ताभिस्तिसृभिस्तिस्रः समिध आदध्यात् //
text_mt: If he desires, 'May it rain,' he should put on three firewood sticks with three verses addressed to Sūrya containing the word 'ray':
'Sūrya plunges into the waters with his rays, best winner of booty;
be attentive to the singer, thou that increasest vitality!

meaning: परि यो रश्मिना दिवो ऽन्तान्ममे पृथिव्याः /
text_mt: He who with his ray measured the ends of heaven and earth,
filled both world-halves with his greatness.
Traversing, O god, thou spreadest the black thread of wealth without unravelling it,
the brandishing rays of Sūrya have set the darkness within the waters like a skin.'

sanskrit_iast: yadi kāmayeta na varṣediti yāḥ saurīrbhrājasvatīstābhistisṛbhistisraḥ samidha ādadhyāt
meaning: यदि कामयेत न वर्षेदिति याः सौरीर्भ्राजस्वतीस्ताभिस्तिसृभिस्तिस्रः समिध आदध्यात्
text_mt: If he desires, 'May it not rain,' he should put on three firewood sticks with three verses addressed to Sūrya containing the word 'bright':

sanskrit_iast: adṛśvamasya ketavo vi raśmayo janām̐ anu /
meaning: अदृश्वमस्य केतवो वि रश्मयो जनाम्̐ अनु /
text_mt: 'Visible were his banners, his rays among the peoples,
shining like fires…
[and] this [verse]: 'Swift, visible to all…'

sanskrit_iast: divo rukma urucakṣā udeti dūre arthastaraṇirbhrājamānaḥ /
meaning: दिवो रुक्म उरुचक्षा उदेति दूरे अर्थस्तरणिर्भ्राजमानः /
text_mt: 'The golden disc of heaven, wide-seeing, rises, its goal far off, swift, shining;

sanskrit_iast: nūnaṃ jaṇāḥ sūryeṇa prasūtā āyannarthāni kṛṇavannapāṃsīti
meaning: नूनं जणाः सूर्येण प्रसूता आयन्नर्थानि कृणवन्नपांसीति
text_mt: Now may people, impelled by the sun, go to their pursuits and perform their works.'

sanskrit_iast: yadyukhye bhriyamāṇe yajamānasya naśyedagne 'bhyāvartinnagne aṅgiraḥ punarūrjā saha rayyetyetābhiścatasṛbhirupatiṣṭheta
meaning: यद्युख्ये भ्रियमाणे यजमानस्य नश्येदग्ने ऽभ्यावर्तिन्नग्ने अङ्गिरः पुनरूर्जा सह रय्येत्येताभिश्चतसृभिरुपतिष्ठेत
text_mt: If, while the fire in the pan is being carried, something of the sacrificer is lost, he should revere [the fire] with these four verses: 'O Agni, turning back…', 'O Agni, Aṅgiras…', 'Again with strength…', and 'Together with wealth…'
'He surely finds it,' so it is taught.

sanskrit_iast: yadahaḥ prayāyādudu tvā viśve devā ityukhyamudyamya sīda tvaṃ māturasyā upastha iti catasṛbhirdvīṣe śakaṭe prauga ukhyamāsādayati
meaning: यदहः प्रयायादुदु त्वा विश्वे देवा इत्युख्यमुद्यम्य सीद त्वं मातुरस्या उपस्थ इति चतसृभिर्द्वीषे शकटे प्रौग उख्यमासादयति
text_mt: On whichever day he would set out, having raised the fire in the pan with [the verse] 'Up may all the gods [bear] you…', he sets down the fire in the pan in the front-part of a two-poled cart with four [verses beginning]: 'Sit you in the lap of this mother…'
Some say he reveres it with the Haṃsavatī verse.
Having united the other two fires, having caused them to ascend [into fire-sticks], he sets out with [the formula]: 'March forth, O Agni, possessing light…'
He addresses the creaking of the axle with: 'Agni has cried out…'
Having settled [at a new dwelling place], he puts on a firewood stick smeared with ghee when he has halted, with [the verse]: 'Tend the fire with firewood…'
With the subsequent Triṣṭubh verse for a Rājanya;
When the kindling of the fire, the vow-meal, and the settling coincide, he places the [stick] smeared with ghee first.

sanskrit_iast: yadyukhāṃ bhasmābhiniṣīdedukhyamādāyodakāntaṃ gatvemaṃ suyoniṃ suvṛtaṃ hiraṇmayaṃ sahasrabhṛṣṭiṃ mahiṣāvaroha /
meaning: यद्युखां भस्माभिनिषीदेदुख्यमादायोदकान्तं गत्वेमं सुयोनिं सुवृतं हिरण्मयं सहस्रभृष्टिं महिषावरोह /
text_mt: If ash settles down into the pan, having taken the fire in the pan and gone to the edge of the water, [with the two verses]: 'Descend, O mighty one, into this good womb, well-turned, golden, thousand-pointed;
Enjoy the sweet spring, enter into the oceanic dwelling;'

sanskrit_iast: imaṃ stanaṃ madhumantaṃ dhyāpāṃ prapyātamagne sarirasya madhe /
meaning: इमं स्तनं मधुमन्तं ध्यापां प्रप्यातमग्ने सरिरस्य मधे /
text_mt: 'This sweet breast of the waters, swollen in the midst of the ocean, O Agni;

sanskrit_iast: utsaṃ juṣasva madhumantamūrva samudriyaṃ sadanamāviśasvetyetābhyāmukhāyā agnimddhṛtyānirūhañchikyādukhāmāpo devīḥ prati gṛhṇīta bhasmaitaditi tisṛbhirapsu bhasma praveśayati
meaning: उत्सं जुषस्व मधुमन्तमूर्व समुद्रियं सदनमाविशस्वेत्येताभ्यामुखाया अग्निम्द्धृत्यानिरूहञ्छिक्यादुखामापो देवीः प्रति गृह्णीत भस्मैतदिति तिसृभिरप्सु भस्म प्रवेशयति
text_mt: Enjoy the sweet spring, enter into the oceanic dwelling'—having raised the fire from the pan with these two [verses], without removing the pan from the halter, he introduces the ash into the waters with three [verses beginning]: 'O divine waters, receive this ash…'

sanskrit_iast: bhasmano 'pādāya prapīḍya prasadya bhasmaneti dvābhyāmukhāyāṃ pratyavadhāya punarūrjā saha rayyeti punarudaiti
meaning: भस्मनो ऽपादाय प्रपीड्य प्रसद्य भस्मनेति द्वाभ्यामुखायां प्रत्यवधाय पुनरूर्जा सह रय्येति पुनरुदैति
text_mt: Having taken [a portion] of the ash, squeezed it, and placed it back into the pan with two [verses beginning]: 'Settling with the ash…', he steps out [of the water] with: 'Again with strength, together with wealth…'
He kindles the fire in the pan again with: 'Again may the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus kindle you…'
He reveres [the fire] with the two Bodhavatī verses: 'Wake…', 'Be awake…'
The introduction of the ash into the waters is obligatory for a consecrated [sacrificer] when the bricks have been made.
When they have not been made, it serves the purpose of mixture [with the clay].
One who desires cattle should place it into the loose soil.
A wandering mendicant should cast it into the waters.

He makes the bricks for a consecrated [sacrificer] in the consecration procedures lasting a month or more; before [the consecration] for an unconsecrated one in other cases; [or] after the Prājāpatya animal sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast: mṛnmayīriṣṭakāḥ karoti pādamātryo 'ratnimātrya ūrvasthimātry 'ṇūkamātrya ṛjulekhā dakṣiṇāvṛtaḥ savyāvṛtastryālikhitāśca
meaning: मृन्मयीरिष्टकाः करोति पादमात्र्यो ऽरत्निमात्र्य ऊर्वस्थिमात्र्य् ऽणूकमात्र्य ऋजुलेखा दक्षिणावृतः सव्यावृतस्त्र्यालिखिताश्च
text_mt: He makes the earthen bricks: of the measure of a foot, of the measure of a cubit, of the measure of a thigh-bone, of the measure of an ankle-bone, straight-lined, turned to the right, turned to the left, and marked with three lines.
They bake them red with churned-out fire.
He should not lay one that is broken, black, or spotted.

sanskrit_iast: puṣkaraparṇaṃ rukmo hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣaḥ srucau sapta svayamātṛṇāḥ śarkarā hiraṇyeṣṭakāḥ pañca ghṛteṣṭakā dūrvāstambaḥ kūrma ulūkhalaṃ musalaṃ śūrpamaśmānaḥ paśuśirāṃsi sarpaśiraścāmṛnmayīriṣṭakāḥ
meaning: पुष्करपर्णं रुक्मो हिरण्मयः पुरुषः स्रुचौ सप्त स्वयमातृणाः शर्करा हिरण्येष्टकाः पञ्च घृतेष्टका दूर्वास्तम्बः कूर्म उलूखलं मुसलं शूर्पमश्मानः पशुशिरांसि सर्पशिरश्चामृन्मयीरिष्टकाः
text_mt: A lotus leaf, a golden disc, a golden man, two ladles, seven naturally perforated [stones], pebbles, golden bricks, five ghee bricks, a clump of dūrvā grass, a tortoise, a mortar, a pestle, a winnowing basket, stones, heads of animals, and a head of a serpent are the non-earthen bricks.
One who piles [the altar] for the first time should pile [it] knee-deep, of a thousand [bricks];
Navel-deep, of two thousand [bricks], for the second;
Mouth-deep, of three thousand [bricks], for the third;
Each subsequent one larger.
'One who desires heaven should pile it great, lofty, unmeasured,' so says the Vājasaneyaka.

sanskrit_iast: apavṛtte dīkṣāparimāṇe 'peta vīteti gārhapatyaciterāyatanaṃ vyāyāmamātraṃ caturasraṃ parimaṇḍalaṃ voddhatya hariṇyā palāśaśākhayā śamīśākhayā vā saṃmṛjya prācīmudīcīṃ vā śākhāmudasitvā śaṃ no devīrabhiṣṭaya ityadbhiravokṣyāgnerbhasmāsīti sikatā nivapati
meaning: अपवृत्ते दीक्षापरिमाणे ऽपेत वीतेति गार्हपत्यचितेरायतनं व्यायाममात्रं चतुरस्रं परिमण्डलं वोद्धत्य हरिण्या पलाशशाखया शमीशाखया वा संमृज्य प्राचीमुदीचीं वा शाखामुदसित्वा शं नो देवीरभिष्टय इत्यद्भिरवोक्ष्याग्नेर्भस्मासीति सिकता निवपति
text_mt: When the measure of the consecration has passed, having dug up the site of the gārhapatya piling measuring a fathom, square or round, with [the formula] 'Begone! Depart…', having swept it with a leafy branch of palāśa or a branch of śamī, having cast away the branch toward the east or the north, and having sprinkled it with water with 'May the divine waters be for our aid…', he pours out sand with 'You are the ash of Agni…'
While pouring them out, he meditates in mind: 'What is black yonder in the moon, let that be here.'

sanskrit_iast: saṃ yā vaḥ priyāstanuva ityūṣānsikatāśca saṃsṛjya cita stha paricita ityekaviṃśatyā śarkarābhirgārhapatyaciterāyatanaṃ pariśrayati /
meaning: सं या वः प्रियास्तनुव इत्यूषान्सिकताश्च संसृज्य चित स्थ परिचित इत्येकविंशत्या शर्कराभिर्गार्हपत्यचितेरायतनं परिश्रयति /
text_mt: Having mixed the saline earth and the sand with 'Together your dear bodies…', he encloses the site of the gārhapatya piling with twenty-one pebbles, [reciting]: 'You are piled, you are enclosed…';
three by three joined together.

sanskrit_iast: vrajaṃ kṛṇudhvaṃ sa hi vo nṛpāṇo varma sīvyadhvaṃ bahulā pṛthūni /
meaning: व्रजं कृणुध्वं स हि वो नृपाणो वर्म सीव्यध्वं बहुला पृथूनि /
text_mt: 'Make an enclosure, for it is your protection for men; sew armor thick and wide;

sanskrit_iast: puraḥ kṛṇudhvamāyasīradhṛṣṭā mā vaḥ susroccamaso dṛṃhatā tamiti śarkarā abhimantryāyaṃ so agniriti catasro madhye prācīriṣṭakā gārhapatyacitāvupadadhāti
meaning: पुरः कृणुध्वमायसीरधृष्टा मा वः सुस्रोच्चमसो दृंहता तमिति शर्करा अभिमन्त्र्यायं सो अग्निरिति चतस्रो मध्ये प्राचीरिष्टका गार्हपत्यचितावुपदधाति
text_mt: Make forts of iron, unassailable; let not your goblet leak, make it firm'—having addressed the pebbles with this [verse], he places four bricks facing east in the middle on the gārhapatya piling, with: 'This is that Agni…'

sanskrit_iast: iḍāmagne 'yaṃ te yonirṛtviya iti dve purastātsamīcī tiraścī vā
meaning: इडामग्ने ऽयं ते योनिरृत्विय इति द्वे पुरस्तात्समीची तिरश्ची वा
text_mt: [He places] two in front, turned toward each other or across, with: 'Refreshment, O Agni…' and 'This is your seasonal womb…'
In the same way [two] behind, with: 'You are piled,' and 'You are enclosed.'
He covers the remaining [space] with thirteen space-filler [bricks].

sanskrit_iast: lokaṃ pṛṇa tā asya sūdadohasa iti dvābhyāṃdvābhyām mantrābhyāmekaikāṃ lokaṃpṛṇāmupadadhāti
meaning: लोकं पृण ता अस्य सूददोहस इति द्वाभ्यांद्वाभ्याम् मन्त्राभ्यामेकैकां लोकंपृणामुपदधाति
text_mt: He places each space-filler [brick] with two formulas each: 'Fill the space…' and 'These, his milking draughts…'
Over all the bricks, he continuously places [the formula]: 'By that deity…'
Having brought loose soil from the pit-mound, he scatters it over the piling with the Vaiśvānara verse: 'Revered in heaven…'
One who piles for the first time should pile [an altar] of five layers;
From then on, he should pile only one-layered ones.

sanskrit_iast: ajījanannamṛtaṃ martyāsa iti gārhapatyacitimabhimṛśya samitamiti tasyāṃ catasṛbhirukhyaṃ saṃnivapati
meaning: अजीजनन्नमृतं मर्त्यास इति गार्हपत्यचितिमभिमृश्य समितमिति तस्यां चतसृभिरुख्यं संनिवपति
text_mt: Having touched the gārhapatya piling with 'Mortals have begotten the immortal…', he pours out together the fire in the pan onto it with four [formulas beginning]: 'Together…'

sanskrit_iast: vijñāyate ca vi vā etau dviṣāte yaścokhāyāṃ yaśca cīyate /
meaning: विज्ञायते च वि वा एतौ द्विषाते यश्चोखायां यश्च चीयते /
text_mt: And it is taught: 'These two surely hate each other: the one in the pan and the one that is piled.
When he distributes [the fire] having poured them together, he pacifies them with the holy power alone.'

sanskrit_iast: sākaṃ hi śucinā śuciḥ praśāstā kratunājani /
meaning: साकं हि शुचिना शुचिः प्रशास्ता क्रतुनाजनि /
text_mt: 'For together with the pure one the pure ruler was born through wisdom;

sanskrit_iast: vidvām̐ asya vratā ghruvā vayā ivānu rohata iti saṃnyuptāvabhimantrya mateva putramiti śikyādukhāṃ nirūhya yadasya pāre rajasa iti vaiśvānaryā śikyamādatte
meaning: विद्वाम्̐ अस्य व्रता घ्रुवा वया इवानु रोहत इति संन्युप्तावभिमन्त्र्य मतेव पुत्रमिति शिक्यादुखां निरूह्य यदस्य पारे रजस इति वैश्वानर्या शिक्यमादत्ते
text_mt: Knowing his fixed ordinances, they grow up like branches'—having addressed the two [fires] poured together with this [verse], having removed the pan from the halter with 'Like a mother her son…', he takes the halter with the Vaiśvānara verse: 'What is on the other side of this space…'

sanskrit_iast: nairṛtīriṣṭakāḥ kṛṣṇāstisrastuṣapakvāstāḥ śikyaṃ rukmasūtramāsandīṃ cādāya dakṣiṇamaparamavāntaradeśaṃ gatvā namaḥ su te nirṛta iti svakṛta iriṇe pradare vā śikyaṃ nidhāya tasyeṣṭakābhiḥ pāśamabhyupadadhāti
meaning: नैरृतीरिष्टकाः कृष्णास्तिस्रस्तुषपक्वास्ताः शिक्यं रुक्मसूत्रमासन्दीं चादाय दक्षिणमपरमवान्तरदेशं गत्वा नमः सु ते निरृत इति स्वकृत इरिणे प्रदरे वा शिक्यं निधाय तस्येष्टकाभिः पाशमभ्युपदधाति
text_mt: Having taken the bricks of Nirṛti—three black ones, baked with chaff—as well as the sling, the gold ornament's cord, and the stool, and having gone to the south-western intermediate quarter, having placed the sling in a natural cleft or in a chasm with the verse: “Homage indeed to you, O Nirṛti,” he sets down [the bricks] upon its noose.

sanskrit_iast: yasyāste asyāḥ krūra āsañjuhomītyetābhistisṛbhiḥ parācīrasaṃspṛṣṭā dakṣiṇāpavargam
meaning: यस्यास्ते अस्याः क्रूर आसञ्जुहोमीत्येताभिस्तिसृभिः पराचीरसंस्पृष्टा दक्षिणापवर्गम्
text_mt: With these three [formulas]: “In whose cruel mouth I sacrifice...”, [he sets down the bricks] facing away, touching each other, ending towards the south.

sanskrit_iast: yatte devī nirṛtirābabandheti śikyajālenaināḥ pracchādya rukmasūtramāsandīṃ ca parastānnidhāyāpāsmadetu nirṛtirnehāsyā api kiṃcana /
meaning: यत्ते देवी निरृतिराबबन्धेति शिक्यजालेनैनाः प्रच्छाद्य रुक्मसूत्रमासन्दीं च परस्तान्निधायापास्मदेतु निरृतिर्नेहास्या अपि किंचन /
text_mt: Having covered them with the netting of the sling with: “What the goddess Nirṛti has bound...”, and having placed the gold ornament's cord and the stool beyond, [with the verses]: “May Nirṛti go away from us; may not even a little of her remain here;
Lack of cattle, destruction, evil—all that we drive away.
Away from us the nooses of Nirṛti, and the hundred and one deaths, which [she brings],

sanskrit_iast: apāsya ye sināḥ pāśā mṛtyūnekaśataṃ suve //
meaning: अपास्य ये सिनाः पाशा मृत्यूनेकशतं सुवे //
text_mt: Away from him whatever binding nooses, the hundred and one deaths, I dispel.

sanskrit_iast: ye te pāśā ekaśataṃ mṛtyo martyāya hantave /
meaning: ये ते पाशा एकशतं मृत्यो मर्त्याय हन्तवे /
text_mt: Whatever hundred and one nooses are yours, O Death, to kill mortal man,
All of them through the power of the sacrifice we appease through sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast: devīmahaṃ nirṛtiṃ bādhamānaḥ piteva putraṃ dasaye vacobhiḥ /
meaning: देवीमहं निरृतिं बाधमानः पितेव पुत्रं दसये वचोभिः /
text_mt: Repelling the goddess Nirṛti, as a father wearying his son with words,

sanskrit_iast: viśvasya yā jāyamānasya veda śiraḥśiraḥ prati sūrī vicaṣṭa ityetābhiścatasṛbhirupahitā abhimantrya yadasya pāre rajasa iti vaiśvānaryā pariṣicya bhūtyai nama ityupasthāyāpratīkṣamāyanti
meaning: विश्वस्य या जायमानस्य वेद शिरःशिरः प्रति सूरी विचष्ट इत्येताभिश्चतसृभिरुपहिता अभिमन्त्र्य यदस्य पारे रजस इति वैश्वानर्या परिषिच्य भूत्यै नम इत्युपस्थायाप्रतीक्षमायन्ति
text_mt: Who knows of every creature being born, wise, she surveys head by head”—having addressed [the bricks] thus placed with these four [verses], having poured water around with the Vaiśvānara verse: “What is on the other side of this space...”, having reverenced them with: “Homage to prosperity,” they return without looking back.
“For the concealment of Nirṛti,” so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].
They cleanse themselves with water with: “May the divine waters be for our welfare...”

sanskrit_iast: ūrjaṃ bibhradvasumanāḥ sumedhā gṛhānaimi manasā modamānaḥ suvarcāḥ /
meaning: ऊर्जं बिभ्रद्वसुमनाः सुमेधा गृहानैमि मनसा मोदमानः सुवर्चाः /
text_mt: “Bearing nourishment, well-minded, wise, of goodly splendor, I enter the house, rejoicing in mind;

sanskrit_iast: aghoreṇa cakṣuṣāhaṃ śivena gṛhāṇāṃ paśyanvaya uttirāṇi //
meaning: अघोरेण चक्षुषाहं शिवेन गृहाणां पश्यन्वय उत्तिराणि //
text_mt: With an unfeared, auspicious eye, looking at the houses, may I prolong life.

sanskrit_iast: gṛhāṇāmāyuḥ pra vayaṃ tirāmo gṛhā asmākaṃ pra tirantvāyuḥ /
meaning: गृहाणामायुः प्र वयं तिरामो गृहा अस्माकं प्र तिरन्त्वायुः /
text_mt: We prolong the life of the houses; may the houses prolong our life;

sanskrit_iast: gṝnahaṃ sumanasaḥ prapadye 'vīraghno vīravataḥ suvīrāniti gṛhānabheti
meaning: गॄनहं सुमनसः प्रपद्ये ऽवीरघ्नो वीरवतः सुवीरानिति गृहानभेति
text_mt: I enter the houses, well-disposed, not slaying our men, full of heroes, possessed of noble men”—with this [verse] he approaches the houses.
They worship the āhavanīya or the gārhapatya with: “The resting place, the assembler of wealth...”
He undertakes the rite beginning with the measuring out of the king [Soma].
Having performed the prāyaṇīyā offering, he measures out the altar ground.
“Having released speech with [the call to] the maker of the oblation,” according to the Vājasaneyaka.
He undertakes the rite beginning with taking [ghee] from the dhruvā ladle for the prāyaṇīyā.
Having performed the ātithyā offering, he measures out the fire [altar].
“Having released speech with [the call to] the maker of the oblation,” according to the Vājasaneyaka.

sanskrit_iast: samūlaṃ haritaṃ darbhastambamāhṛtya madhye 'gnernikhāya juhvāṃ pañcagṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā sajūrabdo 'yāvabhiriti darbhastambe pañcāhutīrjuhoti
meaning: समूलं हरितं दर्भस्तम्बमाहृत्य मध्ये ऽग्नेर्निखाय जुह्वां पञ्चगृहीतं गृहीत्वा सजूरब्दो ऽयावभिरिति दर्भस्तम्बे पञ्चाहुतीर्जुहोति
text_mt: Having brought a green clump of darbha grass along with its roots, having buried it in the middle of the fire [altar], having taken five ladlings into the juhū ladle, he offers five oblations on the clump of darbha grass with: “The year in union with the unassailable...”
He measures out the fire [altar] with a bamboo rod as long as the sacrificer with his arms raised upward:
Three [bamboo rods] to the east, four to the north.
The wings and the tail are one puruṣa in size [each].
He lengthens the right wing to the south by a cubit.
The tail to the west by a span or a vitasti.
The first fire [altar] has a single measure [of one puruṣa];
They rise in this manner up to one of a hundred and one measures.

sanskrit_iast: tadu ha vai saptavidhameva cinvīta saptavidho vāva prākṛto 'gnistata ūrdhvamekottarāniti vājasaneyakam
meaning: तदु ह वै सप्तविधमेव चिन्वीत सप्तविधो वाव प्राकृतो ऽग्निस्तत ऊर्ध्वमेकोत्तरानिति वाजसनेयकम्
text_mt: “Now, he should build only a sevenfold one; indeed the basic fire [altar] is sevenfold; beyond that, they increase by one,” according to the Vājasaneyaka.
“Be pleasant, O earth, thornless, a resting place;
Grant us wide-spreading refuge. //”
With these two verses: [“Be pleasant, O earth...” and] “Truly of the mountains...”, they step upon the measured fire [altar ground].
He issues the call: “Fasten the straps together!”
With: “The pit whose trough is prepared...”, he pours water from the pit into the troughs.
They water the oxen at them.
“The yoking-loop, the inner pole-pin, the shaft, the axle-peg, the hoof,

sanskrit_iast: aṣṭrāṃ tālaṃ pratīnāhamubhe maṇḍūkyau yujāviti yugalāṅgalaṃ saṃprasārayati
meaning: अष्ट्रां तालं प्रतीनाहमुभे मण्डूक्यौ युजाविति युगलाङ्गलं संप्रसारयति
text_mt: The goad, the palm, the outer band, both frog-pieces joined together”—with this formula, he lays out the yoke and the plough.

sanskrit_iast: sīrā yuñjantīti dvābhyāṃ sīraṃ yunakti ṣaḍgavaṃ dvādaśagavaṃ caturviṃśatigavaṃ vā
meaning: सीरा युञ्जन्तीति द्वाभ्यां सीरं युनक्ति षड्गवं द्वादशगवं चतुर्विंशतिगवं वा
text_mt: With the two verses: “They yoke the ploughs...”, he yokes the plough with a team of six oxen, twelve oxen, or twenty-four oxen.
“Of the two draft-oxen, of the two quick ones, and of the two to be bound,

sanskrit_iast: sarveṣāṃ vidma vo nāma vāhāḥ kīlālapeśasa iti yuktānabhimantryodasthādhojiddhanajidaśvajiddhiraṇyajitsūnṛtayā parīvṛtaḥ /
meaning: सर्वेषां विद्म वो नाम वाहाः कीलालपेशस इति युक्तानभिमन्त्र्योदस्थाधोजिद्धनजिदश्वजिद्धिरण्यजित्सूनृतया परीवृतः /
text_mt: We know the name of all of you, draft-animals adorned with drink”—having addressed the yoked [oxen] with this verse, [and then reciting]: “The winner of food, winner of wealth, winner of horses, winner of gold has arisen, encompassed by gracious speech;

sanskrit_iast: ekacakreṇa savitā rathenorjo bhāgaṃ pṛthivīmetvāpṛṇanniti lāṅgalamucchrayati
meaning: एकचक्रेण सविता रथेनोर्जो भागं पृथिवीमेत्वापृणन्निति लाङ्गलमुच्छ्रयति
text_mt: May Savitṛ with his one-wheeled chariot come to the earth, filling the portion of nourishment”—he raises the plough.
This is [the verse]: “The prayer born first...”

sanskrit_iast: anāptā yā vaḥ prathamā yasyāṃ karmāṇi kṛṇvate /
meaning: अनाप्ता या वः प्रथमा यस्यां कर्माणि कृण्वते /
text_mt: “The first [abode] of yours that is unreached, upon which they perform rites,

sanskrit_iast: vīrānno atra mā dabhaṃstadva etatpuro dadhe //
meaning: वीरान्नो अत्र मा दभंस्तद्व एतत्पुरो दधे //
text_mt: May they not harm our heroes here; this of yours I place before you.

sanskrit_iast: paryū ṣu pra dhanva vājasātaye pari vṛtrāṇi sakṣaṇiḥ /
meaning: पर्यू षु प्र धन्व वाजसातये परि वृत्राणि सक्षणिः /
text_mt: Flow forward well for the winning of prize, overcoming the foes;
Like an exacter of debts to overcome the haters, you speed.

sanskrit_iast: sahasradhāre 'va te samasvarandivo nāke madhujihvā asaścataḥ /
meaning: सहस्रधारे ऽव ते समस्वरन्दिवो नाके मधुजिह्वा असश्चतः /
text_mt: In a thousand streams they sounded down to you, honey-tongued, untiring in the vault of heaven;

sanskrit_iast: asya spaśo na ni miṣanti bhūrṇayaḥ padepade pāśinaḥ santi setava iti brahmavarmāṇi juhoti
meaning: अस्य स्पशो न नि मिषन्ति भूर्णयः पदेपदे पाशिनः सन्ति सेतव इति ब्रह्मवर्माणि जुहोति
text_mt: His watchers do not close their eyes, eager; at every step there are snare-holders, binding cords”—with these [formulas] he offers the brahmavarmā oblations.

sanskrit_iast: malimluco nāmāsi trayodaśo māsa indrasya varmāsīndrasya śarmāsīndrasya varūthamasi taṃ tvā prapadye
meaning: मलिम्लुचो नामासि त्रयोदशो मास इन्द्रस्य वर्मासीन्द्रस्य शर्मासीन्द्रस्य वरूथमसि तं त्वा प्रपद्ये
text_mt: With 'You are named the robber (Malimluca), the thirteenth month; you are Indra's armour, you are Indra's shelter, you are Indra's protection; I take refuge in you,'
'I enter the gāyatrī with my body hairs;
I enter the triṣṭubh with my skin;
I enter the jagatī with my flesh;
I enter the anuṣṭubh with my bones;
I enter the paṅkti with my marrow;

sanskrit_iast: aindrāgnaṃ varma bahulaṃ yadugraṃ viśve devā nātividhyanti sūrāḥ /
meaning: ऐन्द्राग्नं वर्म बहुलं यदुग्रं विश्वे देवा नातिविध्यन्ति सूराः /
text_mt: The armour of Indra and Agni, which is thick and formidable, which all the gods, the heroes, cannot pierce through:

sanskrit_iast: tannastrāyatāṃ tanno viśvato mahadāyuṣmanto jarāmupagacchema devā iti vimitamagnimākrmante
meaning: तन्नस्त्रायतां तन्नो विश्वतो महदायुष्मन्तो जरामुपगच्छेम देवा इति विमितमग्निमाक्र्मन्ते
text_mt: May that protect us, may that great [armour] protect us from all sides; endowed with long life, may we attain old age, O gods'—with [these formulas] they step into the measured shed of the fire.
With the two verses beginning 'The plough equipped with a lance…', he ploughs.
Ploughmen drive the oxen.
He ploughs from the tail to the head.

sanskrit_iast: kāmaṃ kāmadugho dhukṣveti pradakṣiṇamāvartayaṃstisrastisraḥ sītāḥ saṃhitāḥ kṛṣati
meaning: कामं कामदुघो धुक्ष्वेति प्रदक्षिणमावर्तयंस्तिस्रस्तिस्रः सीताः संहिताः कृषति
text_mt: Saying, 'Yield desire, yielding wishes,' turning in a sunwise direction, he ploughs sets of three furrows joined together.
They meet in the middle:
From the southern wing to the northern wing;
From the southern hip to the northern shoulder;
'Be unyoked, O unslayable cows, moving on the path of the gods; we have crossed to the other side of this darkness;

sanskrit_iast: jyotirāpāma suvaraganmeti dakṣiṇe 'ṃsa uttare vā balīvardānvimucya tānudīcaḥ prāco votsṛjyādhvaryave dadāti
meaning: ज्योतिरापाम सुवरगन्मेति दक्षिणे ऽंस उत्तरे वा बलीवर्दान्विमुच्य तानुदीचः प्राचो वोत्सृज्याध्वर्यवे ददाति
text_mt: We have attained the light, we have gone to heaven'—having unyoked the oxen at the southern or northern shoulder, having released them towards the north or the east, he gives them to the adhvaryu.
The Vājasaneyins prescribe a four-cornered [ploughing], not crossing in the middle, having sixteen furrows.
He pours out fifteen vessels of water:
Twelve on the ploughed [ground], three on the unploughed.
With the fourteen verses beginning 'The plants which were born…', he sows seeds of plants.

sanskrit_iast: tilamāṣā vrīhiyavāḥ priyaṅgvaṇavo godhūmā veṇuśyāmākanīvārā jartilaśca gavīdhukā āraṇyajā markaṭakā vijñeyāḥ
meaning: तिलमाषा व्रीहियवाः प्रियङ्ग्वणवो गोधूमा वेणुश्यामाकनीवारा जर्तिलश्च गवीधुका आरण्यजा मर्कटका विज्ञेयाः
text_mt: Sesame, black gram, rice, barley, foxtail millet, panic seed, wheat, wild panic, wild rice, wild sesame, and Coix lacryma-jobi, and wild Markaṭaka-grains are to be known [as the seeds].

sanskrit_iast: gārmutasaptamāḥ kulatthasaptamā vā sapta grāmyāḥ kṛṣṭe /
meaning: गार्मुतसप्तमाः कुलत्थसप्तमा वा सप्त ग्राम्याः कृष्टे /
text_mt: Seven cultivated seeds, with Gārmuta as the seventh or with horsegram as the seventh, [he sows] on the ploughed ground;
Whichsoever plant he may not obtain, in its place he should sow barley mixed with honey;

meaning: उप्ता मे ऽसीति वा मनसा ध्यायेत्
text_mt: Or he should meditate in mind: 'You are sown by me.'
When it is obtained, he should bind it up onto whichever firewood comes first.
Those trees which bear fruit—having bound them onto the firewood, he should sprinkle them.

sanskrit_iast: mā no hiṃsījjanitā yaḥ pṛthivyā iti catasṛbhirdigbhyo loṣṭānsamasyati ye 'ntarvidhādbahirvidhamāpannā bhavanti
meaning: मा नो हिंसीज्जनिता यः पृथिव्या इति चतसृभिर्दिग्भ्यो लोष्टान्समस्यति ये ऽन्तर्विधाद्बहिर्विधमापन्ना भवन्ति
text_mt: With the four verses beginning 'May he not harm us who is the creator of the earth…', he gathers from the directions the clods of earth that have fallen outside the perimeter from inside the perimeter.

sanskrit_iast: yaṃ dviṣyādyatra sa syāttasyai diśo jaghanyaṃ loṣṭamāharediṣamūrjamahamita ādada iti
meaning: यं द्विष्याद्यत्र स स्यात्तस्यै दिशो जघन्यं लोष्टमाहरेदिषमूर्जमहमित आदद इति
text_mt: Whomever he might hate, from whichever direction that man might be, from that direction he should fetch the last clod with the formula: 'Here I take sap and nourishment.'
With the verse 'Furrow, with ghee…', he touches the spaces between the furrows,
He strews the high altar to the size of the fire-altar.

sanskrit_iast: vyāghāraṇāntāṃ kṛtvāgne tava śravo vaya iti ṣaḍbhiḥ sikatā nyupya cita stha paricita ityaparimitābhiḥ śarkarābhirāhavanīyaciterāyatanaṃ pariśrayati yathā gārhapatyasyaivam
meaning: व्याघारणान्तां कृत्वाग्ने तव श्रवो वय इति षड्भिः सिकता न्युप्य चित स्थ परिचित इत्यपरिमिताभिः शर्कराभिराहवनीयचितेरायतनं परिश्रयति यथा गार्हपत्यस्यैवम्
text_mt: Having made it end with libation-streaks, having scattered sand with the six verses beginning 'O Agni, your fame, vigor…', he surrounds the seat of the āhavanīya-pile with an unlimited number of pebbles with the formula: 'You are piled, you are enclosed,' just as [was done] for the gārhapatya.
With three times seven [pebbles] for one desiring cattle;
With three times nine for one who has a rival;
With tens for one desiring food;
With an unlimited number for one who has unlimited desire.
For one whom he wishes should be without cattle, 'without measuring for him' has been stated.

sanskrit_iast: āpyāyasva sametu ta iti sikatā vyūhati
meaning: आप्यायस्व समेतु त इति सिकता व्यूहति
text_mt: With the verse 'Swell, let [vigor] gather to you…', he levels the sand.
With the subsequent triṣṭubh verse for a rājanya:

sanskrit_iast: asāvi somo aruṣo vṛṣā harī rajeva dasmo abhi gā acikradat /
meaning: असावि सोमो अरुषो वृषा हरी रजेव दस्मो अभि गा अचिक्रदत् /
text_mt: 'Soma, ruddy, a bull, tawny, has been pressed out; like a king, wonder-working, he roared towards the cows;

sanskrit_iast: punāno vāraṃ paryetyavyayaṃ śyeno na yoniṃ ghṛtavantamāsadamiti jagatyā vaiśayasya
meaning: पुनानो वारं पर्येत्यव्ययं श्येनो न योनिं घृतवन्तमासदमिति जगत्या वैशयस्य
text_mt: Purifying himself, he passes through the sheep's wool filter, to sit, like an eagle, in his ghee-abounding home'—with this jagatī verse for a vaiśya.
Starting from 'From the steady [ladle] of the Ātithyā…', he undertakes this rite.

sanskrit_iast: paurvāhṇikībhyāṃ pracaryāgreṇa prāgvaṃśaṃ lohite carmaṇyānaḍuhe prācīnagrīva uttaralomni prathamasyāściteriṣṭakāḥ saṃsādayati /
meaning: पौर्वाह्णिकीभ्यां प्रचर्याग्रेण प्राग्वंशं लोहिते चर्मण्यानडुहे प्राचीनग्रीव उत्तरलोम्नि प्रथमस्याश्चितेरिष्टकाः संसादयति /
text_mt: Having performed the two morning offerings, in front of the eastern hall, on a red ox-hide with the neck turned to the east and the hair side turned upwards, he places together the bricks of the first layer,
Or three naturally perforated bricks and three Viśvajyotis bricks.

sanskrit_iast: tā darbhāgramuṣṭinājyena vyavokṣya samudyamya cityagnibhyaḥ praṇīyamānebhyo 'nubrūhīti saṃpreṣyati /
meaning: ता दर्भाग्रमुष्टिनाज्येन व्यवोक्ष्य समुद्यम्य चित्यग्निभ्यः प्रणीयमानेभ्यो ऽनुब्रूहीति संप्रेष्यति /
text_mt:
Having sprinkled them with clarified butter with a handful of darbha tops, having lifted them up, he issues the command: 'Recite for the fires of the pile being brought forward!'

Or: 'Recite for [the fires] being brought forward!'

sanskrit_iast: prathamāyāṃ triranūktāyāṃ hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgra iti prāñco 'śvaprathamā abhipravrajanti
meaning: प्रथमायां त्रिरनूक्तायां हिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्र इति प्राञ्चो ऽश्वप्रथमा अभिप्रव्रजन्ति
text_mt: When the first [verse] has been recited three times, with the verse 'The golden embryo arose in the beginning…', they advance towards the east, led by a horse.
They lead a white horse in front.

sanskrit_iast: prajāpatistvā sādayatu tayā devatayāṅgirasvaddhruvā sīdetyuttaravedimabhimṛśya mayi gṛhṇāmyagre agniṃ yo no agniḥ pitara iti dvābhyāmātmannagniṃ gṛhītvā yāste agne samidha iti svayaṃcityābhimṛśati
meaning: प्रजापतिस्त्वा सादयतु तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद्ध्रुवा सीदेत्युत्तरवेदिमभिमृश्य मयि गृह्णाम्यग्रे अग्निं यो नो अग्निः पितर इति द्वाभ्यामात्मन्नग्निं गृहीत्वा यास्ते अग्ने समिध इति स्वयंचित्याभिमृशति
text_mt: Having touched the high altar with 'May Prajāpati seat you; by that deity, firm in the manner of the Aṅgirases, sit firm,' having taken the fire into himself with the two verses 'I take Agni into myself in the beginning…' and 'The fire which is our fathers'…', he touches [the bricks] with the Svayaṃciti formula: 'Whatever firewood is yours, O Agni…'
The adhvaryu or the sacrificer piles the fire with the bricks.
Piling it himself, he does not take the fire into himself nor does he touch it with the Svayaṃciti formula.
'He places [them] facing east, he places [them] facing west' refers to the lines of bricks in groups.
'He places [it] facing east, he places [it] facing west' refers to the face of the performer.
The white horse stands to the south.

sanskrit_iast: tamālabhyendraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhannityuttareṇa pucchāpyayamantarvidha ākramaṇaṃ pratīṣṭakāmupadadhyāt
meaning: तमालभ्येन्द्रं विश्वा अवीवृधन्नित्युत्तरेण पुच्छाप्ययमन्तर्विध आक्रमणं प्रतीष्टकामुपदध्यात्
text_mt: Having touched it, with the verse: “All songs have magnified Indra...”, he should set down a brick to face the approach to the north of the tail's junction, within the measurement [of the altar].
The approach to the fire [altar] is from the north or from the west.
Every time he ascends and descends, he mutters: “Speech in my mouth...”;

sanskrit_iast: tattvā yāmi brahmaṇā vandamāna iti śālāmukhīye hutvā prāñcamaśvamabhyasthādviśvā iti dakṣiṇena padā darbhastambamākramayya pradakṣiṇamāvartayitvā yadakranda iti punarevākramayati
meaning: तत्त्वा यामि ब्रह्मणा वन्दमान इति शालामुखीये हुत्वा प्राञ्चमश्वमभ्यस्थाद्विश्वा इति दक्षिणेन पदा दर्भस्तम्बमाक्रमय्य प्रदक्षिणमावर्तयित्वा यदक्रन्द इति पुनरेवाक्रमयति
text_mt: Having offered [a libation] in the śālāmukhīya fire with, 'Seeking that, I approach you with a prayer…', having made the horse, facing east, step with its right foot upon a bunch of darbha grass with, 'He has overcome all [adversaries]…', and having made it turn clockwise, he makes it step again with, 'When you first whinnied…'.

sanskrit_iast: apāṃ pṛṣṭhamasītyaśvasya pade puṣkaraparṇamuttānamupadhāyāpāṃ nidhiṃ gāyeti saṃpreṣyati
meaning: अपां पृष्ठमसीत्यश्वस्य पदे पुष्करपर्णमुत्तानमुपधायापां निधिं गायेति संप्रेष्यति
text_mt: Having laid down a lotus leaf turned upwards in the footprint of the horse with, 'You are the back of the waters…', he gives the ritual call: 'Sing the Apāṃ nidhi chant!'

sanskrit_iast: brahma jajñānamiti puṣkaraparṇa upariṣṭānnirbādhaṃ rukmamupadhāya hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgra iti tasminhiraṇmayaṃ puruṣaṃ prācīnamuttānaṃ dakṣiṇenātṛṇaṃ prāṅmukha upadhāya puruṣasāma gāyeti saṃpreṣyati
meaning: ब्रह्म जज्ञानमिति पुष्करपर्ण उपरिष्टान्निर्बाधं रुक्ममुपधाय हिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्र इति तस्मिन्हिरण्मयं पुरुषं प्राचीनमुत्तानं दक्षिणेनातृणं प्राङ्मुख उपधाय पुरुषसाम गायेति संप्रेष्यति
text_mt: Having laid a golden disk with protruding points upon the lotus leaf with, 'The prayer born first…', and facing east, having laid upon it a golden man facing east, turned upwards, south of the naturally perforated brick with, 'The Golden Embryo arose in the beginning…', he gives the ritual call: 'Sing the Puruṣasāma chant!'

sanskrit_iast: drapsaścaskandeti puruṣamabhimṛśya namo astu sarpebhya iti tisṛbhirabhimantrya kṛṇuṣva pāja iti pañcabhiruttaravedivatpuruṣaṃ vyāghārya srucāvupadadhātītyuktam
meaning: द्रप्सश्चस्कन्देति पुरुषमभिमृश्य नमो अस्तु सर्पेभ्य इति तिसृभिरभिमन्त्र्य कृणुष्व पाज इति पञ्चभिरुत्तरवेदिवत्पुरुषं व्याघार्य स्रुचावुपदधातीत्युक्तम्
text_mt: Having touched the man with, 'The drop has fallen…', and having consecrated him with the three [verses], 'Homage be to the serpents…', and having anointed the man with ghee like the uttaravedī with the five [verses], 'Put forth your power…', he lays down the two ladles—this has been taught.

sanskrit_iast: api vāgnestvā tejasā sādayāmītyājyasya pūrṇāṃ kārṣmaryamayīṃ dakṣiṇena puruṣam /
meaning: अपि वाग्नेस्त्वा तेजसा सादयामीत्याज्यस्य पूर्णां कार्ष्मर्यमयीं दक्षिणेन पुरुषम् /
text_mt: Or rather, [he lays down] the one made of kārṣmarya wood, full of clarified butter, to the south of the man with, 'With the splendour of Agni I set you down…';

sanskrit_iast: indrasya tvaujasā sādayāmīti dadhnaḥ pūrṇāmaudumbarīmuttareṇa puruṣam
meaning: इन्द्रस्य त्वौजसा सादयामीति दध्नः पूर्णामौदुम्बरीमुत्तरेण पुरुषम्
text_mt: the one made of udumbara wood, full of curd, to the north of the man with, 'With the power of Indra I set you down…'.
He attends upon the one made of kārṣmarya wood with, 'Agni is the head…';
upon the one made of udumbara wood with, 'You are the [protector] of the sacrifice…'.
Some say: he lays them down with the two verses containing the word mūrdhan, and attends upon them with the two yajus formulas.
Here, having anointed the golden disk as [he did] the man,

sanskrit_iast: dhruvāsi dharuṇāstṛteti svayamatṛṇāmabhimṛśyāśvenopaghrāpya prajāpatistvā sādayatu pṛthivyāḥ pṛṣṭha ityaviduṣā brāhmaṇena saha madhye 'gnerupadadhāti /
meaning: ध्रुवासि धरुणास्तृतेति स्वयमतृणामभिमृश्याश्वेनोपघ्राप्य प्रजापतिस्त्वा सादयतु पृथिव्याः पृष्ठ इत्यविदुषा ब्राह्मणेन सह मध्ये ऽग्नेरुपदधाति /
text_mt: having touched the naturally perforated brick with, 'You are firm, a foundation, spread out…', having made the horse smell it, he lays it down in the middle of the fire altar together with an unlearned brahmin with, 'May Prajāpati set you down on the back of the earth…'
and with this mystical utterance: 'Bhūḥ'.
Having offered in the naturally perforated brick with, 'I offer consciousness…', he breathes out.
He gives a choice gift—one, two, or three—to the unlearned brahmin.
Seated, he lays down the first naturally perforated brick;
He gives the ritual call: 'Sing a chant upon the naturally perforated brick!'
In the same manner, having laid down the second and the third, he gives the ritual call.

sanskrit_iast: yadi manyeta yajamānaḥ pūrvo mātikrānto bhrātṛvya iti pratho 'sītyupahitāṃ prācīmudūhet /
meaning: यदि मन्येत यजमानः पूर्वो मातिक्रान्तो भ्रातृव्य इति प्रथो ऽसीत्युपहितां प्राचीमुदूहेत् /
text_mt: If the sacrificer should think, 'My rival has preceded me,' he should push forward towards the east the laid brick with, 'You are broad…';
or if [he should think], 'He is behind,' [he should push it] towards the west with, 'You are the earth…';
if [he should think], 'He is equal to me,' he should shake it with, 'You are being, you are creation…'.

meaning: तेजो ऽसि तेजो मे यच्छेति हिरण्येष्टकाम्
text_mt: [He lays down] the gold-brick with, 'You are radiance, bestow radiance upon me…';
the round brick with, 'The earth [as a stronghold] of water, with food…'.
'You are being, the seed of creation.
Agni is light, light is Agni.
With that deity, like Aṅgiras, sit firm!'
'You are the sun, the seed of generation.
Sūrya is light, light is Sūrya.
With that deity, like Aṅgiras, sit firm!'—[with these] two ascending bricks [are laid].

sanskrit_iast: kāṇḍātkāṇḍātprarohantīti dvābhyāṃ dūrveṣṭakāṃ saloṣṭaṃ haritaṃ dūrvāstambamapracchinnāgraṃ yathāsyopahitasya svayamātṛṇāyāmagraṃ prāpnuyāditi
meaning: काण्डात्काण्डात्प्ररोहन्तीति द्वाभ्यां दूर्वेष्टकां सलोष्टं हरितं दूर्वास्तम्बमप्रच्छिन्नाग्रं यथास्योपहितस्य स्वयमातृणायामग्रं प्राप्नुयादिति
text_mt: With the two [verses], 'Sprouting shoot from shoot…', [he lays down] the dūrvā-brick: a green clump of dūrvā grass with its clod of earth, its tip uncut, in such a way that its tip reaches the naturally perforated brick when laid down.

sanskrit_iast: prabāhugiṣṭakāyāṃ hiraṇyaśakalāvadhyūhya yāste agne sūrye ruca iti dvābhyāṃ vāmabhṛtam
meaning: प्रबाहुगिष्टकायां हिरण्यशकलावध्यूह्य यास्ते अग्ने सूर्ये रुच इति द्वाभ्यां वामभृतम्
text_mt: Having placed two chips of gold facing outwards on the brick, [he lays down] the vāmabhṛt brick with the two [verses], 'The lights that are yours, O Agni, in the sun…'.
[He lays down] the three retaḥsic bricks with, 'The shining ruler is light…'.

sanskrit_iast: tāsāṃ dve prathamāyāṃ cityāṃ yūna upadadhyāt /
meaning: तासां द्वे प्रथमायां चित्यां यून उपदध्यात् /
text_mt: Of these, he should lay down two in the first layer for a young man;
all of them in the middle layer for a middle-aged man;
one in the first layer and one in the top layer for an old man.
He should lay down either of them for one who is hated.
He lays down this one and that one with a yajus formula;

sanskrit_iast: bṛhaspatistvā sādayatu pṛthivyāḥ pṛṣṭhe jyotiṣmatīmiti viśvajyotiṣam
meaning: बृहस्पतिस्त्वा सादयतु पृथिव्याः पृष्ठे ज्योतिष्मतीमिति विश्वज्योतिषम्
text_mt: [He lays down] the viśvajyotis brick with, 'May Bṛhaspati set you down, full of light, on the back of the earth…'.
[He lays down] the two saṃyānī bricks with, 'You are the chariot of Agni…'.
[He lays down] the two seasonal bricks, having the same deity formula, with, 'Madhu and Mādhava…'.
Along with all the seasonal bricks, he lays down avakā plants.
Some say: he sets them down on avakā plants.
With the two [verses], 'You are the unconquered…', [he lays down] the aṣāḍhā brick, with its mark on top.
For one whom he desires to be wealthier, it has its mark on top—so it has been said.
Having laid down the gharma-brick, [he lays down] the kulāyinī brick.
The two mantras for these two are in the Pravargya.

sanskrit_iast: madhu vātā ṛtāyata iti tisṛbhirdadhnā madhumiśreṇa kūrmamabhyajya mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca na iti purastātsvayamātṛṇāyāḥ pratyañcaṃ jīvantaṃ prāṅmukha upadadhāti
meaning: मधु वाता ऋतायत इति तिसृभिर्दध्ना मधुमिश्रेण कूर्ममभ्यज्य मही द्यौः पृथिवी च न इति पुरस्तात्स्वयमातृणायाः प्रत्यञ्चं जीवन्तं प्राङ्मुख उपदधाति
text_mt: Having smeared a tortoise with curd mixed with honey with the three [verses], 'The winds blow honey for the righteous…', and facing east, he lays it down alive to the east of the naturally perforated brick, facing west, with, 'Wide heaven and earth [protect] us…'.

sanskrit_iast: catasra āśāḥ pracarantvagnaya iti vopadhāyāvakābhiḥ parītaṃsya jālena pracchādya śaṅkubhiḥ pariṇihatyāpāṃ gambhīraṃ gaccha mā tvā sūryaḥ parītāpsīnmo agnirvaiśvānaraḥ /
meaning: चतस्र आशाः प्रचरन्त्वग्नय इति वोपधायावकाभिः परीतंस्य जालेन प्रच्छाद्य शङ्कुभिः परिणिहत्यापां गम्भीरं गच्छ मा त्वा सूर्यः परीताप्सीन्मो अग्निर्वैश्वानरः /
text_mt: Or having laid it down with, 'May the fires move along the four quarters…', having surrounded it with avakā plants, covered it with a net, and fastened it around with pegs, [he addresses it with:] 'Go into the deep of the waters; may Sūrya not scorch you, nor Agni Vaiśvānara;

sanskrit_iast: aghoraḥ prajā abhivipaśyānu tvā divyā vṛṣṭiḥ sacatām //
meaning: अघोरः प्रजा अभिविपश्यानु त्वा दिव्या वृष्टिः सचताम् //
text_mt: not terrible, look upon the creatures; may heavenly rain follow you!
Glide through the three oceans, the heavenly worlds, the lord of waters, the bull among the bricks!

sanskrit_iast: tatra gaccha yatra pūrve paretāḥ purīṣaṃ vasānaḥ svāṃ yoniṃ yathāyathamityupahitamabhimantrayate
meaning: तत्र गच्छ यत्र पूर्वे परेताः पुरीषं वसानः स्वां योनिं यथायथमित्युपहितमभिमन्त्रयते
text_mt: Go thither where the ancients have passed away, wearing loose soil, to your proper place of origin.'—thus he addresses [the tortoise] once laid down.
'Since you, O mortar, are employed in house after house,

sanskrit_iast: iha dyumattamaṃ vada jayatāmiva dundubhiriti prādeśamātraṃ catuḥsraktyaudumbaramulūkhalamuttare 'ṃse prayunakti
meaning: इह द्युमत्तमं वद जयतामिव दुन्दुभिरिति प्रादेशमात्रं चतुःस्रक्त्यौदुम्बरमुलूखलमुत्तरे ऽंसे प्रयुनक्ति
text_mt: sound here most splendidly like the drum of victors'—with [this verse] he places a mortar of udumbara wood, a span in size and four-cornered, in the northern shoulder [of the altar].

sanskrit_iast: uta sma te vanaspate vāto vi vātyagramit /
meaning: उत स्म ते वनस्पते वातो वि वात्यग्रमित् /
text_mt: “And surely, O tree, the wind blows upon your crown;

sanskrit_iast: atho indrāya pātave sunu somamulūkhaleti sarvauṣadhasya pūrayitvāvahatyedaṃ viṣṇurvicakrama iti madhye 'gnerupadadhāti
meaning: अथो इन्द्राय पातवे सुनु सोममुलूखलेति सर्वौषधस्य पूरयित्वावहत्येदं विष्णुर्विचक्रम इति मध्ये ऽग्नेरुपदधाति
text_mt: then press Soma for Indra to drink, O mortar!”—having filled [the mortar] with all herbs and pounded them, with “Here Viṣṇu strode,” he places it in the middle of the fire [site].
With “That highest step of Viṣṇu,” [he places] the pestle.
With “From heaven or, O Viṣṇu,” [he places] the winnowing basket.
“Sewn by the two [hands], with immortality she has come; the ukhā-pot has mounted her sister upon the altar ground.

sanskrit_iast: satyaṃ pūrvairṛṣibhiścākupāno 'gniḥ pravidvāniha tatkarotviti ghṛtenokhāṃ pūrayati /
meaning: सत्यं पूर्वैरृषिभिश्चाकुपानो ऽग्निः प्रविद्वानिह तत्करोत्विति घृतेनोखां पूरयति /
text_mt: Finding truth through the ancient seers, may Agni, knowing well, accomplish it here,”—with this he fills the ukhā-pot with ghee;
or with curd, with honey, or with sand, or with all of them.
Having poured it in, he should not look into it when empty;
Some teachers teach that it is filled after having poured [the milk] down.
“He whom he might wish, ‘May he become hungry,’ for him deficient [filling]”—thus it has been declared.
With “You are the firm earth,” he places [the ukhā-pot] in the middle of the fire [site].

sanskrit_iast: pṛthivi pṛthivyāṃ sīda mātā mātari mātā syonā syonāyāmukhāṃ svasāramadhi vedimasthāt /
meaning: पृथिवि पृथिव्यां सीद माता मातरि माता स्योना स्योनायामुखां स्वसारमधि वेदिमस्थात् /
text_mt: “O earth, sit upon the earth, mother upon mother, mother, gentle upon the gentle; the ukhā-pot has mounted her sister upon the altar ground.

sanskrit_iast: satyaṃ pūrvairṛṣibhiścākupāno 'gniḥ pravidvāniha taddadhātviti volūkhalmupadadhātīti vājasaneyakam
meaning: सत्यं पूर्वैरृषिभिश्चाकुपानो ऽग्निः प्रविद्वानिह तद्दधात्विति वोलूखल्मुपदधातीति वाजसनेयकम्
text_mt: Finding truth through the ancient seers, may Agni, knowing well, place it here,”—or he places the mortar [with this formula]; thus the Vājasaneyaka [holds].

sanskrit_iast: agne yukṣvā hi ye tava yukṣvā hi devahūtamāniti dvābhyāmukhāyāṃ hutvā puruṣaśirasi hiraṇyaśalkānpratyasyati
meaning: अग्ने युक्ष्वा हि ये तव युक्ष्वा हि देवहूतमानिति द्वाभ्यामुखायां हुत्वा पुरुषशिरसि हिरण्यशल्कान्प्रत्यस्यति
text_mt: Having made an offering into the ukhā-pot with the two [formulas], “Agni, yoke indeed those that are yours,” [and] “Yoke indeed those most invoking the gods,” he throws gold chips into the human head.
With “The drop fell,” [he throws one] into the mouth;
or with “This has become of the entire world.”
With “To the ṛc, you,” [he throws one] into the right eye-socket;
with “To the brilliance, you,” into the right nostril;
with “To the light, you,” into the northern [i.e., left] one.

sanskrit_iast: samitsravantīti śṛtātaṅkyena dadhnā madhumiśreṇa puruṣaśiraḥ pūrayati
meaning: समित्स्रवन्तीति शृतातङ्क्येन दध्ना मधुमिश्रेण पुरुषशिरः पूरयति
text_mt: With “The firewood sticks flowing,” he fills the human head with curd that has been coagulated with boiled [milk] and mixed with honey.

sanskrit_iast: sarveṣāṃ paśuśirasāṃ pūraṇaṃ ca vājasaneyinaḥ samāmananti
meaning: सर्वेषां पशुशिरसां पूरणं च वाजसनेयिनः समामनन्ति
text_mt: And the Vājasaneyins teach the filling of all the animal heads.

sanskrit_iast: tasmintsuparṇo madhukṛtkulāyīti puruṣaśira ādāyādityaṃ garbhamityukhāyāṃ purastāccubukaṃ prācīnamuttānaṃ prāṅmukha upadhāya citraṃ devānāmityardharcābhyāmakṣikaṭayorhutvā paśuśīrṣāṇyupadadhāti
meaning: तस्मिन्त्सुपर्णो मधुकृत्कुलायीति पुरुषशिर आदायादित्यं गर्भमित्युखायां पुरस्ताच्चुबुकं प्राचीनमुत्तानं प्राङ्मुख उपधाय चित्रं देवानामित्यर्धर्चाभ्यामक्षिकटयोर्हुत्वा पशुशीर्षाण्युपदधाति
text_mt: Taking the human head with “In it the well-winged maker of honey has its nest,” and having set it down in the ukhā-pot facing east, chin to the front, face upwards, facing east with “The sun, the embryo,” having made an offering into the two eye-sockets with the two half-verses of “The bright [face] of the gods,” he places the animal heads.
“He whom he might wish, ‘May he be without cattle,’ for him [turned] away in opposite directions”—thus it has been declared.
With “The rush of the wind,” [he places the head] of the horse to the east, turned westward.
With “The unceasing drop,” [he places that] of the bull to the west, turned eastward.
