Having recited "At the impulse of the god...", [he consecrates] a brahmin with "I sprinkle thee for sovereignty with Agni;"

sanskrit_iast: pṛthagannāni dravīkṛtyaudumbareṇa sruveṇa vājasyemaṃ prasavaḥ suṣuva iti grāmyā hutvāraṇyā juhoti
meaning: पृथगन्नानि द्रवीकृत्यौदुम्बरेण स्रुवेण वाजस्येमं प्रसवः सुषुव इति ग्राम्या हुत्वारण्या जुहोति
text_mt: A kṣatriya with "with Indra;"
A vaiśya with "with Bṛhaspati."

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇaṃ praty apipakṣam audumbarīm āsandīṃ pratiṣṭhāpya tasyāṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ prācīnagrīvam uttaralomāstīrya tasminn āsīnaṃ yajamānam agnimanvārabdhaṃ saṃpātair abhiṣiñcati
meaning: दक्षिणं प्रत्य् अपिपक्षम् औदुम्बरीम् आसन्दीं प्रतिष्ठाप्य तस्यां कृष्णाजिनं प्राचीनग्रीवम् उत्तरलोमास्तीर्य तस्मिन्न् आसीनं यजमानम् अग्निमन्वारब्धं संपातैर् अभिषिञ्चति
text_mt: Some teach the reversal of the formulas for the kṣatriya and the vaiśya.
Standing facing west, having consecrated [the sacrificer] who is seated facing east from his head, he causes [the liquid] to trickle down towards his face.
Having offered with the milk of a black cow having a white calf with "Night and dawn...", he offers the twelve realm-sustaining oblations with six rounds.
Having recited the round formula "Conquering by truth, abiding in truth...", he offers the first offering with "Svāhā to him!";

sanskrit_iast: devasya tvety anudrutyāgnes tvā sāmrājyenābhiṣiñcāmīti brāhmaṇam /
meaning: देवस्य त्वेत्य् अनुद्रुत्याग्नेस् त्वा साम्राज्येनाभिषिञ्चामीति ब्राह्मणम् /
text_mt: The next with "Svāhā to them!"
The [formula] "O lord of the world..." is the seventh of the rounds, and the thirteenth of the oblations.
Some teach the reversal of the mantras for a Rājanya and a Vaiśya.

sanskrit_iast: prāṅmukham āsīnaṃ pratyaṅmukhas tiṣṭhañ śīrṣato 'bhiṣicyā mukhād anvavasrāvayati
meaning: प्राङ्मुखम् आसीनं प्रत्यङ्मुखस् तिष्ठञ् शीर्षतो ऽभिषिच्या मुखाद् अन्ववस्रावयति
text_mt: Standing facing west, having sprinkled [him] from the head as he sits facing east, he makes it flow down along the face.
On this point they say: It must surely be offered; for one who has pressed [soma] does not descend before anyone.

sanskrit_iast: naktoṣāseti kṛṣṇāyai śvetavatsāyai payasā hutvā ṣaḍbhiḥ paryāyairdvādaśa rāṣṭrabhṛto juhoti
meaning: नक्तोषासेति कृष्णायै श्वेतवत्सायै पयसा हुत्वा षड्भिः पर्यायैर्द्वादश राष्ट्रभृतो जुहोति
text_mt: Having offered with the milk of a black [cow] having a white calf with the verse "Night and Dawn", he offers the twelve Rāṣṭrabhṛt [oblations] in six rounds.

sanskrit_iast: ṛtāṣāḍṛtadhāmeti paryāyam anudrutya tasmai svāheti prathamām āhutiṃ juhoti /
meaning: ऋताषाडृतधामेति पर्यायम् अनुद्रुत्य तस्मै स्वाहेति प्रथमाम् आहुतिं जुहोति /
text_mt: Having recited the round, "Conquering by truth, whose abode is truth...", he offers the first oblation with: "To him svāhā!"
With "To them svāhā!" [he offers] the second.
In this manner he divides the other rounds.

sanskrit_iast: bhuvanasya pata iti paryāyāṇāṃ saptamyāhutīnāṃ trayodaśī
meaning: भुवनस्य पत इति पर्यायाणां सप्तम्याहुतीनां त्रयोदशी
text_mt: [The formula] "O lord of the world..." is the seventh of the rounds, the thirteenth of the oblations.
With 'Lord of the world...', he offers five oblations on the front part of the chariot,
Some say he offers upon the head of the chariot while it is being held over the āhavanīya.
Having offered over it, lifting it up, they carry it to the dwelling of the adhvaryu.
He gives them, together with the chariot, to the adhvaryu.

meaning: समुद्रो ऽसि नभस्वानित्यञ्जलिना त्रीणि वातनामानि जुहोति
text_mt: With 'You are the ocean, rich in mist...', he offers with hollowed hands the three names of the wind;
for 'there is no cutting [of a portion] of this,' it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].
Some say: he offers to the wind with a fold of black-antelope skin.

sanskrit_iast: agna udadhe yā ta iṣauryuvā nāmeti pañcājyāhutīrhutvā samīcī namāsi prācī digiti dadhnā madhumiśreṇa ṣaṭ sarpāhutīranuparicāram
meaning: अग्न उदधे या त इषौर्युवा नामेति पञ्चाज्याहुतीर्हुत्वा समीची नमासि प्राची दिगिति दध्ना मधुमिश्रेण षट् सर्पाहुतीरनुपरिचारम्
text_mt: Having offered five butter oblations with 'O Agni, the receptacle of water, what arrow of yours...', 'The youth by name...', [he offers] walking around six serpent oblations with curds mixed with honey with 'You are the concordant ones, the eastern direction...';
six great oblations with 'Weapons by name are you...', just as the serpent oblations;
five Arka oblations with 'Light, O Gharma, svāhā!';

sanskrit_iast: yāste agne sūrye ruca iti tisro rucaḥ
meaning: यास्ते अग्ने सूर्ये रुच इति तिस्रो रुचः
text_mt: three splendour [oblations] with 'What splendours of yours, O Agni, are in the sun...'.
He commences the soma ritual beginning with the strewing of the altar ground.
Having performed whatever comes before the heaping of the dhiṣṇya hearths,
he piles the dhiṣṇyas with bricks mantra by mantra with the anuvāka, 'May my splendour, O Agni, be present in invocations...'.
On the āgnīdhrīya hearth he lays down [bricks] having a stone as the ninth;
twelve, sixteen, twenty-one, or twenty-four on the hotṛ's hearth;
eleven on the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's hearth;
'eight each on the other dhiṣṇyas,' it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].
The dhiṣṇyas are square or circular.
As many bricks as belong to them, so many pebbles are enclosed around [them].

sanskrit_iast: tava śriye vyajihīta parvato gavāṃ gotramudasṛjo yadaṅgiraḥ /
meaning: तव श्रिये व्यजिहीत पर्वतो गवां गोत्रमुदसृजो यदङ्गिरः /
text_mt: 'For your glory the mountain split open, when you, O Aṅgiras, released the pen of cattle;

sanskrit_iast: indreṇa yujā tamasā parīvṛtaṃ bṛhaspate nirapāmaubjo arṇavam //
meaning: इन्द्रेण युजा तमसा परीवृतं बृहस्पते निरपामौब्जो अर्णवम् //
text_mt: With Indra as your ally, O Bṛhaspati, you drove out the ocean of waters that was enclosed by darkness.'
'O Bṛhaspati, whatever surpasses the noble...'

sanskrit_iast: brāhaspatiḥ samajayadvasūni maho vrajāngomato deva eṣaḥ /
meaning: ब्राहस्पतिः समजयद्वसूनि महो व्रजान्गोमतो देव एषः /
text_mt: 'Bṛhaspati won all wealth, the great pens rich in cattle, this god;
Desiring to win the waters, irresistible towards the sun, Bṛhaspati slays the enemy with songs'—with these three [he places bricks] at the seat of the brahman.

sanskrit_iast: yamo dādhāra pṛthivīṃ yamo viśvamidaṃ jagat /
meaning: यमो दाधार पृथिवीं यमो विश्वमिदं जगत् /
text_mt: 'Yama upholds the earth, Yama all this world;
To Yama everything has bowed down, whatever has breathed, protected by the wind.
As the five, as the six, as the fifteen ṛṣis,
He who knows Yama would tell, just as the single ṛṣi discerns.
Through the Trikadruka [days] he flies across the six broad spaces, the one great [domain];

sanskrit_iast: gāyatrī triṣṭup chandāṃsi sarvā tā yama āhiteti tisro mārjālīye
meaning: गायत्री त्रिष्टुप् छन्दांसि सर्वा ता यम आहितेति तिस्रो मार्जालीये
text_mt: The gāyatrī, the triṣṭubh, the metres—all those are placed in Yama'—with these three [he places bricks] on the mārjālīya.
'Have mercy on us, O Rudra, and grant us delight...'

sanskrit_iast: aśyāma te sumatiṃ devayajyayā kṣayadvīrasya tava rudra mīḍhvaḥ /
meaning: अश्याम ते सुमतिं देवयज्यया क्षयद्वीरस्य तव रुद्र मीढ्वः /
text_mt: 'May we attain your goodwill through worship of the gods, of you who rule over heroes, O bounteous Rudra;

sanskrit_iast: sumnāyannidvaśo asmākamā carāriṣṭavīrā juhavāma te haviḥ //
meaning: सुम्नायन्निद्वशो अस्माकमा चरारिष्टवीरा जुहवाम ते हविः //
text_mt: Favouring us, come to our wish; with uninjured heroes may we offer oblation to you.'

sanskrit_iast: tveṣaṃ vayaṃ rudraṃ yajñasādhanaṃ vaṅkuṃ kavimavase ni hvayāmahe /
meaning: त्वेषं वयं रुद्रं यज्ञसाधनं वङ्कुं कविमवसे नि ह्वयामहे /
text_mt: 'Fierce Rudra, the accomplisher of sacrifice, the winding, the poet, we invoke downwards for help;

sanskrit_iast: āre asmadamatiṃ heḍso asyatu sumatimidvayamasyā vṛṇīmaha iti tisraścātvāle
meaning: आरे अस्मदमतिं हेड्सो अस्यतु सुमतिमिद्वयमस्या वृणीमह इति तिस्रश्चात्वाले
text_mt: Far from us may he cast away thoughtlessness, his wrath; we choose only the goodwill of him'—with these three [he places bricks] in the cātvāla trench.

sanskrit_iast: havyaṃ prīṇīhi havyaṃ śrīṇīhi havyaṃ paca havyaṃ śrapaya havyamasi havyāya tvā havyebhyastvā havye sīdetyaṣṭau śāmitre
meaning: हव्यं प्रीणीहि हव्यं श्रीणीहि हव्यं पच हव्यं श्रपय हव्यमसि हव्याय त्वा हव्येभ्यस्त्वा हव्ये सीदेत्यष्टौ शामित्रे
text_mt: With 'Please the oblation, cook the oblation, bake the oblation, boil the oblation, you are the oblation, for the oblation to you, for the oblations to you, sit down on the oblation'—with these eight [he places bricks] in the śāmitra.
'With that prayer I come to you...'—with these three at the avabhṛtha.
Pieces that are broken, black, and spotted he throws away upon the rubbish heap.
Having broken the remaining ones and having performed whatever comes before measuring the sacrificial post, he erects one sacrificial post or eleven sacrificial posts.
Of them, the one facing the fire on the previous day;
Or he assigns [the animals] of the set of eleven to a single post.

sanskrit_iast: agnīṣomīyasya paśupuroḍāśam aṣṭau devasuvāṃ havīṃṣy anunirvapati
meaning: अग्नीषोमीयस्य पशुपुरोडाशम् अष्टौ देवसुवां हवींष्य् अनुनिर्वपति
text_mt: Following the animal cake of the Agni-Soma victim, he dispenses the eight oblations to the divine prompters.
However, the sviṣṭakṛt and the iḍā are common.
Before the morning recitation, touching [the fire altar] with the three [verses], 'I harness Agni...', he harnesses the fire.

sanskrit_iast: yadyenaṃ pūrvo bhrātṛvyo 'bhīva syādaṣṭau gāyatrīḥ purastādbahiṣpavamānādupadadhyāt /
meaning: यद्येनं पूर्वो भ्रातृव्यो ऽभीव स्यादष्टौ गायत्रीः पुरस्ताद्बहिष्पवमानादुपदध्यात् /
text_mt: If a rival who is prior should overpower him, he should lay down eight gāyatrī [bricks] before the Bahiṣpavamāna chant.
[He places] eleven Triṣṭubh [bricks] before the midday [pressing chant],
twelve Jagatī [bricks] before the Ārbhava [pavamāna chant].
Or, if the rival is subsequent, the reverse is done:
they are placed after the pavamāna chants.
At the time of the animal [sacrifice], he dedicates the victim dedicated to Agni for the soma day;

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇākāle hiraṇyapātraṃ madhoḥ pūrṇaṃ śatamānasya kṛtaṃ citraṃ dvānāmityavekṣyāśvenāvaghrāpya brahmaṇe dadāti
meaning: दक्षिणाकाले हिरण्यपात्रं मधोः पूर्णं शतमानस्य कृतं चित्रं द्वानामित्यवेक्ष्याश्वेनावघ्राप्य ब्रह्मणे ददाति
text_mt: At the time of the sacrificial gifts, having looked at a gold vessel filled with honey, made of a hundred manas [in weight], with [the verse,] "A wondrous [face of the gods]...", and having made the horse sniff it, he gives it to the brahman.
He gives suitable sacrificial gifts to the adhvaryu.

sanskrit_iast: yadyasyāgniṃ cinoti yajñāyajñīyasya stotra ekayāprastutaṃ bhavati
meaning: यद्यस्याग्निं चिनोति यज्ञायज्ञीयस्य स्तोत्र एकयाप्रस्तुतं भवति
text_mt: If he piles the fire altar for [a sacrificer], at the Yajñāyajñīya chant [the stotra] is uncompleted by one [verse],

sanskrit_iast: atha namaste astu mā mā hiṃsīriti dvābhyāmagnimabhimṛśyaikādaś samiṣṭayajūṃṣi juhoti
meaning: अथ नमस्ते अस्तु मा मा हिंसीरिति द्वाभ्यामग्निमभिमृश्यैकादश् समिष्टयजूंषि जुहोति
text_mt: then, having touched the fire altar with the two [formulas], "Homage be to you, do not injure me...", he offers the eleven Samiṣṭayajus offerings.

sanskrit_iast: navādhvarikāṇi hutveṣṭo yajño bhṛgubhiriti daśamaikādaśe juhoti
meaning: नवाध्वरिकाणि हुत्वेष्टो यज्ञो भृगुभिरिति दशमैकादशे जुहोति
text_mt: Having offered the nine [formulas] of the normal sacrifice, he offers the tenth and eleventh with [the two formulas beginning,] "The sacrifice has been offered by the Bhṛgus...".

sanskrit_iast: anūbandhyāvapāyāṃ hutāyāmaudumbarīṃ srucaṃ ghṛtasya pūrayitvemaṃ stanamūrjasvantaṃ dhayāpāmityagnervimokaṃ juhoti
meaning: अनूबन्ध्यावपायां हुतायामौदुम्बरीं स्रुचं घृतस्य पूरयित्वेमं स्तनमूर्जस्वन्तं धयापामित्यग्नेर्विमोकं जुहोति
text_mt: When the omentum of the anūbandhyā cow has been offered, having filled the sruc made of udumbara wood with ghee, he offers the unyoking of the fire with [the verse,] "Suck this swelling breast of the waters...".

sanskrit_iast: hute saktuhome yadākūtāditi daśākūtīrhutvā pratyavaruhya punarmanaḥ punarāyurāgātpunaḥ prāṇaḥ punarākūtamāgāt /
meaning: हुते सक्तुहोमे यदाकूतादिति दशाकूतीर्हुत्वा प्रत्यवरुह्य पुनर्मनः पुनरायुरागात्पुनः प्राणः पुनराकूतमागात् /
text_mt: When the barley-meal offering has been made, having offered the ten ākūti offerings with [the formulas beginning,] "From the intention...", having stepped down, [he worships the fire altar with the verse,] "Mind has returned, life has returned, breath has returned, intention has returned;
May Vaiśvānara, growing with his rays, dwell within as the guardian of immortality."

sanskrit_iast: ye 'gnayaḥ purīṣyā iti prayāsyannāptibhiragniṃ yajamāna upatiṣṭhate
meaning: ये ऽग्नयः पुरीष्या इति प्रयास्यन्नाप्तिभिरग्निं यजमान उपतिष्ठते
text_mt: When about to set forth, the sacrificer worships the fire with the āpti formulas: "Whichever fires are rich in loose earth...".

sanskrit_iast: upa tvāgne divediva iti tisṛbhiranyeṣāmagnīn dṛṣṭvāgniṃ citvā sautrāmaṇyā yajeta /
meaning: उप त्वाग्ने दिवेदिव इति तिसृभिरन्येषामग्नीन् दृष्ट्वाग्निं चित्वा सौत्रामण्या यजेत /
text_mt: Having seen the fires of others, [he worships] with the three [verses,] "Towards you, O Agni, day by day...". Having piled the fire altar, he should sacrifice with the Sautrāmaṇī,
and with the curdled milk offering for Mitra and Varuṇa.

sanskrit_iast: saṃvatsaraṃ na kaṃcana pratyavarohenna ca rāmāmupeyāt /
meaning: संवत्सरं न कंचन प्रत्यवरोहेन्न च रामामुपेयात् /
text_mt: For a year he should not descend [to the level of] anyone, nor should he approach a Śūdra woman,

sanskrit_iast: yāvajjīvaṃ ca mastiṣkasya nāśnīyānna ca varṣati dhāvet
meaning: यावज्जीवं च मस्तिष्कस्य नाश्नीयान्न च वर्षति धावेत्
text_mt: and for the rest of his life he should not eat brain, nor should he run when it rains;
if he should run, he should turn back.
Having piled [the fire altar] a second time, he should not approach another's wife;
having piled it a third time, [he should not approach] any woman,

sanskrit_iast: agniṃ citvaitasminsaṃvatsare yo nardhnuyātsa kratumāharamāṇa ekacitīkaṃ cinvīta
meaning: अग्निं चित्वैतस्मिन्संवत्सरे यो नर्ध्नुयात्स क्रतुमाहरमाण एकचितीकं चिन्वीत
text_mt: Having piled the fire altar, he who does not prosper in that year, undertaking a sacrifice, should pile an altar of one layer.
He should place on the high altar eight bricks with distinct formulas, beginning with: "To the ocean you...";
as many space-filler bricks as required, then loose earth.

sanskrit_iast: atha yo na pratitiṣṭhetsa kratumāharamāṇa ekacitīkameva cinvīta
meaning: अथ यो न प्रतितिष्ठेत्स क्रतुमाहरमाण एकचितीकमेव चिन्वीत
text_mt: Then, he who does not obtain a firm support, undertaking a sacrifice, should pile an altar of only one layer.
He should place on the high altar five bricks with distinct formulas: "Uniting, and wise...";
as many space-filler bricks as required, then loose earth.
Some hand down the two desires in reverse order.
The re-piling is prescribed in the sacred texts for three purposes:
for the purpose of renown, for the purpose of prosperity, or for the purpose of continuity.
We shall explain the one for the purpose of renown.

sanskrit_iast: yadīṣṭyā yadi paśunā yadi somena yajeta yo 'sya purāgnistamanvavasāya yajeta
meaning: यदीष्ट्या यदि पशुना यदि सोमेन यजेत यो ऽस्य पुराग्निस्तमन्ववसाय यजेत
text_mt: Whether he sacrifices with an iṣṭi, with an animal sacrifice, or with a soma sacrifice, having shifted the fire that was previously his, he should sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast: api vā yenarṣaya ityaṣṭau nānāmantrā uttaravedyāmupadadhyāt /
meaning: अपि वा येनर्षय इत्यष्टौ नानामन्त्रा उत्तरवेद्यामुपदध्यात् /
text_mt: Or he should place on the high altar eight bricks with distinct formulas, beginning with: "By which the seers...";
as many space-filler bricks as required, then loose earth.

sanskrit_iast: api vottaravedyāmuparyagnau dhāryamāṇe prajāpatistvā sādayatu tayā devatayāṅgirasvaddhruvā sīdetyuttaravedimabhimṛśet
meaning: अपि वोत्तरवेद्यामुपर्यग्नौ धार्यमाणे प्रजापतिस्त्वा सादयतु तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद्ध्रुवा सीदेत्युत्तरवेदिमभिमृशेत्
text_mt: Or, while the fire is held over the high altar, he should touch the high altar with: "May Prajāpati seat you; with that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras."
Or [he places] three naturally perforated bricks.
A naturally perforated brick, a chant, loose earth;
Or [he places] three naturally perforated bricks and three Viśvajyotis bricks.
A naturally perforated brick, a chant, loose earth, then a Viśvajyotis brick;

sanskrit_iast: tṛtīyasyāṃ tu viśvajyotiḥ prathamātha svayamātṛṇātha sāmapurīṣam
meaning: तृतीयस्यां तु विश्वज्योतिः प्रथमाथ स्वयमातृणाथ सामपुरीषम्
text_mt: in the third, however, the Viśvajyotis brick comes first, then the naturally perforated brick, then the chant and loose earth.
Or [he places] eight space-filler bricks [and] loose earth;
eleven space-filler bricks [and] loose earth;
twelve space-filler bricks [and] loose earth.

sanskrit_iast: agniṃ citvā yaḥ somena yajeta sa etā ekatriṃśataṃ lokaṃpṛṇā uttaravedyāmupadhāya yajeta
meaning: अग्निं चित्वा यः सोमेन यजेत स एता एकत्रिंशतं लोकंपृणा उत्तरवेद्यामुपधाय यजेत
text_mt: Having piled the fire altar, he who sacrifices with soma should sacrifice after placing these thirty-one space-filler bricks on the high altar.

sanskrit_iast: samṛddhyarthāyāṃ tu dvitīyaṃ cinvāno dvitīyasyāṃ citau yenarṣaya ityaṣṭau nānāmantrā uttaravedyāmupadadhyāt /
meaning: समृद्ध्यर्थायां तु द्वितीयं चिन्वानो द्वितीयस्यां चितौ येनर्षय इत्यष्टौ नानामन्त्रा उत्तरवेद्यामुपदध्यात् /
text_mt: In the one for the purpose of prosperity, however, piling for the second time, in the second layer he should place on the high altar eight bricks with distinct formulas, beginning with: "By which the seers...";
and eight space-filler bricks, then loose earth.

sanskrit_iast: śvo bhūta etāścaiva nānāmantrā ekādaśa ca lokaṃpṛṇā atha purīṣam
meaning: श्वो भूत एताश्चैव नानामन्त्रा एकादश च लोकंपृणा अथ पुरीषम्
text_mt: On the next day, these very bricks with distinct formulas and eleven space-filler bricks, then loose earth.

sanskrit_iast: śvo bhūta etāścaiva nānāmantrā dvādaśa ca lokaṃpṛṇā atha purīṣam
meaning: श्वो भूत एताश्चैव नानामन्त्रा द्वादश च लोकंपृणा अथ पुरीषम्
text_mt: On the next day, these very bricks with distinct formulas and twelve space-filler bricks, then loose earth.

sanskrit_iast: saṃtānārthāyāṃ tu tṛtīyaṃ cinvānastṛtīyasyāṃ citau yenarṣaya ityaṣṭau nānāmantrā uttaravedyāmupadadhyāt /
meaning: संतानार्थायां तु तृतीयं चिन्वानस्तृतीयस्यां चितौ येनर्षय इत्यष्टौ नानामन्त्रा उत्तरवेद्यामुपदध्यात् /
text_mt: In the one for the purpose of continuity, however, piling for the third time, in the third layer he should place on the high altar eight bricks with distinct formulas, beginning with: "By which the seers...";
as many space-filler bricks as required, then loose earth.
Moreover, they indeed say: "It should not be piled,"
for it has been declared: "Rudra, indeed, is this Fire".
'Piled with metres' are optional [forms of the fire altar];
In the case of the tāpaścita fire-altar, the consecration [lasts] a year.
Before the upasads, [with the five formulas beginning with] ‘The [cake] on eight potsherds for Agni...’, he offers every four months with each upasad formula.
Following the upasads, he piles the fire-altar.
Each layer [takes] two months.
[Drinking milk from] four teats, three teats, two teats, [and] one teat: [these are] the dietary vows for three months each.
During the laying down [of the bricks], he remains for a year with the [hymn] to Agni of the seers.
It is known [from scripture]: ‘This is indeed the [hymn] to Agni of the seers, which is the Yājñasenī layer.’
Or whatever hymns to Agni there may be in the Ṛgveda, he should lay [the bricks] with them.
The bricks have individual mantras of the extent of a hymn.
As needed, the space-filler [bricks], then the loose earth.

meaning: तृतीये संवत्सरे ऽभिजिता विश्वजिता वा यजेत
text_mt: In the third year he should sacrifice with an Abhijit or a Viśvajit.

sanskrit_iast: udavasāya rohiṇīṃ vatsacchavīṃ sakarṇapucchāvacchātāṃ sakhurāṃ sakhurikāṃ vā bahirlomaḥ paridhāyoṣṇīṣeṇa pradakṣiṇaṃ śiro veṣṭayitvaudumbaraṃ camasamādatte /
meaning: उदवसाय रोहिणीं वत्सच्छवीं सकर्णपुच्छावच्छातां सखुरां सखुरिकां वा बहिर्लोमः परिधायोष्णीषेण प्रदक्षिणं शिरो वेष्टयित्वौदुम्बरं चमसमादत्ते /
text_mt: Having concluded the sacrifice, wearing the skin of a red calf, having ears and tail, cut whole, with hooves or small hooves, with the hair outwards, having wound [a turban] clockwise around his head with a turban, he takes up an udumbara goblet,

sanskrit_iast: audumbarīṃ cābhrīṃ vaiṇavīṃ vā kalmāṣīṃ pūrvavatpramāṇām
meaning: औदुम्बरीं चाभ्रीं वैणवीं वा कल्माषीं पूर्ववत्प्रमाणाम्
text_mt: and a spade of udumbara wood, or of bamboo, variegated, of the same size as before.
They [two] stay three nights at an udumbara tree in the forest, feeding on roots and fruits,
Having dug up a root and placed it in this vessel, the wife and the sacrificer feed each other.
The sacrificer should seek food with a broom or a small spade;
the wife with a winnowing basket or a knife, according to some.
They stay three nights among the Niṣādas,
or three nights each among the Brahmins.
and he should not refuse what is given [to him].
If not for a year, [then] twelve days [in each place], twelve days [in each place].

sanskrit_iast: śaradi vājapeyena yajeta brāhmaṇo rājanyo varddhikāmaḥ
meaning: शरदि वाजपेयेन यजेत ब्राह्मणो राजन्यो वर्द्धिकामः
text_mt: In autumn a Brahmin or a Rājanya desiring prosperity should sacrifice with the Vājapeya.
Some teach [it] as an obligatory sacrifice.
Its procedure is like that of the Ṣoḍaśin.
Everything is seventeen-fold.

sanskrit_iast: saptadaśāratnir bailvo yūpaḥ khādiro vā tūparaś caturaśro godhūmapiṣṭacaṣālo godhūmakalāpī vā
meaning: सप्तदशारत्निर् बैल्वो यूपः खादिरो वा तूपरश् चतुरश्रो गोधूमपिष्टचषालो गोधूमकलापी वा
text_mt: The sacrificial post is seventeen cubits [high], of bilva or khadira wood, hornless, four-cornered, with a top-ring of wheat flour or with a wheat band.

sanskrit_iast: yat prāg upasadbhyas tasmin kṛte pratiprasthātā surāyāḥ kalpena surāṃ saṃdadhāti
meaning: यत् प्राग् उपसद्भ्यस् तस्मिन् कृते प्रतिप्रस्थाता सुरायाः कल्पेन सुरां संदधाति
text_mt: When that which precedes the upasads is performed, the pratiprasthātṛ brews the surā according to the procedure for surā.

sanskrit_iast: kharakāle pratiprasthātā dakṣiṇasya havirdhānasyādhastāt paścād akṣaṃ surāgrahārthaṃ dvitīyaṃ kharaṃ karoti
meaning: खरकाले प्रतिप्रस्थाता दक्षिणस्य हविर्धानस्याधस्तात् पश्चाद् अक्षं सुराग्रहार्थं द्वितीयं खरं करोति
text_mt: At the time of [erecting] the mound, the pratiprasthātṛ makes a second mound beneath the southern havirdhāna [cart] behind the axle for the purpose of the surā draughts.
At the time of the cord, he wraps the sacrificial post with seventeen garments.

sanskrit_iast: pātrasaṃsādanakāle aindram atigrāhyapātraṃ prayujya tatsamīpe pañcaindrāṇy atigrāhyapātrāṇi prayunakti
meaning: पात्रसंसादनकाले ऐन्द्रम् अतिग्राह्यपात्रं प्रयुज्य तत्समीपे पञ्चैन्द्राण्य् अतिग्राह्यपात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति
text_mt: At the time of placing the vessels, having set out the atigrāhya vessel for Indra, he sets out near it five atigrāhya vessels for Indra.
Their procedure is explained by the earlier [one].

sanskrit_iast: ṣoḍaśipātraṃ prayujya tatsamīpe saptadaśa prājāpatyāṇi somagrahapātrāṇi prayunakti
meaning: षोडशिपात्रं प्रयुज्य तत्समीपे सप्तदश प्राजापत्याणि सोमग्रहपात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति
text_mt: Having set out the ṣoḍaśin vessel, he sets out near it seventeen soma draught vessels for Prajāpati.
Their procedure is like that of the ṣoḍaśin vessel.

sanskrit_iast: aparasmin khare pratiprasthātā saptadaśopayāmān mṛnmayāni surāgrahapātrāṇi prayunakti
meaning: अपरस्मिन् खरे प्रतिप्रस्थाता सप्तदशोपयामान् मृन्मयानि सुराग्रहपात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति
text_mt: On the other mound, the pratiprasthātṛ sets out seventeen earthenware vessels for the surā draughts along with the upayāma [cups].

sanskrit_iast: grahakāla aindram atigrāhyaṃ gṛhītvopayāmagṛhīto 'si nṛṣadaṃ tveti pañcaindran atigrāhyān gṛhṇāti
meaning: ग्रहकाल ऐन्द्रम् अतिग्राह्यं गृहीत्वोपयामगृहीतो ऽसि नृषदं त्वेति पञ्चैन्द्रन् अतिग्राह्यान् गृह्णाति
text_mt: At the time of the draughts, having drawn the atigrāhya [draught] for Indra, he draws the five atigrāhya [draughts] for Indra with: ‘You are taken with a support; you for the dweller among men...’

sanskrit_iast: ṣoḍaśinaṃ gṛhītvāyā viṣṭhā janayan karvarāṇīti saptadaśa prājāpatyān somagrahān gṛhṇāti
meaning: षोडशिनं गृहीत्वाया विष्ठा जनयन् कर्वराणीति सप्तदश प्राजापत्यान् सोमग्रहान् गृह्णाति
text_mt: Having drawn the ṣoḍaśin [draught], he draws the seventeen soma draughts for Prajāpati with: ‘Pervading the positions, generating the variegated...’

sanskrit_iast: kuvid aṅgety aparasmin khare pratiprasthātā saptadaśabhir upayāmaiḥ surāgrahān gṛhṇāti
meaning: कुविद् अङ्गेत्य् अपरस्मिन् खरे प्रतिप्रस्थाता सप्तदशभिर् उपयामैः सुराग्रहान् गृह्णाति
text_mt: With ‘Surely indeed...’, on the other mound, the pratiprasthātṛ draws the surā draughts with seventeen upayāma [cups].
Some teach the two ladles as reversed.
He draws the surā draughts alternately with the soma draughts.
First the adhvaryu draws;
last the pratiprasthātṛ.
He places the soma draughts in front of the axle;
[The pratiprasthātṛ sets down] the surā draughts behind the axle.

sanskrit_iast: deva savitaḥ pra suveti savanādausavanādau juhoti /
meaning: देव सवितः प्र सुवेति सवनादौसवनादौ जुहोति /
text_mt: With "O divine Savitṛ, impel...", he offers at the beginning of each pressing,
or before each ritual action.
Wearing gold necklaces, the officiating priests proceed on the soma-pressing day.

sanskrit_iast: paśukāle trīn kratupaśūn upākṛtya mārutīṃ vaśām upākaroti /
meaning: पशुकाले त्रीन् क्रतुपशून् उपाकृत्य मारुतीं वशाम् उपाकरोति /
text_mt: At the time of the animal sacrifice, having assigned the three victim animals of the sacrifice, he assigns a barren cow to the Maruts,
and an ewe whose teeth have not fallen out to Sarasvatī.

sanskrit_iast: sārasvataṃ meṣam upākṛtya saptadaśa prājāpatyān paśūn upākaroti śyāmāṃs tūparān ekarūpān
meaning: सारस्वतं मेषम् उपाकृत्य सप्तदश प्राजापत्यान् पशून् उपाकरोति श्यामांस् तूपरान् एकरूपान्
text_mt: Having assigned a ram to Sarasvant, he assigns seventeen hornless, uniform dark animals to Prajāpati.
Of those around which fire has been carried, they immolate the earlier ones ending with the one for Sarasvatī.
They keep the later ones, beginning with the one for Sarasvant, [alive].
It has been stated: "There are two strew-grass bundles for each animal."

sanskrit_iast: prāṅ māhendrāt kṛtvā mādhyaṃdinīyān vā puroḍāśān nirupya sārasvatasya paśupuroḍāśaṃ nirupya bārhaspatyaṃ naivāraṃ saptadaśaśarāvaṃ caruṃ nirvapati /
meaning: प्राङ् माहेन्द्रात् कृत्वा माध्यंदिनीयान् वा पुरोडाशान् निरुप्य सारस्वतस्य पशुपुरोडाशं निरुप्य बार्हस्पत्यं नैवारं सप्तदशशरावं चरुं निर्वपति /
text_mt: Having proceeded [with the ritual] prior to the draught for Mahendra, or having portioned out the cakes of the midday pressing and portioned out the animal cake for Sarasvant, he portions out a wild-rice mess of seventeen dishes for Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit_iast: indrasya vajro 'sīti ratham upāvahṛtyāpsv antar ity aśvān apsu snāpayanti
meaning: इन्द्रस्य वज्रो ऽसीति रथम् उपावहृत्याप्स्व् अन्तर् इत्य् अश्वान् अप्सु स्नापयन्ति
text_mt: having taken down the chariot with "You are Indra's vajra...", they bathe the horses in water with "Within the waters..."
With "O Child of the Waters...", he wipes down their foreheads.

sanskrit_iast: vāyur vā tvā manur vā tveti praṣṭivāhinaṃ rathaṃ yunakti /
meaning: वायुर् वा त्वा मनुर् वा त्वेति प्रष्टिवाहिनं रथं युनक्ति /
text_mt: With "Either Vāyu or Manu [yoke] you...", he yokes the chariot drawn by three horses.
The other sixteen chariots [are yoked] silently.
At the time of the dakṣiṇā, he gives seventeen chariots,

sanskrit_iast: saptadaśānāṃsi saptadaśāśvān saptadaśa hastinaḥ saptadaśa niṣkān saptadaśa dāsyaḥ saptadaśājāḥ saptadaśāvīḥ saptadaśa vāsāṃsi saptadaśa gavāṃ śatāni
meaning: सप्तदशानांसि सप्तदशाश्वान् सप्तदश हस्तिनः सप्तदश निष्कान् सप्तदश दास्यः सप्तदशाजाः सप्तदशावीः सप्तदश वासांसि सप्तदश गवां शतानि
text_mt:
seventeen carts, seventeen horses, seventeen elephants, seventeen gold ornaments, seventeen female slaves, seventeen she-goats, seventeen ewes, seventeen garments, [and] seventeen hundred cows.

He gives seventeen hundred cows,

sanskrit_iast: saptadaśānāṃsi yuktāni saptadaśāśvarathān saptadaśa hastinaḥ saptadaśa niṣkān saptadaśa dāsyaḥ saptadaśa dundubhīn
meaning: सप्तदशानांसि युक्तानि सप्तदशाश्वरथान् सप्तदश हस्तिनः सप्तदश निष्कान् सप्तदश दास्यः सप्तदश दुन्दुभीन्
text_mt: seventeen yoked carts, seventeen horse-drawn chariots, seventeen elephants, seventeen gold ornaments, seventeen female slaves, [and] seventeen drums.
He gives seventeen of each age [group],
the age groups beginning from one-year-olds up to five-year-olds.
When the dakṣiṇās have been assigned, he gives the chariot yoked with the yajus to the adhvaryu.

sanskrit_iast: agreṇāhavanīyam udīcaḥ prāco vā rathān avasthāpayanti
meaning: अग्रेणाहवनीयम् उदीचः प्राचो वा रथान् अवस्थापयन्ति
text_mt: They station the chariots in front of the āhavanīya, facing north or facing east.
The southern one among them is the one yoked with the yajus.

sanskrit_iast: agreṇāgnīdhraṃ rājaputro 'vasthāya saptadaśa pravyādhān iṣum asyati
meaning: अग्रेणाग्नीध्रं राजपुत्रो ऽवस्थाय सप्तदश प्रव्याधान् इषुम् अस्यति
text_mt: Stationing himself in front of the āgnīdhra, a prince shoots seventeen arrow casts.

sanskrit_iast: yatra jaghanyaṃ nipatati tatraudumbarīṃ kāṣṭhāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ minoti
meaning: यत्र जघन्यं निपतति तत्रौदुम्बरीं काष्ठां लक्षणं मिनोति
text_mt: Where the last one falls, there he fixes an udumbara post as a turning mark.

sanskrit_iast: prāṅ māhendrāt kṛtvā naivāre sarpir ānīya cātvāle 'vadadhāti
meaning: प्राङ् माहेन्द्रात् कृत्वा नैवारे सर्पिर् आनीय चात्वाले ऽवदधाति
text_mt: Having proceeded [with the ritual] prior to the draught for Mahendra, having poured clarified butter into the wild-rice [mess], he places it in the cātvāla trench.
A prince guards it.

sanskrit_iast: cātvāle rathākṣākṛti kāṣṭhaṃ nikhāya tasminn audumbaraṃ rathacakraṃ saptadaśāraṃ pratimuñcati
meaning: चात्वाले रथाक्षाकृति काष्ठं निखाय तस्मिन्न् औदुम्बरं रथचक्रं सप्तदशारं प्रतिमुञ्चति
text_mt: Having planted in the cātvāla trench a piece of wood shaped like a chariot axle, he fastens upon it an udumbara chariot wheel having seventeen spokes.
On the northern hip of the altar ground, they fasten seventeen drums.

meaning: विष्णोः क्रमो ऽसीति रथं यजमानो ऽभ्यैति
text_mt: With "You are Viṣṇu's stride...", the sacrificer approaches the chariot.
With "The two curves, the two bends...", he touches the two chariot wheels,
With "Utter your voice for Indra!", they beat the drums together.

sanskrit_iast: devasyāhaṃ savituḥ prasave bṛhaspatinā vājajitā vājaṃ jeṣam ity audumbaraṃ rathacakraṃ brahmārohati
meaning: देवस्याहं सवितुः प्रसवे बृहस्पतिना वाजजिता वाजं जेषम् इत्य् औदुम्बरं रथचक्रं ब्रह्मारोहति
text_mt: With "At the impulse of the divine Savitṛ, with Bṛhaspati who wins the prize, may I win the prize!", the brahman mounts the udumbara chariot wheel.
He says to him: "Sing the sāman of the swift racers."
He turns its wheel three times clockwise.
While it is turning, the brahman sings.

sanskrit_iast: devasyāhaṃ savituḥ prasave bṛhaspatinā vājajitā varṣiṣṭhaṃ nākaṃ ruheyam iti yajuryuktaṃ yajamāna ārohati
meaning: देवस्याहं सवितुः प्रसवे बृहस्पतिना वाजजिता वर्षिष्ठं नाकं रुहेयम् इति यजुर्युक्तं यजमान आरोहति
text_mt: With "At the impulse of the divine Savitṛ, with Bṛhaspati who wins the prize, may I ascend the highest firmament!", the sacrificer mounts the chariot yoked with the yajus.
The prize-racers [mount] the other chariots.

sanskrit_iast: vājino vājajito vājaṃ sariṣyanto vājaṃ jeṣyanto bṛhaspater bhāgam ava jighrateti naivāram aśvau dhuryāv avaghrāpayati /
meaning: वाजिनो वाजजितो वाजं सरिष्यन्तो वाजं जेष्यन्तो बृहस्पतेर् भागम् अव जिघ्रतेति नैवारम् अश्वौ धुर्याव् अवघ्रापयति /
text_mt: With "O swift coursers, winners of the prize, about to run for the prize, about to win the prize, sniff Bṛhaspati's portion!", he makes the two yoke-horses sniff the wild-rice mess,

sanskrit_iast: bṛhaspater bhāge ni mṛḍḍhvam iti praprotheṣu ca lepān nimārṣṭi
meaning: बृहस्पतेर् भागे नि मृड्ढ्वम् इति प्रप्रोथेषु च लेपान् निमार्ष्टि
text_mt: With "Wipe [yourselves] on Bṛhaspati's portion!", he also wipes the remnants upon their nostrils.

sanskrit_iast: aśvājanīty aśvājanīm ādāyādhvaryur yajuryuktam adhiruhyārvāsi saptir asīti tayāśvān samavakṣiṇoti
meaning: अश्वाजनीत्य् अश्वाजनीम् आदायाध्वर्युर् यजुर्युक्तम् अधिरुह्यार्वासि सप्तिर् असीति तयाश्वान् समवक्षिणोति
text_mt: Taking the horse whip with "A horse whip [you are]...", having mounted the chariot yoked with the yajus, the adhvaryu touches the horses with it, reciting: "You are a courser; you are a steed..."
Without overtaking, the other chariots follow behind.

meaning: वाजिनो वाजं धावतेति चतसृभिर् धावतो ऽनुमन्त्रयते
text_mt: With the four [verses] beginning with "O swift coursers, run for the prize...", he follows them as they run with his recitation.
While they are running, he causes the sacrificer to recite the Ujjitis beginning with "Agni by a single syllable..."
Having reached the turning mark, they turn northward and circle around clockwise.
With the four [verses] beginning with "Running with measured pace...", he follows them with his recitation as they run back.

sanskrit_iast: ā mā vājasya prasavo jagamyād iti pratyāsṛteṣu hutvā punar naivāram avaghrāpayati /
meaning: आ मा वाजस्य प्रसवो जगम्याद् इति प्रत्यासृतेषु हुत्वा पुनर् नैवारम् अवघ्रापयति /
text_mt: Having offered with "May the impulsion of the prize come to me..." as they run back, he again makes [the horses] sniff the wild-rice mess.
With "You who have run...", he wipes off the remnants.

sanskrit_iast: iyaṃ vaḥ sā satyā saṃdhābhūd iti dundubhivimocanīyaṃ homaṃ juhoti
meaning: इयं वः सा सत्या संधाभूद् इति दुन्दुभिविमोचनीयं होमं जुहोति
text_mt: With "This true agreement of yours has come about...", he offers the oblation for unfastening the drums.
He gives a kṛṣṇala piece to each of the chariot-racers.
Taking them back, he gives them to the brahman.
And a honey-pot made of gold weighing a hundred mānas.
Now he introduces the chant of Mahendra.

sanskrit_iast: aprastute kṣatrasyolbam asīti tārpyaṃ yajamānaḥ paridhatte
meaning: अप्रस्तुते क्षत्रस्योल्बम् असीति तार्प्यं यजमानः परिधत्ते
text_mt: Before it is chanted, the sacrificer puts on a tārpya garment with "You are the inner membrane of the royal power."
The wife [puts on an apron] made of darbha grass with "You are the womb of the royal power."
The sacrificer calls out to his wife: "Wife, come!"
The other responds: "Let us two climb!"

sanskrit_iast: ahaṃ nāv ubhayoḥ suvo rokṣyāmīti yajamāno 'ntataḥ
meaning: अहं नाव् उभयोः सुवो रोक्ष्यामीति यजमानो ऽन्ततः
text_mt: Finally the sacrificer says: "I will climb to heaven for the two of us."

sanskrit_iast: vājaś ca prasavaś ceti dvādaśa vājaprasavīyān homān hutvāyur yajñena kalpatām iti daśabhiḥ kalpaiḥ sarajase niśraṇyā yūpaṃ yajamāna ārohati
meaning: वाजश् च प्रसवश् चेति द्वादश वाजप्रसवीयान् होमान् हुत्वायुर् यज्ञेन कल्पताम् इति दशभिः कल्पैः सरजसे निश्रण्या यूपं यजमान आरोहति
text_mt: Having offered the twelve vājaprasavīya oblations with "Strength and impulse...", the sacrificer ascends the sacrificial post by a ladder with "May life prosper by sacrifice..." through the ten kalpa formulas, accompanied by [a wheel] with pollen.

sanskrit_iast: suvar devām̐ aganmety agraṃ prapya japati
meaning: सुवर् देवाम्̐ अगन्मेत्य् अग्रं प्रप्य जपति
text_mt: Having reached the top, he mutters: "We have gone to heaven, to the gods!"

sanskrit_iast: sam ahaṃ prajayā saṃ mayā prajeti gṛhān prekṣate
meaning: सम् अहं प्रजया सं मया प्रजेति गृहान् प्रेक्षते
text_mt: He looks at his home with "May I be united with offspring, may offspring be united with me!"

sanskrit_iast: tam āśvatthair āsapuṭair ūṣapuṭair ubhayair vā vaiśyāḥ pratidiśam arpayanti /
meaning: तम् आश्वत्थैर् आसपुटैर् ऊषपुटैर् उभयैर् वा वैश्याः प्रतिदिशम् अर्पयन्ति /
text_mt: The vaiśyas throw at him from each direction [packets of food] in packets of aśvattha leaves or packets of saline earth, or both.
Or the principal priests, having tied them onto long bamboos, [throw them]:
The adhvaryu from the east with "To food for you!";
The brahman from the south with "To the eating of food for you!";
The hotṛ from the west with "To strength for you!";
The udgātā from the north with "To winning strength for you!"
He turns toward each thrower.

sanskrit_iast: iyaṃ te rāṇ mitrāya yantrāya dhartrāya kṛṣyai kṣemāya rayyai poṣāyeti pratyavarohati
meaning: इयं ते राण् मित्राय यन्त्राय धर्त्राय कृष्यै क्षेमाय रय्यै पोषायेति प्रत्यवरोहति
text_mt: He descends with "This is your rule: for friendship, for restraint, for support, for agriculture, for security, for wealth, for prosperity!"
In front of the sacrificial post, having spread out a he-goat skin with the neck to the east and the hair upward,

sanskrit_iast: tasmiñ chatamānaṃ hiraṇyaṃ nidhāyāmṛtaṃ asīti hiraṇye dakṣiṇaṃ pādaṃ yajamānaḥ pratiṣṭhāpayate
meaning: तस्मिञ् छतमानं हिरण्यं निधायामृतं असीति हिरण्ये दक्षिणं पादं यजमानः प्रतिष्ठापयते
text_mt: and placed gold weighing a hundred mānas upon it, the sacrificer sets his right foot upon the gold with "You are immortality."

sanskrit_iast: puṣṭir asi prajananam asīti bastājine savyam
meaning: पुष्टिर् असि प्रजननम् असीति बस्ताजिने सव्यम्
text_mt: His left [foot] upon the he-goat skin with "You are nourishment, you are procreation."
From there he ascends a chair.

sanskrit_iast: divaṃ proṣṭhinīm āroha tām āruhya prapaśyaikarāṇ manuṣyāṇām ity ārohantam abhimantrayate
meaning: दिवं प्रोष्ठिनीम् आरोह ताम् आरुह्य प्रपश्यैकराण् मनुष्याणाम् इत्य् आरोहन्तम् अभिमन्त्रयते
text_mt: He addresses him as he ascends with "Ascend heaven, the bench; having ascended it, look out as the sole ruler among men!"
With seven [formulas], he offers the seven preliminary food-oblations.
He is consecrated during the chant of Mahendra, just as at the piling of the fire altar.

sanskrit_iast: mādhyaṃdinasya savanasya madhyama ukthyaparyāye brahmasāmny upākṛte 'tra sārasvataprabhṛtīn uttarān ālabhante
meaning: माध्यंदिनस्य सवनस्य मध्यम उक्थ्यपर्याये ब्रह्मसाम्न्य् उपाकृते ऽत्र सारस्वतप्रभृतीन् उत्तरान् आलभन्ते
text_mt: At the midday pressing, in the middle ukthya round, when the Brahman's saman has been introduced, they seize the later [victims] beginning with the one for Sarasvatī.
He proceeds with their omenta without basting them.

sanskrit_iast: sārasvatasya vapayā pracarya samavadāyetareṣāṃ vapābhiḥ pracarati
meaning: सारस्वतस्य वपया प्रचर्य समवदायेतरेषां वपाभिः प्रचरति
text_mt: Having proceeded with the omentum of the victim for Sarasvatī, he cuts off [portions] together and proceeds with the omenta of the other [victims].
Having proceeded with the animal cake of the victim for Sarasvatī, he proceeds with the [cake] made of wild rice.
However, the sviṣṭakṛt and the iḍā are common.
The principal priests are the eaters of the remnants of the oblation.
They partake of the remnants of the oblation in the āgnīdhra [shed].
Now he proceeds with the portions for the deity of those ending with the one for Sarasvatī, up to the conversation of the iḍā,

sanskrit_iast: ṣoḍaśinā pracarya hotṛcamasamukhyāṃś camasān unnīya bṛhataḥ stotram upākaroti
meaning: षोडशिना प्रचर्य होतृचमसमुख्यांश् चमसान् उन्नीय बृहतः स्तोत्रम् उपाकरोति
text_mt: Having proceeded with the ṣoḍaśin [draught] and drawn the goblets, beginning with the hotṛ's goblet, he introduces the chant of the Bṛhat [sāman].
At the time of proceeding, the adhvaryu takes up the hotṛ's goblet,
the camasādhvaryus the goblets,
the [other] priests the remaining soma draughts,
the pratiprasthātṛ takes up the chief of the surā draughts,
the chariot-racers the remaining surā draughts.

sanskrit_iast: saṃpṛca stha saṃ mā bhadreṇa pṛṅkteti prāṅ adhvaryuḥ somagrahair uddravati /
meaning: संपृच स्थ सं मा भद्रेण पृङ्क्तेति प्राङ् अध्वर्युः सोमग्रहैर् उद्द्रवति /
text_mt: With "You are united; unite me with good fortune!", the adhvaryu runs forward toward the east with the soma draughts.

sanskrit_iast: vipṛca stha vi mā pāpmanā pṛṅkteti pratyaṅ pratiprasthāṭ surāgrahaiḥ
meaning: विपृच स्थ वि मा पाप्मना पृङ्क्तेति प्रत्यङ् प्रतिप्रस्थाट् सुराग्रहैः
text_mt: With "You are disunited; disunite me from evil!", the pratiprasthātṛ [runs] toward the west with the surā draughts.
They stand near the edge of the āhavanīya with the soma draughts,
near the edge of the mārjālīya with the surā draughts.
He proceeds with the soma draughts.
Following the vaṣaṭ-call and the secondary vaṣaṭ-call, they shake the surā draughts.
The partaking of the soma has been explained.
He modifies the formula for partaking: "...having the virāj as metre."
They bring the cut-off portions of the victim for the Maruts and the soma draughts to the priests,
the non-cut-off portions and the surā draughts to the chariot-racers.
Having torn them apart on the southern hip of the altar ground, they partake of them.

sanskrit_iast: kakudo rājaputro dhruvagopo naivāragopo vā prāśnīyāt /
meaning: ककुदो राजपुत्रो ध्रुवगोपो नैवारगोपो वा प्राश्नीयात् /
text_mt: A foremost prince, a constant protector, or a protector of wild rice should eat [them].
Or [he offers] the whole peak [mess] after all the soma [oblations].
Here he proceeds with the deity-section of the animals beginning with that for Sarasvant.
"They proceed in the forest of the sacrifice," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

sanskrit_iast: tad yatreṣṭā anūyājā bhavanty avyūḍhāḥ srucaḥ /
meaning: तद् यत्रेष्टा अनूयाजा भवन्त्य् अव्यूढाः स्रुचः /
text_mt: When the after-offerings are offered, [and] the ladles are not yet displaced,

sanskrit_iast: hvalati vā etad yajño yad evaṃ kurvantīti
meaning: ह्वलति वा एतद् यज्ञो यद् एवं कुर्वन्तीति
text_mt: "The sacrifice indeed stumbles when they do so," [so says the Brāhmaṇa].

sanskrit_iast: tasmād yatraiva pūrveṣāṃ vapābhiś careyus tad itareṣām /
meaning: तस्माद् यत्रैव पूर्वेषां वपाभिश् चरेयुस् तद् इतरेषाम् /
text_mt: Therefore, wherever they proceed with the omenta of the earlier [victims], there [they should proceed with the omenta] of the others;
and wherever [they proceed] with the oblation-materials, there [they should proceed] with the oblation-materials.
The Vājapeya is concluded.
Having sacrificed with it, he should sacrifice with the Sautrāmaṇī,
or with the curd-mixture for Mitra and Varuṇa.
As long as he lives, he should not descend before anyone;
or he should sacrifice with the Bṛhaspatisava that causes descending.
"He becomes one who possesses a white umbrella," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].
A king desiring heaven should sacrifice with the Rājasūya.
The first day is an Agniṣṭoma terminating with five [stotras].
He gives five thousand at the Pavitra,
thirty [thousand] at the Abhiṣecanīya,
twenty [thousand] at the Vyuṣṭi-dvirātra,
[and] five [thousand] at the Kṣatradhṛti.
Or else, four [thousand] at the Abhiṣecanīya,
and one thousand for each of the other days.

sanskrit_iast: ṣaṣṭitrīṇi śatāni sahasrāṇāṃ dadātīti bahvṛcabrāhmaṇaṃ bhavhati
meaning: षष्टित्रीणि शतानि सहस्राणां ददातीति बह्वृचब्राह्मणं भव्हति
text_mt: "He gives three hundred and sixty thousands," so states the Brāhmaṇa of the Rigvedins.
He should distribute the sacrificial gifts in such a way that his days [of ritual] have their own proper times.
On the next day, he sacrifices day after day with the eight [offerings] beginning with the one to Anumati.
While grinding [the grains] for the offering to Anumati, he scatters [some] to the west and to the north.
Those that fall off towards the west of the yoke-pin form the cake on one potsherd for Nirṛti.

sanskrit_iast: ya udañcastānudaṅ paretya valmīkavapāmuddhatyedamahamamuṣyāmuṣyāyaṇasya kṣetriyamavayaja iti śuktyā valmīkavapāyāṃ hutvedamahamamuṣyāmuṣyāyaṇasya kṣetriyamapidadhāmīti tayaiva śuktyā valmīkavapāmapidadhyāt
meaning: य उदञ्चस्तानुदङ् परेत्य वल्मीकवपामुद्धत्येदमहममुष्यामुष्यायणस्य क्षेत्रियमवयज इति शुक्त्या वल्मीकवपायां हुत्वेदमहममुष्यामुष्यायणस्य क्षेत्रियमपिदधामीति तयैव शुक्त्या वल्मीकवपामपिदध्यात्
text_mt: Those that [fall off] towards the north, having gone north with them and taken up the moist earth of an anthill, [and] having made an offering into the moist earth of the anthill with a shell with the words: "Herewith I sacrifice away the hereditary disease of so-and-so, son of so-and-so," he should cover the moist earth of the anthill with that same shell, with the words: "Herewith I cover the hereditary disease of so-and-so, son of so-and-so."
"He offers with the moist earth of an anthill, [and] he covers with the moist earth of an anthill," say some.
Having placed the oblation for Anumati, he proceeds with the offering for Nirṛti.

sanskrit_iast: vīhi svāheti gārhaptye hutvā dakṣiṇāgnerekolmukaṃ dhūpāyaddharati
meaning: वीहि स्वाहेति गार्हप्त्ये हुत्वा दक्षिणाग्नेरेकोल्मुकं धूपायद्धरति
text_mt: Having offered into the gārhapatya with the words, "Svāhā to the bird!", he takes a smoking brand from the southern fire.

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇamaparamavāntaradeśaṃ gatvā svakṛta iriṇe pradare vopasamādhāyaiṣa te nirṛte bhāga ityaṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ visraṃsikākāṇḍābhyāṃ vā nairṛtaṃ sarvahutaṃ juhoti
meaning: दक्षिणमपरमवान्तरदेशं गत्वा स्वकृत इरिणे प्रदरे वोपसमाधायैष ते निरृते भाग इत्यङ्गुष्ठाभ्यां विस्रंसिकाकाण्डाभ्यां वा नैरृतं सर्वहुतं जुहोति
text_mt: Having gone to the south-western direction, [and] having established [the fire] in a natural cleft or chasm, he offers the oblation for Nirṛti as a whole-offering with the thumbs or with stems of visraṃsikā-reeds, with the words: "This is your share, O Nirṛti!"
A black garment with black fringe is the sacrificial gift.
"A black garment with torn border," say some.
"They return without looking back, for concealment from Nirṛti," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

sanskrit_iast: svāhā namo ya idaṃ cakāreti punaretya gārhapatye hutvānumatena pracarati
meaning: स्वाहा नमो य इदं चकारेति पुनरेत्य गार्हपत्ये हुत्वानुमतेन प्रचरति
text_mt: Having returned, [and] having offered into the gārhapatya with the words, "Svāhā, homage to him who did this!", he proceeds with the offering to Anumati.
Having sacrificed day after day with these [offerings ending with] the mess of boiled rice for the Ādityas, he undertakes the Cāturmāsyas.
He sacrifices with them for a year.
He does not combine the Śunāsīrīya [with the other seasonal sacrifices].
Then he sacrifices with the Indraturīya having four oblations,
namely, [the cake] on eight potsherds for Agni, and so on.
With it he should cause one who has a rival, or one who is dear, to sacrifice.
In the night of that very night, he sacrifices with the Pañcedhmīya.

sanskrit_iast: caturdhāhavanīyaṃ pratidiśaṃ vyuddhṛtya madhye pañcamaṃ kṛtvā pṛthagidhmānupasamādhāya juhvāṃ pañcagṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā ye devāḥ puraḥsada ityetairyathāliṅgaṃ juhoti /
meaning: चतुर्धाहवनीयं प्रतिदिशं व्युद्धृत्य मध्ये पञ्चमं कृत्वा पृथगिध्मानुपसमाधाय जुह्वां पञ्चगृहीतं गृहीत्वा ये देवाः पुरःसद इत्येतैर्यथालिङ्गं जुहोति /
text_mt: Having taken up the āhavanīya in four parts toward each direction, having made a fifth in the middle, having placed separate piles of firewood [on them], [and] having taken five ladlings into the juhū ladle, he offers with the verses, "The gods who sit in the front...", according to their characteristics,

sanskrit_iast: samūḍhaṃ rakṣa iti madhya idhmānupasamūhyaikadhopasamādhāyāparaṃ pañcagṛhītaṃ gṛhītvāgnaye rakṣoghne svāhetyuttarāḥ pañcāhutīrjuhoti
meaning: समूढं रक्ष इति मध्य इध्मानुपसमूह्यैकधोपसमाधायापरं पञ्चगृहीतं गृहीत्वाग्नये रक्षोघ्ने स्वाहेत्युत्तराः पञ्चाहुतीर्जुहोति
text_mt: Having gathered the firewood together into the middle with the words, "Gathered together is the rakṣas!", having laid them together as one, [and] having taken another five ladlings, he offers the subsequent five oblations with the words, "Svāhā to Agni, the slayer of rakṣases!"
A chariot drawn by three horses is the sacrificial gift,

sanskrit_iast: tena yajeta yo rakṣobhyo bibhīyātpiśācebhyo vā
meaning: तेन यजेत यो रक्षोभ्यो बिभीयात्पिशाचेभ्यो वा
text_mt: He who fears rakṣases or piśācas should sacrifice with it.
At dawn, before the agnihotra, they proceed with the Apāmārga-homa.
Having fetched apāmārga plants from a pool of water, having turned them into groats, he takes a smoking brand from the southern fire.

sanskrit_iast: uttaramaparamavāntaradeśaṃ gatvā svakṛta iriṇe pradare vopasamādhāya devasya tvetyanudrutya rakṣaso vadhaṃ juhomīti parṇamayena sruveṇa juhoti
meaning: उत्तरमपरमवान्तरदेशं गत्वा स्वकृत इरिणे प्रदरे वोपसमाधाय देवस्य त्वेत्यनुद्रुत्य रक्षसो वधं जुहोमीति पर्णमयेन स्रुवेण जुहोति
text_mt: Having gone to the north-western direction, having established [the fire] in a natural cleft or chasm, [and] having recited, "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ...", he offers with a spoon of parṇa wood with the words, "I offer the slaying of the rakṣas!"

sanskrit_iast: hataṃ rakṣa iti sruvamanuprahṛtyāvadhiṣma rakṣa ityupatiṣṭhate
meaning: हतं रक्ष इति स्रुवमनुप्रहृत्यावधिष्म रक्ष इत्युपतिष्ठते
text_mt: Having thrown in the spoon with the words, "Slain is the rakṣas!", he attends [the fire] with the words, "We have slain the rakṣas!"
They return without looking back, 'for the concealment of the demons', so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].
Having offered the agnihotra, he pours out the offerings to the Devikās:
a twelve-pot-sherd cake for Dhātṛ—[these] five.
A pair of cattle is the dakṣiṇā.
An animal is also to be immolated here for Dhātṛ;
An eleven-pot-sherd [cake] for Agni-and-Viṣṇu—[these are] three offerings.
With the first of these, one desiring a village should sacrifice;
with the second, one desiring spiritual brilliance;
He pours out a twelve-pot-sherd cake for Vaiśvānara.
[He pours out] a pap of barley, solid, a span in measure in all directions;
a horse that carries [a draft] without being castrated is the dakṣiṇā.
A pap for Bṛhaspati—[these are] twelve offerings to the Jewel-holders day after day.

sanskrit_iast: yasya gṛhe nirvapati tata iṣṭipariveṣaṇaṃ dakṣiṇā ca
meaning: यस्य गृहे निर्वपति तत इष्टिपरिवेषणं दक्षिणा च
text_mt: In whosever house he pours out [the offering], from there come the distribution of food at the sacrifice and the dakṣiṇā.
The fourth [offering] is a pap for Bhaga in the house of the favorite wife.
A heifer whose embryo has miscarried is the dakṣiṇā.
Some say there is an offering to Nirṛti, a pap the measure of a thumb-joint in all directions.
A three-pot-sherd [cake] to Viṣṇu, the thirteenth, in the house of the carpenter and chariot-maker.
or [he offers] in [the house] of the carpenter or the chariot-maker, say some.
A gavidhukā-pap to Rudra in the house of the dice-keeper;
A halter made of horsehair is the dakṣiṇā;
or a sword wrapped in hair, or a spotted [bull];
'a three-year-old', so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

sanskrit_iast: asirvālāvṛto vārdhrīvālapratigrathitā govyacchinī barāsī dāmatūṣā śabalo vā vatsataraḥ
meaning: असिर्वालावृतो वार्ध्रीवालप्रतिग्रथिता गोव्यच्छिनी बरासी दामतूषा शबलो वा वत्सतरः
text_mt: A sword wrapped with hair, a strap interwoven with hair, a cow-slayer, a coarse cloth with long fringes, or a spotted young bull.
A red-eared horse, say some.
'To the road, svāhā!'—thus he offers in the house of the messenger.
Three leather [quivers] containing arrows are the dakṣiṇā;
or a bow wrapped with reed.
In the house of the sacrificer, he pours out in return an eleven-pot-sherd cake to Indra the Good Protector;
an eleven-pot-sherd [cake] to Indra the Deliverer from Distress.

sanskrit_iast: ayaṃ no rājā vṛtrahā rājā bhūtvā vṛtraṃ vadhyāditi purastātsviṣṭakṛto 'dhvaryurjapati
meaning: अयं नो राजा वृत्रहा राजा भूत्वा वृत्रं वध्यादिति पुरस्तात्स्विष्टकृतो ऽध्वर्युर्जपति
text_mt: 'May this our king, the slayer of Vṛtra, having become king, slay Vṛtra'—thus the adhvaryu mutters before the sviṣṭakṛt.

sanskrit_iast: svayamavapannāyā aśvatthaśākhāyai maitraṃ pātraṃ catuḥsraktiṃ karoti
meaning: स्वयमवपन्नाया अश्वत्थशाखायै मैत्रं पात्रं चतुःस्रक्तिं करोति
text_mt: From a branch of an aśvattha tree that has fallen by itself, he makes a four-cornered vessel for Mitra.
They milk a white cow having a white calf into a skin bag made of unprocessed hide.
They carry it about continuously until it thickens of itself.
Having churned of itself, they hang it in the sun.
Then, having melted of itself, it becomes clarified butter.
On the next day, he initiates the consecrations of the Abhiṣecanīya, which is an Ukthya.
The consecratory offering belongs to Mitra-and-Bṛhaspati.
The altar ground is self-made;
they make half of the altar ground;
he binds up half that is self-cut;
he fells half of the firewood;

sanskrit_iast: pātrasaṃsādanakāle bārhaspatyaṃ caruṃ maitraṃ ca pātraṃ kapālānāṃ sthāne prayunakti
meaning: पात्रसंसादनकाले बार्हस्पत्यं चरुं मैत्रं च पात्रं कपालानां स्थाने प्रयुनक्ति
text_mt: At the time of setting down the vessels, he employs a vessel for the mess of boiled rice for Bṛhaspati and a vessel for Mitra in place of the potsherds.
With the dividing mantra, he separates the husked rice grains into those with ears and those without ears.
"The smallest and the largest," say some.
Those that are with ears [broken grains] become the Bārhaspatya [mess of boiled rice] cooked in milk.
When it is cooked, he covers it with the vessel for Mitra.
Into it he pours self-melted [ghee].
He scatters the earless [whole grains] into the ghee with the strainer.
He places the two [vessels] one above the other.
Thus both are cooked together.
Having placed the Bārhaspatya [mess], he places the Maitra [mess].
A white-backed [ox] is the sacrificial gift for the Bārhaspatya [offering];
And that [cow] which is white and has a white calf.

sanskrit_iast: tathābhiṣecanīyasyokthyasya dīkṣāḥ pravardhayati yathā saṃvatsarasya daśarātre śiṣṭe daśapeyo bhaviṣyatīti
meaning: तथाभिषेचनीयस्योक्थ्यस्य दीक्षाः प्रवर्धयति यथा संवत्सरस्य दशरात्रे शिष्टे दशपेयो भविष्यतीति
text_mt: He extends the consecration days of the Abhiṣecanīya Ukthya sacrifice in such a way that the Daśapeya will take place when ten nights of the year remain.
He buys both somas together, for the Abhiṣecanīya and for the Daśapeya;

sanskrit_iast: ardhaṃ rājñaḥ purohitasya gṛhe daśapeyārthaṃ nidadhāti
meaning: अर्धं राज्ञः पुरोहितस्य गृहे दशपेयार्थं निदधाति
text_mt: He deposits half of the king [Soma] in the house of the domestic priest for the sake of the Daśapeya.

sanskrit_iast: agnīṣomīyasya paśupuroḍāśam aṣṭau devasuvāṃ havīṃṣy anunirvapati
meaning: अग्नीषोमीयस्य पशुपुरोडाशम् अष्टौ देवसुवां हवींष्य् अनुनिर्वपति
text_mt: After the animal cake for Agni-Soma, he pours out the eight offerings that impel the gods (devasū).
The Sviṣṭakṛt offering and the iḍā, however, are common.

sanskrit_iast: purastāt sviṣṭakṛtaḥ savitā tvā prasavānāṃ suvatām iti brahmā yajamānasya hastaṃ gṛhṇāti
meaning: पुरस्तात् स्विष्टकृतः सविता त्वा प्रसवानां सुवताम् इति ब्रह्मा यजमानस्य हस्तं गृह्णाति
text_mt: Before the Sviṣṭakṛt offering, the brahman priest takes the hand of the sacrificer with [the verse]: "May Savitṛ impel you of the impellers..."

sanskrit_iast: athainaṃ ratnibhya āvedayatyeṣa vo bharatā rājeti /
meaning: अथैनं रत्निभ्य आवेदयत्येष वो भरता राजेति /
text_mt: Then he announces him to the royal dignitaries: "This, O Bharatas, is your king!"
"This, O Kurus, is your king!" to a descendant of Kuru;
"This, O Pañcālas, is your king!" to a descendant of Pañcāla;

sanskrit_iast: eṣa vaḥ kurupañcālā rājeti vā kurupāñcālān /
meaning: एष वः कुरुपञ्चाला राजेति वा कुरुपाञ्चालान् /
text_mt: Or "This, O Kuru-Pañcālas, is your king!" to the Kuru-Pañcālas;
"This, O people, is your king!" to other kings.

meaning: सोमो ऽस्माकं ब्राह्मणानां राजेति ब्रह्मा जपति
text_mt: "Soma is the king of us, the brāhmaṇas," mutters the brahman priest.

sanskrit_iast: prati tyan nāma rājyam adhāyīti vāruṇībhyāṃ yajamāno mukhaṃ vimṛṣṭe
meaning: प्रति त्यन् नाम राज्यम् अधायीति वारुणीभ्यां यजमानो मुखं विमृष्टे
text_mt: The sacrificer wipes his face with the two [verses] addressed to Varuṇa: "This name, the kingship, has been assumed..."

sanskrit_iast: viṣṇoḥ kramo 'sīti trīn viṣṇukramān prācaḥ krāmati
meaning: विष्णोः क्रमो ऽसीति त्रीन् विष्णुक्रमान् प्राचः क्रामति
text_mt: With [the formula]: "You are the stride of Viṣṇu," he strides three Viṣṇu-strides toward the east.

sanskrit_iast: prāṅ māhendrāt kṛtvā mādhyaṃdinīyān puroḍāśān nirupya mārutam ekaviṃśatikapālaṃ nirvapati /
meaning: प्राङ् माहेन्द्रात् कृत्वा माध्यंदिनीयान् पुरोडाशान् निरुप्य मारुतम् एकविंशतिकपालं निर्वपति /
text_mt: Having performed [the rites] up to the draught for Mahendra and having poured out the midday sacrificial cakes, he pours out [an oblation] on twenty-one potsherds for the Maruts,
He arranges its potsherds with the third sets of the Araṇye'nuvākya;
With these two [sets]: "Thus and otherwise...";
In the middle with an Araṇye'nuvākya [formula].
Having covered [the cake with ashes], he takes the draughts of water.
In the Āgnīdhra [shed] they are taken into Vāyu-vessels.
Sixteen or seventeen oblations are offered;
Just as many draughts are taken.

sanskrit_iast: artheta stheti sārasvatiṣv apsu hutvaitenaiva mantreṇa gṛhṇāti
meaning: अर्थेत स्थेति सारस्वतिष्व् अप्सु हुत्वैतेनैव मन्त्रेण गृह्णाति
text_mt: Having offered into the waters of the Sarasvatī with: "You are fit for the purpose...", he takes [water] with this very formula.
With whichever [formula] he makes the offering, with that he takes [the water].

sanskrit_iast: apāṃ patir iti samudriyāḥ saindhavīrvā yo vānyaḥ puṃnadaḥ syāt
meaning: अपां पतिर् इति समुद्रियाः सैन्धवीर्वा यो वान्यः पुंनदः स्यात्
text_mt: With "Lord of the waters..." [he takes water] from the ocean or from the Sindhu, or whichever other river has a masculine name.
When a man or an animal has stepped in, one wave fights against the current,
With "You are having a bull-host..." that which goes with the current.
With "You dwell in the pen..." [he takes] of well-waters.
With "You are the might of the Maruts..." of those which flow against the current;

sanskrit_iast: prahāvarī stheti yā utsyanditvā tatraiva pratyavasicyante
meaning: प्रहावरी स्थेति या उत्स्यन्दित्वा तत्रैव प्रत्यवसिच्यन्ते
text_mt: With "You are overflowing..." of those which, having welled up, are poured down right there.
With "You flow around..." of flowing rivers.
With "Sun-splendoured..." of rainwater when the sun shines.
With "Sun-skinned..." of those in which reflections are seen.
With "Mighty ones..." of the amniotic fluid of a cow.
With "All-nourishing..." of milk.
With "Born of the brilliance of Agni..." of ghee.
With "The sap of waters and plants..." of honey.

sanskrit_iast: apo devīr madhumatīr agṛhṇann iti sarvatra home grahaṇe cānuṣajati
meaning: अपो देवीर् मधुमतीर् अगृह्णन्न् इति सर्वत्र होमे ग्रहणे चानुषजति
text_mt: With 'The divine waters took what contains sweetness', he appends [this formula] everywhere at an oblation and at a drawing.

sanskrit_iast: rāṣṭradā stha rāṣṭraṃ datta svāheti homasaṃyukte /
meaning: राष्ट्रदा स्थ राष्ट्रं दत्त स्वाहेति होमसंयुक्ते /
text_mt: With 'You are kingdom-givers; give kingdom, svāhā!' [at that which is] accompanied by an oblation;
with 'You are kingdom-givers; give kingdom to so-and-so' [at that which is] accompanied by a drawing.

sanskrit_iast: devīrāpa iti vaitase sate grahānsamavanīyānādhṛṣṭāḥ sidatetyantarā hoturdhiṣṇiyaṃ brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaśca sādayitvānibhṛṣṭamasīti tasmiñchatamānaṃ hiraṇyamavadhāya śukrā vaḥ śukreṇotpunāmīti tenotpūya sadhamādo dyumninīrūrja etā iti caturṣu pātreṣu vyānayati /
meaning: देवीराप इति वैतसे सते ग्रहान्समवनीयानाधृष्टाः सिदतेत्यन्तरा होतुर्धिष्णियं ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनश्च सादयित्वानिभृष्टमसीति तस्मिञ्छतमानं हिरण्यमवधाय शुक्रा वः शुक्रेणोत्पुनामीति तेनोत्पूय सधमादो द्युम्निनीरूर्ज एता इति चतुर्षु पात्रेषु व्यानयति /
text_mt: Having poured together the draughts into a reed bowl with 'O divine waters', having placed [it] between the dhiṣṇiya of the hotṛ and [that] of the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin with 'Unassailable, sit down', having put a gold piece weighing a hundred mānas into it with 'You are unburned', having purified [the waters] with it with 'Bright ones, I purify you with the bright one', he distributes [the waters] into four vessels with 'These are the rapturous, brilliant invigorating draughts.'
[Into vessels] of palāśa wood, of udumbara wood, of aśvattha wood, and of nyagrodha wood.

sanskrit_iast: yaḥ sate prarekas tam udaṅ paretya rudra yat te krayī paraṃ nāmety āgnīdhrīye juhoti
meaning: यः सते प्ररेकस् तम् उदङ् परेत्य रुद्र यत् ते क्रयी परं नामेत्य् आग्नीध्रीये जुहोति
text_mt: Going north, he offers the remnant that is in the bowl on the āgnīdhra fire with 'O Rudra, your highest name is the purchaser.'
With 'You are the outer membrane of dominion', the sacrificer puts on a tārpya garment.

sanskrit_iast: kṣatrasya yonir asīti pāṇḍaram uṣṇīṣaṃ dvitīyam
meaning: क्षत्रस्य योनिर् असीति पाण्डरम् उष्णीषं द्वितीयम्
text_mt: With 'You are the womb of dominion', [he puts on] a white [undergarment, and] a turban as the second.
They call a white [garment] pāṇḍara.
Some [prescribe] three: the pāṇḍara, the tārpya, and the turban.
Then he purifies him with one hundred and one blades of darbha grass.
the right eye with fifty;
Then he feeds him curd.

meaning: अङ्क्ते ऽभ्यङ्क्ते ऽश्नाति वासः परिधत्त इत्येवमनुपूर्वाण्येके समामनन्ति
text_mt: Some traditionally teach the order in this way: he anoints [his eyes], rubs [his body], eats, [and] puts on the garment.
These rites are performed at the āgnīdhra [hearth].

sanskrit_iast: apa upasparśayitvāvinno agnir ity āvido yajamānaṃ vācayan bahir udānīyaiṣa vo bharatā rājety uktvendrasya vajro 'sīti dhanur yajamānāya prayacchati
meaning: अप उपस्पर्शयित्वाविन्नो अग्निर् इत्य् आविदो यजमानं वाचयन् बहिर् उदानीयैष वो भरता राजेत्य् उक्त्वेन्द्रस्य वज्रो ऽसीति धनुर् यजमानाय प्रयच्छति
text_mt: Having made him touch water, causing the sacrificer to recite the proclamations beginning with 'Agni is found', having led him out towards the north, and having said 'This is your king, O Bharatas', he hands the bow to the sacrificer with 'You are Indra's thunderbolt.'
With 'You are expellers of enemies', [he gives him] three barbed arrows.

sanskrit_iast: pāta mā pratyañcam iti pradīyamānān anumantrayate
meaning: पात मा प्रत्यञ्चम् इति प्रदीयमानान् अनुमन्त्रयते
text_mt: With 'Protect me towards the west', [the sacrificer] recites over them as they are being handed over.

sanskrit_iast: pāta prāñcaṃ pāta pratyañcaṃ pātodañcam iti prayacchann adhvaryur japati
meaning: पात प्राञ्चं पात प्रत्यञ्चं पातोदञ्चम् इति प्रयच्छन्न् अध्वर्युर् जपति
text_mt: The adhvaryu whispers while handing [them] over: 'Protect [him] towards the east; protect [him] towards the west; protect [him] towards the north.'

meaning: मित्रो ऽसीति दक्षिणं बाहुं यजमान उद्यच्छते /
text_mt: The sacrificer raises his right arm with 'You are Mitra';
He addresses the raised [arms] with 'Golden-colored ones'.
Then he causes him to step out to the [five] directions with five [formulas],
And he steps along mentally.
Or at this point he should offer [the cake] for the Maruts.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ barhiṣadaṃ kṛtvainā vyāghraṃ pariṣasvajānāḥ siṃhaṃ hinvanti mahate saubhagāya /
meaning: तं बर्हिषदं कृत्वैना व्याघ्रं परिषस्वजानाः सिंहं हिन्वन्ति महते सौभगाय /
text_mt: Having placed it on the barhis, [he mutters:] 'Embracing this tiger, they urge the lion toward great prosperity;

sanskrit_iast: samudraṃ na suhavaṃ tasthivāṃsaṃ marmṛjyante dvīpinamapsvantariti sphyena puroḍāśamabhicarannihanti
meaning: समुद्रं न सुहवं तस्थिवांसं मर्मृज्यन्ते द्वीपिनमप्स्वन्तरिति स्फ्येन पुरोडाशमभिचरन्निहन्ति
text_mt: they groom the panther seated within the waters as an easily invoked sea'—with this he strikes down upon the sacrificial cake with the wooden sword, performing sorcery.

sanskrit_iast: yatsphya āśliṣyati yacca pratiśīryate tadviṣṇave śipiviṣṭāya juhoti
meaning: यत्स्फ्य आश्लिष्यति यच्च प्रतिशीर्यते तद्विष्णवे शिपिविष्टाय जुहोति
text_mt: Whatever adheres to the wooden sword and whatever breaks off, he offers that to Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa.

sanskrit_iast: agreṇa praśāsturdhiṣṇiyaṃ khādirīmaudumbarīṃ vāsandīṃ pratiṣṭhāpya somasya tviṣirasīti tasyāṃ śārdūlacarma prācīnagrīvamuttaralomāstīryāmṛtamasīti tasmiñchatamānaṃ hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya didyonmā pāhīti sauvarṇena śatamānena śatakṣareṇa śatakṛṣṇalena vā yajamānasya śīrṣannadhi nidhatte
meaning: अग्रेण प्रशास्तुर्धिष्णियं खादिरीमौदुम्बरीं वासन्दीं प्रतिष्ठाप्य सोमस्य त्विषिरसीति तस्यां शार्दूलचर्म प्राचीनग्रीवमुत्तरलोमास्तीर्यामृतमसीति तस्मिञ्छतमानं हिरण्यं निधाय दिद्योन्मा पाहीति सौवर्णेन शतमानेन शतक्षरेण शतकृष्णलेन वा यजमानस्य शीर्षन्नधि निधत्ते
text_mt: Having set up a chair of khadira or udumbara wood in front of the dhiṣṇiya of the praśāstṛ, having spread a tiger skin on it with the neck to the east and the hairy side up with 'You are the splendor of Soma', having placed a gold piece weighing a hundred mānas on it with 'You are immortality', he places [another gold piece] upon the sacrificer's head with 'Protect me from the missile', either a gold [piece] weighing a hundred mānas, or one of a hundred syllables, or one weighing a hundred kṛṣṇalas.

sanskrit_iast: tamārohanyajamāno 'veṣṭā dandaśūkā iti dakṣiṇena padā sīsaṃ paṇḍakāya pratyasyati /
meaning: तमारोहन्यजमानो ऽवेष्टा दन्दशूका इति दक्षिणेन पदा सीसं पण्डकाय प्रत्यस्यति /
text_mt: Mounting it, the sacrificer kicks away a lead [piece] with his right foot to a eunuch with 'The biters are uncoiled';

sanskrit_iast: nirastaṃ namuceḥśira iti savyena lohitāyasaṃ keśavāpāya
meaning: निरस्तं नमुचेःशिर इति सव्येन लोहितायसं केशवापाय
text_mt: with the left [foot], a copper [piece] to a barber with 'Cast away is the head of Namuci.'
They two throw them outside the altar ground.

sanskrit_iast: agnaye svāheti ṣaṭ pārthāni purastād abhiṣekasya juhoti
meaning: अग्नये स्वाहेति षट् पार्थानि पुरस्ताद् अभिषेकस्य जुहोति
text_mt: Before the consecration he offers the six Pārtha oblations with 'To Agni, svāhā!'
With 'To the earth, svāhā!', [he offers] the six aveṣṭi oblations of the beings.

sanskrit_iast: ūrdhvabāhuṃ tiṣṭhantaṃ māhendrasya stotraṃ praty abhiṣiñcati
meaning: ऊर्ध्वबाहुं तिष्ठन्तं माहेन्द्रस्य स्तोत्रं प्रत्य् अभिषिञ्चति
text_mt: He sprinkles him while he is standing with raised arms, in response to the Māhendra chant,

sanskrit_iast: <somo rājā> \ ity abhimantrya <somasya tvā dyumnenābhiṣiñcāmi> \ iti
meaning: <सोमो राजा> \ इत्य् अभिमन्त्र्य <सोमस्य त्वा द्युम्नेनाभिषिञ्चामि> \ इति
text_mt: having addressed him with 'King Soma', [and then sprinkling] with 'I consecrate you with the brilliance of Soma.'
The adhvaryu [sprinkles him] from the front with the palāśa [vessel].
the brahman from the south with the udumbara [vessel],
the vaiśya from the west with the aśvattha [vessel];
a relative [or] friend from the north with the nyagrodha [vessel].
He addresses him while he is being consecrated with 'You are the lord of dominion among dominions.'

meaning: समाववृत्रन्न् इति ये ऽभिषिच्यमानस्य लेपा व्यवस्रवन्ति
text_mt: With 'They have rolled together', [he addresses] the drippings that flow down the one being consecrated;

sanskrit_iast: indrasya yonir asi janadhā iti kṛṣṇaviṣāṇayā vāsāṃsi vicacṛte /
meaning: इन्द्रस्य योनिर् असि जनधा इति कृष्णविषाणया वासांसि विचचृते /
text_mt: With 'You are Indra's womb, sustaining the people', he loosens the garments with a black antelope horn,
He casts them onto the rubbish heap with 'Protect [me] from the sky.'

sanskrit_iast: indrāya svāheti ṣaṭ pārthāny upariṣṭād abhiṣekasya juhoti
meaning: इन्द्राय स्वाहेति षट् पार्थान्य् उपरिष्टाद् अभिषेकस्य जुहोति
text_mt: After the consecration, he offers the six Pārtha oblations with 'To Indra, svāhā!'
With 'To the waters, svāhā!', [he offers] the six aveṣṭi oblations of the beings.
Or at this point he should offer the remnant.

sanskrit_iast: yāṃ bhāryāṃ kāmayeta rāṣṭramasyai prajā syāditi tasyā aupāsane pratihitamārambhayitvā ye pātreṣu lepā vyavasṛtāstebhyo nāmavyatiṣañjanīyau homau juhuyātprajāpate na tvadetānīti
meaning: यां भार्यां कामयेत राष्ट्रमस्यै प्रजा स्यादिति तस्या औपासने प्रतिहितमारम्भयित्वा ये पात्रेषु लेपा व्यवसृतास्तेभ्यो नामव्यतिषञ्जनीयौ होमौ जुहुयात्प्रजापते न त्वदेतानीति
text_mt: For whichever wife he desires, 'May her offspring possess the kingdom', having made her touch [the oblation] placed on the aupāsana fire, he should offer out of the drippings that have flowed down into the vessels the two name-intertwining oblations with 'O Prajāpati, none other than you [pervades all these things]'.

sanskrit_iast: asāvamuṣya putro 'muṣyā asau putra iti nāmanī vyatiṣajati
meaning: असावमुष्य पुत्रो ऽमुष्या असौ पुत्र इति नामनी व्यतिषजति
text_mt: He intertwines the two names: 'So-and-so is the son of such-and-such [a woman]; so-and-so is the son of such-and-such [a woman].'

sanskrit_iast: indrasya vajro 'sīti ratham upāvahṛtya mitrāvaruṇayos tvā praśāstroḥ praśiṣā yunajmīti praṣṭivāhinaṃ rathaṃ yunakti
meaning: इन्द्रस्य वज्रो ऽसीति रथम् उपावहृत्य मित्रावरुणयोस् त्वा प्रशास्त्रोः प्रशिषा युनज्मीति प्रष्टिवाहिनं रथं युनक्ति
text_mt: Having brought down the chariot with, 'You are Indra's thunderbolt,' he yokes the chariot drawn by three horses with, 'By the command of Mitra and Varuṇa, the two rulers, I yoke you.'

meaning: विष्णोः क्रमो ऽसीति रथं यजमानो ऽभ्येति
text_mt: With "You are the stride of Viṣṇu," the sacrificer approaches the chariot.
The kṣatriya who has been assigned takes hold of him from behind.
The brahman follows on the right with the very [verse]: "Thou hast prevailed, O thou invoked by many."
He sets out with: "May I conquer under the impulse of the Maruts!"
A noble with a bow stands in front or to the north.

sanskrit_iast: tasmā etān iṣūn asyaty āptaṃ mana iti
meaning: तस्मा एतान् इषून् अस्यत्य् आप्तं मन इति
text_mt: He discharges these arrows at him with: "The mind is obtained."

sanskrit_iast: ekaikamutsṛjya taṃ jitvā samahamindriyeṇa vīryeṇeti pradakṣiṇamāvartate
meaning: एकैकमुत्सृज्य तं जित्वा समहमिन्द्रियेण वीर्येणेति प्रदक्षिणमावर्तते
text_mt: Having shot them one by one [and] having defeated him, he turns around sunwise with: "Together with sensory power, with virility."
He comes to a halt where he sets out from.
With: "Thou art the thunderbolt of Indra," he nudges the wife and the horses with the end of the bow.

sanskrit_iast: eṣa vajro vājasāstena nau putro vājaṃ sediti dhanuḥ patnyai prayacchati
meaning: एष वज्रो वाजसास्तेन नौ पुत्रो वाजं सेदिति धनुः पत्न्यै प्रयच्छति
text_mt: With: "This thunderbolt wins booty; through it may a son conquer booty for the two of us," he hands the bow over to his wife.

sanskrit_iast: paśūnāṃ manyurasīti vārāhī upānahāvupamucya namo mātra ityavarokṣyanpṛthivīmabhimantryāvaruhya maṇīnpratimuñcate /
meaning: पशूनां मन्युरसीति वाराही उपानहावुपमुच्य नमो मात्र इत्यवरोक्ष्यन्पृथिवीमभिमन्त्र्यावरुह्य मणीन्प्रतिमुञ्चते /
text_mt: Having put on boar-skin sandals with: "Thou art the fury of cattle," having addressed the earth with: "Homage to the mother!" as he is about to descend, having descended, he attaches amulets [to himself]:
Some teach [putting] the golden one in the middle.

sanskrit_iast: agnaye gṛhapataye svāheti rathavimocanīyānhomānhutvā haṃsaḥ śuciṣaditi saha saṃgrahītrā rathavāhane rathamatyādadhāti
meaning: अग्नये गृहपतये स्वाहेति रथविमोचनीयान्होमान्हुत्वा हंसः शुचिषदिति सह संग्रहीत्रा रथवाहने रथमत्यादधाति
text_mt: Having offered the chariot-releasing oblations with: "To Agni, lord of the house, svāhā," he places the chariot onto the chariot-stand together with the charioteer with: "The goose sitting in the pure."
When it is placed, the charioteer steps down.

meaning: मित्रो ऽसीति दक्षिणं बाहुं यजमान उपावहरते /
text_mt: The sacrificer lowers his right arm with: "Thou art Mitra";
He lowers his two hands into the curd-mixture for the Viśvedevas with: "Together with all the gods."

sanskrit_iast: sadasi sanme bhūyā iti vā maitrāvaruṇīmāmikṣāmeke samāmananti
meaning: सदसि सन्मे भूया इति वा मैत्रावरुणीमामिक्षामेके समामनन्ति
text_mt: Some teach [lowering them into] the curd-mixture for Mitra and Varuṇa with: "May I have a being in the assembly!"

sanskrit_iast: agreṇāgnīdhraṃ caturapasrāvaṃ vimitaṃ viminvanti purastādunnataṃ paścānninatam
meaning: अग्रेणाग्नीध्रं चतुरपस्रावं विमितं विमिन्वन्ति पुरस्तादुन्नतं पश्चान्निनतम्
text_mt: In front of the Āgnīdhra they erect a four-eaved shed, raised in the east [and] sloping downward in the west.

sanskrit_iast: syonāsi suṣadeti tasminkhādirīmāsandīṃ pratiṣṭhāpya kṣatrasya nābhirasīti tasyāṃ kṛttyadhīvāsamāstīryāvanahani viśi mā dṛṃhetyavanahyati
meaning: स्योनासि सुषदेति तस्मिन्खादिरीमासन्दीं प्रतिष्ठाप्य क्षत्रस्य नाभिरसीति तस्यां कृत्त्यधीवासमास्तीर्यावनहनि विशि मा दृंहेत्यवनह्यति
text_mt: Having set up a throne of khadira wood in it with: "Soft art thou, good to sit upon," having spread an upper-cloth of skin upon it with: "Thou art the navel of the nobility," he ties it down with: "At the binding, strengthen me among the people."

sanskrit_iast: syonāmā sīda suṣadāmā sīdeti tāmāsādya yajamāno mā tvāhiṃsīnmā mā hiṃsīdityupaviśati
meaning: स्योनामा सीद सुषदामा सीदेति तामासाद्य यजमानो मा त्वाहिंसीन्मा मा हिंसीदित्युपविशति
text_mt: Having approached it with: "Sit on the soft one, sit on the one good to sit upon," the sacrificer sits down with: "May it not harm thee; may it not harm me."
He addresses him as he is seated with: "He has sat down, he whose ordinance is firm."
The priests and the courtiers sit around him on all sides:
When they are seated, the king addresses the adhvaryu: "O brahma3n!"
The other replies: "Thou, O king, art Brahman."
In the same way [he addresses] the brahman, the hotṛ, and the udgātṛ.
The others reply with each subsequent formula.

sanskrit_iast: indrasya vajro 'sīti sphyaṃ brahmā rājñe prayacchati /
meaning: इन्द्रस्य वज्रो ऽसीति स्फ्यं ब्रह्मा राज्ञे प्रयच्छति /
text_mt: With: "Thou art the thunderbolt of Indra," the brahman gives the wooden sword to the king;
The king to the deputy; the deputy to the royal chaplain;
They pass it on to each successive lower person,
With it the dice-thrower, having dug up the gaming ground [and] sprinkled it with water, should pour out the dice,
More than a hundred or more than a thousand made of gold.
Four [persons], a brāhmaṇa, a kṣatriya, a vaiśya, and a śūdra, being its team, playing for a four-year-old cow, state the rice-mess [as the stake].
Then the sacrificial gift for this rite is the two front draught-oxen.

sanskrit_iast: audbhidyaṃ rājña iti tebhyaścatuḥśatānsauvarṇānakṣānudupya vijitya diśo 'bhyayaṃ rājābhūditi pañcākṣānrājñe prayacchati
meaning: औद्भिद्यं राज्ञ इति तेभ्यश्चतुःशतान्सौवर्णानक्षानुदुप्य विजित्य दिशो ऽभ्ययं राजाभूदिति पञ्चाक्षान्राज्ञे प्रयच्छति
text_mt: Having scooped out four hundred golden dice from them with: "The king's victory!", [and] having won with: "This king has overcome the directions!", he hands five dice to the king.
The king calls those with auspicious names:
The charioteer as: "O Suśloka3!";
The collector as: "O Sumaṅgala3!";
The chamberlain as: "O Satyarājan3!"
Having summoned them, he gives a four-cornered field to the brahman.
They become the witnesses.
Or here he should offer the two oblations connecting the names.
He causes the story of Śunaḥśepa to be narrated,
More than a hundred or more than a thousand verses mixed with narrative stanzas.
Sitting on a golden cushion, the hotṛ recites.
Standing on two golden bundles of grass, the adhvaryu responds.
When the Śunaḥśepa [story] is concluded, he gives the golden cushion to the hotṛ,
The two golden bundles of grass to the adhvaryu,
And the two gold plates used at the consecration.
At this point, he proceeds with the [offering] for the Maruts and the one for the Viśve Devas.
However, the sviṣṭakṛt-offering and the iḍā are common.
When the iḍā has been invoked, he unties the beads and gives them to the Brahman.
He undertakes the rites beginning with the proceeding for the Mahendra [draught].
Having proceeded with the purificatory bath, he offers into the waters with: “To the child of the waters, svāhā!”

sanskrit_iast: ūrjo naptre svāhetyantarā darbhastambe sthāṇau valmīkavapāyāṃ vā hutvāgnaye gṛhapataye svāheti pratyetya gārhapatye hutvaindrīṃ sūtavaśāmanūbandhyāmālabhate
meaning: ऊर्जो नप्त्रे स्वाहेत्यन्तरा दर्भस्तम्बे स्थाणौ वल्मीकवपायां वा हुत्वाग्नये गृहपतये स्वाहेति प्रत्येत्य गार्हपत्ये हुत्वैन्द्रीं सूतवशामनूबन्ध्यामालभते
text_mt: Having offered in between into a clump of darbha, on a stump, or into a molehill with: “To the child of vigor, svāhā!”, and having returned and offered into the gārhapatya with: “To Agni, lord of the house, svāhā!”, he immolates an anūbandhyā cow, a barren cow that has calved, dedicated to Indra.

sanskrit_iast: tasyāḥ paśupuroḍāśaṃ naivāraṃ catuṣpadyāḥ sūnāyā nirvapati
meaning: तस्याः पशुपुरोडाशं नैवारं चतुष्पद्याः सूनाया निर्वपति
text_mt: For its animal-cake, he pours out [wild rice] of nīvāra grain from a four-legged plaited basket.
“It serves as a substitute for the cart,” so it is taught.

sanskrit_iast: śvobhūte 'pareṇa saumikaṃ devayajanaṃ daśabhiḥ saptabhirvā saṃsṛpāṃ havirbhiryajeta /
meaning: श्वोभूते ऽपरेण सौमिकं देवयजनं दशभिः सप्तभिर्वा संसृपां हविर्भिर्यजेत /
text_mt: On the next day, behind the soma-sacrificial place, he should sacrifice with the ten or seven oblations of the Saṃsṛps:
“[A cake] on eight potsherds for Agni…”
He shifts progressively forward to each succeeding sacrificial place.
Where the āhavanīya of the preceding [offering] was, there is the gārhapatya of the subsequent one.
For the last one, the āhavanīya is in the prāgvaṃśa hall;
Having sacrificed with that, in the afternoon he initiates the framework of the Daśapeya.

sanskrit_iast: apo dīkṣāyāḥ sthāne dvādaśapuṇḍarīkāṃ srajaṃ pratimuñcate
meaning: अपो दीक्षायाः स्थाने द्वादशपुण्डरीकां स्रजं प्रतिमुञ्चते
text_mt: In place of the waters of consecration, he puts on a garland of twelve lotus flowers.
He purchases the soma with ten uncastrated yearling calves.
He does not bargain; he does not carry [it] around.
There is one consecration day and three Upasads.
Before the Upasads, he sets out a caru for Soma;
between [them], [a cake] on eight potsherds for Tvaṣṭṛ;
after [them], [a cake] on three potsherds for Viṣṇu.
For these, the grass bunch and enclosing sticks are the very same as those of the Upasads.
The Śrāyantīya is the brahmasāman.
The Vāravantīya is the agniṣṭomasāman.
He draws water from the Sarasvatī.
On the next day, at the time of arranging the vessels, he sets out ten additional goblets.
He fills them at the time of drawing up [the soma].

sanskrit_iast: bhakṣaṇakāle daśadaśaikaikasmiṃścamase brāhmaṇāḥ somapāḥ somaṃ bhakṣayantyā daśamātpuruṣādavicchinnasomapīthāḥ
meaning: भक्षणकाले दशदशैकैकस्मिंश्चमसे ब्राह्मणाः सोमपाः सोमं भक्षयन्त्या दशमात्पुरुषादविच्छिन्नसोमपीथाः
text_mt:
At the time of partaking, ten soma-drinking Brahmins partake of the soma from each individual goblet, their lineage of soma-drinking unbroken down to the tenth generation.

He who can recount [his ancestors] down to the tenth generation is eligible to partake.

sanskrit_iast: ā daśamātpuruṣādanvākhyāyaṃ sa bhakṣasya kartā bhavati
meaning: आ दशमात्पुरुषादन्वाख्यायं स भक्षस्य कर्ता भवति

text_mt: A hundred soma-drinking Brahmins glide into the sadas.
At the time of the sacrificial gifts, he gives two gold mirrors to the adhvaryu,
a golden garland to the udgātṛ,
a gold plate to the hotṛ, as handed down in the sacred text.
He gives [a cow] that appears to be miscarrying to the unnetṛ,
[and] a one-horse cart loaded with barley to the acchāvāka.
Having offered the daśāmaveṣṭi, he concludes [the rite].
There are five [oblations]: “[A cake] on eight potsherds for Agni…”

sanskrit_iast: tayā brāhmaṇo rājanyo vaiśyo vā tejaskāmo yajeta
meaning: तया ब्राह्मणो राजन्यो वैश्यो वा तेजस्कामो यजेत
