text_mt: With it, a Brahmin, a nobleman, or a Vaiśya desiring spiritual luster should sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast: yadi brāhmaṇo yajeta bārhaspatyaṃ madhye kṛtvāhutimāhutiṃ hutvā tamabhighārayet /
meaning: यदि ब्राह्मणो यजेत बार्हस्पत्यं मध्ये कृत्वाहुतिमाहुतिं हुत्वा तमभिघारयेत् /
text_mt: If a Brahmin sacrifices, he should place [the oblation] for Bṛhaspati in the middle, and after making each oblation, he should baste it [with clarified butter];
if a Vaiśya, [the oblation] for the Viśve Devas.
In the afternoon, he should sacrifice with an animal sacrifice of two victims.
He immolates a pregnant cow with dewlaps on the neck dedicated to Aditi,
[and] a dappled four-year-old heifer dedicated to the Maruts.
For the one dedicated to Aditi, he calls for the prompt aloud;
he proceeds silently for the one dedicated to the Maruts.
The call and the response are [performed] silently.
On the next day, he sets out the three-oblation offering of the Satyadhūtas:
“A cake on twelve potsherds for the Aśvins and Pūṣan…”
A bow with three arrows and a dry waterskin are the sacrificial gift.
A staff and boar-skin sandals, say some.

sanskrit_iast: daṇḍo vā śuṣko vā dṛtirjaradupānahau vā
meaning: दण्डो वा शुष्को वा दृतिर्जरदुपानहौ वा
text_mt: Or a staff, or a dry waterskin, or old sandals.
Having made them bathe, he sends [messengers] to the neighboring kings.
He announces: “I have been consecrated; I have become king.”
In the afternoon, he sacrifices with the six Prayuj offerings,
[beginning with] “An eight-pot-sherd [cake] to Agni.”
The right-hand ox of the chariot-carrier is the sacrificial gift.
The next day, [he sacrifices] with the latter six.
The left-hand ox of the chariot-carrier is the sacrificial gift.
Having offered the agnihotra for a year, he sacrifices with the Keśavapanīya Atirātra.

sanskrit_iast: ye keśinaḥ prathamāḥ sattramāsateti vapanapravādā mantrāḥ
meaning: ये केशिनः प्रथमाः सत्त्रमासतेति वपनप्रवादा मन्त्राः
text_mt: “Those hairy ones who first sat at the sattra”—these are the mantras mentioning hair-shaving.
With those mentioning the beginning, he has [the hair] shaved from the beginning;
with those mentioning the end, at the end.
Immediately afterward, he sacrifices with the Vyuṣṭi two-day rite.
The Agniṣṭoma is the first day;
The first day is on the full-moon day;
Or the first day is on the new-moon day,

sanskrit_iast: āpūryamāṇapakṣasya vā ye puṇye ahanī syātām
meaning: आपूर्यमाणपक्षस्य वा ये पुण्ये अहनी स्याताम्
text_mt: Or on whichever two days of the waxing half of the month are auspicious.
They seize five of the eleven animals on the first day,
The Kṣatradhṛti is an Agniṣṭoma with the Triṣṭoma chant, having five terminations.
The Rājasūya is concluded.
Having sacrificed with it, he should sacrifice with the Sautrāmaṇī,
or with the curd mixture for Mitra and Varuṇa.
The days have separate concluding baths, except for the very first [day] of a two-day rite.

sanskrit_iast: tryahe purastātsīsena klībācchaṣpāṇi krītvā kṣaume vāsasyupanahya nidhāya sautrāmaṇyāstantraṃ prakramayati
meaning: त्र्यहे पुरस्तात्सीसेन क्लीबाच्छष्पाणि क्रीत्वा क्षौमे वासस्युपनह्य निधाय सौत्रामण्यास्तन्त्रं प्रक्रमयति
text_mt: Three days beforehand, having bought young barley sprout with lead from a eunuch, tied it in a linen garment, and set it down, he begins the procedure of the Sautrāmaṇī.
Its ritual is like that of the independent animal sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast: agnīnanvādhāya vedaṃ kṛtvāgnīnparistīrya pāṇiprakṣālanādi karma pratipadyate
meaning: अग्नीनन्वाधाय वेदं कृत्वाग्नीन्परिस्तीर्य पाणिप्रक्षालनादि कर्म प्रतिपद्यते
text_mt: Having added fuel to the fires, made the grass broom, and strewn grass around the fires, he proceeds with the work beginning with washing the hands.
He sets out the vessels as needed,
and a pot in place of the pot-sherds.

meaning: निर्वपणकाले ऽश्विभ्यां सरस्वत्या इन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे प्रभूतान्व्रीहीन्निर्वपति
text_mt: At the time of pouring out the offerings, he pours out abundant paddy for the Aśvins, for Sarasvatī, and for Indra the Good Protector.
The procedure for the caru has been explained.

sanskrit_iast: śrapayitvāgreṇa gārhapatyamavaṭaṃ khātvā tasminsurāyāḥ kalpena surāṃ saṃdadhāti
meaning: श्रपयित्वाग्रेण गार्हपत्यमवटं खात्वा तस्मिन्सुरायाः कल्पेन सुरां संदधाति
text_mt: Having cooked [it] and dug a pit in front of the gārhapatya, he brews liquor therein according to the ritual of liquor.

sanskrit_iast: svādvīṃ tvā svāduneti śaṣpaiḥ surāṃ saṃsṛjati
meaning: स्वाद्वीं त्वा स्वादुनेति शष्पैः सुरां संसृजति
text_mt: With [the mantra]: “Thee, the sweet one, with the sweet,” he mixes the liquor with young barley sprouts.
Mixed, it sits for three nights.
he accomplishes the requirements with the one made beforehand.
“He sacrifices in one third of the altar ground of a Soma sacrifice,” so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

sanskrit_iast: uttaravedyāṃ kriyamāṇāyāṃ pratiprasthātā cātvālātpurīṣamāhṛtya dakṣiṇenottaravediṃ kharaṃ kṛtvāgreṇānvāhāryapacanaṃ surāgrahārthaṃ dvitīyaṃ kharaṃ karoti
meaning: उत्तरवेद्यां क्रियमाणायां प्रतिप्रस्थाता चात्वालात्पुरीषमाहृत्य दक्षिणेनोत्तरवेदिं खरं कृत्वाग्रेणान्वाहार्यपचनं सुराग्रहार्थं द्वितीयं खरं करोति
text_mt: While the high altar is being prepared, the pratiprasthātṛ brings loose earth from the cātvāla pit, makes a mound south of the high altar, and makes a second mound in front of the anvāhāryapacana for the draughts of liquor.

sanskrit_iast: agnau praṇīyamāne pratiprasthātā dakṣiṇāgneragnimāhṛtya dakṣiṇenottaravediṃ khare nyupyopasamādadhāti
meaning: अग्नौ प्रणीयमाने प्रतिप्रस्थाता दक्षिणाग्नेरग्निमाहृत्य दक्षिणेनोत्तरवेदिं खरे न्युप्योपसमादधाति
text_mt: While the fire is being brought forward, the pratiprasthātṛ, having taken fire from the southern fire, pours it out on the mound south of the high altar and adds fuel to it.

sanskrit_iast: pātrasaṃsādanakāle 'śvibhyāṃ sarasvatyā indrāya sutrāmṇe trīni pātrāṇi prayunakti /
meaning: पात्रसंसादनकाले ऽश्विभ्यां सरस्वत्या इन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे त्रीनि पात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति /
text_mt: At the time of arranging the vessels, he sets out three vessels for the Aśvins, for Sarasvatī, and for Indra the Good Protector,
a basin, a hair strainer, a falcon-leaf [strainer], and cooking vessels.

sanskrit_iast: prāk paśūpākaraṇātkṛtvodbhidya surāṃ brāhmaṇasya mūrdhankhare vā sādayitvā punātu te parisrutamiti vālamayena pavitreṇa surāṃ pāvayati
meaning: प्राक् पशूपाकरणात्कृत्वोद्भिद्य सुरां ब्राह्मणस्य मूर्धन्खरे वा सादयित्वा पुनातु ते परिस्रुतमिति वालमयेन पवित्रेण सुरां पावयति
text_mt: Prior to bringing up the victim, having uncovered the liquor and placed it on the head of a Brahmin or on the mound, he purifies the liquor with a strainer of hair, with [the mantra]: “May it purify thy fermenting liquor.”
“Forward hath soma run beyond,” in the case of one who has vomited soma;
“Backward hath soma run beyond,” in the case of one purged by soma.
Having placed the purified [liquor] in its proper place, he brings up the animal victims at the single sacrificial post:

sanskrit_iast: āśvinaḥ dhūmramajaṃ sārasvataṃ meṣamaindramṛṣabhaṃ vṛṣṇiṃ vā bārhaspatyam
meaning: आश्विनः धूम्रमजं सारस्वतं मेषमैन्द्रमृषभं वृष्णिं वा बार्हस्पत्यम्
text_mt: a dusky he-goat for the Aśvins, a ram for Sarasvatī, and a bull for Indra, or a ram for Bṛhaspati,
as the fourth for one who has vomited soma or one purged by soma.

sanskrit_iast: hutāsu vapāsu niṣkamṛṣabhaṃ sātvarīṃ ca vaḍabāṃ dadāti
meaning: हुतासु वपासु निष्कमृषभं सात्वरीं च वडबां ददाति
text_mt: When the omenta have been offered, he gives a gold ornament, a bull, and a fast mare.
They explain [sātvarī as] one that has strayed and returned.
A mare with a foal is the sacrificial gift;
and gold and silver plates weighing a hundred mānas, say some.
Having cleansed themselves at the cātvāla pit, they draw the draughts of liquor on the western mound.

sanskrit_iast: kuvidaṅgeti sarveṣāmekā purorugekā puro'nuvākyaikaḥ praiṣa ekā yājyā
meaning: कुविदङ्गेति सर्वेषामेका पुरोरुगेका पुरोऽनुवाक्यैकः प्रैष एका याज्या
text_mt: With [the verse beginning] 'kuvid aṅga', there is one introductory verse, one invitatory verse, one ritual call, and one consecratory verse for all [the draughts].
With: 'You are taken with a base; I take you, who are uninjured, through an uninjured [strainer], dear to the Aśvins', the adhvaryu takes the draught for the Aśvins.

sanskrit_iast: etenaiva sarasvatyā iti sārasvataṃ pratiprasthātāgnīdhro vā /
meaning: एतेनैव सरस्वत्या इति सारस्वतं प्रतिप्रस्थाताग्नीध्रो वा /
text_mt: With the very same [formula, but saying] 'for Sarasvatī', the pratiprasthātṛ or the agnīdh [takes] the draught for Sarasvatī.
With: '...for Indra', the brahman or the sacrificer [takes] the draught for Indra.
He mixes the draught for the Aśvins with groats of kvala-jujube and with lion's hairs.
The draught for Sarasvatī with groats of badara-jujube and tiger's hairs.
The draught for Indra with groats of karkandhu-jujube and wolf's hairs.
In the absence of these, the adhvaryu should meditate mentally on two lions;
the pratiprasthātṛ on two tigers;

sanskrit_iast: sarvāñchyenapattreṇa parimṛjyaiṣa te yoniriti yathādevataṃ yathāyatanaṃ sādayati
meaning: सर्वाञ्छ्येनपत्त्रेण परिमृज्यैष ते योनिरिति यथादेवतं यथायतनं सादयति
text_mt: Having wiped all around them with an eagle's feather, he sets them down with: 'This is your seat...', according to each deity and according to each place.
Having taken the clarified butter portions for the animal sacrifice, they should take the draughts.
Then he apportions the sacrificial cakes:
having apportioned the animal-cake of the victim for Bṛhaspati, [he apportions] the eleven-pot-sherd cake for Indra, and so on.
Taking those three [draughts], they proceed with the draughts.
To those who take them, the adhvaryu issues the ritual call:

sanskrit_iast: aśvibhyāṃ sarasvatyā indrāya sutrāmṇe somānāṃ surāmṇāmanubrūhi /
meaning: अश्विभ्यां सरस्वत्या इन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे सोमानां सुराम्णामनुब्रूहि /
text_mt: 'Recite for the Aśvins, for Sarasvatī, and for Indra the Good Protector, for the somas and the surās!'

sanskrit_iast: aśvibhyāṃ sarasvatyā indrāya sutrāmṇe somānāṃ surāmṇāṃ preṣyeti saṃpraiṣau /
meaning: अश्विभ्यां सरस्वत्या इन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे सोमानां सुराम्णां प्रेष्येति संप्रैषौ /
text_mt: 'Urge for the Aśvins, for Sarasvatī, and for Indra the Good Protector, for the somas and the surās!'—these are the two ritual calls;
or: 'Urge for the somas and the surās that have been set forward!'
'You two, O Aśvins, [drank] surā together with the Asura Namuci;
drinking intensely, O lords of brilliance, you aided Indra in his deeds.'
'Like parents aiding a son, both Aśvins aided Indra by deed and wonders,

sanskrit_iast: yatsurāmaṃ vyapibaḥ śacībhiḥ sarasvatī tvā maghavannabhīṣṇāditi sarvadevatye yājyānuvākye bhavataḥ
meaning: यत्सुरामं व्यपिबः शचीभिः सरस्वती त्वा मघवन्नभीष्णादिति सर्वदेवत्ये याज्यानुवाक्ये भवतः
text_mt: when you, O bounteous one, drank surā by your powers and Sarasvatī healed you'—these are the invitatory and consecratory verses addressed to all deities.
He offers the secondary offering with: 'O Agni, enjoy the soma!'

sanskrit_iast: ahāvyagne havirāsye te srucīva ghṛtaṃ camū iva somaḥ /
meaning: अहाव्यग्ने हविरास्ये ते स्रुचीव घृतं चमू इव सोमः /
text_mt: 'The oblation, O Agni, has been poured into your mouth, as ghee into the ladle, as soma into the vats;

sanskrit_iast: vājasaniṃ rayimasme suvīraṃ praśataṃ dhehi yaśasaṃ bṛhantam //
meaning: वाजसनिं रयिमस्मे सुवीरं प्रशतं धेहि यशसं बृहन्तम् //
text_mt: confer upon us prize-winning wealth, rich in good heroes, renowned, great, and celebrated!'

sanskrit_iast: aysminnaśvāsa ṛṣabhāsa ukṣaṇo vaśā meṣā avasṛṣṭāsa āhutāḥ /
meaning: अय्स्मिन्नश्वास ऋषभास उक्षणो वशा मेषा अवसृष्टास आहुताः /
text_mt: 'In whom horses, bulls, oxen, barren cows, and sheep are released and offered;

sanskrit_iast: kīlālape somapṛṣṭhāya vedhase hṛdā matiṃ janaye cārumagnaya iti hutāṃ hūyamānāṃ vā yajamāno 'numantrayate
meaning: कीलालपे सोमपृष्ठाय वेधसे हृदा मतिं जनये चारुमग्नय इति हुतां हूयमानां वा यजमानो ऽनुमन्त्रयते
text_mt: for Agni, who drinks sweet drink, whose back is soma, the dispenser, I produce a pleasing thought from the heart'—with these [verses] the sacrificer follows [the oblation] with a mantra, either when offered or while being offered.
He should hire a Brahmin who will be the drinker of the residue.

sanskrit_iast: nānā hi vāṃ devahitaṃ sado mitaṃ mā saṃsṛkṣāthāṃ parame vyoman /
meaning: नाना हि वां देवहितं सदो मितं मा संसृक्षाथां परमे व्योमन् /
text_mt: 'For separately have your seats, arranged for the gods, been measured out; do not mingle in the highest heaven!

sanskrit_iast: surā tvamasi śuṣmiṇī soma eṣa mā mā hiṃsīḥ svāṃ yonimāviśan //
meaning: सुरा त्वमसि शुष्मिणी सोम एष मा मा हिंसीः स्वां योनिमाविशन् //
text_mt: You are spirited surā; this here is soma. Do not injure me as you enter your own seat!'

sanskrit_iast: yadatra śiṣṭaṃ rasinaḥ sutasya yadindro apibacchacībhiḥ /
meaning: यदत्र शिष्टं रसिनः सुतस्य यदिन्द्रो अपिबच्छचीभिः /
text_mt: 'What is left here of the savoury pressed juice, which Indra drank through his powers,

sanskrit_iast: ahaṃ tadasya manasā śivena somaṃ rājānamiha bhakṣayāmīti vā svayaṃ pibet
meaning: अहं तदस्य मनसा शिवेन सोमं राजानमिह भक्षयामीति वा स्वयं पिबेत्
text_mt: that King Soma belonging to him do I consume here with a benevolent mind'—with this [formula] he may himself drink it;

sanskrit_iast: dve srutī aśṛṇavaṃ pitṝṇāmahaṃ devānāmuta martyānām /
meaning: द्वे स्रुती अशृणवं पितॄणामहं देवानामुत मर्त्यानाम् /
text_mt: or with: 'Two paths have I heard of for the ancestors, for gods, and for mortals;

sanskrit_iast: tābhyāmidaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ sametyantarā pūrvamaparaṃ ca ketumiti vā valmīkavapāyāmavanayet
meaning: ताभ्यामिदं विश्वं भुवनं समेत्यन्तरा पूर्वमपरं च केतुमिति वा वल्मीकवपायामवनयेत्
text_mt: by these all this world meets together, between the eastern and the western beacon'—with this he may pour it down into the mound of an anthill.

meaning: दक्षिणे ऽग्नौ शतातृणां स्थालीं प्रबद्धां धारयति
text_mt: He holds a perforated pot suspended over the southern fire.

sanskrit_iast: tasyā bila udīcīnadaśaṃ pavitraṃ vitatya yanme manaḥ parāgatamiti tasmiñchatamānaṃ hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya somapratīkāḥ pitarastṛpṇuteti tasminsurāśeṣamānayati /
meaning: तस्या बिल उदीचीनदशं पवित्रं वितत्य यन्मे मनः परागतमिति तस्मिञ्छतमानं हिरण्यं निधाय सोमप्रतीकाः पितरस्तृप्णुतेति तस्मिन्सुराशेषमानयति /
text_mt:
Having spread over its opening a strainer with fringe turned northward, and placing on it a gold piece weighing one hundred measures with: 'That mind of mine which has departed...', he pours into it the residue of the surā with: 'O ancestors who present the appearance of soma, be satisfied!';

or with: 'O ancestors who present the appearance of soma, rejoice! May we attain the full life-span established by the gods!'

sanskrit_iast: somapratīkāḥ pitaro madantāṃ vyaśema devahitaṃ yadāyuḥ /
meaning: सोमप्रतीकाः पितरो मदन्तां व्यशेम देवहितं यदायुः /

sanskrit_iast: indrapīto vicakṣaṇo vyaśema devahitaṃ yadāyuriti vā
meaning: इन्द्रपीतो विचक्षणो व्यशेम देवहितं यदायुरिति वा
text_mt: or: 'Drunk by Indra, far-seeing, may we attain the full life-span established by the gods!'
As it flows down, they stand by it, each following in order, reciting three verses to Soma associated with the Fathers;

sanskrit_iast: tvaṃ soma pracikita ityetā āmnātā bhavanti
meaning: त्वं सोम प्रचिकित इत्येता आम्नाता भवन्ति
text_mt: these are handed down [in the canon] as: 'You, O Soma, knowledgeable...'

sanskrit_iast: yadagne kavyavāhaneti kāvyavāhanībhirdakṣiṇe 'gnau śatātṛṇāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati yadi brāhmaṇo yajate
meaning: यदग्ने कव्यवाहनेति काव्यवाहनीभिर्दक्षिणे ऽग्नौ शतातृणां प्रतिष्ठापयति यदि ब्राह्मणो यजते
text_mt: With the verses addressed to Agni Kavyavāhana, beginning 'yad agne kavyavāhana', he sets the perforated pot firmly down over the southern fire, if a Brahmin is sacrificing.

sanskrit_iast: atha yadi rājanyo vaiśyo vā nādriyeta dakṣiṇamagniṃ praṇayitum
meaning: अथ यदि राजन्यो वैश्यो वा नाद्रियेत दक्षिणमग्निं प्रणयितुम्
text_mt: Now, if he is a nobleman or a Vaiśya, he should not pay heed to bringing forward the southern fire;
he should sit consuming this residue of surā himself as his ritual food.

sanskrit_iast: bārhaspatyasya paśupuroḍāśena pracarya paśubhiḥ pracarya puroḍāśaiḥ pracarati
meaning: बार्हस्पत्यस्य पशुपुरोडाशेन प्रचर्य पशुभिः प्रचर्य पुरोडाशैः प्रचरति
text_mt: Having proceeded with the animal-cake of the victim for Bṛhaspati and with the animal victims, he proceeds with the sacrificial cakes.
The Sviṣṭakṛt offering and the iḍā, however, are common.
He begins the animal ritual procedure starting with: 'Agnīdh, bring the coals for the secondary offerings!'
They go down to the purificatory bath with the heart-spits, the fermentation dregs, and the vessels.
He disposes of the fermentation dregs in the manner of the pressed soma husks.
They refer to sediment as fermentation dregs.

sanskrit_iast: yaste deva varuṇa gāyatracchandāḥ pāśas taṃ ta etenāvayaje svāhety āśvinapātram avabhṛthe pravidhyati /
meaning: यस्ते देव वरुण गायत्रच्छन्दाः पाशस् तं त एतेनावयजे स्वाहेत्य् आश्विनपात्रम् अवभृथे प्रविध्यति /
text_mt: With: 'Whatever noose of yours, O god Varuṇa, has the gāyatrī metre, that [noose] of yours I cast off with this, svāhā!', he throws the vessel of the Aśvins into the purificatory bath;
with the very same [formula, but saying] '...has the triṣṭubh metre', [he throws the vessel] of Sarasvatī;
saying '...has the jagatī metre', [the vessel] of Indra;

sanskrit_iast: anuṣṭupchandā iti sataṃ vālasrāvaṃ śyenapattraṃ ca /
meaning: अनुष्टुप्छन्दा इति सतं वालस्रावं श्येनपत्त्रं च /
text_mt: saying '...has the anuṣṭubh metre', the broad vessel, the hair-strainer, and the eagle's feather;
saying '...has the paṅkti metre', the spits.
With it he should cause one who vomits soma, one through whom soma purges, an exiled king, one being exiled, one being consecrated, or one who has consecrated himself, to sacrifice.
Or one practicing sorcery, one desiring food, one desiring offspring, or one desiring cattle [should sacrifice].
It is taught in all consecrations.

sanskrit_iast: tayā brāhmaṇo rājanyo vaiśyo vā tejaskāmo yajeta
meaning: तया ब्राह्मणो राजन्यो वैश्यो वा तेजस्कामो यजेत
text_mt: With it a brāhmaṇa, a rājanya, or a vaiśya desiring splendour should sacrifice.
Now then we shall explain the Kaukikī [Sautrāmaṇī].
Its procedure is as before.
At the time of measuring out [the offerings], he seizes an animal for Indra.

sanskrit_iast: purastādeva kālāyasena kālānuśātanena kālena tasareṇa pakṣmaṇā vrīhiyavaśyāmākānkrītvā kṣaume vāsasyupanaddhānvrīhīṃstokmāni kurvanti /
meaning: पुरस्तादेव कालायसेन कालानुशातनेन कालेन तसरेण पक्ष्मणा व्रीहियवश्यामाकान्क्रीत्वा क्षौमे वासस्युपनद्धान्व्रीहींस्तोक्मानि कुर्वन्ति /
text_mt: Well beforehand, having bought rice, barley, and millet with dark iron, with a dark cutting implement, with a black shuttle, and with a lash, and having tied the rice in a linen cloth, they make sprouts.

sanskrit_iast: cūrṇāni tāni dadhnodaśvitā vā saṃsṛjya darbhaiḥ paritaṃsya nidadhāti
meaning: चूर्णानि तानि दध्नोदश्विता वा संसृज्य दर्भैः परितंस्य निदधाति
text_mt: Having mixed their meal with curd or buttermilk, and having wrapped it around with darbha grass, he places it.
Coarse meal of the very same [grains], sprinkled with scum—that is nagnahu.

sanskrit_iast: śyāmākānsaktūnkṛtvā surāyāḥ saṃdhānakāle tokmairmāsareṇa nagnahunā ca surāṃ saṃsṛjya saktūnāṃ tṛtīyena parikīrya parīto ṣiñcatā sutamityekasyā gordugdhena pariṣicyāpareṇa tṛtīyena parikīryaitayaiva dvayordugdhenāpareṇa tṛtīyena parikīryaitayaiva tisṛṇāṃ dugdhena tisro rātrīḥ saṃsṛṣṭā vasati
meaning: श्यामाकान्सक्तून्कृत्वा सुरायाः संधानकाले तोक्मैर्मासरेण नग्नहुना च सुरां संसृज्य सक्तूनां तृतीयेन परिकीर्य परीतो षिञ्चता सुतमित्येकस्या गोर्दुग्धेन परिषिच्यापरेण तृतीयेन परिकीर्यैतयैव द्वयोर्दुग्धेनापरेण तृतीयेन परिकीर्यैतयैव तिसृणां दुग्धेन तिस्रो रात्रीः संसृष्टा वसति
text_mt: Having made groats of the millet, at the time of fermenting the surā, having mixed the surā with the sprouts, with the māsara, and with the nagnahu, having scattered around a third of the groats, having poured [around] with the milk of one cow with "Poured around, pour the pressed [soma]...", having scattered around another third and [poured] with this very [formula] with the milk of two [cows], having scattered around another third and [poured] with this very [formula] with the milk of three [cows], mixed together, it rests for three nights.
Some teach a kārotara in place of a pit.
It is made of split cane, bound with leather.
Into it he sets a spout-mouthed vessel of split cane.
Its opening is covered with leather.
What flows out into it, that becomes parisrut.

sanskrit_iast: pātrasaṃsādanakāle 'śvibhyāṃ sarasvatyā indrāya sutrāmṇe trīṇi pātrāṇi prayunakti
meaning: पात्रसंसादनकाले ऽश्विभ्यां सरस्वत्या इन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे त्रीणि पात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति
text_mt: At the time of placing the vessels, he sets out three vessels: for the Aśvins, for Sarasvatī, and for Indra the Good Protector.
Three [kinds of] groats—of barley, wheat, and upavāka—in a falcon-leaf, in a hair strainer, or in a wooden trough.
The filter of the adhvaryu is made of goat and sheep hair.
[The filter] of the pratiprasthātṛ is made of cow and horse [hair].
Having poured out ghee, the adhvaryu pours out abundant milk into a wooden trough.
With a mantra, says Āśmarathya.
Having purified the ghee, he purifies the milk with the hair strainer.
With "Eastward the soma has run beyond..." for one who vomits soma.
With "Westward the soma has run beyond..." for one through whom soma purges.

sanskrit_iast: brahma kṣatraṃ pavata iti surāṃ pratiprasthātā
meaning: ब्रह्म क्षत्रं पवत इति सुरां प्रतिप्रस्थाता
text_mt: The pratiprasthātṛ [purifies] the surā with "The sacred lore and the ruling power are purified..."
Having taken the clarified butter for the animals, the adhvaryu draws the milk draughts.

sanskrit_iast: kuvidaṅgeti sarveṣāmekā purorugekā puro'nuvākyaikaḥ praiṣa ekā yājyā
meaning: कुविदङ्गेति सर्वेषामेका पुरोरुगेका पुरोऽनुवाक्यैकः प्रैष एका याज्या
text_mt: With "Truly indeed..." there is for all [three] one preliminary verse, one invitatory verse, one ritual call, and one consecratory verse.

sanskrit_iast: upayāmagṛhīto 'syaśvibhyāṃ tvā juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmīti gṛhītvā yavasaktubhiḥ śrītvā pavitreṇa parimṛjyaiṣa te yonistejase tveti sādayitvopayāmagṛhīto 'si sarasvatyai tvā juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmīti gṛhītvā godhūmasaktubhiḥ śrītvā pavitreṇa parimṛjyaiṣa te yonirvīryāya tveti sādayitvopayāmagṛhīto 'sīndrāya tvā sutrāmṇe juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmīti gṛhītvopavākāsaktubhiḥ śrītvā pavitreṇa parimṛjyaiṣa te yonirbalāya tveti sādayitvottarairyathāliṅgamupatiṣṭhate
meaning: उपयामगृहीतो ऽस्यश्विभ्यां त्वा जुष्टं गृह्णामीति गृहीत्वा यवसक्तुभिः श्रीत्वा पवित्रेण परिमृज्यैष ते योनिस्तेजसे त्वेति सादयित्वोपयामगृहीतो ऽसि सरस्वत्यै त्वा जुष्टं गृह्णामीति गृहीत्वा गोधूमसक्तुभिः श्रीत्वा पवित्रेण परिमृज्यैष ते योनिर्वीर्याय त्वेति सादयित्वोपयामगृहीतो ऽसीन्द्राय त्वा सुत्राम्णे जुष्टं गृह्णामीति गृहीत्वोपवाकासक्तुभिः श्रीत्वा पवित्रेण परिमृज्यैष ते योनिर्बलाय त्वेति सादयित्वोत्तरैर्यथालिङ्गमुपतिष्ठते
text_mt: Having drawn with "You are taken with a receptacle; I take you pleasing to the Aśvins," having mixed it with barley groats, having wiped it around with the filter, and having set it down with "This is your cradle; for splendour you!", having drawn with "You are taken with a receptacle; I take you pleasing to Sarasvatī," having mixed it with wheat groats, having wiped it around with the filter, and having set it down with "This is your cradle; for virility you!", having drawn with "You are taken with a receptacle; I take you pleasing to Indra the Good Protector," having mixed it with upavāka groats, having wiped it around with the filter, and having set it down with "This is your cradle; for strength you!", he attends [them] with the subsequent [verses] according to their characteristic marks.

sanskrit_iast: surāyāṃ vāla ānīyamānāyāṃ dhārāyāḥ pratiprasthātā surāgrahāngṛhṇāti
meaning: सुरायां वाल आनीयमानायां धारायाः प्रतिप्रस्थाता सुराग्रहान्गृह्णाति
text_mt: While the surā is being brought through the hair strainer in a stream, the pratiprasthātṛ draws the surā draughts.

sanskrit_iast: nānā hi vāṃ devahitaṃ sadaḥ kṛtamiti sarveṣāmekā purorugekā puro'nuvākyaikaḥ praiṣa ekā yājyā
meaning: नाना हि वां देवहितं सदः कृतमिति सर्वेषामेका पुरोरुगेका पुरोऽनुवाक्यैकः प्रैष एका याज्या
text_mt: With "Distinct indeed for the two of you has the seat pleasing to the gods been made..." there is for all [three] one preliminary verse, one invitatory verse, one ritual call, and one consecratory verse.

sanskrit_iast: upayāmagṛhīto 'syāśvinaṃ tejo 'śvibhyāṃ tvā juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmīti gṛhītvā pavitreṇa parimṛjyaiṣa te yonirmodāya tveti sādayati
meaning: उपयामगृहीतो ऽस्याश्विनं तेजो ऽश्विभ्यां त्वा जुष्टं गृह्णामीति गृहीत्वा पवित्रेण परिमृज्यैष ते योनिर्मोदाय त्वेति सादयति
text_mt: Having drawn with "You are taken with a receptacle; splendour of the Aśvins, I take you pleasing to the Aśvins," and having wiped it around with the filter, he sets it down with "This is your cradle; for joy you!"

sanskrit_iast: upapayāmagṛhīto 'si sārasvataṃ vīryaṃ sarasvatyai tvā juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmīti gṛhītvā pavitreṇa parimṛjyaiṣa te yonirānandāya tveti sādayati
meaning: उपपयामगृहीतो ऽसि सारस्वतं वीर्यं सरस्वत्यै त्वा जुष्टं गृह्णामीति गृहीत्वा पवित्रेण परिमृज्यैष ते योनिरानन्दाय त्वेति सादयति
text_mt: Having drawn with "You are taken with a receptacle; virility of Sarasvatī, I take you pleasing to Sarasvatī," and having wiped it around with the filter, he sets it down with "This is your cradle; for delight you!"

sanskrit_iast: upayāmagṛhīto 'syaindraṃ balamindrāya tvā sutrāmṇe juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmīti gṛhītvā pavitreṇa parimṛjyaiṣa te yonirmahase tveti sādayati
meaning: उपयामगृहीतो ऽस्यैन्द्रं बलमिन्द्राय त्वा सुत्राम्णे जुष्टं गृह्णामीति गृहीत्वा पवित्रेण परिमृज्यैष ते योनिर्महसे त्वेति सादयति
text_mt: Having drawn with "You are taken with a receptacle; strength of Indra, I take you pleasing to Indra the Good Protector," and having wiped it around with the filter, he sets it down with "This is your cradle; for greatness you!"
With the remainder of the section, the adhvaryu and the sacrificer attend upon the [draughts] that have been set down.
He assigns the animal victims as before.
Excepting that for Bṛhaspati, it is identical up to the carrying of fire around [the victims].
In the middle round of the carrying of fire around, having poured out a portion of the firebrand on the mound, he adds fuel.
Having carried fire around with the remainder, he brings this very [firebrand] forward for the cooking of the animal victims.
When the omenta have been offered, he gives forty cows as the sacrificial gift.
Or they may draw the draughts here.
"All should be offered in the āhavanīya," says Āśmarathya.
"The surā draughts [should be offered] in the southern fire," says Ālekhana.
He offers the milk draughts with "Possessing surā..."
The surā draughts with "Whatever sap of yours has been collected..."
Having offered when the secondary vaṣaṭ-call has been made silently, the adhvaryu partakes of the draught for the Aśvins with "Whom the two Aśvins from Namuci..."
With "What here is defiled..." the pratiprasthātṛ and the agnīdh [partake of] that for Sarasvatī.
With "This oblation..." the brahman and the sacrificer [partake of] that for Indra.
The disposal of the surā has been explained.

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇenāhavanīyaṃ payaḥśeṣaṃ pitṛpitāmahaprapitāmahebhyo dadāti pitṛbhyaḥ svadhāvibhyaḥ svadhā nama iti
meaning: दक्षिणेनाहवनीयं पयःशेषं पितृपितामहप्रपितामहेभ्यो ददाति पितृभ्यः स्वधाविभ्यः स्वधा नम इति
text_mt: To the south of the āhavanīya, he gives the remainder of the milk to the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather with: 'To the fathers who possess the svadhā, svadhā, homage!'
He pays reverence with: 'May the soma-loving fathers purify me!'
The adhvaryu with: 'Those who are equal...';
The pratiprasthātṛ with: 'Those who are of the same kin...'

sanskrit_iast: manotākāle pṛthak pātreṣu paśūnāṃ yūṣāṇi nidadhāti
meaning: मनोताकाले पृथक् पात्रेषु पशूनां यूषाणि निदधाति
text_mt: At the time of the Manotā hymn, he places the broths of the victims in separate vessels.
Before the sviṣṭakṛt, he offers the subsidiary oblations with the horns and hooves.
For each [victim] there are eight dewclaws and hooves.

sanskrit_iast: āśvinasya yūṣeṇa kuṣṭhikāṃ śaphaṃ ca pūrayitvā sīsena tantramityaṣṭarcena pratimantraṃ dvābhyāṃdvābhyāṃ kuṣṭhikāśaphābhyāṃ juhoti
meaning: आश्विनस्य यूषेण कुष्ठिकां शफं च पूरयित्वा सीसेन तन्त्रमित्यष्टर्चेन प्रतिमन्त्रं द्वाभ्यांद्वाभ्यां कुष्ठिकाशफाभ्यां जुहोति
text_mt: Having filled a dewclaw and a hoof with the broth of the [victim] belonging to the Aśvins, he offers with an eight-verse hymn, 'With lead the web...', verse by verse, with two dewclaws and hooves each time.
At the last [verse], he fastens the two horns.
Each time after offering, having poured down the residues into the respective anointing vessels, he casts the dewclaws and hooves into the āhavanīya.
In the same manner, [he offers] of the Sarasvatī victim with the subsequent eight verses.
With the whole anuvāka, [he offers] of the Indra victim.
There is a chair of udumbara wood, its headpiece and crossbars measuring a cubit, its legs reaching up to the navel, woven with muñja grass.

meaning: मित्रो ऽसि वरुणो ऽसीति तां यजमानायातने प्रतिष्ठापयति
text_mt: He sets it down in the place of the sacrificer with: 'You are Mitra, you are Varuṇa.'
The setting down, sitting upon, and addressing [of the chair] are as in the Rājasūya.

sanskrit_iast: tasyāṃ prāṅmukhamāsīnaṃ pratyaṅmukhastiṣṭhannāśvinasaṃpātairabhiṣiñcati devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinorbāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāmaśvinorbhaiṣajyena tejase brahmavarcasāyābhiṣiñcāmīti
meaning: तस्यां प्राङ्मुखमासीनं प्रत्यङ्मुखस्तिष्ठन्नाश्विनसंपातैरभिषिञ्चति देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऽश्विनोर्बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्यामश्विनोर्भैषज्येन तेजसे ब्रह्मवर्चसायाभिषिञ्चामीति
text_mt: Standing facing west, he anoints him seated on it facing east with the residues of the Aśvin offering, saying: 'At the impulse of the divine Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, with the healing medicine of the Aśvins, I anoint you for brilliance, for spiritual luster.'
In the same manner, [he anoints him with the residue] of the Sarasvatī offering with the next formula.

meaning: को ऽसि कतमो ऽसीति पाणी संमृश्याध्वर्युर्व्याहृतीर्जुहोति
text_mt: Having touched both hands with: 'Who are you? Which one are you?', the adhvaryu offers the vyāhṛtis.

sanskrit_iast: atra rājasūyavanmaṅgalyanāmna āhūya śiro me śrīriti yathāliṅgamaṅgāni saṃmṛśya jaṅghābhyāṃ padbhyāmiti pratyavaruhya prati kṣatre pratitiṣṭhāmi rāṣṭra iti japitvā trayā devā ityāhutīrhutvā lomāni prayatirmameti yathāliṅgamaṅgāni saṃmṛśate
meaning: अत्र राजसूयवन्मङ्गल्यनाम्न आहूय शिरो मे श्रीरिति यथालिङ्गमङ्गानि संमृश्य जङ्घाभ्यां पद्भ्यामिति प्रत्यवरुह्य प्रति क्षत्रे प्रतितिष्ठामि राष्ट्र इति जपित्वा त्रया देवा इत्याहुतीर्हुत्वा लोमानि प्रयतिर्ममेति यथालिङ्गमङ्गानि संमृशते
text_mt: Here, having called out auspicious names as in the Rājasūya, having touched the limbs in accordance with the markers with: 'My head is prosperity...', having descended with: 'With two shanks, with two feet...', having whispered: 'I establish myself in royal power, in dominion', having offered the oblations with: 'Three gods...', he touches the limbs in accordance with the markers with: 'My body hairs are exertion...'
From the sviṣṭakṛt onward, it is identical [with the animal sacrifice] up to the purificatory bath.
Āśmarathya says: 'He offers five oblations at the purificatory bath with: "Whatever offense against the gods, O gods..."'
Ālekhana says: 'They should be offered in the āhavanīya.'

sanskrit_iast: avabhṛtha nicaṅkaṇetyavabhṛthaṃ yajamāno 'bhimantrya sumitrā na āpo drupadādivenmumucāna ityāplutyodvayaṃ tamasasparītyādityamupasthāya pratiyuto varuṇasya pāśa ityudakāntaṃ pratyasyati
meaning: अवभृथ निचङ्कणेत्यवभृथं यजमानो ऽभिमन्त्र्य सुमित्रा न आपो द्रुपदादिवेन्मुमुचान इत्याप्लुत्योद्वयं तमसस्परीत्यादित्यमुपस्थाय प्रतियुतो वरुणस्य पाश इत्युदकान्तं प्रत्यस्यति
text_mt: Having addressed the purificatory bath with: 'O purificatory bath, gliding down...', having bathed with: 'May the waters be friendly to us...', 'As if released from a wooden post...', and having reverenced the sun with: 'Arising from the darkness...', the sacrificer throws [a stick] towards the edge of the water with: 'Repelled is Varuṇa's noose.'
[Putting on] firewood and reverencing are as in the animal sacrifice.
Having paid reverence with: 'The returner...', having offered an oblation with: 'Bhūḥ svāhā', the sacrifice to the ancestors is performed as before.
He seizes an animal victim for Indra Vayodhas.
'He gives the calf at the former [sacrifice];
One who desires heaven should sacrifice with it.
One who desires heaven should pile the Sāvitra [altar].

sanskrit_iast: ceṣyamāṇa upakalpayate pañcāśītiśataṃ hiraṇyeṣṭakā yāvaduttamamaṅguliparu tāvatīḥ śarkarā vābhyaktāścatasraḥ svayamātṛṇā aparimitā lokaṃpṛṇāḥ
meaning: चेष्यमाण उपकल्पयते पञ्चाशीतिशतं हिरण्येष्टका यावदुत्तममङ्गुलिपरु तावतीः शर्करा वाभ्यक्ताश्चतस्रः स्वयमातृणा अपरिमिता लोकंपृणाः
text_mt: One about to pile procures one hundred and eighty-five golden bricks, or as many pebbles anointing them as measure up to the last finger-joint, four naturally perforated bricks, and an unlimited number of space-filling bricks.
He commences the ritual of the animal sacrifice beginning with the six Hotṛs formula.
It is declared: 'He sacrifices on a third of the altar ground.'

sanskrit_iast: prāguttarātparigrāhātkṛtvottaravedideśasya madhye śaṅkuṃ nihatya sarvataḥ parimaṇḍalaṃ rathacakramātraṃ sāvitraṃ parilikhyā samūlaṃ haritaṃ darbhastambamāhṛtya madhye 'gnernikhāya juhvāṃ pañcagṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā sajūrabdo 'yāvabhiriti darbhastambe pañcāhutīrhutvoddhatyāvokṣya vyāghāraṇāntāmuttaravediṃ kṛtvā likhāyā abhyantaraṃ nava parimaṇḍalā lekhā likhitvā sikatābhiravakīrya darbhaiḥ pracchādya dadhnā madhumiśreṇa śarkarābhiriti bāhyāṃ lekhāṃ saṃpūrya vasati
meaning: प्रागुत्तरात्परिग्राहात्कृत्वोत्तरवेदिदेशस्य मध्ये शङ्कुं निहत्य सर्वतः परिमण्डलं रथचक्रमात्रं सावित्रं परिलिख्या समूलं हरितं दर्भस्तम्बमाहृत्य मध्ये ऽग्नेर्निखाय जुह्वां पञ्चगृहीतं गृहीत्वा सजूरब्दो ऽयावभिरिति दर्भस्तम्बे पञ्चाहुतीर्हुत्वोद्धत्यावोक्ष्य व्याघारणान्तामुत्तरवेदिं कृत्वा लिखाया अभ्यन्तरं नव परिमण्डला लेखा लिखित्वा सिकताभिरवकीर्य दर्भैः प्रच्छाद्य दध्ना मधुमिश्रेण शर्कराभिरिति बाह्यां लेखां संपूर्य वसति
text_mt: Before the upper enclosing boundary, having driven in a peg in the middle of the high altar's area, having marked all around the Sāvitra [ground] circular, the size of a chariot-wheel, having fetched a green clump of darbha grass with its roots, having planted it in the middle of the fire[-site], having drawn five ladlings into the offering ladle, having offered five oblations onto the darbha clump with: 'In union, the year with its months...', having excavated [the site], having sprinkled it with water, having completed the high altar up to the pourings of clarified butter, having drawn nine circular furrows inside the marked area, having scattered them with sand, having covered them with darbha grass, having filled the outer furrow with curd mixed with honey and pebbles, he remains overnight.

sanskrit_iast: hute prātaragnihotre prajāpatistvā sādayatu tayā devatayāṅgirasvaddhruvā sīdetyuttaravedimabhimṛśya mayi gṛhṇāmyagre agniṃ yo no agniḥ pitara iti dvābhyāmātmannagniṃ gṛhītvā yāste agne samidha iti svayaṃdityābhimṛśyāgnerbhasmāsīti sikatā nivapati /
meaning: हुते प्रातरग्निहोत्रे प्रजापतिस्त्वा सादयतु तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद्ध्रुवा सीदेत्युत्तरवेदिमभिमृश्य मयि गृह्णाम्यग्रे अग्निं यो नो अग्निः पितर इति द्वाभ्यामात्मन्नग्निं गृहीत्वा यास्ते अग्ने समिध इति स्वयंदित्याभिमृश्याग्नेर्भस्मासीति सिकता निवपति /
text_mt: When the morning agnihotra has been offered, having touched the high altar with: 'May Prajāpati seat you; with that deity, in the manner of the Aṅgirases, sit firm', having taken the fire into himself with the two verses: 'I take Agni into myself at first...', 'The fire of ours which, O fathers...', having touched the self-perforated [brick] with: 'Agni, the firewood that is yours...', he scatters the sand with: 'You are Agni's ashes.'
While scattering them, he mentally meditates: 'Whatever black spot is there in the moon, may that be here.'

sanskrit_iast: saṃ yā vaḥ priyāstanuva ityūṣānsikatāśca saṃsṛjya cita stha paricita ityaparimitābhiḥ śarkarābhiḥ pariśrityā pyāyasva sametu ta iti sikatā vyūhati
meaning: सं या वः प्रियास्तनुव इत्यूषान्सिकताश्च संसृज्य चित स्थ परिचित इत्यपरिमिताभिः शर्कराभिः परिश्रित्या प्यायस्व समेतु त इति सिकता व्यूहति
text_mt: Having mixed the saline earth and the sand with: 'Those dear bodies of yours that unite...', having enclosed [the altar] with an unlimited number of pebbles with: 'You are piled, you are enclosed', he spreads out the sand with: 'Swell up, may it gather together for you...'
They do not obscure the furrows.

sanskrit_iast: abhyantaraṃ jaghanārdha udapātramupadadhāti vāktvā samudra upadadhe suprajāvaniṃ rāyaspoṣavaniṃ mahyaṃ vājināyeti
meaning: अभ्यन्तरं जघनार्ध उदपात्रमुपदधाति वाक्त्वा समुद्र उपदधे सुप्रजावनिं रायस्पोषवनिं मह्यं वाजिनायेति
text_mt: Inside, in the western half, he places a water pot with: 'I place speech, you the ocean, bestowing good offspring, bestowing increase of wealth, for me, the energetic.'

sanskrit_iast: navamyāṃ bāhyāyāṃ lekhāyāṃ pañcadaśa pūrvapakṣasyāhānyupadadhāti saṃjñānaṃ vijñānamiti
meaning: नवम्यां बाह्यायां लेखायां पञ्चदश पूर्वपक्षस्याहान्युपदधाति संज्ञानं विज्ञानमिति
text_mt: In the ninth, outer furrow, he places the fifteen days of the waxing fortnight with: 'Agreement, understanding...'
In the intervals between those days, he places fifteen [hours] with: 'Bright, banner...'

sanskrit_iast: athāntarasyāṃ pañcadaśa pūrvapakṣasya rātrīrupadadhāti darśā dṛṣṭeti
meaning: अथान्तरस्यां पञ्चदश पूर्वपक्षस्य रात्रीरुपदधाति दर्शा दृष्टेति
text_mt: Then in the inner [furrow], he places the fifteen nights of the waxing fortnight with: 'The new moon, the visible...'

sanskrit_iast: tāsāmantarāleṣvetāsāṃ rātrīṇāṃ pañcadaśa muhūrtānupadadhāti dātā pradāteti
meaning: तासामन्तरालेष्वेतासां रात्रीणां पञ्चदश मुहूर्तानुपदधाति दाता प्रदातेति
text_mt: In the intervals between those nights, he places the fifteen muhūrtas with: 'Giver, bestower...'
Then in the inner [furrow], he places the fifteen days of the waning fortnight with: 'Puffed, chanted...'
In the intervals between those days, he places the fifteen muhūrtas with: 'Savitṛ, the impeller...'
Then in the inner [furrow], he places the fifteen nights of the waning fortnight with: 'Pressed, pressing...'
In the intervals between those nights, he places the fifteen muhūrtas with: 'Accuser, approver...'
Then in the inner [furrow], he places the twelve waxing fortnights with: 'The strainer, about to purify...'
Then in the inner [ring] he lays down the twelve dark fortnights with: 'Sahasvān sahīyān…' [TB 3.10.1.2].
Then in the inner [ring] he lays down the thirteen month-names with: 'Aruṇo 'ruṇarajas…' [TB 3.10.1.3].
Then he lays down sand with: 'Ejatkā jovatkā…' [TB 3.10.1.4].
Then in the inner [ring] he lays down the fifteen muhūrtas with: 'Idānīṃ tadānīm…' [TB 3.10.1.4].
Then in the inner [ring] he lays down the six sacrificial rites [and] three four-names with: 'Agniṣṭoma ukthyo agnirṛtuḥ…' [TB 3.10.1.4].

sanskrit_iast: atha nābhyāṃ catvāri saṃvatsaranāmānyupadadhāti prajāpatiḥ saṃvatsaro mahānka iti
meaning: अथ नाभ्यां चत्वारि संवत्सरनामान्युपदधाति प्रजापतिः संवत्सरो महान्क इति
text_mt: Then on the navel he lays down the four year-names with: 'Prajāpatiḥ saṃvatsaro mahānkaḥ…' [TB 3.10.1.4].

sanskrit_iast: catasraḥ svayamātṛṇā dikṣūpadadhāti bhūragniṃ ca pṛthivīṃ ca māṃ ceti
meaning: चतस्रः स्वयमातृणा दिक्षूपदधाति भूरग्निं च पृथिवीं च मां चेति
text_mt: He lays down four naturally perforated [bricks] in the quarters with: 'Bhūr agniṃ ca pṛthivīṃ ca māṃ ca…' [TB 3.10.2.1].
He lays down the space-filling [bricks] with: 'Fill the space…' [TB 3.10.2.1].
Having brought loose earth from the pit, he spreads it out over the piling with the verse addressed to Vaiśvānara: 'Pṛṣṭo divi…' [TB 3.10.2.2].

sanskrit_iast: upasthānenopatiṣṭhate tvameva tvāṃ vettha yo 'si so 'sīti
meaning: उपस्थानेनोपतिष्ठते त्वमेव त्वां वेत्थ यो ऽसि सो ऽसीति
text_mt: He reveres [the fire] with the attendance verse: 'Thou alone knowest thyself, who thou art, that art thou' [TB 3.10.2.3].

sanskrit_iast: dhenūḥ kṛtvā yajamānaḥ saṃhāravihārābhyāmupatiṣṭhate saṃvatsaro 'si parivatsaro 'sīti
meaning: धेनूः कृत्वा यजमानः संहारविहाराभ्यामुपतिष्ठते संवत्सरो ऽसि परिवत्सरो ऽसीति
text_mt: Having made cows, the sacrificer attends [the fire] with contraction and expansion, [reciting]: 'Thou art the Saṃvatsara, thou art the Parivatsara…' [TB 3.10.4.1].
To the north, on the highest brick, he offers goat's milk with an arka-leaf.

sanskrit_iast: tvamagne rudra iti śatarudrīyasya rūpamasaṃcare paśūnāmarkaparṇa udasyati valmīkavapāyāṃ vāvadadhāti
meaning: त्वमग्ने रुद्र इति शतरुद्रीयस्य रूपमसंचरे पशूनामर्कपर्ण उदस्यति वल्मीकवपायां वावदधाति
text_mt: With 'Thou, O Agni, art Rudra…' [TB 3.10.5.1], which has the form of the Śatarudrīya; he throws away the arka-leaf where cattle do not roam, or places it in the mound of an anthill.

sanskrit_iast: jaghanenāgniṃ prāṅmukha upaviśya saṃcitokthyena hotānuśaṃsati bhūrbhuvaḥ svarityanuvākena
meaning: जघनेनाग्निं प्राङ्मुख उपविश्य संचितोक्थ्येन होतानुशंसति भूर्भुवः स्वरित्यनुवाकेन
text_mt: Seated facing east behind the fire, the hotṛ recites the accompaniment with the Saṃcitokthya, [namely] with the anuvāka: 'Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ…' [TB 3.10.5.1].
He undertakes the animal sacrifice rites beginning with the leading forward of the fire, identical [with the archetype] up to the Atimukti offerings.
Having offered the Atimukti libations, he offers a fourfold-drawn portion [of clarified butter]:
'Thou, O Agni, art Rudra…' [TB 3.10.6.1], which is the form of the Śatarudrīya.
'Agnāviṣṇū…' [TB 3.10.6.1] for the Vasordhārā.
'Annapate…' [TB 3.10.6.1] is the food-offering.

sanskrit_iast: sapta te agne samidhaḥ sapta jihvā iti viśvaprīḥ
meaning: सप्त ते अग्ने समिधः सप्त जिह्वा इति विश्वप्रीः
text_mt: 'Seven are thy kindling-sticks, O Agni, seven thy tongues…' [TB 3.10.6.1] is the Viśvaprī offering.

sanskrit_iast: aparaṃ caturgṛhītaṃ vasūnāṃ tvādhītena rudrāṇāmūrmyādityānāṃ tejasā viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ dratunā marutāmemnā juhomi svāheti
meaning: अपरं चतुर्गृहीतं वसूनां त्वाधीतेन रुद्राणामूर्म्यादित्यानां तेजसा विश्वेषां देवानां द्रतुना मरुतामेम्ना जुहोमि स्वाहेति
text_mt: Another fourfold-drawn portion [he offers] with: 'With the design of the Vasus, with the surge of the Rudras, with the brilliance of the Ādityas, with the resolve of the Viśvedevas, with the host of the Maruts, I offer, svāhā!' [TB 3.10.6.1].

sanskrit_iast: tāsāṃ saṃsrāveṇa yajamāno mukhaṃ vimṛṣṭe rājñī virājñītyanuvākena
meaning: तासां संस्रावेण यजमानो मुखं विमृष्टे राज्ञी विराज्ञीत्यनुवाकेन
text_mt: With the residue of those [libations] the sacrificer wipes his face, with the anuvāka: 'Rājñī virājñī…' [TB 3.10.7.1].
Then he offers twenty-one oblations with the anuvāka: 'To Asu svāhā, to Vasu svāhā…' [TB 3.10.8.1], mantra by mantra.

sanskrit_iast: barhiṣaḥ saṃbharaṇādi pāśukaṃ karma pratipadyate samānamā vapāyā homāt
meaning: बर्हिषः संभरणादि पाशुकं कर्म प्रतिपद्यते समानमा वपाया होमात्
text_mt: He undertakes the animal sacrifice rites beginning with the gathering of the sacrificial grass, identical [with the archetype] up to the offering of the omentum.
When the omentum has been offered, he gives four-year-old heifers as sacrificial gifts corresponding to the bricks.
If he cannot afford so many sacrificial gifts, he should give that many brāhmaṇas groats-drinks to drink,

sanskrit_iast: teno haivāsya sa kāma upāpto bhavati
meaning: तेनो हैवास्य स काम उपाप्तो भवति
text_mt: By that indeed that wish of his becomes attained.
He should, however, give one pregnant four-year-old heifer, gold, and a garment.

sanskrit_iast: yatprāṅ manotāyāstatkṛtvaudumbarapātreṇa yuṣṇo mṛtyave grahaṃ gṛhṇāti
meaning: यत्प्राङ् मनोतायास्तत्कृत्वौदुम्बरपात्रेण युष्णो मृत्यवे ग्रहं गृह्णाति
text_mt: Having performed what comes before the Manotā hymn, he draws a draught of broth for Mṛtyu with an udumbara cup.
With 'To the wise, to the purifying…' [TB 3.10.8.2] are the drawing and depositing [mantras].
According to another view, the draught to Mṛtyu should belong only to the Nāciketa [fire].
Its offering is after the Sviṣṭakṛt.
About to offer, he touches water with: 'Thou art lightning; sever my sin!' [TB 3.10.8.3].
Then he offers with: 'Away death, away hunger…' [TB 3.10.8.4].
Then having offered, he touches [water] with: 'Thou art rain; cut away my sin!' [TB 3.10.8.5].
He partakes with: 'Thou art the portion, the immortal portion…' [TB 3.10.8.6].
Having partaken, he establishes the breath-calls in himself with the remainder of the anuvāka: 'Mandrābhibhūtiḥ…' [TB 3.10.8.7].
From here onwards the animal sacrifice rites are identical [with the archetype].
By this the Nāciketa is explained.

sanskrit_iast: ekaviṃśatirhiraṇyeṣṭakāḥ śarkarā vābhyaktā upadhānakāle nābhyāmevopadhīyante caturaśraṃ parimaṇḍalaṃ vā loko 'si svargo 'sītyanuvākena pratimantram
meaning: एकविंशतिर्हिरण्येष्टकाः शर्करा वाभ्यक्ता उपधानकाले नाभ्यामेवोपधीयन्ते चतुरश्रं परिमण्डलं वा लोको ऽसि स्वर्गो ऽसीत्यनुवाकेन प्रतिमन्त्रम्
text_mt: Twenty-one gold bricks or greased pebbles are laid down only on the navel at the time of laying down, square or circular, with the anuvāka: 'Thou art the world, thou art heaven…' [TB 3.11.1.1], mantra by mantra.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ haitameke paśubandha evottaravedyāṃ cinvata iti brāhmaṇavyākhyātā vikārāḥ
meaning: तं हैतमेके पशुबन्ध एवोत्तरवेद्यां चिन्वत इति ब्राह्मणव्याख्याता विकाराः
text_mt: Some pile this very [Nāciketa fire] on the uttaravedī only in an animal sacrifice; thus are the modifications explained in the Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: paśubandhe some sattre sahasre sarvavedase vā yatra vā bhūyiṣṭhā āhutayo hūyeraṃstatra cetavyaḥ
meaning: पशुबन्धे सोमे सत्त्रे सहस्रे सर्ववेदसे वा यत्र वा भूयिष्ठा आहुतयो हूयेरंस्तत्र चेतव्यः
text_mt: In an animal sacrifice, in a Soma sacrifice, in a sacrificial session, in a thousand-cow sacrifice, or in an all-property sacrifice, or wherever the most oblations are offered, there it should be piled.
Desiring a firm foundation in a sacrificial session, desiring glory, offspring, cattle, heaven, [or] prosperity, according to opportunity [and] according to the traditional text.
Everywhere the beginning is in the east, the completion is in the north in a clockwise direction.
One who desires cattle should pile [the bricks] only in a fivefold manner:
five in each direction, one in the middle.
One desiring pre-eminence, glory, or offspring [should pile them] in a threefold manner:

sanskrit_iast: sapta purastāttisro dakṣiṇataḥ sapta paścāttisra uttarata ekāṃ madhye
meaning: सप्त पुरस्तात्तिस्रो दक्षिणतः सप्त पश्चात्तिस्र उत्तरत एकां मध्ये
text_mt: seven in the east, three in the south, seven in the west, three in the north, one in the middle.
One who desires pre-eminence should proceed starting from the middle along an upward row.
One who desires heaven should proceed starting from the west along an eastward row.

sanskrit_iast: sa yadīcchettejasvī yaśasvī brahmavarcasī syāmiti prāgdakṣiṇebhyaḥ prāṅā hoturdhiṣṇyādutsarpedyeyaṃ prāgādyaśasvatī sā mā prorṇotu tejasā yaśasā brahmavarcaseneti
meaning: स यदीच्छेत्तेजस्वी यशस्वी ब्रह्मवर्चसी स्यामिति प्राग्दक्षिणेभ्यः प्राङा होतुर्धिष्ण्यादुत्सर्पेद्येयं प्रागाद्यशस्वती सा मा प्रोर्णोतु तेजसा यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेनेति
text_mt: If he should desire: 'May I be brilliant, renowned, endowed with spiritual luster', he should glide forward to the east from the southern ones, up to the dhiṣṇya hearth of the hotṛ, with: 'May this renowned one that has gone east cover me with brilliance, with renown, with spiritual luster.'

sanskrit_iast: atha yadīcchedbhūyiṣṭhaṃ me śraddadhīranbhūyiṣṭhā dakṣiṇā nayeyuriti dakṣiṇāsu nīyamānāsu prācyehi prācyehīti
meaning: अथ यदीच्छेद्भूयिष्ठं मे श्रद्दधीरन्भूयिष्ठा दक्षिणा नयेयुरिति दक्षिणासु नीयमानासु प्राच्येहि प्राच्येहीति
text_mt: Now, if he should wish: “May they place the utmost faith in me; may they lead away the most abundant sacrificial gifts,” while the sacrificial gifts are being led away, with the words: “Come facing east, come facing east;”

sanskrit_iast: prācī juṣāṇā vetvājyasya svāheti sruveṇopahatyāhavanīye juhuyāt
meaning: प्राची जुषाणा वेत्वाज्यस्य स्वाहेति स्रुवेणोपहत्याहवनीये जुहुयात्
text_mt: having scooped [ghee] with the sruva, he should offer into the āhavanīya with the formula: “Facing east, enjoying, let her partake of the ghee, svāhā!”
The subsequent [procedure], beginning with the self-perforated [brick], is the same.
The Nāciketa [fire-altar] is concluded.
By this, the Cāturhotra [fire-altar] is explained.
As many gold bricks or smeared pebbles as there are pādas [are used].
At the time of piling, he piles [the bricks of] the Daśahotṛ northwards in front of the tuft of darbha grass, mantra by mantra.

sanskrit_iast: hṛdayaṃ grahaṃ catvāri padāni saṃbhārāṇāṃ dve patnīnām
meaning: हृदयं ग्रहं चत्वारि पदानि संभाराणां द्वे पत्नीनाम्
text_mt: The heart, the cup, four pādas of the materials, [and] two of the wives.
Similarly, [he piles the bricks of] the Caturhotṛ eastwards to the south.
[He piles the bricks of] the Pañcahotṛ northwards to the west.
[He piles the bricks of] the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ eastwards to the north.
[He piles the bricks of] the Saptahotṛ eastwards above.
Here [there are] five pādas of the materials and the remaining ones of the wives.
The subsequent [procedure], beginning with the self-perforated [brick], is the same.
The Cāturhotra [fire-altar] is concluded.
By this, the Vaiśvasṛja [fire-altar] is explained.
As many gold bricks or smeared pebbles as there are mantras [are used].
At the time of piling, he piles the fire in a clockwise direction in front of the northern navel with these three anuvākas: “What is immortal and what is mortal...”
Or [there are] three layers by means of the three anuvākas.
The subsequent [procedure], beginning with the self-perforated [brick], is the same, except for the subsequent recitation.
He recites subsequently with this anuvāka: “The eastern great quarter of the verses is declared...”

sanskrit_iast: rātrisattreṣu śatarātrānteṣu samahāvrateṣu triṣu ca sārasvateṣu sattreṣu kāṭhakacāturmāsyeṣu sādhyānāṃ ṣaḍahavarjiteṣu viśvasṛjāmayane prajāpateḥ sahasrasaṃvatsarayośca vaiśvasṛjo 'gnirniyataḥ
meaning: रात्रिसत्त्रेषु शतरात्रान्तेषु समहाव्रतेषु त्रिषु च सारस्वतेषु सत्त्रेषु काठकचातुर्मास्येषु साध्यानां षडहवर्जितेषु विश्वसृजामयने प्रजापतेः सहस्रसंवत्सरयोश्च वैश्वसृजो ऽग्निर्नियतः
text_mt: The Vaiśvasṛja fire is prescribed in night sessions, in those ending in a hundred nights, in those accompanied by the Mahāvrata, in the three Sārasvata sessions, in the Cāturmāsyas of the Kaṭhas, in [sessions] of the Sādhyas excluding the six-day period, in the course of the Viśvasṛjs, and in the two thousand-year [sessions] of Prajāpati.
If they should pile it upon marching forward, he should touch the site of the high altar with these mantras.

sanskrit_iast: yo 'sya supriyaḥ suvicita iva syāttasmai vaiśvasṛjam /
meaning: यो ऽस्य सुप्रियः सुविचित इव स्यात्तस्मै वैश्वसृजम् /
text_mt: For one who is very dear to him and thoroughly examined, as it were, he should pile the Vaiśvasṛja [fire-altar].
Combining the Sāvitra, Nāciketa, Cāturhotra, Vaiśvasṛja, and Āruṇaketuka [altars], one may pile [the fire-altar] even in a Soma sacrifice.
The Sāvitra is the first layer;
He draws a draught for Death from the broth of the animal victim belonging to the pressing day.

sanskrit_iast: ya etānagnīnpṛthak samāsena vā cinvāna ubhayīrdakṣiṇā dadāti kratudakṣiṇā yathāsamāmnātamagnidakṣināśceti
meaning: य एतानग्नीन्पृथक् समासेन वा चिन्वान उभयीर्दक्षिणा ददाति क्रतुदक्षिणा यथासमाम्नातमग्निदक्षिनाश्चेति
text_mt: One who piles these fires separately or combined gives both kinds of sacrificial gifts: the sacrificial gifts for the sacrifice as handed down by tradition, and the sacrificial gifts for the fire-altar.
Here, without having employed them separately, they are not combined.
Having piled the fire-altar, one should sacrifice with the Sautrāmaṇī;
or with the curd mess dedicated to Mitrā-Varuṇā.
The Āruṇaketuka is explained by the Brāhmaṇa.
Desiring heaven, one should sacrifice day after day with the Divaḥśyenī [bricks];
They are explained by the Brāhmaṇa.
One should sacrifice with the optional animal sacrifices on the new-moon day or on the full-moon day.
The ritual procedure for them is like that of the independent animal sacrifice.
They are explained by the Brāhmaṇa beginning: “A white [animal] dedicated to Vāyu...”
In their variable places, he inserts six verses according to the deity:
two each for the omentum, the sacrificial cake, [and] the oblation [of meat].

sanskrit_iast: pīvo 'nnāṃ rayivṛdhaḥ sumedhā ityetāni yathāpūrvaṃ yathāliṅgamāmnātāni bhavanti
meaning: पीवो ऽन्नां रयिवृधः सुमेधा इत्येतानि यथापूर्वं यथालिङ्गमाम्नातानि भवन्ति
text_mt: These verses: “Pīvo'nnām...”, “Rayivṛdhaḥ...”, “Sumedhāḥ...” are handed down according to previous order and according to characteristic marks.

sanskrit_iast: sarveṣvābhicaraṇikeṣu lohitoṣṇīṣā lohitavasanā nivītā ṛtvijaḥ pracaranti malhā iti
meaning: सर्वेष्वाभिचरणिकेषु लोहितोष्णीषा लोहितवसना निवीता ऋत्विजः प्रचरन्ति मल्हा इति
text_mt: In all sorcery rites, the priests perform their duties wearing red turbans, red garments, with sacred threads suspended [around the neck], and malhāḥ.

sanskrit_iast: viṣama ālabheteti viṣamaṃ devayajanaṃ syātpaśuṃ vā viṣama ālabheta
meaning: विषम आलभेतेति विषमं देवयजनं स्यात्पशुं वा विषम आलभेत
text_mt: As for “he should immolate on an uneven [ground]”: the sacrificial site should be uneven, or he should immolate the animal on uneven [ground].
There is a discussion regarding the deity of the ten-bull [sacrifice]:

sanskrit_iast: ādityā syātprājāpatyā vaikādaśinadevatā vā yaddevatā vā garbhiṇayaḥ
meaning: आदित्या स्यात्प्राजापत्या वैकादशिनदेवता वा यद्देवता वा गर्भिणयः
text_mt: She should be dedicated to Aditi, or dedicated to Prajāpati, or having the deities of the Ekādaśinī, or belonging to the deity to whom pregnant [victims] belong.
“Paryāriṇī” means she is one that gives birth successively.

sanskrit_iast: sphyo yūpa iti sphyākṛtiyūpa agnyāgāriko vā
meaning: स्फ्यो यूप इति स्फ्याकृतियूप अग्न्यागारिको वा
text_mt: As for “the sacrificial post is a sphya”: it is a sacrificial post shaped like a wooden sword, or one belonging to the fire house.
As for “a mare dedicated to Tvaṣṭṛ”: one which mounts [another] while being male.

sanskrit_iast: apāṃ cauṣahīnāṃ ca saṃdhāviti prāvṛṣi śaratpratipattau vā /
meaning: अपां चौषहीनां च संधाविति प्रावृषि शरत्प्रतिपत्तौ वा /
text_mt: As for “at the junction of waters and plants”: in the rainy season or at the onset of autumn;
or at the junction of waters and plants.
As for “a forked sacrificial post”: that which is above the girdle is forked;
or both branches above the peg should be eight-cornered and equipped with top-rings.

sanskrit_iast: prāśṛṅgo 'vāśṛṅga ukṣā vaśā vehaddhenurvatsa ṛṣabho 'naḍvānpunarutsṛṣṭo gomṛga iti gavyāḥ
meaning: प्राशृङ्गो ऽवाशृङ्ग उक्षा वशा वेहद्धेनुर्वत्स ऋषभो ऽनड्वान्पुनरुत्सृष्टो गोमृग इति गव्याः
text_mt: One with forward-pointing horns, one with downward-pointing horns, an ox, a barren cow, a miscarrying cow, a milk cow, a calf, a bull, a draft-ox, a bull set free again, and a gomṛga: these are bovine [victims].
He seizes a miscarrying cow for Food.
The subsidiary offerings are [performed with the verses] 'The cows have come…'.
There he should offer along with it [the verse beginning with] 'Bhartāram…'.
For Sun and Moon, twins, one white and one black, at a single sacrificial post.
There he should offer along with it [the verse beginning with] 'Salilam…'.
For those animals which come after the animal for the Aśvins, the procedure is according to the order of the hymn.
When the bull among the cattle has grown old, he should whisper into the ear of a young [bull with these two verses]: 'Of reddish-brown form…' and 'That fourth of ours…'.
Then he sends him forth among the cows with [the verse]: 'This young one…'.
Then he seizes the old one for Prajāpati, for Indra, or for Tvaṣṭṛ.
At the dedication he follows up with [the verse]: 'Homage to greatness…'.
With the fifth, the [oblation] to Sviṣṭakṛt.
Having apportioned a cake on eight potsherds for Agni, he seizes a barren she-goat.
'One desiring prosperity should seize [a barren she-goat] sacred to Vāyu'—thus the deities have been stated.
He dedicates [her] with the verse to Vāyu: 'Come, O Vāyu, adorn [our sacrifice], drinker of the pure…'.

sanskrit_iast: ākūtyai tvā kāmāya tveti paryagnau kriyamāṇe juhoti
meaning: आकूत्यै त्वा कामाय त्वेति पर्यग्नौ क्रियमाणे जुहोति
text_mt: While carrying fire around [her], he offers with: 'To intention thee, to desire thee…'.
He addresses [the victim] being led northwards with: 'Thou art the fourth, the ruling barren cow…'.
As she is being struck down, with: 'Thou art a she-goat, abiding in wealth…'.
With 'Extending the web…' he offers the omentum.
With 'Weave an uninterrupted web…' [he offers] the oblation.
With 'Thou art the oblation of the mind…' they eat the remnants of the oblation.
'Indeed, that one [secures the wish] of only three'—thus it is declared [in the Brāhmaṇa].

sanskrit_iast: tasyai vā etasyā ekamevādevayajanaṃ yadālabdhāyāmabhro bhavati
meaning: तस्यै वा एतस्या एकमेवादेवयजनं यदालब्धायामभ्रो भवति
text_mt:
Indeed, for this one there is only one unfitness for sacrifice: namely, when a cloud appears after she has been seized.

If a cloud should appear after she has been seized, he should either make [her] enter into the waters, or the sacrificer alone should eat the entire [victim] day after day.

sanskrit_iast: yadālabdhāyāmabhraḥ syādapsu vā praveśayetsarvāṃ vā yajamāna evānvahaṃ prāśnīyāt
meaning: यदालब्धायामभ्रः स्यादप्सु वा प्रवेशयेत्सर्वां वा यजमान एवान्वहं प्राश्नीयात्

text_mt: The Jayas, the Abhyātānas, and the Rāṣṭrabhṛts have been explained in the Brāhmaṇa.
In the Abhyātānas, he adds [the words] 'In this holy power…'.

sanskrit_iast: yena karmaṇertsettatra hotavyā ṛdhnotyeva tena karmaṇeti vijñāyate
meaning: येन कर्मणेर्त्सेत्तत्र होतव्या ऋध्नोत्येव तेन कर्मणेति विज्ञायते
text_mt: 'For whichever rite he desires success, therein they should be offered; he indeed prospers through that rite'—so it is known.
One should sacrifice with the optional sacrifices on the new moon day or on the full moon day.
They have been explained in the Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: samidhyamānavatīṃ samiddhavatīṃ cāntareṇa pṛthupājavatyau dhāyye dadhāti /
meaning: समिध्यमानवतीं समिद्धवतीं चान्तरेण पृथुपाजवत्यौ धाय्ये दधाति /
text_mt: Between the verse containing [the word] 'being kindled' and the one containing 'kindled', he inserts two supplementary kindling verses containing [the word] 'pṛthupājas'.
Or the two portions of clarified butter are matching as prescribed.
They should contain mention of whatever the desire of the sacrifice is, because they are for that purpose, [and] because they bear its characteristic mark;
Where there is no specific instruction, the standard form is to be understood.
'Thee, O Agni, mortals with oblations praise as god;

sanskrit_iast: manye tvā jātavedasaṃ sa havyā vakṣyānuṣagityete āmnāte bhavataḥ
meaning: मन्ये त्वा जातवेदसं स हव्या वक्ष्यानुषगित्येते आम्नाते भवतः
text_mt: I think of thee as Jātavedas; do thou carry the oblations in succession'—these two are handed down.

sanskrit_iast: ubhā vāmindrāgnī āhuvadhyā ityetāsāṃ yathāpūrvamāmnātā yājyānuvākyā liṅgairniyamyante
meaning: उभा वामिन्द्राग्नी आहुवध्या इत्येतासां यथापूर्वमाम्नाता याज्यानुवाक्या लिङ्गैर्नियम्यन्ते
text_mt: [For the optional sacrifices beginning with] 'Both of you, Indra and Agni, we call upon…', the invitatory and consecratory verses handed down in their order are determined by their characteristic marks:
That which has the deity mentioned in the first half-verse, having its mark in front, is the invitatory verse;
that which has its mark later is the consecratory verse.
The remaining ones are for the purpose of option.
Or the subsidiary offerings there are doubtful.

sanskrit_iast: agnaye rakṣoghne puroḍāśamaṣṭākapālamamāvāsyāyāṃ niśāyāṃ nirvapettasyāḥ sādguṇyasāmarthyāt
meaning: अग्नये रक्षोघ्ने पुरोडाशमष्टाकपालममावास्यायां निशायां निर्वपेत्तस्याः साद्गुण्यसामर्थ्यात्
text_mt: He should apportion a cake on eight potsherds for Agni, slayer of demons, at night on the new moon day, because of its suitability for that excellence.
There should be a removal of the time of the new moon.

sanskrit_iast: kṛṇuṣva pāja iti rakṣoghnīḥ parācīḥ sāmidhenīranvāha
meaning: कृणुष्व पाज इति रक्षोघ्नीः पराचीः सामिधेनीरन्वाह
text_mt: With 'Put forth thy strength…' he recites straight through the kindling verses which slay demons.
The invitatory and consecratory verses are [the two verses beginning with] 'With light…'.
One about to set out for battle should apportion boiled rice for the Ādityas.
Having gone to the battlefield, he should apportion a cake on twelve potsherds for Agni Vaiśvānara.

sanskrit_iast: yayā rajjvottamāṃ gāmājettayā bhrātṛvyagavīmabhidadhyādgoṣṭhe vāsya nyasyet
meaning: यया रज्ज्वोत्तमां गामाजेत्तया भ्रातृव्यगवीमभिदध्याद्गोष्ठे वास्य न्यस्येत्
text_mt: With the rope with which he drives the last cow, he should bind the rival's cow, or cast it into his cow-pen.
He should bind balbaja-grass into the firewood.
He should sprinkle it together with the firewood.
With the formula 'O Sarasvatī, having ghee as your share,' the oblation consists of ghee.
'Ghee is the sprinkling; with ghee they wipe'—thus all sprinklings and cleansings are done with ghee.
He should make two verses belonging to Manu the insertion verses.
Two from among these beginning with 'Quickly for one possessing gods…'
He should offer this very [sacrifice] having reached the proper ground.
Having gone to the field of the rival, he should perform this offering.

sanskrit_iast: tatra dakṣiṇamardhaṃ vedyā uddhatya tadevārdhena barhiṣa stṛṇīyāt /
meaning: तत्र दक्षिणमर्धं वेद्या उद्धत्य तदेवार्धेन बर्हिष स्तृणीयात् /
text_mt: Having raised up the southern half of the altar ground there, he should strew only that with half of the sacrificial grass.
He should place half of the firewood on [the fire].
One desirous of a village should offer an eleven-pot-sherd [cake] to Indra and a seven-pot-sherd [cake] to the Maruts.
He places the one for Indra over the āhavanīya fire.
At the proper time, he sets down the one for Indra.
While the kindling verses are being recited, [he sets down] the one for the Maruts.
Now, where 'Recite for Indra' is the invitatory verse relating to Indra,
'Worship the Maruts' is the consecratory verse relating to the Maruts.
'Recite for the Maruts' is the invitatory verse relating to the Maruts.
'Worship Indra' is the consecratory verse relating to Indra.
One desirous of a village should offer an eleven-pot-sherd [cake] to Indra and a twelve-pot-sherd [cake] to the All-Gods.
Having cut the first portion of that for Indra there, he should cut both portions of that for the All-Gods.
Then, the remaining portion of that for Indra is taken on top.

meaning: इन्द्राय विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यो ऽनुब्रूहीन्द्रं विश्वान्देवान्यजेति संप्रेष्यति
text_mt: He gives the ritual call: 'Recite for Indra [and] for the All-Gods; worship Indra [and] the All-Gods.'
[The two verses] beginning with 'Indra in the battles…' serve as the invitatory and consecratory verses.
A garment with an ornamented upper border is the sacrificial gift.

sanskrit_iast: saṃjñānīṃ pṛthaṅnirupya sarvataḥ samavadāya sarvā devatā anudrutya saṃpreṣyati
meaning: संज्ञानीं पृथङ्निरुप्य सर्वतः समवदाय सर्वा देवता अनुद्रुत्य संप्रेष्यति
text_mt: Having poured out the concord offering separately, having cut portions from all sides, and having recited the names of all the deities in succession, he issues the ritual call.

sanskrit_iast: agniḥ prathamo vasubhiriti sarvadevatye yājyānumākye bhavataḥ
meaning: अग्निः प्रथमो वसुभिरिति सर्वदेवत्ये याज्यानुमाक्ये भवतः
text_mt: [The two verses] beginning with 'Agni first with the Vasus…' serve as the invitatory and consecratory verses addressed to all the deities.

sanskrit_iast: aparuddho 'prarudhyamāno vā dhārayadvatīyaṃ nirupyāsīta yāvadenaṃ nāparundhyuḥ
meaning: अपरुद्धो ऽप्ररुध्यमानो वा धारयद्वतीयं निरुप्यासीत यावदेनं नापरुन्ध्युः
text_mt: One who has been expelled or is being expelled should, having poured out the [oblation] accompanied by the dhārayadvat verses, remain seated as long as they do not banish him.
Then, while being expelled, he should take the footprint of the expeller with the formula 'O Aditi, agree!' and depart.
He should bring rice grains from the house of whoever might be a speaker on behalf of the village beyond.
He should separate the white and the black [grains].
Those that are white, he should offer as that boiled rice oblation for the Ādityas.

sanskrit_iast: ye kṛṣṇāstānkṛṣṇājina upanahya nidhāya haviṣkṛtā vācaṃ visṛjyopa preta marutaḥ sudānava iti yajamānamabhyaiti
meaning: ये कृष्णास्तान्कृष्णाजिन उपनह्य निधाय हविष्कृता वाचं विसृज्योप प्रेत मरुतः सुदानव इति यजमानमभ्यैति
text_mt: Those that are black, having tied them up in a black antelope skin and set them down, releasing speech with the call to the preparer of the oblation, he approaches the sacrificer with the formula: 'Come forward, O Maruts of generous gifts!'
With the formula 'True is the blessing…', he scatters a portion of the [dust of the] footprint into the upper garment of the sacrificer.
With the formula 'Here is the mind…', he pours down the remainder on his chest.
The offering is completed according to the established rule.

sanskrit_iast: yadi nāvagacchedimamahamādityebhyo bhāgaṃ nirvapāmyāmuṣmādamuṣyai viśo 'vagantorityaparoddhurnāma gṛhṇīyāttasyai ca viśaḥ
meaning: यदि नावगच्छेदिममहमादित्येभ्यो भागं निर्वपाम्यामुष्मादमुष्यै विशो ऽवगन्तोरित्यपरोद्धुर्नाम गृह्णीयात्तस्यै च विशः
text_mt: If he does not return, he should utter the name of the expeller and of that settlement, saying: 'This share I offer to the Ādityas, so that so-and-so may return from such-and-such a settlement.'

If he does not return, he should drive seven pegs of Aśvattha wood into the middle pole of the chariot, saying: 'Here I bind the Ādityas, so that so-and-so may return from such-and-such a settlement'—
three pointing eastward and four pointing northward.
If he does not return, he should offer this very boiled rice oblation to the Ādityas.
He should also bind the pegs into the firewood.
He should place them on [the fire] together with the firewood.

sanskrit_iast: avagataḥ kṛṣṇānāṃ vrīhīṇāṃ vāruṇaṃ caruṃ nirvapati
meaning: अवगतः कृष्णानां व्रीहीणां वारुणं चरुं निर्वपति
text_mt: Having returned, he offers a boiled rice oblation of black rice to Varuṇa.
The offering is completed according to the established rule.
One desirous of life should offer a hundred-kṛṣṇala oblation to Prajāpati.

sanskrit_iast: śataṃ hiraṇyakṛṣṇalāni kākiṇyā māṣeṇa vā saṃmitāni
meaning: शतं हिरण्यकृष्णलानि काकिण्या माषेण वा संमितानि
text_mt: There are one hundred gold kṛṣṇala berries, measured by the weight of a kākiṇī or a māṣa.
He pours them into the clarified butter over the strainers.
The boiling is purely symbolic.
At the time of offering, he cuts off eight for the deity.
Two for the prāśitra portion; eight for the iḍā.

sanskrit_iast: caturdhākaraṇakāle sarvāṇi prāśitre samopyaikadhā brahmaṇa upaharati
meaning: चतुर्धाकरणकाले सर्वाणि प्राशित्रे समोप्यैकधा ब्रह्मण उपहरति
text_mt: At the time of dividing into four parts, having thrown all of them together into the prāśitra vessel, he presents them at once to the brahman priest.
The brahman priest consumes them.
For the others, the consumption is omitted.
He sets down the boiled rice oblation for Sūrya, clasping it between two gold plates.
At each fore-offering of it, he sacrifices a kṛṣṇala berry.
Having removed the two gold plates, he proceeds with the boiled rice oblation.
These very two gold plates are the sacrificial gift.
[With the words], "To Agni the giver, an eight-potsherd sacrificial cake," [there are] three [oblations].
Among them, the third belongs to Prajāpati, consisting of mixed sacrificial substance.
Curd, honey, clarified butter, water, roasted grains, and unhusked rice: according to some, [this is] a modification of clarified butter.
Honey and water being mixed, when primary, have their own ritual rules.

sanskrit_iast: ghṛtaṃ na pūtamubhe suścandreti yājyānuvākye bhavataḥ
meaning: घृतं न पूतमुभे सुश्चन्द्रेति याज्यानुवाक्ये भवतः
text_mt: "Like clarified butter, purified…" and "Both of great radiance…" are the invitatory and consecratory verses.

sanskrit_iast: āgneyasya ca saumyasya caindre samāśleṣayediti saṃhitāni havīṃṣyadhiśrayedityarthaḥ
meaning: आग्नेयस्य च सौम्यस्य चैन्द्रे समाश्लेषयेदिति संहितानि हवींष्यधिश्रयेदित्यर्थः
text_mt: [With the rule,] "One should join the [substance] of Agni and that of Soma onto that of Indra," the meaning is that one should place the sacrificial substances [on the fire] adjoining one another.
Or, one should join the two scrapings onto it.
[With the formula,] "May I destroy the people among the brahmins," everything belongs to Bṛhaspati (Brahmaṇaspati).
One should make the invitatory and consecratory verses addressed to the Maruts.
Then he places this three-layered [cake] on eleven upturned potsherds.

sanskrit_iast: prathamaṃ puroḍāśamadhiśritya paritapanāntaṃ kṛtvā tasminnuttaraṃ jyāyāṃsamadhiśritya tadantameva kṛtvā tasminnuttaraṃ jyāyāṃsamadhiśrayati
meaning: प्रथमं पुरोडाशमधिश्रित्य परितपनान्तं कृत्वा तस्मिन्नुत्तरं ज्यायांसमधिश्रित्य तदन्तमेव कृत्वा तस्मिन्नुत्तरं ज्यायांसमधिश्रयति
text_mt: Having placed the first sacrificial cake [on the potsherds] and carried [the procedure] up to scorching, he places a larger one on top of it, carries [the procedure] up to that very [scorching], and then places a [yet] larger one on top of it.
At the time of performance, he should sacrifice from the southern half to the first deity,
It has been said: "Bringing them all together, he cuts [portions]."

sanskrit_iast: prācyāṃ diśi tvamindreti tisra ṛco vyatyāsamanvāha
meaning: प्राच्यां दिशि त्वमिन्द्रेति तिस्र ऋचो व्यत्यासमन्वाह
text_mt: He recites the three verses, "In the eastern quarter you, O Indra…", in alternate order.
Having recited the first [as the invitatory verse], he should sacrifice with the middle one [as the consecratory verse];
having recited the middle one [as the invitatory verse], he should sacrifice with the last one [as the consecratory verse];
having recited the last one [as the invitatory verse], he should sacrifice with the first one [as the consecratory verse].
In this manner are all the consecratory and invitatory verses.
He prepares the Sarvapṛṣṭhā [offering].
As traditionally prescribed, with [the formula], "Since to Indra Rathantara…", he places [the cake] on twelve upturned potsherds.
At the time of performance, he sacrifices to the first deity from the eastern half;
similarly to the others, turning clockwise, ending in the north.
It has been said: "He cuts portions all around progressively."

sanskrit_iast: abhi tvā sūra nonuma iti ṣaḍṛco vyatyāsamanvāha
meaning: अभि त्वा सूर नोनुम इति षडृचो व्यत्यासमन्वाह
text_mt: He recites the six verses, "Unto thee, hero, we shout…", in alternate order.
He should not pronounce the vaṣaṭ-call with a bṛhatī verse.
He should carry four syllables of the invitatory verse over into the consecratory verse.

sanskrit_iast: anuṣṭubhaṃ ca ha vā etatsaṃpādayanti paṅktiṃ ceti te manyāmahe
meaning: अनुष्टुभं च ह वा एतत्संपादयन्ति पङ्क्तिं चेति ते मन्यामहे
text_mt: "Indeed, thus they produce an anuṣṭubh and a paṅkti," so we think.

sanskrit_iast: abhi tvā śūra nonumo 'dugdhā iva dhenavaḥ /
meaning: अभि त्वा शूर नोनुमो ऽदुग्धा इव धेनवः /
text_mt: "Unto thee, hero, we shout like unmilked cows,

sanskrit_iast: īśānamasya jagataḥ suvardṛśamīśānamomityanūcya [ndratasthuṣa] stvāmiddhi havāmaha iti yajet
meaning: ईशानमस्य जगतः सुवर्दृशमीशानमोमित्यनूच्य [न्द्रतस्थुष] स्त्वामिद्धि हवामह इति यजेत्
text_mt:
ruler of this moving world, beholding the sun, ruler—om!" Having recited this, he should sacrifice with: "[…of what stands, O Indra,] thee indeed we invoke!"

"Thee indeed we invoke, the makers [of hymns], for the winning of booty;

sanskrit_iast: tvāṃ vṛtreṣvindra satpatiṃ narastvāṃ kāṣṭhomityanūcya [svarvato] 'bhi tvā śūra nonuma iti yajet
meaning: त्वां वृत्रेष्विन्द्र सत्पतिं नरस्त्वां काष्ठोमित्यनूच्य [स्वर्वतो] ऽभि त्वा शूर नोनुम इति यजेत्
text_mt: thee, O Indra, true lord among the Vṛtras, the heroes [call] thee, at the goal—om!" Having recited this, he should sacrifice with: "[…of heaven,] unto thee, hero, we shout!"
As the fourth among these [verses], he places: "Never art thou barren…"
It has been said: "To Agni the radiant, an eight-potsherd sacrificial cake."

sanskrit_iast: caturdhākaraṇakāle sauryāṃstrīnpiṇḍānuddhṛtyodu tyaṃ jātavedasaṃ sapta tvā harito rathe citraṃ devānāmudagādanīkamiti piṇḍānyajamānāya prayacchati
meaning: चतुर्धाकरणकाले सौर्यांस्त्रीन्पिण्डानुद्धृत्योदु त्यं जातवेदसं सप्त त्वा हरितो रथे चित्रं देवानामुदगादनीकमिति पिण्डान्यजमानाय प्रयच्छति
text_mt: At the time of making the fourfold division, having taken up three lumps of the [mess] for Sūrya, he hands the lumps to the sacrificer with: "Up that known to all beings…", "Seven bay steeds in the chariot [draw] thee…", [and] "The wondrous countenance of the gods has arisen…"
The sacrificer eats them.
One who desires a village should offer the Sāṃgrahaṇī [iṣṭi] dedicated to the Viśvedevas.
With [the formulas] beginning with, "Thou art steadfast…", he lays down the enclosing sticks, each to its mantra.

sanskrit_iast: yo jyogāmayāvī syādyo vā kāmayeta sarvamāyuriyāmiti tasmā etāmiṣṭiṃ nirvapet /
meaning: यो ज्योगामयावी स्याद्यो वा कामयेत सर्वमायुरियामिति तस्मा एतामिष्टिं निर्वपेत् /
text_mt: One should offer this iṣṭi for one who has been ill for a long time, or who wishes, "May I attain the full span of life."
At the time of setting out the vessels, he employs a four-cornered vessel of khadira wood,
and a golden ear-ornament made of a hundred measures.

sanskrit_iast: atho khalu yāvatīḥ samā eṣyanmanyeta tāvanmānaṃ syāt
meaning: अथो खलु यावतीः समा एष्यन्मन्येत तावन्मानं स्यात्
text_mt: Or rather, of as many years as he expects he will live, of that many measures it should be.

sanskrit_iast: yannavamaittannavanītamabhavadityājyamavekṣyājyagrahaṇakāle tūṣṇīṃ khādire caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā sādanakāla uttareṇa dhruvāṃ khādiraṃ sādayitvā tasminpravartamavadadhāti
meaning: यन्नवमैत्तन्नवनीतमभवदित्याज्यमवेक्ष्याज्यग्रहणकाले तूष्णीं खादिरे चतुर्गृहीतं गृहीत्वा सादनकाल उत्तरेण ध्रुवां खादिरं सादयित्वा तस्मिन्प्रवर्तमवदधाति
text_mt: Having looked at the clarified butter with, "Because it gathered afresh, that became fresh butter…", at the time of taking the clarified butter, having taken four ladlings silently into the khadira vessel, and at the time of placing [it] having set the khadira vessel north of the dhruvā ladle, he drops the ear-ornament into it.

sanskrit_iast: upahomakāle śvinoḥ prāṇo 'sītyetaiḥ pratimantraṃ catura upahomāñjuhoti
meaning: उपहोमकाले श्विनोः प्राणो ऽसीत्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रं चतुर उपहोमाञ्जुहोति
text_mt: At the time of the minor libations, he offers four minor libations, each to its mantra, with [the formulas] beginning with, "Thou art the breath of the Aśvins…"

sanskrit_iast: hutvāhutvā pravartamabhighārayati rāḍasi virāḍasi samrāḍasi svarāḍasīti
meaning: हुत्वाहुत्वा प्रवर्तमभिघारयति राडसि विराडसि सम्राडसि स्वराडसीति
text_mt: Each time after offering, he bastes the ear-ornament with: "Thou art the king, thou art the wide ruler, thou art the sovereign ruler, thou art the self-ruler."

sanskrit_iast: yatkhādira ājyaṃ tadagreṇāhavanīyaṃ paryāhṛtya dakṣiṇasyāṃ vediśroṇyāṃ sādayati
meaning: यत्खादिर आज्यं तदग्रेणाहवनीयं पर्याहृत्य दक्षिणस्यां वेदिश्रोण्यां सादयति
text_mt: Having brought the clarified butter which is in the khadira vessel around past the front of the āhavanīya, he sets it down on the southern hip of the altar ground.
The sacrificer looks at it with: "The stream of clarified butter, the path of immortality."
Then the brahman takes his right hand.

sanskrit_iast: brahmaṇa itara ṛtvijo hastamanvārabhya yajamānaṃ paryāhuḥ pāvamānena tvā stomeneti
meaning: ब्रह्मण इतर ऋत्विजो हस्तमन्वारभ्य यजमानं पर्याहुः पावमानेन त्वा स्तोमेनेति
text_mt: The other priests, holding onto the hand of the brahman, address the sacrificer all around with: "With the Pāvamāna stoma…"
Then the sacrificer sips the clarified butter from the gold.
[The adhvaryu] consecrates him while he is eating with: "Make him, O Agni, unto life and brilliance…"

sanskrit_iast: uddhṛtya hiraṇyaṃ prakṣālyāyuṣṭe viśvato dadhaditi yajamānāya prayacchati
meaning: उद्धृत्य हिरण्यं प्रक्षाल्यायुष्टे विश्वतो दधदिति यजमानाय प्रयच्छति
text_mt: Having taken out the gold and washed it, he hands it to the sacrificer with: "Bestowing life upon thee from all sides…"

sanskrit_iast: tadyajamāna ācamya pratigṛhya pradakṣiṇaṃ dakṣiṇe karṇa ābadhnātyāyurasi viśvāyurasi sarvāyurasi sarvamāyurasi sarvaṃ ma āyurbhūyātsarvamāyurgeṣamiti
meaning: तद्यजमान आचम्य प्रतिगृह्य प्रदक्षिणं दक्षिणे कर्ण आबध्नात्यायुरसि विश्वायुरसि सर्वायुरसि सर्वमायुरसि सर्वं म आयुर्भूयात्सर्वमायुर्गेषमिति
text_mt: The sacrificer, having sipped water and accepted it, binds it clockwise on his right ear with: "Thou art life, thou art all-life, thou art full life, thou art the full span of life; may all life be mine, may I attain the full span of life."
With the remainder of the section, "Agni is possessed of life…", the adhvaryu takes his right hand.
The iṣṭi concludes in the established manner.
Having poured out [grains for] a sacrificial cake for Indra-Varuṇa, he should offer a curdled milk offering for Indra-Varuṇa.
Having taken it off [the fire] and adorned it, he places the sacrificial cake down into the curd mixture (payasyā).
Having covered it with this very [curd mixture], he sets it down.

sanskrit_iast: athāsmātpratidiśaṃ payasyāṃ vyūhati yā vāmindrāvaruṇā yatavyā tanūrity
meaning: अथास्मात्प्रतिदिशं पयस्यां व्यूहति या वामिन्द्रावरुणा यतव्या तनूरित्य्
text_mt: Then, in every direction from it, he pushes aside the curd mixture with: 'O Indra and Varuṇa, whatever body of yours is to be propitiated…'
With the very same [formulas] he pushes it back together.
He bends the endings of the formulas, saying: 'is released.'
He cuts portions of the curd mixture together with the sacrificial cake.
The supplementary oblations are: 'O Indra and Varuṇa, whatever weak part in Agni…'
'To Agni the gatherer, a sacrificial cake on eight potsherds'—this has been explained.
He recites fifteen kindling verses, beginning with: 'Harness the most divine-invoking…'
'Surely for us, in search of cattle…' are the invitatory and consecratory verses.
'Whose [offering] he enjoyed…' and 'For we know thee…' are the concluding verses.
On the full moon of the Citrā month, he should perform the Citrā sacrifice.
The supplementary oblations are: 'O Agni, come to us with cattle…'
Having moved away under abundant constellations, one desiring rain should sacrifice with the Kārīrī.

sanskrit_iast: agnīnanvādhāyāpareṇāhavanīyaṃ dakṣiṇātikramyopaviśya yajamāno mārutamasi marutāmoja iti kṛṣṇaṃ vāsaḥ kṛṣṇatūṣaṃ paridhatte
meaning: अग्नीनन्वाधायापरेणाहवनीयं दक्षिणातिक्रम्योपविश्य यजमानो मारुतमसि मरुतामोज इति कृष्णं वासः कृष्णतूषं परिधत्ते
text_mt: Having added fuel to the fires, stepped past south of the āhavanīya and sat down, the sacrificer puts on a black garment with black fringe, with: 'Thou art related to the Maruts; thou art the vigor of the Maruts.'
With 'Stay, O Maruts, the advancing falcon!', he pushes back the west wind.
He brings forth the east wind with: 'Come, O wind!'
A black horse stands in front, facing west.
