sanskrit_iast: sattre tu dākṣiṇau homau hutvedamahaṃ māṃ kalyānyai kīrtyai svargāya lokāya dakṣiṇāṃ nayāmīti yajamānāḥ kṛṣṇājināni dhūnvanta udañco dakṣiṇāpathenātiyanti
meaning: सत्त्रे तु दाक्षिणौ होमौ हुत्वेदमहं मां कल्यान्यै कीर्त्यै स्वर्गाय लोकाय दक्षिणां नयामीति यजमानाः कृष्णाजिनानि धून्वन्त उदञ्चो दक्षिणापथेनातियन्ति
text_mt: In a sattra, however, having offered the two dakṣiṇā libations, [saying,] "Here I lead myself as a sacrificial gift for good fame, for the heavenly world," the sacrificers, shaking their black-antelope skins, pass across along the path of gifts towards the north.
Only on the last day do they dissolve friendships,
and cast away the black antelope horns.
On the previous day itself, at the time of the yajñāyajñīya stotra, he draws the vasatīvarī waters for the following day.

sanskrit_iast: vartamāna evātirātra uttarasmā ahne payāṃsi viśāsti
meaning: वर्तमान एवातिरात्र उत्तरस्मा अह्ने पयांसि विशास्ति
text_mt: While the Atirātra is still in progress, he assigns the milk portions for the following day.

sanskrit_iast: yatra maitrāvaruṇasyābhijānāti śvaḥsutyāmindrāgnibhyāṃ viśvebhyo devebhyo brāhmaṇebhyaḥ somyebhyaḥ somapebhyaḥ somaṃ prabrūtātsubrahmaṇya subrahmaṇyāmāhvayeti
meaning: यत्र मैत्रावरुणस्याभिजानाति श्वःसुत्यामिन्द्राग्निभ्यां विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यो ब्राह्मणेभ्यः सोम्येभ्यः सोमपेभ्यः सोमं प्रब्रूतात्सुब्रह्मण्य सुब्रह्मण्यामाह्वयेति
text_mt: When he understands the Maitrāvaruṇa’s [call]: "Announce the tomorrow's soma pressing for Indra and Agni, for all the gods, for the Brahmins who are worthy of soma and drinkers of soma; O Subrahmaṇya, call out the subrahmaṇyā recitation!"—

sanskrit_iast: tadāgnīdhra āgnīdhrāgāraṃ praviśya saṃpreṣyati śvaḥsutyāmindrāgnibhyāṃ viśvebhyo devebhyo brāhmaṇebhyaḥ somyebhyaḥ somapebhyaḥ somaṃ prabravīmi subrahmaṇya subrahmaṇyāmāhvayeti
meaning: तदाग्नीध्र आग्नीध्रागारं प्रविश्य संप्रेष्यति श्वःसुत्यामिन्द्राग्निभ्यां विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यो ब्राह्मणेभ्यः सोम्येभ्यः सोमपेभ्यः सोमं प्रब्रवीमि सुब्रह्मण्य सुब्रह्मण्यामाह्वयेति
text_mt: then the āgnīdhra, having entered the fire chamber of the āgnīdh, issues the ritual call: "I announce tomorrow's soma pressing for Indra and Agni, for all the gods, for the Brahmins who are worthy of soma and drinkers of soma; O Subrahmaṇya, call out the subrahmaṇyā recitation!"
"He indeed should say, 'tomorrow's soma pressing'," according to Āśmarathya;
"today's soma pressing," according to Ālekhana.
From then onwards he should say only "tomorrow's soma pressing".
The day concludes with the offerings to the wives of the gods.
When the day is concluded, the brahman priest releases his speech.
They carry water around for the wives.
having returned, they put it onto the āhavanīya fire.
Right then they commence the nine-versed Agniṣṭoma whose chant is the Rathantara.
With the sound of a chariot, he commences the Mahendra chant.
The sound takes the place of the mantra.
On the next day, they undertake the fifteenfold Ukthya having the Bṛhat-sāman.
With the sound of a drum, he commences the Mahendra chant.

sanskrit_iast: yadyu vai stanayitnuḥ syātsa eva syācchabdo mantrasthāne
meaning: यद्यु वै स्तनयित्नुः स्यात्स एव स्याच्छब्दो मन्त्रस्थाने
text_mt: If, indeed, there should be thunder, that itself would be the sound in place of the mantra.
On the next day, they undertake the seventeenfold Ukthya having the Vairūpa-sāman.
In place of the sacrificial grass, he commences the Mahendra chant with a water-pail.
The sāman is commenced, [yet] not [yet] chanted by the prastotṛ.
Then the udgātṛ shakes [the water] with the water-pail.
On the next day, they undertake the twenty-one-fold Ṣoḍaśin having the Vairāja-sāman.
This day is [characterized by] the nyuṅkha.
In place of the sacrificial grass, he commences the Mahendra chant with the two churning sticks.
The sāman is commenced, [yet] not [yet] chanted by the prastotṛ.
Then, having covered the right thigh of the udgātṛ with avakā plants, he churns fire on it.
Over that [fire], when produced, the udgātṛ utters "hiṅ" and hands it to the prastotṛ;

sanskrit_iast: tamadhvaryuruttareṇa dhiṣṇiyānparyāhṛtyāhavanīye prahṛtya preddho agne dīdihīti virājābhijuhoti
meaning: तमध्वर्युरुत्तरेण धिष्णियान्पर्याहृत्याहवनीये प्रहृत्य प्रेद्धो अग्ने दीदिहीति विराजाभिजुहोति
text_mt: The adhvaryu, having brought it around to the north of the dhiṣṇya hearths and cast it into the āhavanīya, makes an offering upon it with the virāj [verse]: "Kindled, O Agni, shine forth..."
On the next day, they undertake the twenty-seven-fold Ukthya having the Śākvara-sāman.
In place of the sacrificial grass, he commences the Mahendra chant with water in which avakā plants are placed.
The sāman is commenced, [yet] not [yet] chanted by the prastotṛ.

sanskrit_iast: atha tisraḥ saharṣabhā agreṇa sado 'pareṇāgnīdhramudīcīnaṃ dakṣiṇāpathenātiyanti
meaning: अथ तिस्रः सहर्षभा अग्रेण सदो ऽपरेणाग्नीध्रमुदीचीनं दक्षिणापथेनातियन्ति
text_mt: Then three [cows], accompanied by a bull, pass across along the dakṣiṇā path northwards, in front of the sadas [and] west of the āgnīdhra.
On the next day, they undertake the thirty-three-fold Ukthya having the Raivata-sāman.
This day is [characterized by] the nyūṅkha.
The adhvaryu himself offers the season sacrifice (ṛtuyāja);

sanskrit_iast: adhvaryū yajataṃ gṛhapate yajetyabhijñāyādhvaryurhavirdhānaṃ praviśya praiṣottarayarcā yajati /
meaning: अध्वर्यू यजतं गृहपते यजेत्यभिज्ञायाध्वर्युर्हविर्धानं प्रविश्य प्रैषोत्तरयर्चा यजति /
text_mt: Upon recognising [the call], "O two adhvaryus, sacrifice! O householder, sacrifice!", the adhvaryu, having entered the havirdhāna shed, sacrifices with a verse following the ritual call,
or with the ritual call following the verse:
"O Aśvins, drink the pressed [soma], shining fires, of pure vows,
"With the season, drink the soma! Vauṣaṭ!"—if it is unshifted (avyūḍha).

sanskrit_iast: vyūḍhe tvarvāñcamadya yayyaṃ nṛvāhaṇaṃ rathaṃ yuñjāthāmiha vāṃ vimocanam /
meaning: व्यूढे त्वर्वाञ्चमद्य यय्यं नृवाहणं रथं युञ्जाथामिह वां विमोचनम् /
text_mt: In the shifted (vyūḍha) [order], however: "Yoke your chariot today hitherward, going swiftly, carrying men; here is unyoking for the two of you;

sanskrit_iast: pṛṅktaṃ havīṃṣi madhunā hi kaṃ gatamathā somaṃ pibataṃ vājinīvasū //
meaning: पृङ्क्तं हवींषि मधुना हि कं गतमथा सोमं पिबतं वाजिनीवसू //
text_mt: mingle the oblations with honey, for indeed you have come; then drink the soma, rich in steeds!"

sanskrit_iast: ṛtunā somaṃ pibataṃ vauṣaḍiti tasya pracaritaṃ marutvatīyairbhavati
meaning: ऋतुना सोमं पिबतं वौषडिति तस्य प्रचरितं मरुत्वतीयैर्भवति
text_mt: "With the season, drink the soma! Vauṣaṭ!"—the proceeding for this takes place along with the Marutvatīya [draughts].

sanskrit_iast: atha pratiprasthātottareṇāgnīdhramudīcīṃ tantiṃ vitatya tasyāṃ vatsānbadhnāti
meaning: अथ प्रतिप्रस्थातोत्तरेणाग्नीध्रमुदीचीं तन्तिं वितत्य तस्यां वत्सान्बध्नाति
text_mt: Then the pratiprasthātṛ, having stretched a tether northward to the north of the āgnīdhra, ties the calves to it.
To the south of the mārjālīya, they shut in the mothers [cows].
In place of the sacrificial grass, he commences the Mahendra chant with water in which dūrvā grass is placed.
The sāman is commenced, [yet] not [yet] chanted by the prastotṛ.
Then, having united these calves with the mothers, they make them low to one another.
They drive them across northwards along the dakṣiṇā path, in front of the sadas [and] west of the āgnīdhra.
The pṛṣṭhya six-day period is concluded.
When it is concluded, they consume ghee or honey.
"Just as one would anoint the shoulder of an ox, such indeed is that," it is known [from scripture].
Then, day after day, they undertake three Chandoma Ukthya [days]:
the twenty-four-fold, the forty-four-fold, [and] the forty-eight-fold.
The first has the Rathaṃtara-sāman;
the second has the Bṛhat and Rathaṃtara sāmans;
Then they undertake the tenth day, the indisputable (avivākya):
a twenty-four-fold Agniṣṭoma having the Rathaṃtara-sāman.
Here no one speaks to anyone who is challenged [or struck down].
Those outside who are lookers-on should speak in dispute;
if they do not find [an answer] there, it must be spoken from among the members of the sadas;
if they do not find [an answer] there, it must be spoken by the householder.
"It must indeed be spoken," he says finally.
"One should speak in an anuṣṭubh," it is known [from scripture].
Having recited an anuṣṭubh [verse], he should then say that.
With respect to that in which he is challenged, he accomplishes it by means of the anuṣṭubh.
On this day, they bring two kinds of firewood:
To the north of the āhavanīya, they set down those of udumbara wood.
Then, while [the others] touch him from behind, he offers two oblations into the gārhapatya:

sanskrit_iast: amūryā upa sūrye yābhirvā sūryaḥ saha /
meaning: अमूर्या उप सूर्ये याभिर्वा सूर्यः सह /
text_mt: "Those [waters] which are up by the sun, or with which the sun is united,
may they impel our sacrifice."

sanskrit_iast: iha ratiriha rantiriha ramatiriha ramadhvamiha vo ramatiḥ svāheti
meaning: इह रतिरिह रन्तिरिह रमतिरिह रमध्वमिह वो रमतिः स्वाहेति
text_mt: with: "Here is delight, here is resting, here is rejoicing; rejoice here, here is your resting; svāhā!"
and with "Releasing the support..." Then, having gone to the āhavanīya,

meaning: अतिच्छन्दसोपतिष्ठन्ते ऽयं सहस्रमानवो दृशः कवीनां मतिर्ज्योतिर्विधर्मा /
text_mt: they worship [it] with an aticchandas verse: "This one, having thousandfold human forms, the vision of the poets, the thought, the light, the supporter of the cosmos;
the ruddy one sent forth the dawns together;

sanskrit_iast: arepasaḥ samokasaḥ sacetasaḥ saretasaḥ svasare manyumantaścidākoriti
meaning: अरेपसः समोकसः सचेतसः सरेतसः स्वसरे मन्युमन्तश्चिदाकोरिति
text_mt: spotless, dwelling together, having one mind, having the same seed, in the early morning, even those who are full of anger [brought gifts]..."
From there, they glide together for the mental draught (manograha) dedicated to Prajāpati.

sanskrit_iast: prasṛpteṣūpāṃśupātreṇa gṛhṇātyanayā tvā pṛthivyā pātreṇa samudraṃ rasayā prajāpataye juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmīti
meaning: प्रसृप्तेषूपांशुपात्रेण गृह्णात्यनया त्वा पृथिव्या पात्रेण समुद्रं रसया प्रजापतये जुष्टं गृह्णामीति
text_mt: When they have glided forward, he draws [the draught] with the upāṃśu vessel: "With this earth as a vessel, the ocean with juice, I draw you agreeable to Prajāpati."
"He should draw it from empty space," says one [view].

sanskrit_iast: tārtīyasavanikasya somasya pariśāyayedyāvantamekasmai camasagaṇāya sagrahāyāptaṃ manyetetyaparam
meaning: तार्तीयसवनिकस्य सोमस्य परिशाययेद्यावन्तमेकस्मै चमसगणाय सग्रहायाप्तं मन्येतेत्यपरम्
text_mt: "He should leave over from the soma of the third pressing as much as he considers sufficient for a set of goblets together with a draught," says another [view].
The beginning of the chant (stotropākaraṇa), the prastāva, the udgītha, and the pratihāra are [performed] mentally.

sanskrit_iast: manasā tisṛṇāṃ sarparājñīnāṃ ṣaṭkṛtvaḥ pratigṛṇāti yadyardharcaśaḥ śaṃsati /
meaning: मनसा तिसृणां सर्पराज्ञीनां षट्कृत्वः प्रतिगृणाति यद्यर्धर्चशः शंसति /
text_mt: He responds mentally six times to the three Sarparājñī verses, if [the hotṛ] recites by half-verses;
nine times, if by verse-quarters.
The hotṛ recites the Caturhotṛ formulas.
"Om" is the response to the Daśahotṛ;
"We have prospered, O hotṛ!" [is the response] to the Saptahotṛ.
The call (āśruta), the counter-call (pratyāśruta), the consecratory verse, the vaṣaṭ-call, and the second vaṣaṭ-call are [performed] mentally.
Having offered mentally, he brings the portion for partaking.
The fact that they look at one another constitutes the mutual invitation.
It is known [from the Brāhmaṇa]: "They discuss the theological discourse (brahmavādya)."
"Having sat down, there should be a conversation," says one [view].
"The chief officiating priests, having sat around the master of the house (gṛhapati) himself, should question him," says another [view].
The adhvaryu asks him:

sanskrit_iast: yaddaśahotāraḥ sattramāsata kena te gṛhapatinārdhnuvankena prajā asṛjanteti
meaning: यद्दशहोतारः सत्त्रमासत केन ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन्केन प्रजा असृजन्तेति
text_mt: "When the Daśahotṛs held a sacrificial session, through which master of the house did they prosper, and with what did they create creatures?"

sanskrit_iast: prajāpatinā vai te gṛhapatinārdhnuvaṃstena prajā asṛjanteti prativacanaḥ
meaning: प्रजापतिना वै ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवंस्तेन प्रजा असृजन्तेति प्रतिवचनः
text_mt: "Through Prajāpati as the master of the house they prospered; with him they created creatures," is the answer.

sanskrit_iast: brahmā pṛcchati yaccaturhotāraḥ sattramāsata kena te gṛhapatinārdhnuvankenauṣadhīrasṛjanteti
meaning: ब्रह्मा पृच्छति यच्चतुर्होतारः सत्त्रमासत केन ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन्केनौषधीरसृजन्तेति
text_mt: The brahman asks: "When the Caturhotṛs held a sacrificial session, through which master of the house did they prosper, and with what did they create plants?"
"Through Soma as the master of the house they prospered; with him they created plants," is the answer.

sanskrit_iast: hotā pṛcchati yatpañcahotāraḥ sattramāsata kena te gṛhapatinārdhnuvankenaibhyo lokebhyo 'surānprāṇudanta kenaiṣāṃpaśūnavṛñjateti
meaning: होता पृच्छति यत्पञ्चहोतारः सत्त्रमासत केन ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन्केनैभ्यो लोकेभ्यो ऽसुरान्प्राणुदन्त केनैषांपशूनवृञ्जतेति
text_mt: The hotṛ asks: "When the Pañcahotṛs held a sacrificial session, through which master of the house did they prosper, with what did they drive away the Asuras from these worlds, and with what did they take away their cattle?"

sanskrit_iast: agninā vai te gṛhapatinārdhnuvaṃstenaibhyo lokebhyo 'surānprāṇudanta tenaiṣāṃ paśūnavṛñjateti prativacanaḥ
meaning: अग्निना वै ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवंस्तेनैभ्यो लोकेभ्यो ऽसुरान्प्राणुदन्त तेनैषां पशूनवृञ्जतेति प्रतिवचनः
text_mt: "Through Agni as the master of the house they prospered; with him they drove away the Asuras from these worlds, and with him they took away their cattle," is the answer.

sanskrit_iast: hotrakāḥ pṛcchanti yatṣaḍḍhotāraḥ sattramāsata kena te gṛhapatinārdhnuvankenartūnakalpayanteti
meaning: होत्रकाः पृच्छन्ति यत्षड्ढोतारः सत्त्रमासत केन ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन्केनर्तूनकल्पयन्तेति
text_mt: The hotrakas ask: "When the Ṣaḍḍhotṛs held a sacrificial session, through which master of the house did they prosper, and with what did they fashion the seasons?"
"Through Dhātṛ as the master of the house they prospered; with him they fashioned the seasons," is the answer.

sanskrit_iast: udgātā pṛcchati yatsapatahotāraḥ sattramāsata kena te gṛhapatinārdhnuvankena suvarāyankenemāṃllokānsamatanvanniti
meaning: उद्गाता पृच्छति यत्सपतहोतारः सत्त्रमासत केन ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन्केन सुवरायन्केनेमांल्लोकान्समतन्वन्निति
text_mt: The udgātṛ asks: "When the Saptahotṛs held a sacrificial session, through which master of the house did they prosper, with what did they go to heaven, and with what did they extend these worlds?"

sanskrit_iast: aryamṇā vai te gṛhapatinārdhnuvaṃstena suvarāyaṃstenemāṃllokānsamatanvanniti prativacanaḥ
meaning: अर्यम्णा वै ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवंस्तेन सुवरायंस्तेनेमांल्लोकान्समतन्वन्निति प्रतिवचनः
text_mt: "Through Aryaman as the master of the house they prospered; with him they went to heaven, and with him they extended these worlds," is the answer.

sanskrit_iast: api vā yadevaitatūṣṇīkaṃ mānasaṃ tasyaiṣa vādaḥ
meaning: अपि वा यदेवैततूष्णीकं मानसं तस्यैष वादः
text_mt: Or else, this is the discussion for whatever is performed silently and mentally.
Or rather, when the hotṛ recites the Caturhotṛ formulas,
it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa]: "They reproach Prajāpati."

sanskrit_iast: akuśalo vā ayaṃ prajāpatiryo daṃśamaśakānsasṛje ya stenāniti prajāpatiparivādaḥ
meaning: अकुशलो वा अयं प्रजापतिर्यो दंशमशकान्ससृजे य स्तेनानिति प्रजापतिपरिवादः
text_mt: "Indeed, unskilled is this Prajāpati who created biting flies and mosquitoes, who [created] thieves"—such is the reproach of Prajāpati.
Or rather, they recite the mantras reproaching Prajāpati.
"That Prajāpati created forests and cities, mountains

sanskrit_iast: kartāni ca na tadbhadraṃ yadbhadraṃ tanma āsuva //
meaning: कर्तानि च न तद्भद्रं यद्भद्रं तन्म आसुव //
text_mt: and chasms, that is not good. What is good, impel that to me!
That the dawn, joined with darkness, burned most fiercely by day;
both the flood of water and the excessive heat—so it was when heated by Prajāpati.
That there are thieves, that there are wolves, biting flies, and mosquitoes, that there are malicious ones—

sanskrit_iast: tadu te vṛjinaṃ tvetadvratametanna me matam //
meaning: तदु ते वृजिनं त्वेतद्व्रतमेतन्न मे मतम् //
text_mt: that is crookedness of yours; this vow is not my opinion.
Worship Prajāpati on the tenth day, the thought of poets, the bull of peoples;

sanskrit_iast: sa suṣṭutiṃ sudraviṇaṃ dadhānaḥ pūto vipāpmā vijahāti loka iti
meaning: स सुष्टुतिं सुद्रविणं दधानः पूतो विपाप्मा विजहाति लोक इति
text_mt: bearing good praise and good wealth, purified and free from evil, he leaves the world behind."

meaning: अथ व्रं वृणीते ऽदो नो ऽस्त्विति यत्कामयते /
text_mt: Then he chooses a wish: "May this be ours," whichever he desires.
And indeed, a brahmin has many desires.

sanskrit_iast: bhūrbhuvaḥ suvaḥ suprajāḥ prajayā bhūyāsaṃ suvīro vīraiḥ suvarcā varcasā supoṣaḥ poṣairityetadvidadaḥti
meaning: भूर्भुवः सुवः सुप्रजाः प्रजया भूयासं सुवीरो वीरैः सुवर्चा वर्चसा सुपोषः पोषैरित्येतद्विददःति
text_mt: They perform this: "Bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, suvaḥ! May I be rich in offspring through offspring, rich in heroes through heroes, rich in luster through luster, rich in nourishment through nourishments!"

sanskrit_iast: caturhotṝnvyākhyāya dvārau saṃvṛtya yathādhiṣṇiyaṃ patnīrvyāsādyāthābhyo vācamupākaroti
meaning: चतुर्होतॄन्व्याख्याय द्वारौ संवृत्य यथाधिष्णियं पत्नीर्व्यासाद्याथाभ्यो वाचमुपाकरोति
text_mt: Having recited the caturhotṛ formulas, having closed the two doors, and having seated the wives according to their dhiṣṇya hearths, he then commences speech for them.

sanskrit_iast: iha dhṛtiriha svadhṛtiriha rantiriha ramatirityaudumbarīṃ pariṣvajyodarairupaspṛśanto vāgyatāstiṣṭhanti
meaning: इह धृतिरिह स्वधृतिरिह रन्तिरिह रमतिरित्यौदुम्बरीं परिष्वज्योदरैरुपस्पृशन्तो वाग्यतास्तिष्ठन्ति
text_mt: With [the words], "Here is firmness, here is self-firmness, here is delight, here is revelry," having embraced the audumbarī post, touching it with their bellies, they stand restraining their speech.
When the sun has reached above the tree-tops, they creep forward, keeping hold of one another.

sanskrit_iast: yuvaṃ tamindrāparvatā puroyudhā yo naḥ pṛtanyādapa taṃtamiddhataṃ vajreṇa taṃtamiddhatam /
meaning: युवं तमिन्द्रापर्वता पुरोयुधा यो नः पृतन्यादप तंतमिद्धतं वज्रेण तंतमिद्धतम् /
text_mt: "You two, Indra and Parvata, fighting in the forefront, strike down whoever assails us; strike him down with the thunderbolt!
Let the deep [abode] please him driven far away, when he reaches it!

sanskrit_iast: asmākaṃ śatrūnpari śūra viśvato darmā darṣīṣṭa viśvata ityuttareṇa havirdhānaṃ dakṣiṇairhastaiḥ kaṭāṃstejanīrvā niṣevamāṇāḥ prāñco gatvā pañca vacāṃsi vyāharanti vāgvāgaitu vāgupaitu vāk samaitūpa maitu vāgbhūrbhuvaḥ suvariti
meaning: अस्माकं शत्रून्परि शूर विश्वतो दर्मा दर्षीष्ट विश्वत इत्युत्तरेण हविर्धानं दक्षिणैर्हस्तैः कटांस्तेजनीर्वा निषेवमाणाः प्राञ्चो गत्वा पञ्च वचांसि व्याहरन्ति वाग्वागैतु वागुपैतु वाक् समैतूप मैतु वाग्भूर्भुवः सुवरिति
text_mt: O hero, from every side, breaker [of forts], smash our enemies completely!"—touching mats or stalks with their right hands, having gone eastward to the north of the havirdhāna shed, they utter the five utterances: "May speech come! May speech approach! May speech assemble! May speech come unto me! Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svar!"

sanskrit_iast: ahnā rātriṃ dhyātvādhivṛkṣasūrye subrahmaṇyayā vācaṃ visṛjyaudumbarīḥ samidha ādadhāti
meaning: अह्ना रात्रिं ध्यात्वाधिवृक्षसूर्ये सुब्रह्मण्यया वाचं विसृज्यौदुम्बरीः समिध आदधाति
text_mt: Having meditated on the night by day, when the sun has reached above the tree-tops, having released speech with the Subrahmaṇyā formula, he puts kindling sticks of udumbara wood on [the fire].
The tenth day is concluded.
They undertake the concluding day like the opening day.
There are no ahīna-continuations here.
What is done on a preceding day for the following day, those are the ahīna-continuations.
If it is a sacrificial session, they shave [their heads], including the tufts, at the time of shaving.

sanskrit_iast: udavasānīyayeṣṭvānyānṛtvijo vṛtvā pṛṣṭhaśamanīyena yajanate jyotiṣṭomenāgniṣṭomena sahasradakṣiṇena
meaning: उदवसानीययेष्ट्वान्यानृत्विजो वृत्वा पृष्ठशमनीयेन यजनते ज्योतिष्टोमेनाग्निष्टोमेन सहस्रदक्षिणेन
text_mt: Having sacrificed with the Udavasānīyā offering, having chosen other officiating priests, they sacrifice with the Pṛṣṭhaśamanīya, an Agniṣṭoma-Jyotiṣṭoma with a thousand [cows] as sacrificial gifts.
On the opening and concluding [days], and on the tenth day, he draws the Pṛśni and Prāṇa draughts
intertwining [them] with the measures of soma.

sanskrit_iast: prākṛtaṃ yajurmānamanudrutya vāyurasi prāṇo nāmeti daśabhiḥ pṛśnigrahāṇāṃ mantrairdaśa mānāni mimīte
meaning: प्राकृतं यजुर्मानमनुद्रुत्य वायुरसि प्राणो नामेति दशभिः पृश्निग्रहाणां मन्त्रैर्दश मानानि मिमीते
text_mt: Having recited the standard measuring yajus, he measures ten measures with the ten mantras of the Pṛśni draughts: "You are Vāyu; breath by name..."

sanskrit_iast: uttaraṃ yajurmānamanudrutyāyaṃ puro bhuva iti daśabhiḥ prāṇagrahāṇāṃ mantrairdaśa mānāni mimīte
meaning: उत्तरं यजुर्मानमनुद्रुत्यायं पुरो भुव इति दशभिः प्राणग्रहाणां मन्त्रैर्दश मानानि मिमीते
text_mt: Having recited the following measuring yajus, he measures ten measures with the ten mantras of the Prāṇa draughts: "This one in front, Bhuva..."
In this way, he intertwines the subsequent measures.
There are nine stalks each [for each measure, and] ten mantras.
Or rather, he measures with nine [mantras] of nine [stalks] each.
The remaining [mantras] are for the purpose of option.

sanskrit_iast: api vā mānamanudrutya pṛśnī atha prāṇena nivapet
meaning: अपि वा मानमनुद्रुत्य पृश्नी अथ प्राणेन निवपेत्
text_mt: Or rather, having recited the measuring [formula], one should scatter [stalks] with the two Pṛśni [mantras], then with the Prāṇa [mantra].
Then one should scatter [the stalks of] the Prāṇa [draught], the measure, with the two Pṛśni [mantras].
Then one should scatter [the stalks of] the two Pṛśni [draughts], the Prāṇa [draught], with the measuring [mantra].
In this manner the two subsequent rounds are arranged.
That which is the first is the fourth;
that which is the second is the fifth.

sanskrit_iast: uttareṣu triṣu pṛṣṭhyāhaḥsu trīnatigrāhyāngṛhṇāti āgneyamekaviṃśa aindraṃ triṇave sauryaṃ trayastriṃśe
meaning: उत्तरेषु त्रिषु पृष्ठ्याहःसु त्रीनतिग्राह्यान्गृह्णाति आग्नेयमेकविंश ऐन्द्रं त्रिणवे सौर्यं त्रयस्त्रिंशे
text_mt: On the later three days of the six-day pṛṣṭhya period, he draws three atigrāhya draughts: the one for Agni on the twenty-one-fold [day], the one for Indra on the twenty-seven-fold [day], the one for Sūrya on the thirty-three-fold [day].
The Vājasaneyins prescribe [them] in the former triad of days.
Where the Gaurīvīta sāman is [used], there he draws many atigrāhya draughts.
We shall explain the three-fronted arrangement [of draughts].
The opening and concluding days and the tenth day have the Aindravāyava draught first.
Then, of the other nine [days], the first day has the Aindravāyava draught first;
The three-fronted arrangement thus established rotates three times, if it is not shifted.
If it is shifted, however, the opening and concluding days have the Aindravāyava draught first;
then, of the other ten [days], the first day has the Aindravāyava draught first;
then two [days] have the Aindravāyava draught first.
They immolate a beast for Agni on the opening day;
on the next day, an ewe for Sarasvatī.
Thus arranged, they immolate the eleven animals day by day.
One who desires spiritual brilliance [offers] one for Sūrya.
If there should be eleven sacrificial posts, he should erect the posts one by one each day;
Day after day, the spare post is turned towards [the next post in order].
At the post standing opposite the fire, he dedicates the animal on the concluding day.
There are twelve Agniṣṭomas having the Rathaṃtara as chant.

sanskrit_iast: gavāmayanena prajāṃ bhūtiṃ bhūmānaṃ gacchantyabhi svargaṃ lokaṃ jayantyeṣu lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhanti
meaning: गवामयनेन प्रजां भूतिं भूमानं गच्छन्त्यभि स्वर्गं लोकं जयन्त्येषु लोकेषु प्रतितिष्ठन्ति
text_mt: By means of the Gavāmayana, they attain offspring, prosperity, and abundance; they win the heavenly world; they establish themselves firmly in these worlds.
Its procedure has been explained by means of the twelve-day rite constituting a sacrificial session.
Some prescribe seventeen consecrations.
It has been stated: "Those who are about to consecrate themselves for a year-long session should consecrate themselves on the Ekāṣṭakā."
They should consecrate themselves four days before the full-moon day.
"Before the Māghī full moon," says Āśmarathya.
Having undertaken the introductory Atirātra, they undertake the introductory twenty-four-stoma Ukthya day.
These two become inserted days.
Then they undertake the Abhiplava six-day period:
the Jyotiṣ-Agniṣṭoma with the Rathaṃtara-sāman;
the Go-Ukthya with the Bṛhat-sāman;
the Āyus-Ukthya with the Rathaṃtara-sāman;
the Go-Ukthya with the Bṛhat-sāman;
the Āyus-Ukthya with the Rathaṃtara-sāman;
the Jyotiṣ-Agniṣṭoma with the Bṛhat-sāman.
They undertake four Abhiplava periods arranged in this manner,
and the Pṛṣṭhya six-day period at the end of the month.
They undertake five months arranged in this manner.
three Paraḥsāman days as Ukthyas, or as Agniṣṭomas,
Then they undertake the Viṣuvant day, a twenty-one-stoma Agniṣṭoma with the Divākīrtya-sāman.
When the sun has risen on it, he begins the morning recitation.
This day is [celebrated as] Divākīrtya.

sanskrit_iast: uttare pakṣa āvṛttā gaṇā anyatra dvādaśāhīyāddaśarātrāt
meaning: उत्तरे पक्ष आवृत्ता गणा अन्यत्र द्वादशाहीयाद्दशरात्रात्
text_mt: In the latter half [of the year], the groups of days are reversed, except for the ten-day period of the twelve-day sacrifice.
Then they undertake three Arvāksāman days as Ukthyas,
and the Viśvajit-Agniṣṭoma.
These four are inserted days.
Having undertaken the reversed Pṛṣṭhya six-day period, [and] four reversed Abhiplava periods at the end of the month,
they undertake five months arranged in this manner.
the ten days of the twelve-day sacrifice,
the latter four inserted days,
and the Mahāvrata and the Atirātra.

sanskrit_iast: uttarasya pakṣasa upariṣṭādviśvajita āvṛttaṃ pṛṣṭhyaṃ ṣaḍahamupetya trīnabhiplavānāvṛttān
meaning: उत्तरस्य पक्षस उपरिष्टाद्विश्वजित आवृत्तं पृष्ठ्यं षडहमुपेत्य त्रीनभिप्लवानावृत्तान्
text_mt: In the latter half [of the year], after the Viśvajit, having undertaken the reversed Pṛṣṭhya six-day period and three reversed Abhiplava periods,
these, together with the earlier ones, are twenty-eight inserted days.
Having undertaken the reversed Pṛṣṭhya six-day period, [and] four reversed Abhiplava periods at the end of the month,
they undertake four months arranged in this manner.
three Abhiplava periods, the Āyus and Go days, the ten days of the twelve-day sacrifice,
the latter twenty-eight inserted days, and the Mahāvrata and the Atirātra.
In the first half [of the year], before the final Pṛṣṭhya period, [they undertake] the Abhijit-Agniṣṭoma;
in the latter half, after the first Pṛṣṭhya period, [they undertake] the Viśvajit-Agniṣṭoma.
The rest is the same as the Śāṭyāyanaka.

sanskrit_iast: api vā saṃvatsaraṃ saṃpādyottame māsi dvādaśāhīye daśarātre sakṛtpṛṣṭhānyupeyuḥ
meaning: अपि वा संवत्सरं संपाद्योत्तमे मासि द्वादशाहीये दशरात्रे सकृत्पृष्ठान्युपेयुः
text_mt: Or rather, having completed the year, they should undertake the pṛṣṭha stotras only once, during the ten-day period of the twelve-day sacrifice in the last month.
In that case, Abhiplava periods should be substituted in place of the Pṛṣṭhya periods.
After the ten-day period of the Dvādaśāha is the Mahāvrata.
Then they undertake the Mahāvrata, a twenty-five-fold Agniṣṭoma.
With nine verses addressed to Indra and lacking a pratihāra, the adhvaryu sings as udgātṛ.
The wives sing along to the Bhadra Sāman.
Its performance has already proceeded through the Marutvatīya [draughts].
Then the pratiprasthātṛ arranges the special artistic performances of the Mahāvrata.
There are ten holes bored through the neck of an udumbara harp.
Through each bored hole he strings ten strings of muñja grass.
Saying, 'Earth, thirty-three strings,' the adhvaryu stretches thirty-three strings;
Saying, 'Atmosphere, thirty-three strings,' the hotṛ thirty-three strings;
Saying, 'Heaven, thirty-three strings,' the udgātṛ thirty-three strings;
He sets down an udumbara chair at the place of the udgātṛs, woven with muñja grass, directly above the seat of the hotṛ.

sanskrit_iast: audumbaraṃ pleṅkhaṃ hotre prabadhnāti mauñjyā rajjvā
meaning: औदुम्बरं प्लेङ्खं होत्रे प्रबध्नाति मौञ्ज्या रज्ज्वा
text_mt: He fastens an udumbara swing for the hotṛ with a cord of muñja grass.
He places two udumbara wooden boards for the adhvaryu,
Upon grass cushions the assistant hotṛs, the accompanying singers, and the wives sit.
The wives prepare themselves with apāghāṭalikā lutes, tambalavīṇās, and piccholās.
The lute-players prepare themselves with conch shells, reed flutes, and tūṇava pipes.

sanskrit_iast: nikalpete brahmacārī puṃścalī cāgreṇa sadaso dakṣiṇāṃ dvārbāhumārtiṣyamāṇau
meaning: निकल्पेते ब्रह्मचारी पुंश्चली चाग्रेण सदसो दक्षिणां द्वार्बाहुमार्तिष्यमाणौ
text_mt: A student and a courtesan prepare themselves in front of the sadas, intending to touch against the southern doorpost.

sanskrit_iast: uttarasyāṃ vediśroṇyāṃ puṃścalyai māgadhāya ca pariśrayanti
meaning: उत्तरस्यां वेदिश्रोण्यां पुंश्चल्यै मागधाय च परिश्रयन्ति
text_mt: On the northern buttock of the altar ground they screen off [an enclosure] for the courtesan and a Māgadha.
They tie drums in the cardinal directions,
West of the āgnīdhra fire chamber they dig a pit for the earth-drum,
Half inside the altar ground, half outside the altar ground.
Having covered it with a wet hide whose hair is turned upwards and secured it around with pegs, he places this tail-stalk here to serve as a drumstick.
In front of the āgnīdhra fire chamber a Śūdra and an Āryan prepare themselves, about to wrestle over a piece of hide.

sanskrit_iast: uttareṇāgnīdhraṃ kaṭasaṃghāte tejanasaṃghāte vārdraṃ carma vyadhanārthaṃ vitatyocchrayanti
meaning: उत्तरेणाग्नीध्रं कटसंघाते तेजनसंघाते वार्द्रं चर्म व्यधनार्थं वितत्योच्छ्रयन्ति
text_mt: North of the āgnīdhra fire chamber they stretch out and raise a wet hide upon a clump of reed mats or cane stalks for target-piercing.
In front of the āhavanīya fire, armored men don their armor in chariots.
At the edge of the mārjālīya, eight maidservants prepare themselves with water pots.

sanskrit_iast: vāgbhadraṃ mano bhadraṃ māno bhadraṃ tanno bhadramiti triḥ parvayet
meaning: वाग्भद्रं मनो भद्रं मानो भद्रं तन्नो भद्रमिति त्रिः पर्वयेत्
text_mt: He should repeat three times: 'Speech is auspicious, mind is auspicious, measure is auspicious, that is auspicious for us.'

sanskrit_iast: kaṭaśalākayekṣukāṇḍena veṇukāṇḍena vetasakāṇḍena vā vāṇaṃ saṃhrādya tena māhendrasya stotramupākaroti
meaning: कटशलाकयेक्षुकाण्डेन वेणुकाण्डेन वेतसकाण्डेन वा वाणं संह्राद्य तेन माहेन्द्रस्य स्तोत्रमुपाकरोति
text_mt: Having caused the harp to sound by means of a mat splint, a piece of sugarcane, a piece of bamboo, or a reed-stalk, he introduces the chant of the draught for Mahendra with it.
'The udgātṛ plays [it],' so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].
The udgātṛ gives it to the prastotṛ;
The adhvaryu gives it to another.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ so 'greṇa sadaso dakṣiṇāṃ dvārbāhuṃ prativādayannāste
meaning: तं सो ऽग्रेण सदसो दक्षिणां द्वार्बाहुं प्रतिवादयन्नास्ते
text_mt: He sits in front of the sadas, playing it against the southern doorpost.

sanskrit_iast: upākṛte māhendrasya stotre sarvā vāco vadanti
meaning: उपाकृते माहेन्द्रस्य स्तोत्रे सर्वा वाचो वदन्ति
text_mt: When the chant of the draught for Mahendra is introduced, all voices sound.
The sacrificers utter an uproar.
The wives play apāghāṭalikā lutes, tambalavīṇās, and piccholās.
The lute-players sound together conch shells, reed flutes, and tūṇava pipes.

sanskrit_iast: ṛtīyete brahmacārī puṃścalī ca dakṣiṇaṃ dvārbāhumāśliṣyamāṇau
meaning: ऋतीयेते ब्रह्मचारी पुंश्चली च दक्षिणं द्वार्बाहुमाश्लिष्यमाणौ
text_mt: The student and the courtesan revile each other, clinging to the southern doorpost.
The courtesan and the Māgadha unite.
They beat the drums,
[And beat] the earth-drum with the tail-stalk.

sanskrit_iast: śūdrāryau carmakarte vyāyacchete ārdre śvete parimaṇḍale /
meaning: शूद्रार्यौ चर्मकर्ते व्यायच्छेते आर्द्रे श्वेते परिमण्डले /
text_mt: The Śūdra and the Āryan wrestle over the piece of hide, which is wet, white, and circular,
The Brahmin inside the altar ground, the Śūdra outside the altar ground.
'These have succeeded; these have done well,' says the Brahmin;
'These are evictors; these have done ill,' says the Śūdra.
Having won it, the Brahmin tosses the hide onto the āgnīdhra hearth.
The armored men drive around this hide.
He directs each of them: 'Do not miss! Do not shoot past!'
Piercing [it] when stretched, they do not shoot beyond it.
According to some, princely sons pierce [it].
Having gone an unmeasured distance towards the north and having returned, they unyoke [the chariots].

sanskrit_iast: atraitā dāsakumārya udakumbhānadhinidhāya triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ mārjālīyaṃ parinṛtyanti dakṣiṇānpado nighnantīridaṃmadhuṃ gāyantyaḥ
meaning: अत्रैता दासकुमार्य उदकुम्भानधिनिधाय त्रिः प्रदक्षिणं मार्जालीयं परिनृत्यन्ति दक्षिणान्पदो निघ्नन्तीरिदंमधुं गायन्त्यः
text_mt: Now these slave girls, having placed water-jars on [their heads], dance thrice clock-wise around the mārjālīya, beating their right feet, singing the Idaṃmadhu [song]:

sanskrit_iast: idameva sāraghaṃ madhvayaṃ somaḥ suto iha /
meaning: इदमेव सारघं मध्वयं सोमः सुतो इह /
text_mt: "This indeed is honey made by bees; this soma is pressed here.

sanskrit_iast: tasyeha piva tātṛpurhaimahā idaṃ madhvidaṃ madhvityeva gāyeyurityāśmarathyaḥ
meaning: तस्येह पिव तातृपुर्हैमहा इदं मध्विदं मध्वित्येव गायेयुरित्याश्मरथ्यः
text_mt: Drink of it here, become satisfied! Haimahā!" They should sing just: "This is honey! This is honey!"—thus says Āśmarathya.

sanskrit_iast: vāgveda himbinīṃ saināṃ gāyatu prāṇasya vādite /
meaning: वाग्वेद हिम्बिनीं सैनां गायतु प्राणस्य वादिते /
text_mt: "Speech knows the Himbinī; let her sing it when the breath is sounded.
May she, being sung, help the sacrificers here!

sanskrit_iast: vāgveda hastāvārāṃ saināṃ gāyatu prāṇasya vādite /
meaning: वाग्वेद हस्तावारां सैनां गायतु प्राणस्य वादिते /
text_mt: "Speech knows the Hastāvārā; let her sing it when the breath is sounded.
May she, being sung, help the sacrificers here!"—so [runs the verse].
Then the Saṃvatsaragāthā:
"Cows alone are fragrant; cows are scented like bdellium.

sanskrit_iast: gāvo dhṛtasya mātarastā iha santu bhūyasīḥ //
meaning: गावो धृतस्य मातरस्ता इह सन्तु भूयसीः //
text_mt: Cows are the mothers of ghee; may they be abundant here!

sanskrit_iast: nanu gāvo maṅkīrasya gaṅgāyā udakaṃ papuḥ /
meaning: ननु गावो मङ्कीरस्य गङ्गाया उदकं पपुः /
text_mt: Did not the cows drink the water of the Gaṅgā of Maṅkīra?
They drank of the Sarasvatī river and plunged in, heading eastward.
We swim across these, like pegs across a ford.

sanskrit_iast: nikīrya tubhyaṃ madhya ākarśye karśyo yathā //
meaning: निकीर्य तुभ्यं मध्य आकर्श्ये कर्श्यो यथा //
text_mt: Scattering for you in the middle, like a lean one in a lean [pasture] (?).

meaning: यदा भङ्ग्यश्विनौ वदत ऋतपर्णक यो ऽवधीः /
text_mt: When the two Bhaṅgyaśvins say: 'O Ṛtaparṇaka, who struck
the spoil of what was manifested and what was unmanifested of both?'
When the two Rākhāṭīs say: 'The village-dwelling Maṅkīra and Dāśaka—
when peaceful ease is ruined by the village, the draft-ox suffers while carrying.'
"The dappled cows drank this; this soma was pressed.
Here with gold pieces they wove pegs, ointment for the thighs."

sanskrit_iast: haimahā idaṃ madhu hilluhillviti sarvāsāmṛganteṣu samayaḥ
meaning: हैमहा इदं मधु हिल्लुहिल्ल्विति सर्वासामृगन्तेषु समयः
text_mt: "Haimahā! This is honey! Hillu, hillu!"—such is the conclusion at the ends of all the verses.
Then these slave girls, having poured out the water-jars, go as they please.
Following the chant for Mahendra, the noises cease.

sanskrit_iast: arkaḥ pavitraṃ rajaso vimānaḥ punāti devānāṃ bhuvanāni viśvā /
meaning: अर्कः पवित्रं रजसो विमानः पुनाति देवानां भुवनानि विश्वा /
text_mt: "The sun, the strainer, measuring out space, purifies all the realms of the gods.

sanskrit_iast: dyāvāpṛthivī payasā saṃvidāne ghṛtaṃ duhāte amṛtaṃ prapīne //
meaning: द्यावापृथिवी पयसा संविदाने घृतं दुहाते अमृतं प्रपीने //
text_mt: Heaven and earth, agreeing through milk, swell yielding ghee and nectar.

sanskrit_iast: pavitramarko rajaso vimānaḥ punāti devānāṃ bhuvanāni viśvā /
meaning: पवित्रमर्को रजसो विमानः पुनाति देवानां भुवनानि विश्वा /
text_mt: "The sun, the strainer, measuring out space, purifies all the realms of the gods.

sanskrit_iast: suvarjyotiryaśo mahadaśīmahi gādhamuta pratiṣṭhāmiti phalake kūrcau vādhiruhyādhvaryuḥ śastraṃ pratigṛṇāti
meaning: सुवर्ज्योतिर्यशो महदशीमहि गाधमुत प्रतिष्ठामिति फलके कूर्चौ वाधिरुह्याध्वर्युः शस्त्रं प्रतिगृणाति
text_mt: May we attain light, splendour, great glory, and a firm footing!"—having mounted two planks or two grass bundles, the adhvaryu responds to the recitation.
The Mahāvrata is concluded.
The concluding rite (udayanīya) and the Pṛṣṭhya-śamanīya day have been explained.
On the three Paraḥsāman days he draws three atigrāhya draughts.

meaning: उपयामगृहीतो ऽस्यद्भ्यस्त्वौषधीभ्यो जुष्टं गृह्णामीति प्रथमे ऽहनि गृह्णाति /
text_mt: On the first day he draws with: "You are taken with a base: I draw you, agreeable to the waters, to the plants";
on the second with: "To the plants, to the offspring";
on the third with: "To the offspring, to Prajāpati."
These same ones in reverse order on the Arvāksāman days;
those same ones in forward and reverse order on the Viṣuvant day.
In their middle is the one for Sūrya: "Up that all-knowing god..."

sanskrit_iast: etasminnevāhani vaiśvakarmaṇamatigrāhyāṇāmaṣṭamaṃ gṛhṇāti vācaspatiṃ viśvakarmāṇamūtaya iti
meaning: एतस्मिन्नेवाहनि वैश्वकर्मणमतिग्राह्याणामष्टमं गृह्णाति वाचस्पतिं विश्वकर्माणमूतय इति
text_mt: On this very day, he draws the eighth among the atigrāhya draughts, the one for Viśvakarman, with: "The lord of speech, Viśvakarman, for help..."

sanskrit_iast: śvo bhūta ādityaṃ mahīmū ṣu mātaramiti
meaning: श्वो भूत आदित्यं महीमू षु मातरमिति
text_mt: On the next day, the one for Āditya, with: "The great mother..."
In this very manner he draws the two alternately until the Mahāvrata.
and the five-cup draught for Prajāpati.
On this day he draws thirty-three atigrāhya draughts:

sanskrit_iast: daśāgneyā daśindrā daśa sauryā vaiśvakarmaṇa ādityaḥ pañcapātra iti trayastriṃśat
meaning: दशाग्नेया दशिन्द्रा दश सौर्या वैश्वकर्मण आदित्यः पञ्चपात्र इति त्रयस्त्रिंशत्
text_mt: ten for Agni, ten for Indra, ten for Sūrya, the one for Viśvakarman, the one for Āditya, and the five-cup draught—thus thirty-three.
In the place for the atigrāhya draughts, four atigrāhya cups are set down, one in each direction;

sanskrit_iast: indramidgāthina ityanudrutyopayāmagṛhīto 'sīndrāya tvārkavate juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmīti gṛhītvaiṣa te yonirindrāya tvārkavata iti sādayati
meaning: इन्द्रमिद्गाथिन इत्यनुद्रुत्योपयामगृहीतो ऽसीन्द्राय त्वार्कवते जुष्टं गृह्णामीति गृहीत्वैष ते योनिरिन्द्राय त्वार्कवत इति सादयति
text_mt: Having recited along: "Indra indeed the singers...", he draws with: "You are taken with a base; I draw you, agreeable to Indra possessing Arka"; having drawn, he sets it down with: "This is your womb; for Indra possessing Arka!"
In this manner he adapts the drawing and setting-down formulas everywhere.

sanskrit_iast: abhi tvā śūra nonuma iti dakṣiṇārdhe
meaning: अभि त्वा शूर नोनुम इति दक्षिणार्धे
text_mt: In the southern part with: "Towards you, hero, we shout..."

sanskrit_iast: imā nu kaṃ bhuvanā sīṣadhemendraśca viśve ca devāḥ /
meaning: इमा नु कं भुवना सीषधेमेन्द्रश्च विश्वे च देवाः /
text_mt: "May Indra and all the gods accomplish these realms for us!

sanskrit_iast: yajñaṃ ca nastanvaṃ ca prajāṃ cādityairindraḥ saha sīṣadhātu /
meaning: यज्ञं च नस्तन्वं च प्रजां चादित्यैरिन्द्रः सह सीषधातु /
text_mt:
May Indra, along with the Ādityas, accomplish our sacrifice, our body, and our offspring!

[With the verse] "May Indra, accompanied by the Ādityas and the band of Maruts, grant us healing remedies," on the western half;

sanskrit_iast: ādityairindraḥ sagaṇo marudbhirasmabhyaṃ bheṣajā karaditi paścārdhe
meaning: आदित्यैरिन्द्रः सगणो मरुद्भिरस्मभ्यं भेषजा करदिति पश्चार्धे

text_mt: [with the verse] "Thee alone do we invoke," on the northern half.

sanskrit_iast: tadidāsa bhuvaneṣu jyeṣṭhaṃ yato jajña ugrastveṣanṛmṇaḥ /
meaning: तदिदास भुवनेषु ज्येष्ठं यतो जज्ञ उग्रस्त्वेषनृम्णः /
text_mt: "That indeed was the eldest in the worlds, from which was born the fierce one of glittering valour;

sanskrit_iast: sadyo jajñāno ni riṇāti śatrūnanu yaṃ viśve madantyūmā iti madhyame
meaning: सद्यो जज्ञानो नि रिणाति शत्रूननु यं विश्वे मदन्त्यूमा इति मध्यमे
text_mt: Born immediately, he lays low the foes, whom all the protectors cheer": [with these two verses] on the middle [cup].

sanskrit_iast: tānanyasminpātra ānīya sarvānmadhyame gṛhṇāti tve kratumapi vṛñjanti viśva iti
meaning: तानन्यस्मिन्पात्र आनीय सर्वान्मध्यमे गृह्णाति त्वे क्रतुमपि वृञ्जन्ति विश्व इति
text_mt: Pouring them all together into another vessel, he takes [the draught] on the middle [cup] with: "In you all direct their insight."
"If he should offer them separately, he would sever the limbs from himself.
If he should withhold the oblations by bringing them together, the sacrificers would then be restricted.
Just drops, having been poured back into oneself, are to be offered.

sanskrit_iast: pratyahāṅgāni dadāti nāhutīḥ saṃruṇaddhi na yajñaṃ vicchinattīti vijñāyate

text_mt: Day after day he gives limbs; he does not withhold the oblations, nor does he sever the sacrifice": thus it is known from scripture.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ bhakṣayati mahaste bhakṣayāmi te bhakṣayāmi bhujaṃ te bhakṣayāmyannādyaṃ te bhaksāyāmīti
meaning: तं भक्षयति महस्ते भक्षयामि ते भक्षयामि भुजं ते भक्षयाम्यन्नाद्यं ते भक्सायामीति
text_mt: He consumes it with: "I consume your greatness, I consume you, I consume your enjoyment, I consume your food."
We shall explain the three-pointed arrangement.
The first day has the draught for Indra and Vāyu first, then [a day] with the Śukra draught first, then [a day] with the Āgrayaṇa draught first.

sanskrit_iast: evaṃvihitā tryanīkā parivartata ita ūrdhvā pragviṣuvataḥ

text_mt: The three-pointed arrangement arranged in this way revolves upwards from here before the central day.
After the central day, [it revolves] through the reversed [days].
They immolate a victim for Agni on the opening day;
on the next day, a ewe for Sarasvatī.
They immolate day after day the sets of eleven victims arranged in this manner.
On the central day, an additional victim for Sūrya is to be immolated.

sanskrit_iast: teṣāmevamupākurvatāṃ dvādaśāhīyasya daśarātrasya saptadaśa ukthye dvātriṃśatamekādaśinyo 'pavṛjyante
meaning: तेषामेवमुपाकुर्वतां द्वादशाहीयस्य दशरात्रस्य सप्तदश उक्थ्ये द्वात्रिंशतमेकादशिन्यो ऽपवृज्यन्ते
text_mt: For them performing thus, on the seventeenth day, an Ukthya day, of the ten-day period of the twelve-day rite, thirty-two sets of eleven victims are completed.
On these they immolate the extra victims belonging to the cow [rite]:
a dwarf [victim] for Viṣṇu on the twenty-first [day];
one for the All-gods on the thirty-third;
a milch cow for Heaven and Earth on the first Chandoma day;
a calf for Vāyu, from that very cow, on the middle [Chandoma day];
a barren sheep for the Ādityas on the last [Chandoma day];
one for Mitra and Varuṇa on the Avivākya day;
a hornless bull for Prajāpati on the Mahāvrata day;
They immolate the sets of eleven victims on the opening and concluding days, either distributing them or not distributing them.
On the intermediate [days], an [animal] for Agni on those with the Rathaṃtara as the Pṛṣṭha chant, and one for Indra on those with the Bṛhat as the Pṛṣṭha chant.
Or rather, one for Agni and Indra on those with the Rathaṃtara as the Pṛṣṭha chant, and one for Indra and Agni on those with the Bṛhat as the Pṛṣṭha chant.
one with a white back for Bṛhaspati on the thirty-third [day];
a hornless bull of two colours, marked on both sides, for Viśvakarman on the Mahāvrata day.
They should immolate day after day the rite victims just like an accumulation, if there should be sufficient victims;
or the sets of eleven distributed: thus the Vājasaneyaka [holds].
Or one for Indra and Agni everywhere.
The Course of the Days-omitters is the Gavāmayana modified in attributes.

sanskrit_iast: yadyahānyutsṛjeyuḥ prathamaṃ pṛṣṭhyaṃ saṃsthāpyāparasmā ahne vasatīvarīḥ parihṛtya vastīvarīṣu mṛtpiṇḍamavadhāyaindraṃ sāṃnāyyaṃ nirupyopavasanti
meaning: यद्यहान्युत्सृजेयुः प्रथमं पृष्ठ्यं संस्थाप्यापरस्मा अह्ने वसतीवरीः परिहृत्य वस्तीवरीषु मृत्पिण्डमवधायैन्द्रं सांनाय्यं निरुप्योपवसन्ति
text_mt: If they omit days, having concluded the first Pṛṣṭhya six-day period, having carried around the Vasatīvarī waters for the next day, having put a lump of clay into the Vasatīvarī waters, and having apportioned the ritual milk offering for Indra, they observe fast.
On the next day, having omitted the day, they immolate an animal victim for Prajāpati.

sanskrit_iast: tasya yathākālaṃ vapayā pracaryāgnaye vasumate puroḍāśamaṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapatyaindraṃ ca dadhi
meaning: तस्य यथाकालं वपया प्रचर्याग्नये वसुमते पुरोडाशमष्टाकपालं निर्वपत्यैन्द्रं च दधि
text_mt: Having proceeded with its omentum at the proper time, he apportions a sacrificial cake on eight potsherds for Agni accompanied by the Vasus, and curd for Indra.

When the iḍā has been invoked, having invoked the ritual milk offering together, they consume it.

sanskrit_iast: mādhyaṃdinakāle paśupuroḍāśena pracaryendrāya marutvate puroḍāśamekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapatyaindraṃ ca carum
meaning: माध्यंदिनकाले पशुपुरोडाशेन प्रचर्येन्द्राय मरुत्वते पुरोडाशमेकादशकपालं निर्वपत्यैन्द्रं च चरुम्
text_mt: At midday, having proceeded with the animal cake, he apportions a sacrificial cake on eleven potsherds for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, and a cooked mess for Indra.

sanskrit_iast: havirāhutiprabhṛtīḍāntaṃ saṃsthāpya tṛtīyasavanakāle paśunā pracarya vaiśvadevaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapati vaiśvadevaṃ ca caruṃ
meaning: हविराहुतिप्रभृतीडान्तं संस्थाप्य तृतीयसवनकाले पशुना प्रचर्य वैश्वदेवं द्वादशकपालं निर्वपति वैश्वदेवं च चरुं
text_mt: Having concluded [the rites] beginning with the oblations of the offering and ending with the iḍā, having proceeded with the animal victim at the time of the third pressing, he apportions a sacrificial cake on twelve potsherds for the All-gods, and a cooked mess for the All-gods.
He should conclude the two oblations as before.

sanskrit_iast: api vā savanīyāneva puroḍāśāneteṣāṃ haviṣāṃ sthāne /

for that becomes a rent in the year.

Jyotiṣ, Gauḥ, and Āyus: these are the Trikadrukas.

sanskrit_iast: sahasraṃ dakṣiṇā sarvavedasaṃ vā yāvatīrvā kratoḥ stotrīyāḥ

In the case of one's entire property, having allotted a share to the eldest son, he should beg back what is agreed upon.
Whatever property he possesses at the time of giving the sacrificial gifts, he should give all of that, other than land and human beings.

sanskrit_iast: uttamāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ nītvodavasāya vā dakṣiṇenaudumbarīṃ prāṅniṣadya brūyādyanme 'da ṛṇaṃ yadadastatsarvaṃ dadāmīti
meaning: उत्तमां दक्षिणां नीत्वोदवसाय वा दक्षिणेनौदुम्बरीं प्राङ्निषद्य ब्रूयाद्यन्मे ऽद ऋणं यददस्तत्सर्वं ददामीति
text_mt: Having led forth the final sacrificial gift, or having performed the udavasānīyā rite, seated facing east south of the audumbarī post, he should say: 'Whatever debt I owe of that, whatever of that, all of that I give.'

Indra's Abhijit Agniṣṭoma is for the conquest of what has not yet been conquered.
Both Bṛhat and Rathaṃtara [sāmans] are used, or it has a transcendent pṛṣṭha.
The Bṛhat is for the hotṛ, and there are eleven sacrificial animals at a single sacrificial post.

sanskrit_iast: sahasraṃ dakṣiṇā varāṇāṃ vā dvādaśaṃ śatam

text_mt: The sacrificial gift is a thousand, or one hundred and twelve choice [cows].
By means of the Sarvajit Agniṣṭoma, one obtains everything and conquers everything,
Its Mahāvrata is recited as the Arkya pṛṣṭha-recitation.
The sacrificial gift is a thousand, or twenty times twenty-eight [cows].
The first is the Jyotiṣ Agniṣṭoma with the Rathaṃtara sāman.
He is established in the vital breaths and in the eating of food.
The second is the Gauḥ Ukthya with the Bṛhat sāman.
The third is the Sarvajyotiṣ Agniṣṭoma with both sāmans.
He obtains everything and conquers everything.
The fourth is the Agniṣṭoma equal to a three-day rite (trirātra), with the Bṛhat sāman.
He obtains the fruit of a three-day rite.
The first has the Rathaṃtara sāman, the Bṛhat sāman, or both sāmans.

sanskrit_iast: tasminkāmāḥ spardhāyāṃ bhrātṛvyatistīrṣā svargaḥ paśavo vā

text_mt: In it, the desired objects are: in a rivalry, the desire to overcome a rival, heaven, or cattle.

sanskrit_iast: hiraṇyaṃ mukhe nyasyāntarorū priyāyai bhāryāyai brahmacārī śete śva iṣṭyā paśunā vā yakṣya iti
meaning: हिरण्यं मुखे न्यस्यान्तरोरू प्रियायै भार्यायै ब्रह्मचारी शेते श्व इष्ट्या पशुना वा यक्ष्य इति
text_mt: Having placed gold in his mouth, keeping celibacy between the thighs of his dear wife, he lies down, thinking: 'Tomorrow I shall sacrifice with an iṣṭi or with an animal sacrifice.'

sanskrit_iast: tānyathālokaṃ vinidhāya sarvā diśaḥ sakṣīradṛtayo 'śvarathāḥ somapravākā vidhāvanti

text_mt: Having placed them according to their respective places, horse-drawn chariots carrying skin bags with milk run forth in all directions as soma-announcers.

When the sacrificer is consecrated after sunrise, the avabhṛtha takes place before sunset.
During the upasads, he should close his eyes three times;

sanskrit_iast: sphyo yūpaḥ sphyāgro vā khalevālī lāṅgaleṣā vā

meaning: सवनीयकाले सह पशूनालभते ऽग्निषोमीयं सवनीयमनूबन्ध्यां च

In place of the Agnīṣomīya [animal], an eleven-potsherd cake for Agni-Soma;
In place of the anūbandhyā, a curd-mess for Mitra-Varuṇa.
At the time of its sacrificial gift, a noble white horse is the sacrificial gift.
He should give it to an Āṅgirasa or to a rival.

sanskrit_iast: dveṣyaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vṛtvā tasmā aśvaṃ rukmapratimuktaṃ dadyāt
meaning: द्वेष्यं वा ब्राह्मणं वृत्वा तस्मा अश्वं रुक्मप्रतिमुक्तं दद्यात्
text_mt: Or having chosen an enemy brahmin, he should give him a horse adorned with a gold ornament.

meaning: द्वितीयस्य पञ्चदशमग्निष्टोमसाम कृत्वामयाविनमन्नाद्यकामं प्रजाकामं पशुकामं वा याजयेत्

meaning: आग्नेयीषु स्तुवते ऽजा हिरण्यं च दक्षिणा

meaning: एतस्यैव वायव्यासु पञ्चदशमग्निष्टोमसाम कृत्वामयाविनमन्नाद्यकामं प्रजाकामं पशुकामं वा याजयेत् /
text_mt: Having made the fifteen-versed Agniṣṭoma chant of this very [rite] on verses to Vāyu, one should officiate for one who is chronically ill, one who desires food, one who desires offspring, or one who desires cattle;
having made the Vāravantīya the Agniṣṭoma chant of this very [rite] on Revatī verses, [one should officiate] for one who desires spiritual luster;
having made this very [rite] a Catuṣṭoma, [one should officiate] for one who desires a village.
Some say: they are without the Pravargya.
one desiring valor, with the fifteen-versed.

sanskrit_iast: saptadaśenāgniṣṭutāgniṣṭomena yajñavibhraṣṭo yajeta yasminvā kratau vibhraṃśeta
meaning: सप्तदशेनाग्निष्टुताग्निष्टोमेन यज्ञविभ्रष्टो यजेत यस्मिन्वा क्रतौ विभ्रंशेत
text_mt: One who has fallen away from sacrifice should sacrifice with the seventeen-versed Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma, or [he should sacrifice with it] in whatever rite he fell away.
The threefold is for one who speaks blame;
the fifteen-versed is prescribed for one guilty of killing;
the seventeen-versed is for one who has eaten uneatable food;
the twenty-one-versed is for one going among the people of Gandhāra, Kaliṅga, Magadha, Pāraskara, or Sauvīra;
one desiring heaven, with the thirty-three-versed.
[or] in the Agniṣṭoma, one may desire all desires.
There are four trivṛt Agniṣṭomas having the Rathaṃtara-sāman.
One who desires a village should sacrifice with the first of these, which is unexpressed (anirukta).
"The morning pressing is expressed (nirukta)," say some.
The second is the Bṛhaspatisava.

sanskrit_iast: brāhmaṇo brahmavarcasakāmaḥ purodhākāmo vā yajeta yaṃ vā sthāpatyāyābhiṣiñceyuḥ
meaning: ब्राह्मणो ब्रह्मवर्चसकामः पुरोधाकामो वा यजेत यं वा स्थापत्यायाभिषिञ्चेयुः
text_mt: A brahmin desiring brahmic luster, or desiring the office of purohita, or one whom they would consecrate to governorship (sthāpatya), should sacrifice [with it].
The hotṛ wears a garland, is reddish, blinking, and thrice-pure.

sanskrit_iast: bṛhaspate juṣasva na iti bārhaspatyamatigrāhyaṃ gṛhṇāti
meaning: बृहस्पते जुषस्व न इति बार्हस्पत्यमतिग्राह्यं गृह्णाति
text_mt: With "O Bṛhaspati, enjoy our...", he draws the Bārhaspatya atigrāhya draught.
An animal dedicated to Bṛhaspati is to be seized.
At the morning pressing, when the nārāśaṃsa goblets are deposited, he assigns eleven sacrificial gifts.

sanskrit_iast: ājyena mādhyaṃdine savane kṛṣṇājina āsīnamabhiṣiñcati śukrāmanthinorvā saṃsrāveṇa bṛhaspate yuvamindraśca vasvo divyasyeśāthe uta pārthivasya /
meaning: आज्येन माध्यंदिने सवने कृष्णाजिन आसीनमभिषिञ्चति शुक्रामन्थिनोर्वा संस्रावेण बृहस्पते युवमिन्द्रश्च वस्वो दिव्यस्येशाथे उत पार्थिवस्य /
text_mt: At the midday pressing, he consecrates [the sacrificer] seated on a black antelope skin with clarified butter or with the residue of the Śukra and Manthin [draughts], with: "O Bṛhaspati, you two and Indra rule over divine wealth and earthly;

sanskrit_iast: dhattaṃ rayiṃ stuvate kīraye cidyūyaṃ pāta svastibhiḥ sadā na iti
meaning: धत्तं रयिं स्तुवते कीरये चिद्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा न इति
text_mt: give wealth to the praising singer; do you protect us always with well-being."
At the midday [pressing], [eleven cattle] together with a horse making twelve;

sanskrit_iast: api vāṣṭau prātaḥsavana ekādaśa mādhyaṃdine dvādaśa tṛtīyasavane /
meaning: अपि वाष्टौ प्रातःसवन एकादश माध्यंदिने द्वादश तृतीयसवने /
text_mt: Or rather, eight at the morning pressing, eleven at the midday pressing, twelve at the third pressing;
They lead the horse at each pressing in three shares;
or rather, he should contemplate [it] with the mind at the other two pressings;
Having made the iṣu-viṣṭuti of the third, one should sacrifice while practicing sorcery.
The rest is identical with the Śyena.
The fourth is the Sarvasvāra, the Śunaskarṇastoma.

sanskrit_iast: maraṇakāmo yajeta yaḥ kāmayetānāmayatā svargaṃ lokamiyāmiti
meaning: मरणकामो यजेत यः कामयेतानामयता स्वर्गं लोकमियामिति
text_mt: One desiring death should sacrifice [with it], who desires, "May I go to the heavenly world free from disease."
An animal dedicated to Yama, parrot-green, is to be seized.

sanskrit_iast: ārbhave stūyamāne dakṣiṇenaudumbarīṃ pattodaśenāhatena vāsasā dakṣiṇāśirāḥ prāvṛtaḥ saṃviśannāha brāhmaṇāḥ samāpayata me yajñamiti
meaning: आर्भवे स्तूयमाने दक्षिणेनौदुम्बरीं पत्तोदशेनाहतेन वाससा दक्षिणाशिराः प्रावृतः संविशन्नाह ब्राह्मणाः समापयत मे यज्ञमिति
text_mt: While the Ārbhava-pavamāna is being chanted, lying down to the south of the udumbara post, wrapped with his head to the south in an unwashed garment with fringes at the feet, he says, "O brahmins, bring my sacrifice to completion!"
One desiring prosperity should sacrifice with the Bhuva-ukthya having the Rathaṃtara-sāman.

sanskrit_iast: akṣayyaṃ ha vai cāturmāsyayājinaḥ sukṛtaṃ bhavati
meaning: अक्षय्यं ह वै चातुर्मास्ययाजिनः सुकृतं भवति
text_mt: Imperishable indeed is the merit of one who sacrifices with the Cāturmāsya sacrifices.
In place of the Vaiśvadeva [offering], there is a trivṛt Agniṣṭoma.
the anūbandhyā cow is dedicated to Bṛhaspati.
Subsequent to the morning pressing oblations, he offers the Vaiśvadeva oblations.
The sviṣṭakṛt and iḍā offerings, however, are common.
they do not heap up the high altar (uttaravedi).
They bind the animal to an enclosing stick,
In the subsequent [sacrifices], they erect the sacrificial posts;
they heap up the high altar.

meaning: ततश्चतुर्षु मासेषु वरुणप्रघासानां लोके ऽग्निष्टोम उक्थ्यः /
text_mt: Then, after four months, in place of the Varuṇapraghāsa offerings, there is an Agniṣṭoma and an Ukthya;
the anūbandhyā cow is dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa.
The oblations of the Varuṇapraghāsa offerings are [offered] like those of the Vaiśvadeva.
At the mārjālīya fire, they perform the ritual with the dishes of barley flour.

meaning: ततश्चतुर्षु मासेषु साकमेधानां लोके ऽग्निष्टोम उक्थ्यो ऽतिरात्रः
text_mt: Then, after four months, in place of the Sākamedha offerings, there is an Agniṣṭoma, an Ukthya, and an Atirātra.
in the third, the eleven [animals of the ekādaśinī], or [an animal] dedicated to Prajāpati;
On the first day, [he offers the oblations] dedicated to Agni Anīkavat [subsequent to] the morning pressing oblations.
[The offerings of the] Sāṃtapana [belong] to the midday pressing.
When the Vasatīvarī waters have been carried around, they proceed with the Gṛhamedhīya [offering].
On the next day, after the morning litany has been commenced, they proceed with the full-ladle offering.
[The offerings of the] Krīḍin [Maruts belong] to the morning pressing;
[those of the] Svātavas [Maruts] to the midday pressing;
the great offering (Mahāhavis) to the third pressing.

sanskrit_iast: sanneṣu nārāśaṃseṣu pariśrite mārjālīye pitṛyajñena caranti
meaning: सन्नेषु नाराशंसेषु परिश्रिते मार्जालीये पितृयज्ञेन चरन्ति
text_mt: When the Nārāśaṃsa goblets have been placed down and the mārjālīya [shed] has been enclosed, they proceed with the Pitṛyajña.
Having performed the Traiyambaka offerings and returned, they proceed with the Āditya [offering].
Then, after four months, in the place of the Śunāsīrīya, [there is] a Jyotiragniṣṭoma.
The Śunāsīrīya offerings are like the Vaiśvadeva.
The intermediate vows are like those of the Cāturmāsya sacrifices.
Everywhere he emerges from the final bath wearing an unwashed garment.
Day after day he gives fifty cows as sacrificial gift;
Or [he gives gifts] according to each season, or respectively as in the Cāturmāsya sacrifices;
at the third pressing, [he gives] the calves along with their mothers.
One desiring a village should sacrifice with the Upahavya Agniṣṭoma performed indistinctly (anirukta).
Some say that the morning pressing is distinctly recited (nirukta).
One desiring heaven [should sacrifice] with the Ṛtapeya Agniṣṭoma having the Bṛhatsāman.
When the soma has been bought, the vow [food] is as much as the first finger-joint;
with each subsequent joint [in size] he undertakes the vow.
At night he sits facing the āhavanīya;
Having spoken truth, they glide forward;
speaking truth, they partake [of the soma].

sanskrit_iast: audumbaraścamsaścatuḥsraktiḥ somasya pūrṇaḥ sagotrāya priyāya brahmaṇe deyaḥ
meaning: औदुम्बरश्चम्सश्चतुःस्रक्तिः सोमस्य पूर्णः सगोत्राय प्रियाय ब्रह्मणे देयः
text_mt: A four-cornered goblet of udumbara wood, full of soma, should be given to a dear brahman priest of the same lineage.
With the Bahuhiraṇya Agniṣṭoma, one attains the realm of the draft ox and conquers radiant realms.
He gives twelve measures of gold at the consecration offering;
twice as much at the opening offering;

sanskrit_iast: evamata ūrdhvaṃ dviguṇābhyāsenātithyāyāmupasatprayogeṣvagnīṣomīyasya vapāyāmagnīṣomīye savanīyasya vapāyāṃ savanīye prataḥsavane
meaning: एवमत ऊर्ध्वं द्विगुणाभ्यासेनातिथ्यायामुपसत्प्रयोगेष्वग्नीषोमीयस्य वपायामग्नीषोमीये सवनीयस्य वपायां सवनीये प्रतःसवने
text_mt: in this manner, henceforth by doubling [each time]: at the guest offering, at the performances of the upasads, at the omentum of the Agnīṣomīya [victim], at the Agnīṣomīya [sacrifice], at the omentum of the animal for the pressing, at the animal for the pressing, and at the morning pressing.
When the Nārāśaṃsa goblets have been placed down, he gives an additional one hundred oxen.

sanskrit_iast: hiraṇyasrajamudgātre ṣaṭpuṣkarāṃ dvādaśapuṣkarāṃ vā yajñāyajñīyasya stotre 'vabhṛtheṣṭyāmudayanīyāyāmanūbandhyāyāmudavasānīyāyāṃ ca
meaning: हिरण्यस्रजमुद्गात्रे षट्पुष्करां द्वादशपुष्करां वा यज्ञायज्ञीयस्य स्तोत्रे ऽवभृथेष्ट्यामुदयनीयायामनूबन्ध्यायामुदवसानीयायां च
text_mt: He gives a golden garland having six lotuses, or having twelve lotuses, to the udgātṛ priest at the chant of the Yajñāyajñīya, at the final bath offering, at the concluding offering, at the barren cow offering, and at the departure offering.
A brahmin desiring spiritual splendour [should sacrifice] with the Trivṛt Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma having the Rathaṃtara-sāman.
A kṣatriya desiring valour [should sacrifice] with the fifteen-versed Indrastoma Ukthya having the Bṛhat-sāman.
A vaiśya desiring cattle [should sacrifice] with the seventeen-versed Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma having the Kaṇvarathaṃtara-sāman.
The morning pressing is performed with fresh warm milk, as has been said.

sanskrit_iast: tīvrasutokthyena rathaṃtarasāmnā bṛhatsāmnobhayasāmnā vāmayāvinamannādyakāmaṃ prajākāmaṃ paśukāmaṃ śriyā vā pratyavarūḍhaṃ yājayet
meaning: तीव्रसुतोक्थ्येन रथंतरसाम्ना बृहत्साम्नोभयसाम्ना वामयाविनमन्नाद्यकामं प्रजाकामं पशुकामं श्रिया वा प्रत्यवरूढं याजयेत्
text_mt: With the Tīvrasut Ukthya having the Rathaṃtara-sāman, having the Bṛhat-sāman, or having both sāmans, one should officiate for one who is chronically ill, one desiring proper food, one desiring offspring, one desiring cattle, or one who has fallen from prosperity.
The curds and other admixtures are as in the Vaiśyasava.
Or, with a boiled mixture at the third pressing.
the priests only smell [them], they do not partake [of them].
They partake of them at the chant of the acchāvāka priest.
The secondary hotṛ priests seek permission from the brahman priest.
Both adhvaryus and all camasādhvaryus respond to the acchāvāka.
A set of eleven stakes facing east is measured out.
He excavates the altar ground as far as the post.
A white pregnant mare is the sacrificial gift.
With the Marutstoma, a king and his domestic priest [achieve] union [with the deities].

sanskrit_iast: yo rājyamāśaṃsamāno na labheta sa etena
meaning: यो राज्यमाशंसमानो न लभेत स एतेन
text_mt: one who hopes for kingship but does not obtain it [should sacrifice] with this.
One who desires firm standing [sacrifices] with the Svarāj.

sanskrit_iast: bahu pratigṛhya yo garagīriva manyeta sa punastomena /
meaning: बहु प्रतिगृह्य यो गरगीरिव मन्येत स पुनस्तोमेन /
text_mt: One who, having accepted much, considers himself as if poisoned, [sacrifices] with the Punastoma.
Or having eaten food that ought not to be eaten,
or having sacrificed for one for whom one ought not to sacrifice, say some.
One who is as if light [and] not established should [sacrifice] with this [sacrifice].
One who desires offspring [sacrifices] with the twenty-one-fold Upacchada.
At chant after chant, one stotrīyā-verse is added.
At the morning pressing, [with the formula:] “May the gandharvas and apsarases intoxicate [themselves]!"
when the nārāśaṃsa [goblets] have been deposited, he throws down a stalk [of soma] beneath the pūtabhṛt.
At the midday pressing, [with the formula:] “May the divine gandharvas intoxicate [themselves]!"
At the third pressing, [with the formula:] “May the ancestral gandharvas intoxicate [themselves]!"
At chant after chant, one stotrīyā-verse drops away.
“As it drops away, [the rival] drops away along with it,” so it is known [from sacred tradition].
One who desires, “May I become all this,” [sacrifices] with the Sarvatomukha.
In every direction are the soma-grounds.
The Rāśi and Arāyu catuṣṭomas belong to one who desires proper food.
At the former he gives a heap of grain [as dakṣiṇā].
One who desires cattle [sacrifices] with the two Gotamacatuṣṭomas.
The latter is an Ukthya with a Ṣoḍaśin.
[The offerings] are like asexual animals.
One who desires cattle [sacrifices] with the Udbhid and Valabhid.
Having sacrificed with the Udbhid, he should sacrifice after a year with the Valabhid.
He undertakes the interval with an eight-pot-sherd [cake] for Agni.
In both cases, he gives full gāyatrī-gifts as dakṣiṇā:
One who desires respect [sacrifices] with the two Apacitis.
They have both sāmans.
For them, a horse-drawn chariot with four yoked [horses] is the dakṣiṇā.
He [the sacrificer or sārathi] has gold ornaments, a trembling garland, all kinds of ornaments, and radiant rays.

sanskrit_iast: tasya vaiyāghraḥ parivāro dvaipo dhanvadhirārkṣaḥ kavacaḥ
meaning: तस्य वैयाघ्रः परिवारो द्वैपो धन्वधिरार्क्षः कवचः
text_mt: Its casing is of tiger-skin, the quiver of leopard-skin, the bow of bear-wood, and the armor [fitted].
The chariot-rider is armored, the charioteer is armored, enclosed by the two stationed [guards];
“the charioteer wears a gold breastplate and a wreath,” so it is known [from sacred tradition].

sanskrit_iast: pakṣibhyāṃ sāgnicityābhyāṃ yaḥ kāmyeta pakṣī jyotiṣmataḥ svargāṃllokānanusaṃcareyamiti
meaning: पक्षिभ्यां साग्निचित्याभ्यां यः काम्येत पक्षी ज्योतिष्मतः स्वर्गांल्लोकाननुसंचरेयमिति
text_mt: One who desires, “Becoming winged, may I wander over the radiant heavenly worlds,” [sacrifices] with the two winged [sacrifices] accompanied by the piling of the fire-altar.

sanskrit_iast: ṛṣabheṇāgniṣṭomena rathaṃtarasāmnā rājānaṃ sāmgrāme saṃyatte yājayet
meaning: ऋषभेणाग्निष्टोमेन रथंतरसाम्ना राजानं साम्ग्रामे संयत्ते याजयेत्
text_mt: With the Ṛṣabha Agniṣṭoma having the Rathaṃtara-sāman, he should sacrifice for a king engaged in battle.
Whatever they obtain there, from that one hundred and twelve [cows] are the dakṣiṇā.
Both the Bṛhat and Rathaṃtara [sāmans] are [used].
The whole [sacrifice] is seventeenfold.
The twenty-one-fold is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman.

sanskrit_iast: gosavena ṣaṭtriṃśenokthyena rathaṃtarasāmnā bṛhatsāmnobhayasāmnā vā svārājyakāmaḥ
meaning: गोसवेन षट्त्रिंशेनोक्थ्येन रथंतरसाम्ना बृहत्साम्नोभयसाम्ना वा स्वाराज्यकामः
text_mt: One who desires independent rule [sacrifices] with the Gosava, a thirty-six-fold Ukthya having the Rathaṃtara-sāman, the Bṛhat-sāman, or both sāmans.
The Kaṇvarathaṃtara is at the pavamāna-chant.

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇenāhavanīyamanuddhate vedyai bṛhataḥ stotraṃ pratyabhiṣicyate pratidhuṣā revajjātaḥ sahasā vṛddhaḥ kṣatrāṇāṃ kṣatrabhṛttamo vayodhāḥ /
meaning: दक्षिणेनाहवनीयमनुद्धते वेद्यै बृहतः स्तोत्रं प्रत्यभिषिच्यते प्रतिधुषा रेवज्जातः सहसा वृद्धः क्षत्राणां क्षत्रभृत्तमो वयोधाः /
text_mt: South of the āhavanīya on unraised ground of the altar ground, during the stotra of the Bṛhat, he is consecrated with fresh warm milk [with the verse:] “Born with wealth, grown with might, best bearer of royal power among rulers, bestower of strength;

sanskrit_iast: mahānmahitve tastabhānaḥ kṣatre rāṣṭre ca jāgṛhi /
meaning: महान्महित्वे तस्तभानः क्षत्रे राष्ट्रे च जागृहि /
text_mt: firmly supported in great majesty, watch over the royal power and the realm!
I consecrate you with the independent rule of Prajāpati Parameṣṭhin.”
Having sacrificed with it, he observes the vow of a beast for a year.
Bending down, he should drink water, and he should crop grass;
he may approach his mother, he may approach his sister, he may approach a female of the same lineage;
wherever excretion overtakes him, there he should void [it].
With the Marutstoma one wins endless fortune.
With this he should sacrifice for two or three [persons].
The two Kulāyas of Agni belong to one who desires proper food.
The two Kulāya sacrifices of Indra and Agni are for one desiring heaven.
With the Indrastuta or Indrastoma, an Ukthya with the Bṛhat-sāman, a nobleman [sacrifices] desiring heroic power.
With the stoma of Indra and Agni, he should sacrifice for both the king and the royal priest, sharing a single prosperity.
Brilliance and spiritual luster [accrue] to the brāhmaṇa;
With the Vighana he destroys evil and his rival;
with it he destroys all enemies.
With the Vajra Ṣoḍaśin, [one sacrifices] when performing sorcery;
For both of them, the ritual procedure is explained by the Śyena.
With the Sarvastoma, one wishing to become prosperous [sacrifices].
With the Aptoryāma, for one from whom cattle would tend to fall away;
he obtains everything, he conquers everything.
With the Navasaptadaśa, [one sacrifices] desiring offspring.
With the Viṣuvat, the son of the eldest wife [sacrifices];
With the Viśvajit, one who has rivals [sacrifices].
With the Pañcadaśa, [one sacrifices] desiring heroic power.
With the Saptadaśa, [one sacrifices] desiring offspring.
With the Ekaviṃśa, [one sacrifices] desiring a firm footing.
The ahīna sacrifices, beginning with the two-day sacrifice and ending with the eleven-day sacrifice, have an Atirātra at the end.
Their ritual procedure is explained by the Dvādaśāha in its form as an ahīna.
Of the two-day sacrifice, the first day begins with the Aindravāyava cup, the subsequent [day] begins with the Śukra cup.
Of the three-day sacrifice, this same [order applies], and [the third day] begins with the Āgrayaṇa cup.
Of the four-day sacrifice, this same [order applies], and [the fourth day] begins with the Aindravāyava cup.
Of the five-day sacrifice, this same [order applies], and [the fifth day] begins with the Śukra cup.
In the six-day sacrifice, [the series] recurs twice.
Of the seven-day sacrifice, this same [order applies], and [the seventh day] begins with the Aindravāyava cup.
Of the eight-day sacrifice, this same [order applies], and [the eighth day] begins with the Śukra cup.
In the nine-day sacrifice, [the series] recurs three times.
Of the ten-day sacrifice, this same [order applies], and [the tenth day] begins with the Aindravāyava cup.
Of the eleven-day sacrifice, this same [order applies], and [the eleventh day] begins with the Śukra cup.
In the twelve-day sacrifice, [the series] recurs four times.
The drawing of the Ṣoḍaśin cup takes place on the later day of the two-day sacrifice.
It should be drawn on the middle [day] of the three-day sacrifice,
and on every fourth day in the various ahīnas beginning with the four-day sacrifice.
The Vyuṣṭidvirātra is the first;

sanskrit_iast: āṅgīrasena yaḥ puṇyo hīna iva syāt sa etena
meaning: आङ्गीरसेन यः पुण्यो हीन इव स्यात् स एतेन
text_mt: With the Āṅgīrasa [dvirātra], one who is virtuous but feels as though deficient [sacrifices] with this.
The earlier [day] is a Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma;
the later is a Sarvastoma Atirātra.

sanskrit_iast: kāpivanena yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate tamabhyaśnute 'lūkṣo bhavati
meaning: कापिवनेन यं कामं कामयते तमभ्यश्नुते ऽलूक्षो भवति
text_mt: With the Kāpivana [dvirātra], he attains whichever wish he desires; he becomes unimpoverished.
The earlier [day] is a Jyotis Ukthya or Agniṣṭoma;
With the Caitraratha [dvirātra], he finds a firm footing in vital breaths and in proper food.

sanskrit_iast: gargatrirātreṇa prajātiṃ bhūmānaṃ gacchatyabhi svargaṃ lokaṃ jayatyeṣu lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhati vasūnrukrānādityānanvārohati
meaning: गर्गत्रिरात्रेण प्रजातिं भूमानं गच्छत्यभि स्वर्गं लोकं जयत्येषु लोकेषु प्रतितिष्ठति वसून्रुक्रानादित्यानन्वारोहति
text_mt: With the Garga three-day sacrifice, he attains offspring and abundance, conquers the heavenly world, finds a firm footing in these worlds, and ascends to the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas.
The Traidhātavīyā is the consecratory offering.

sanskrit_iast: rohiṇī babhrurvā piṅgalaikahāyanī dvihāyani vā somakrayaṇī
meaning: रोहिणी बभ्रुर्वा पिङ्गलैकहायनी द्विहायनि वा सोमक्रयणी
text_mt: The soma-purchasing cow is red or reddish-brown, tawny, one year old or two years old.
[The days are:] Agniṣṭoma, Ukthya, [and] Atirātra.
The pṛṣṭha stotras are the Rathaṃtara, Vāmadevya, and Bṛhat.

sanskrit_iast: trīṇi śatāni trayastriṃśataṃ ca prathame 'hani dadāti /
meaning: त्रीणि शतानि त्रयस्त्रिंशतं च प्रथमे ऽहनि ददाति /
text_mt: On the first day he gives three hundred and thirty-three.
The thousandth [cow] remains over: red, speckle-spotted, of two colors, [or] black-and-white on both sides or on one side.
It is said: "whichever is the chosen, beautiful one."
On the first day, the prominent [animal given] is one having protruding horns.
He addresses it: "O Agni, bring the thousand; you split the hide of Vala.

sanskrit_iast: sa naḥ sahasramā naya prajayā paśubhiḥ saha punarmā viśatādriyiriti
meaning: स नः सहस्रमा नय प्रजया पशुभिः सह पुनर्मा विशताद्रियिरिति
text_mt: Do you bring to us the thousand, together with offspring and cattle; let wealth enter me again."

sanskrit_iast: tāmabhimantrayate tvamapāmoṣadhīnāṃ rasena rasinī babhūvitha sā mā sahasra ā bhaja prajayā paśubhiḥ saha punarmā viśatādriyiriti
meaning: तामभिमन्त्रयते त्वमपामोषधीनां रसेन रसिनी बभूविथ सा मा सहस्र आ भज प्रजया पशुभिः सह पुनर्मा विशताद्रियिरिति
text_mt: He addresses her: "Through the sap of the waters [and] of the plants you have become full of sap; do you grant me a share in the thousand, together with offspring and cattle; let wealth enter me again."
He addresses him: "You are the foundation of the thousand, you are the dwarf sacred to Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast: sa naḥ sahasra ā dhehi prajayā paśubhiḥ saha punarmā viśatādrayiriti
meaning: स नः सहस्र आ धेहि प्रजया पशुभिः सह पुनर्मा विशताद्रयिरिति
text_mt: Do you place us in the thousand, together with offspring and cattle; let wealth enter me again."
It has been said: "to the north of the āgnīdhra [he should lead her]."

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇena vā vediṃ nītvāntarā yūpamāhavanīyaṃ ca droṇakalaśamavadhrāpayedā jighra kalaśamiti /
meaning: दक्षिणेन वा वेदिं नीत्वान्तरा यूपमाहवनीयं च द्रोणकलशमवध्रापयेदा जिघ्र कलशमिति /
text_mt: Or having led [her] to the south of the altar ground, between the sacrificial post and the āhavanīya, he should make her sniff the droṇakalaśa with: "Smell the vat."
[This takes place] at the āgnīdhra or at the havirdhāna shed.
Having led her northward to the āgnīdhra, he places a tārpya garment upon her back.
On it the form of the dhiṣṇya hearths is woven.
Then, while she stands facing west in front [of the fires], he should offer with: "Both of you have conquered..."
He offers the forms that are on her.
Some hand down [here the verses] belonging to the Aśvamedha.

sanskrit_iast: pratīcīṃ sadasaḥ sraktimānīya tasyā upotthāya dakṣiṇaṃ karṇamājapediḍe ranta iti
meaning: प्रतीचीं सदसः स्रक्तिमानीय तस्या उपोत्थाय दक्षिणं कर्णमाजपेदिडे रन्त इति
text_mt: Having brought her to the western corner of the sadas [hall], having stepped up close to her, he should whisper into her right ear: "O Iḍā, Rantā..."
Having released her, he attends to the omen:

sanskrit_iast: yadyapuruṣābhivītā prācīyādarātsīdayaṃ yajamānaḥ kalyāṇaṃ lokamajaiṣīditi vidyāt /
meaning: यद्यपुरुषाभिवीता प्राचीयादरात्सीदयं यजमानः कल्याणं लोकमजैषीदिति विद्यात् /
text_mt: If, unprompted by men, she should go eastward, he should know: "This sacrificer has succeeded, he has won a good world."
If southward: "He will quickly depart from this world."
If westward: "He will have much grain."
If northward: "He will be superior in this world."

sanskrit_iast: tāṃ yajamāno 'bhimantrayate sā mā suvargaṃ lokaṃ gamayeti
meaning: तां यजमानो ऽभिमन्त्रयते सा मा सुवर्गं लोकं गमयेति
text_mt: The sacrificer addresses her: "Do you cause me to reach the heavenly world."

sanskrit_iast: yāstisrastisrastriṃśatyadhi tāsvenāmupasamāhṛtya tāmagnīdhe brahmaṇe hotra udgātra unnetre 'dhvaryave vā dadyāt
meaning: यास्तिस्रस्तिस्रस्त्रिंशत्यधि तास्वेनामुपसमाहृत्य तामग्नीधे ब्रह्मणे होत्र उद्गात्र उन्नेत्रे ऽध्वर्यवे वा दद्यात्
text_mt: Having united her with the three [cows] that are over and above the thirty [on each of the three days], he should give her to the agnīdh, to the brahman, to the hotṛ, to the udgātṛ, to the unnetṛ, or to the adhvaryu.

sanskrit_iast: dvau vonnetārau vṛtvā yataro nāśrāvayettasmai vā
meaning: द्वौ वोन्नेतारौ वृत्वा यतरो नाश्रावयेत्तस्मै वा
text_mt: Or, having chosen two unnetṛs, [he should give her] to whichever does not make the ritual call.
Or two shares to the brahman [and] a third to the agnīdh.
Or to all the sadasyas.
Or, after being driven out, she should roam at will.
It has been said: "Whoever receives her without knowing [her ritual meaning]..."

sanskrit_iast: tāṃ śatamānena hiraṇyena niṣkrīya yajamānasya goṣṭhe visṛjati
meaning: तां शतमानेन हिरण्येन निष्क्रीय यजमानस्य गोष्ठे विसृजति
text_mt: Having redeemed her with gold of a hundred mānas' [weight], he releases her into the cow-pen of the sacrificer.
They milk ten [cows] for the milk-admixture on the first day;
Cooked food is to be given on the first day;
gold, a cow, [and] a garment on the second;

sanskrit_iast: ano ratho 'śvo hastī puruṣa iti tṛtīye
meaning: अनो रथो ऽश्वो हस्ती पुरुष इति तृतीये
text_mt: a cart, a chariot, a horse, an elephant, [and] a slave on the third.
He should not give anything over and above the thousand [cows].

sanskrit_iast: yadi dadyādanūbandhyāvapāyāṃ hutāyāṃ dakṣiṇā nayannnanyūnā daśato nayet
meaning: यदि दद्यादनूबन्ध्यावपायां हुतायां दक्षिणा नयन्न्नन्यूना दशतो नयेत्
text_mt: If he should give, when the omentum of the anūbandhyā cow has been offered, leading the sacrificial gifts, he should not lead less than a decade.
To whomever he intends to give one cow, to ten of those he should present the tenth;
In this manner up to a hundred or up to a thousand.
Having led out the final sacrificial gift, or having performed the final leaving-rite, [he performs] the Śabalī [rite].

sanskrit_iast: samudro 'si viśvavyacā brahmā devānāṃ prathamajā ṛtasya /
meaning: समुद्रो ऽसि विश्वव्यचा ब्रह्मा देवानां प्रथमजा ऋतस्य /
text_mt: "You are the ocean, all-encompassing, the Brahman of the gods, the first-born of truth.
You are food, you are seed, you are light, you are immortality.
We know you, O Śabalī, shining brightly.

sanskrit_iast: tasyāste pṛthivī pādo 'ntarikṣaṃ pādo dyauḥ pādaḥ samudraḥ pādaḥ /
meaning: तस्यास्ते पृथिवी पादो ऽन्तरिक्षं पादो द्यौः पादः समुद्रः पादः /
text_mt: Of that you, the earth is a foot, the atmosphere is a foot, heaven is a foot, the ocean is a foot.

sanskrit_iast: eṣāsi śabali tāṃ tvā vidma sā na iṣamūrjaṃ dhukṣva vasordhārāṃ śabali prajānāṃ śaviṣṭhā vrajamanugeṣaṃ svāheti śabalihomaṃ juhoti
meaning: एषासि शबलि तां त्वा विद्म सा न इषमूर्जं धुक्ष्व वसोर्धारां शबलि प्रजानां शविष्ठा व्रजमनुगेषं स्वाहेति शबलिहोमं जुहोति
text_mt: This you are, O Śabalī; as such we know you; do you yield us vigor and nourishment, a stream of wealth, O Śabalī, most mighty among creatures; may I follow the cow-pen, svāhā"—with this he offers the Śabalihoma.
The [three days] of the Aśvamedha are Agniṣṭoma, Ukthya, [and] Atirātra.
The pṛṣṭha stotras are the Rathaṃtara, the Mahānāmnī, and the Bṛhat.

sanskrit_iast: rājā yajeta yaḥ kāmayeta sarvamidaṃ bhaveyamiti
meaning: राजा यजेत यः कामयेत सर्वमिदं भवेयमिति
text_mt: A king who desires: "May I become all this," should sacrifice [with it].
With the Baida three-day sacrifice, [one sacrifices] desiring independent rule.
There are three nine-versed Atirātras containing the Ṣoḍaśin.
The pṛṣṭha [chants] are Rathaṃtara, Vāmadevya, and Bṛhat.
By means of the Garga trirātra, the days and the pṛṣṭha [chants] of the subsequent three have been explained.
One who desires cattle [sacrifices] with the Chandomapavamāna.
By means of the Antarvasu, he obtains cattle.
The first is Atri's Caturvīra.

meaning: चत्वारो ऽस्य वीराः कुल आजायन्ते सुहोतेत्युक्तम्
text_mt: Four heroes are born in his family: "Suhotā..." has been stated.
There are an Agniṣṭoma, two Ukthyas, and an Atirātra; these are Atri's four catuṣṭomas.
"Atri, the faithful..." has been stated.
One who desires prosperity [sacrifices] with the Jāmadagnya rite.
The upasads are accompanied by cakes.
