sanskrit_iast: āgneya ekakapāla āśvino dvikapālo vaiṣṇavatrikapālaḥ saumyaścatuṣkapālaḥ sāvitraḥ pañcakapālo dhātraḥ ṣaṭkapālo mārutaḥ saptakapālo bārhaspatyo 'ṣṭākapālo maitro navakapālo vāruṇo daśakapāla aindra ekādaśakapālo vaiśvadevo dvādaśakapālaḥ
meaning: आग्नेय एककपाल आश्विनो द्विकपालो वैष्णवत्रिकपालः सौम्यश्चतुष्कपालः सावित्रः पञ्चकपालो धात्रः षट्कपालो मारुतः सप्तकपालो बार्हस्पत्यो ऽष्टाकपालो मैत्रो नवकपालो वारुणो दशकपाल ऐन्द्र एकादशकपालो वैश्वदेवो द्वादशकपालः
text_mt: [There are] a cake on one potsherd for Agni, on two potsherds for the Aśvins, on three potsherds for Viṣṇu, on four potsherds for Soma, on five potsherds for Savitṛ, on six potsherds for Dhātṛ, on seven potsherds for the Maruts, on eight potsherds for Bṛhaspati, on nine potsherds for Mitra, on ten potsherds for Varuṇa, on eleven potsherds for Indra, and on twelve potsherds for the Viśvedevas.

sanskrit_iast: agne verhotraṃ veradhvaramā pitaraṃ vaiśvānaramavase karindrāya devebhyo juṣatāṃ haviḥ svāhā /
meaning: अग्ने वेर्होत्रं वेरध्वरमा पितरं वैश्वानरमवसे करिन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुषतां हविः स्वाहा /
text_mt: "O Agni, accept the hotṛ's office, accept the solemn ritual! Bring Father Vaiśvānara to help! For Indra, for the gods, let the oblation be relished! Svāhā!"
"O divine Aśvins, sprinkle with the honey-whip today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"
"O divine Viṣṇu, stride widely today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"
"O divine Soma, be the bestower of seed today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"
"O divine Savitṛ, impel good impelling today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"
"O divine Dhātṛ, be a good creator today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"

sanskrit_iast: devā grāvāṇo madhumatīmadyāsminyajñe yajamānāya vācaṃ vadata /
meaning: देवा ग्रावाणो मधुमतीमद्यास्मिन्यज्ञे यजमानाय वाचं वदत /
text_mt: "O divine pressing-stones, speak sweet speech today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"
"O divine Aditi, follow along today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"
"O divine Anumati, approve today this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"
"O heavenly waters, bow down today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"
"To each assembly hall, possessing offspring, the Ṛbhu taking pleasure..."
"O divine Indra, be power today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"

sanskrit_iast: deva tvaṣṭaḥ suretodhā adyāsminyajñe yajamānāyaidhīti pratinigadya homāḥ
meaning: देव त्वष्टः सुरेतोधा अद्यास्मिन्यज्ञे यजमानायैधीति प्रतिनिगद्य होमाः
text_mt: "O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, be a good bestower of seed today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"—having recited [each formula] respectively, the oblations [are made].

sanskrit_iast: indrāya devebhyo juṣatāṃ haviḥ svāheti sarvatrānuṣajati
meaning: इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुषतां हविः स्वाहेति सर्वत्रानुषजति
text_mt: He attaches everywhere: "For Indra, for the gods, let the oblation be relished! Svāhā!"
The Saṃsarpa belongs to Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit_iast: yaḥ puṇyo hīna iva syātsa etena
meaning: यः पुण्यो हीन इव स्यात्स एतेन
text_mt: He who is virtuous but feels deprived should sacrifice with this.
The Saṃjaya belongs to Viśvāmitra.
"The year, verily, was this one alone..." has been stated.
Whatever desire he desires, he attains it.
[Its days are:] an Agniṣṭoma, three Ukthyas, and an Atirātra.
Two pressings are trivṛt, one is pañcadaśa.
Two are pañcadaśa, one is saptadaśa.
Two are saptadaśa, one is ekaviṃśa.
Two are ekaviṃśa, one is triṇava.
Two are triṇava, one is trayastriṃśa.
By means of the Pañcaśāradīya, one becomes greater than the many.
Every year he sacrifices with an animal sacrifice.
They bring seventeen dapple-grey five-year-old oxen,
and seventeen dapple-grey three-year-old unbred heifers.
Having sprinkled the oxen and carried fire around them, they release them;
We shall explain their colors.
Having immolated striped ones, butter-spotted ones, reddish ones, yellowish-brown ones, and at last multi-colored ones, they undergo consecration.

sanskrit_iast: trivṛdagniṣṭomaḥ pañcadaśa ukthyaḥ saptadaśa ukthyaḥ pañcadaśa ukthyaḥ saptadaśo 'tirātraḥ
meaning: त्रिवृदग्निष्टोमः पञ्चदश उक्थ्यः सप्तदश उक्थ्यः पञ्चदश उक्थ्यः सप्तदशो ऽतिरात्रः
text_mt: A trivṛt Agniṣṭoma, a pañcadaśa Ukthya, a saptadaśa Ukthya, a pañcadaśa Ukthya, and a saptadaśa Atirātra [constitute the five days].
They immolate three each day,
If Rudra should afflict the oxen,
he should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni associated with Rudra.
[He should offer] a mess of boiled rice sacred to Apāṃ Napāt, if [the ox] should fall into water.
A mess of boiled rice sacred to Nirṛti, if it should sink down.

sanskrit_iast: bhaumaṃ carumekakapālaṃ vā yadyavasannaḥ saṃśīrṇo vā
meaning: भौमं चरुमेककपालं वा यद्यवसन्नः संशीर्णो वा
text_mt: A mess of boiled rice sacred to Bhūmi, or a cake on one potsherd, if it has sunk down or is broken up.

sanskrit_iast: bārhaspatyaṃ caruṃ yadi śloṇaḥ kūṭo vā
meaning: बार्हस्पत्यं चरुं यदि श्लोणः कूटो वा
text_mt: A mess of boiled rice sacred to Bṛhaspati, if it is lame or hornless.
If it should be lost, a mess of boiled rice sacred to Vāyu.
If an invading army should seize [it], a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra the Conqueror.
If they should carry it off by force, a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra the Forceful.
If it should become blind, a mess of boiled rice sacred to Sūrya, or a cake on one potsherd.
If it should fall into a pit, a mess of boiled rice sacred to Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast: yadyavijñātena yakṣmaṇā mriyeta prājāpatyaṃ caruṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ vā
meaning: यद्यविज्ञातेन यक्ष्मणा म्रियेत प्राजापत्यं चरुं द्वादशकपालं वा
text_mt: If it should die of an unknown disease, a mess of boiled rice sacred to Prajāpati, or a cake on twelve potsherds.
The fourth [four-day rite] has the Mahāvrata within.

sanskrit_iast: trivṛdagniṣṭomaḥ pañcadaśa ukthyo mahāvrataṃ saptadaśa ukthya ekaviṃśo 'tirātraḥ
meaning: त्रिवृदग्निष्टोमः पञ्चदश उक्थ्यो महाव्रतं सप्तदश उक्थ्य एकविंशो ऽतिरात्रः
text_mt: A Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma, a Pañcadaśa Ukthya, the Mahāvrata [as] a Saptadaśa Ukthya, and an Ekaviṃśa Atirātra.
The fifth is the Puruṣamedha.
The days are like [those of] the Pañcaśāradīya.
He gives ten thousand on the first day,
a hundred million and a thousand million on the third.
As on the first two [days], so on the latter two.
"The Sādhyas were indeed gods desirous of heaven," as has been said.
One desirous of offspring [should sacrifice] with the second, [that] of the seasons.
With the third, which has the Trikadruka days following it, he attains whatever desire he desires.

sanskrit_iast: trivṛdagniṣṭomaḥ pañcadaśa ukthyaḥ saptadaśa ukthyo jyotirgaurāyuratirātraḥ
meaning: त्रिवृदग्निष्टोमः पञ्चदश उक्थ्यः सप्तदश उक्थ्यो ज्योतिर्गौरायुरतिरात्रः
text_mt: A Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma, a Pañcadaśa Ukthya, a Saptadaśa Ukthya, Jyotis, Go, Āyus, and an Atirātra.
With the fourth, he indeed propagates with offspring and cattle.
An Abhyāsaṅgya five-day rite and a Viśvajit Atirātra.
One desirous of cattle [should sacrifice] with the Kausurubinda.
One desirous of heaven [should sacrifice] with the second, [that] of the Seven Seers.
A Pṛṣṭhya-six-day rite and an Atirātra possessing the Mahāvrata.
One desirous of offspring [should sacrifice] with the Prājāpatya.
A Pṛṣṭhya-six-day rite, and the Prājāpatya Mahāvrata on an Atirātra.
One desirous of cattle [should sacrifice] with the Chandomapavamāna.
A Pṛṣṭhya-six-day rite, and the Chandomapavamāna Mahāvrata on an Atirātra.
One desirous of food [should sacrifice] with the Pṛṣṭhyāvalamba.
A Pṛṣṭhyastoma-six-day rite and an Atirātra possessing the Mahāvrata.
One desirous of food [should sacrifice] with the Sattrasaṃmita.
The days are like [those of] the Kausurubinda.
Jyotis, Go, Āyus, then Abhijit, Viśvajit, Sarvajit, and a Sarvastoma Atirātra.

sanskrit_iast: janakasaptarātreṇa prajātiṃ bhūmānaṃ gacchatyabhi svargaṃ lokaṃ jayatyeṣu lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
meaning: जनकसप्तरात्रेण प्रजातिं भूमानं गच्छत्यभि स्वर्गं लोकं जयत्येषु लोकेषु प्रतितिष्ठति
text_mt: With the Janakasaptarātra he attains progeny and abundance, conquers the heavenly world, and is firmly established in these worlds.

meaning: चत्वारि त्रिवृन्त्यहान्यग्निष्टोममुखानि विश्वजिन्महाव्रतं ज्योतिष्टोमो वैश्वानरो ऽतिरात्रः
text_mt: Four Trivṛt days beginning with an Agniṣṭoma, a Viśvajit, a Mahāvrata, and a Jyotiṣṭoma Vaiśvānara Atirātra.
One desirous of spiritual lustre [should sacrifice] with the eight-day rite.
A Pṛṣṭhya-six-day rite, Jyotis, Go, Āyus, and an Atirātra.
One desirous of spiritual lustre [should sacrifice] with the second.

sanskrit_iast: trivṛdagniṣṭomaḥ pañcadaśa ukthyaḥ sapatadaśa ukthyo 'bhyāsaṅgyaḥ pañcāho viśvajidatirātraḥ
meaning: त्रिवृदग्निष्टोमः पञ्चदश उक्थ्यः सपतदश उक्थ्यो ऽभ्यासङ्ग्यः पञ्चाहो विश्वजिदतिरात्रः
text_mt: A Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma, a Pañcadaśa Ukthya, a Saptadaśa Ukthya, an Abhyāsaṅgya five-day rite, and a Viśvajit Atirātra.
One desirous of food [should sacrifice] with the Śalalīpiśaṅga.
Jyotis, Go, Āyus, Jyotis, Go, Āyus, Āyus, Go, Jyotis, and an Atirātra.

sanskrit_iast: daśarātrāya dīkṣiṣyamāṇo daśahotāraṃ manasānudrutyāhavanīye sagrahaṃ juhuyāt
meaning: दशरात्राय दीक्षिष्यमाणो दशहोतारं मनसानुद्रुत्याहवनीये सग्रहं जुहुयात्
text_mt: Intending to be consecrated for a ten-day rite, having recited the Daśahotṛ mentally, he should offer [it] with the draught into the āhavanīya.
He becomes pre-eminent among offspring and among his peers.

sanskrit_iast: trivṛdagniṣṭomaḥ pañcadaśa ukthyastrivṛdagniṣṭomaḥ saptadaśo 'gniṣṭoma ekaviṃśa ukthyaḥ saptadaśo 'gniṣṭomastriṇavo 'gniṣṭomastrayastriṃśa ukthyastriṇavo 'gniṣṭomo viśvajitsarvapṛṣṭho 'tirātraḥ
meaning: त्रिवृदग्निष्टोमः पञ्चदश उक्थ्यस्त्रिवृदग्निष्टोमः सप्तदशो ऽग्निष्टोम एकविंश उक्थ्यः सप्तदशो ऽग्निष्टोमस्त्रिणवो ऽग्निष्टोमस्त्रयस्त्रिंश उक्थ्यस्त्रिणवो ऽग्निष्टोमो विश्वजित्सर्वपृष्ठो ऽतिरात्रः
text_mt: A Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma, a Pañcadaśa Ukthya, a Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma, a Saptadaśa Agniṣṭoma, an Ekaviṃśa Ukthya, a Saptadaśa Agniṣṭoma, a Triṇava Agniṣṭoma, a Trayastriṃśa Ukthya, a Triṇava Agniṣṭoma, and a Viśvajit Sarvapṛṣṭha Atirātra.
One against whom sorcery is being practiced [should sacrifice] with the Devapura.

sanskrit_iast: triṣṭomo 'gniṣṭomo jyotirukthyastriṣṭomo 'gniṣṭomo 'bhijidagniṣṭomo gaurukthyo 'bhijidagniṣṭomo viśvajidagniṣṭoma āyurukthyo viśvajidagniṣṭomaḥ sarvastomo 'tirātraḥ
meaning: त्रिष्टोमो ऽग्निष्टोमो ज्योतिरुक्थ्यस्त्रिष्टोमो ऽग्निष्टोमो ऽभिजिदग्निष्टोमो गौरुक्थ्यो ऽभिजिदग्निष्टोमो विश्वजिदग्निष्टोम आयुरुक्थ्यो विश्वजिदग्निष्टोमः सर्वस्तोमो ऽतिरात्रः
text_mt: A triṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma, a jyotiḥ Ukthya, a triṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma, an abhijit Agniṣṭoma, a go-Ukthya, an abhijit Agniṣṭoma, a viśvajit Agniṣṭoma, an āyur-Ukthya, a viśvajit Agniṣṭoma, and a sarvastoma Atirātra [constitute the rites].
Through the [rite] accompanied by Chandomas, he obtains man, cattle, vitality, and heroic might.
[The order is:] an abhyāsaṅgya six-day period, three chandoma days, and an Atirātra.
An abhyāsaṅgya five-day period, four chandoma days, and an Atirātra.
By means of the Kausurubinda [rite], one who is already great becomes greater.

sanskrit_iast: trayastrivṛto 'gniṣṭomāstrayaḥ pañcadaśā ukthyāstrayaḥ saptadaśā ukthyā ekaviṃśo 'tirātraḥ
meaning: त्रयस्त्रिवृतो ऽग्निष्टोमास्त्रयः पञ्चदशा उक्थ्यास्त्रयः सप्तदशा उक्थ्या एकविंशो ऽतिरात्रः
text_mt: There are three trivṛt Agniṣṭomas, three fifteenfold Ukthyas, three seventeenfold Ukthyas, and a twenty-one-fold Atirātra.
The Pauṇḍarīka is an eleven-day rite with a sacrificial gift of ten thousand [cattle].
Day after day he gives thousands;
On the last [day], a thousand horses, or a hundred horses.

sanskrit_iast: tena sarvāmṛddhimṛdhnīti parameṣṭhitāṃ gacchatyabhi svargaṃ lokaṃ jayatyeṣu lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
meaning: तेन सर्वामृद्धिमृध्नीति परमेष्ठितां गच्छत्यभि स्वर्गं लोकं जयत्येषु लोकेषु प्रतितिष्ठति
text_mt: By this he attains all prosperity, reaches the highest station, conquers the heavenly world, and is established in these worlds.
An abhyāsaṅgya six-day period, a fourfold Agniṣṭoma, three chandoma days, and an Atirātra.
An abhyāsaṅgya five-day period, four chandoma days, the Mahāvrata, a Viśvajit with all pṛṣṭhas, and an Atirātra.
Now, among the unction-sacrifices (sava), the Bṛhaspatisava has been explained.
He offers the seven oblations beginning with the Agni-oblation.
A dappled two-year-old heifer dedicated to the Maruts is seized.

sanskrit_iast: tasyāḥ purastātsviṣṭakṛto yajamānāyatana ṛṣabhacarma prācīnagrīvamuttaralomāstīrya tasminnāsīnaṃ yajamānaṃ dadhnābhiṣiñcati
meaning: तस्याः पुरस्तात्स्विष्टकृतो यजमानायतन ऋषभचर्म प्राचीनग्रीवमुत्तरलोमास्तीर्य तस्मिन्नासीनं यजमानं दध्नाभिषिञ्चति
text_mt: Before the sviṣṭakṛt of it, having spread out a bull's hide in the sacrificer's place with its neck pointing eastward and its hairy side upward, he consecrates the sacrificer sitting upon it with sour milk.
A brāhmaṇa desiring spiritual splendour [performs the following]:
He offers the eight oblations beginning with the Agni-oblation.

sanskrit_iast: purastātsviṣṭakṛto hiraṇyena ghṛtamutpūya tena kṛṣṇājina āsīnamabhiṣiñcati
meaning: पुरस्तात्स्विष्टकृतो हिरण्येन घृतमुत्पूय तेन कृष्णाजिन आसीनमभिषिञ्चति
text_mt: Before the sviṣṭakṛt, having purified ghee by means of gold, he consecrates him sitting upon a black-antelope skin with it.
Whatever belongs to the Rājasūya, except for the soma [sacrifice], all that takes place.
Having concluded the Maitrābārhaspatya [oblation], he seizes a barren cow who has brought forth once, dedicated to Soma.

sanskrit_iast: tasyāḥ purastātsviṣṭakṛto 'ṣāḍhaṃ yutsu pṛtanāsu paprimiti saumyarcādbhirabhiṣiñcati
meaning: तस्याः पुरस्तात्स्विष्टकृतो ऽषाढं युत्सु पृतनासु पप्रिमिति सौम्यर्चाद्भिरभिषिञ्चति
text_mt: Before the sviṣṭakṛt of it, he consecrates him with water with the verse addressed to Soma: 'Unconquered in battles, filling in fights…'

sanskrit_iast: śeṣaṃ saṃsthāpya saṃsṛpāṃ havirbhirdiśāmaveṣṭyā dvipaśunā paśubandhena sātyadūtānāṃ havirbhiḥ prayujāmiti yajate
meaning: शेषं संस्थाप्य संसृपां हविर्भिर्दिशामवेष्ट्या द्विपशुना पशुबन्धेन सात्यदूतानां हविर्भिः प्रयुजामिति यजते
text_mt: Having concluded the remainder, he sacrifices with the oblations of the Saṃsṛps, with the Diśāmaveṣṭi, with the animal sacrifice of two victims, and with the oblations of the Sātyadūtas [known as] the Prayujs.
One desiring cattle [sacrifices] with the Pṛthisava.
Whatever belongs to the Rājasūya that does not involve the high altar, all that takes place.

sanskrit_iast: maitrābārhaspatyasya purastātsviṣṭakṛto ye me pañcāśatamiti nārāśaṃsyarcādbhirabhiṣiñcati
meaning: मैत्राबार्हस्पत्यस्य पुरस्तात्स्विष्टकृतो ये मे पञ्चाशतमिति नाराशंस्यर्चाद्भिरभिषिञ्चति
text_mt: Before the sviṣṭakṛt of the Maitrābārhaspatya [oblation], he consecrates him with water with the praise verse of men: 'Those who fifty to me…'
The subsequent [procedure] is identical with the previous one, with the omission of the animal sacrifice.
One desiring food [sacrifices] with the Odanasava.
He sacrifices under the Rohiṇī constellation; he cooks [the mess of rice] at dawn.

sanskrit_iast: udita āditye siṃhe vyāghra iti catasra āhutīrodanāddhutvā rāḍasi virāḍasītyetaiḥ pratimantram
meaning: उदित आदित्ये सिंहे व्याघ्र इति चतस्र आहुतीरोदनाद्धुत्वा राडसि विराडसीत्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रम्
text_mt: When the sun has risen, having offered four oblations from the mess of rice with the formula 'A lion, a tiger…', [he consecrates him] with these [formulas] verse by verse: 'You are a sovereign; you are an all-ruler…'

sanskrit_iast: ājyamanthaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ payomanthaṃ rājanyo dadhimanthaṃ vaiśya udamanthaṃ śūdraḥ
meaning: आज्यमन्थं ब्राह्मणः पयोमन्थं राजन्यो दधिमन्थं वैश्य उदमन्थं शूद्रः
text_mt: The brāhmaṇa [prepares] a mash with ghee, the rājanya a mash with milk, the vaiśya a mash with sour milk, and the śūdra a mash with water.

sanskrit_iast: indrāya tvā tejasvate tejasvantaṃ śrīṇāmīti brāhmaṇaḥ saktubhirājyaṃ śrītvā tejo 'sītyabhimantrya tatte prayacchāmīti yajamānāya prayacchati
meaning: इन्द्राय त्वा तेजस्वते तेजस्वन्तं श्रीणामीति ब्राह्मणः सक्तुभिराज्यं श्रीत्वा तेजो ऽसीत्यभिमन्त्र्य तत्ते प्रयच्छामीति यजमानाय प्रयच्छति
text_mt: With the formula 'For Indra endowed with splendour, I mix you endowed with splendour', the brāhmaṇa, having mixed the ghee with barley-groats and addressed it with 'You are splendour', hands it to the sacrificer with 'That I offer to you.'
Having received it with 'Let my mouth be endowed with splendour', he consumes it.

meaning: एवमितरेषामुत्तरौत्तरः श्रयणो ऽभिमन्त्रणः प्रदानो भक्षणश्च यथालिङ्गम्
text_mt: In this way for the others, the mixing, addressing, handing over, and consuming are done one after another according to their distinctive marks.
Having consumed them all, the sacrificer gives gold to the brāhmaṇa;
A bow with three arrows to the rājanya;
A leather-bag water-pot to the śūdra.
The sacrificer eats the remainder of the mess of rice.
He addresses him while eating with: 'O Agni, make this man [long-lived] for life, for splendour.'
He fastens gold onto the sacrificer.
While it is being fastened, he murmurs: 'You are life, you are all-life.'

sanskrit_iast: apāṃ grahāngṛhṇanti ye manthānkalpayantyapāṃ yo dravaṇe rasa ityetaiḥ pratimantram
meaning: अपां ग्रहान्गृह्णन्ति ये मन्थान्कल्पयन्त्यपां यो द्रवणे रस इत्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रम्
text_mt: Those who prepare the mashes draw draughts of water, each with one of these formulas: 'The juice of the waters which runs in the current…'

sanskrit_iast: tairenaṃ saṃsṛṣṭairabhiṣiñcati yato vāto manojavā iti
meaning: तैरेनं संसृष्टैरभिषिञ्चति यतो वातो मनोजवा इति
text_mt: With them combined, he consecrates him with: 'From where the wind, swift as thought…'
Having addressed him with 'You are like an ocean, unfathomable', he then purifies him with three clusters of darbha grass.
'It serves as a substitute for the final bath,' so it is known.
In front of the āhavanīya, a chariot stands ready.
The sacrificer approaches it with: 'Come forward.'
He addresses him as he mounts it with: 'Mount, O augmenter of friends!'
With 'The two curved pins, the two lower pins…' he touches the two chariot wheels,
When he has mounted, [he addresses him] with five [verses beginning with]: 'Mount, O slayer of Vṛtra!'

sanskrit_iast: didṛkṣeṇyo darśanīyo bhavati ya etena yajata iti vijñāyate
meaning: दिदृक्षेण्यो दर्शनीयो भवति य एतेन यजत इति विज्ञायते
text_mt: 'He who sacrifices with this becomes worthy of being seen and handsome,' so it is known.
The Odanasava is concluded.
The Pañcaśāradīya has been explained.
"asyājarāso 'gna āyūṃṣi pavase" for the [draught] for Indra and Vāyu.
The second for the [draught] for Mitra and Varuṇa.
The fourth and fifth for the Śukra and Manthin [draughts]; the sixth for the Āgrayaṇa [draught].
He employs another, dedicated to Agni, for the Ukthya [draught].
He employs [another] for the [draughts] for Indra-and-Agni and for the Viśvedevas.
"agniśriyaḥ"—[these] three are for the Marutvatīya [draughts].
"śrudhi śrutkarṇa"—the next is for the Mahendra [draught].
"viśveṣāmaditiḥ"—[these] three are for the Āditya draught.
He employs [another] for the Vaiśvadeva [draught].
He employs [another] for the Hāriyojana [draught].
One desirous of power of the senses or desirous of virility should sacrifice with the Indrastut, [which is] an Ukthya with the Indrastoma.
"tiṣṭhā harī kasya vṛṣā" for the [draught] for Indra and Vāyu.
The third for the [draught] for Mitra and Varuṇa.
The fifth and sixth for the Śukra and Manthin [draughts].
He employs [another] for the Dhruva, Aindrāgna, and Vaiśvadeva [draughts].
The regular ones are for the Marutvatīya and Mahendra [draughts].
"ā no viśvābhirūtibhiḥ"—[these] three are for the Āditya draught.
He employs [another] for the Vaiśvadeva and Pātnīvata [draughts].

sanskrit_iast: rājābhiṣekṣyamāṇo janapadeṣu samaveteṣu dvayoḥ puṇyāhayoḥ pūrvasminsthaṇḍilaṃ kalpayitvāgnimupasamādhāya saṃparistīrya vasati
meaning: राजाभिषेक्ष्यमाणो जनपदेषु समवेतेषु द्वयोः पुण्याहयोः पूर्वस्मिन्स्थण्डिलं कल्पयित्वाग्निमुपसमाधाय संपरिस्तीर्य वसति
text_mt: A king who is to be consecrated, when the people of the realm have assembled, on the earlier of two auspicious days, having prepared a raised mound, having added fuel to the fire, and having strewn [grass] around it, stays [there for the night].

sanskrit_iast: udita āditye ye keśino narte brahmaṇa iti dve āhutī hutvā rāḍasi virāḍasīti yajamānāyatana audumbarīmāsandīṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati
meaning: उदित आदित्ये ये केशिनो नर्ते ब्रह्मण इति द्वे आहुती हुत्वा राडसि विराडसीति यजमानायतन औदुम्बरीमासन्दीं प्रतिष्ठापयति
text_mt: When the sun has risen, having offered two oblations with "ye keśinaḥ" and "narte brahmaṇaḥ", he sets up an udumbara throne in the sacrificer's place with "rāḍasi virāḍasi".
With "āroha proṣṭham" he addresses him as he mounts.
Sitting on it, he has his hair shaved with "yenāvapatsavitā kṣureṇa".
With "mā te keśān" he addresses the hair as it is being scattered.
Having gathered them together, he places them in a clump of darbha grass with "tebhyo nidhānam".
Then he anoints him with milk mixed with clarified butter
his two arms with "balaṃ te bāhuvoh"

sanskrit_iast: vyāghro 'yamagnāviti saptāhutīrhutvā dyaurasi pṛthivyasīti yajamānāyatane śārdūlacarma prācīnagrīvamuttaralomāstṛṇāti
meaning: व्याघ्रो ऽयमग्नाविति सप्ताहुतीर्हुत्वा द्यौरसि पृथिव्यसीति यजमानायतने शार्दूलचर्म प्राचीनग्रीवमुत्तरलोमास्तृणाति
text_mt: Having offered seven oblations with "vyāghro 'yamagnau", he spreads a tiger skin with the neck to the east and the hair side up in the sacrificer's place with "dyaurasi pṛthivyasi".
With "vyāghro vaiyyāghraḥ" he addresses him as he sits.

sanskrit_iast: athainaṃ tokmāvāstābhirdūrvāvāstābhirvādbhirabhiṣiñcati yā divyā āpa iti pratipadyā pāṅktāt
meaning: अथैनं तोक्मावास्ताभिर्दूर्वावास्ताभिर्वाद्भिरभिषिञ्चति या दिव्या आप इति प्रतिपद्या पाङ्क्तात्
text_mt: Then he sprinkles him with water containing green barley sprouts or water containing dūrvā grass, beginning with "yā divyā āpaḥ" down to the end of the pāṅkta verse.

sanskrit_iast: aruṇaṃ tvā vṛkamityenamabhimantrya pra bāhaveti bāhū prasāryendrasya te vīryakṛta ityupāvaharati
meaning: अरुणं त्वा वृकमित्येनमभिमन्त्र्य प्र बाहवेति बाहू प्रसार्येन्द्रस्य ते वीर्यकृत इत्युपावहरति
text_mt: Having addressed him with "aruṇaṃ tvā vṛkam", having extended his two arms with "pra bāhava", he brings them down with "indrasya te vīryakṛte".
A chariot stands placed in front of the fire.
The king goes towards it with "abhi prehī".
With "ātiṣṭha vṛtrahantama" he addresses him as he mounts.
With "aṅkau nyaṅkau" he touches the two chariot wheels
With "namasta ṛṣe" he addresses the royal chaplain.
With "tiṣṭhā rathe" [he addresses] the charioteer.
With "ā raśmīn" he takes hold of the reins.
With the six [verses] beginning with "ātiṣṭha vṛtrahan" [he addresses him] when he has mounted.
Having made him recite the two [verses] beginning with "pari mā senyāḥ" and having addressed him with the next three, he makes him look up at the sun with "udasāvetu".
With "annavatām" he surveys the people of the realm.
The royal consecration concludes.
The savas are concluded; the savas [are concluded].
Up to twenty-four [persons] may sit [for] a sattra.

sanskrit_iast: teṣāṃ dvādaśāhena sattrabhūtena kalpo vyākhyāto yāni purastātsaṃvatsarāt /
meaning: तेषां द्वादशाहेन सत्त्रभूतेन कल्पो व्याख्यातो यानि पुरस्तात्संवत्सरात् /
text_mt: For those [sattras] which are before [i.e. shorter than] a year, the procedure is explained by the Dvādaśāha in its form as a sattra;
There are Atirātras on both ends [of them],

sanskrit_iast: tṛtīyaṃ pañcadaśarātraṃ parihāpya kuṇḍapāyināṃ ca sattram
meaning: तृतीयं पञ्चदशरात्रं परिहाप्य कुण्डपायिनां च सत्त्रम्
text_mt: with the exception of the third fifteen-day rite (Pañcadaśarātra) and the sattra of the Kuṇḍapāyins.

sanskrit_iast: ṛtūnāmekādaśarātreṇa prajāṃ sṛjante prajāmavarundhate prajāṃ vindante prajāvanto bhavanti
meaning: ऋतूनामेकादशरात्रेण प्रजां सृजन्ते प्रजामवरुन्धते प्रजां विन्दन्ते प्रजावन्तो भवन्ति
text_mt: By means of the eleven-day rite (Ekādaśarātra) of the seasons, they generate offspring, secure offspring, obtain offspring, and become possessors of offspring.
[Its order is:] an Atirātra, a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, three Chandomas, [and] an Atirātra.
Whatever desire they desire, that they obtain.

meaning: अतिरात्रः पृष्ठ्यः षडहः सर्वस्तोमो ऽतिरात्रश्चत्वारश्छन्दोमा अतिरात्रः
text_mt: [The first has:] an Atirātra, a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, a Sarvastoma Atirātra, four Chandomas, [and] an Atirātra.
Those desirous of spiritual lustre should undertake the second.
[Its order is:] an Atirātra, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.
There are three fourteen-day rites (Caturdaśarātras).
Whatever desire they desire, that they obtain.

sanskrit_iast: atirātraḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaha āvṛttaḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tirātraḥ
meaning: अतिरात्रः पृष्ठ्यः षडह आवृत्तः पृष्ठ्यः षडहो ऽतिरात्रः
text_mt: [The first has:] an Atirātra, a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, a reversed Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, [and] an Atirātra.

sanskrit_iast: dvitīyaṃ yāṃstalpa udake vivāhe vā mīmāṃseran
meaning: द्वितीयं यांस्तल्प उदके विवाहे वा मीमांसेरन्
text_mt: Those regarding whom people might question regarding bed, water, or marriage should undertake the second.
[Its order is:] two Atirātras, a three-day rite of Jyotis, Gauḥ, and Āyus, a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, Āyus, Gauḥ, Jyotis, [and] an Atirātra.
Those desirous of prosperity should undertake the third.
[Its order is:] an Atirātra, the Gauḥ and Āyus [days], the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, [and] an Atirātra.
There are four fifteen-day rites (Pañcadaśarātras).
On the new moon is the opening day (prāyaṇīya); on the eighth day is the Mahāvrata; on the full moon is the concluding day (udayanīya);

sanskrit_iast: atirātraḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho mahāvratamāvṛttaḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tirātraḥ
meaning: अतिरात्रः पृष्ठ्यः षडहो महाव्रतमावृत्तः पृष्ठ्यः षडहो ऽतिरात्रः
text_mt: [The first has:] an Atirātra, a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, the Mahāvrata, a reversed Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, [and] an Atirātra.
Those desirous of spiritual lustre should undertake the second.
[Its order is:] an Atirātra, the Trivṛt-Agniṣṭut, a three-day rite of Jyotis, Gauḥ, and Āyus, a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, Āyus, Gauḥ, Jyotis, [and] an Atirātra.
By means of the third they secure both desires: that which is in a sattra and that which is in an ahīna.
[Its order is:] the Trivṛt-Agniṣṭut, a three-day rite of Jyotis, Gauḥ, and Āyus, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, [and] an Atirātra.
By means of the fourth they propagate indeed with offspring and cattle.
[Its order is:] an Atirātra, a three-day rite of Jyotis, Gauḥ, and Āyus, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, [and] an Atirātra.
Those desirous of vigor should undertake the sixteen-day rite (Ṣoḍaśarātra) dedicated to Indra.
Those desirous of food should undertake the seventeen-day rite (Saptadaśarātra).
[Its order is:] an Atirātra, a five-day rite of Jyotis, Gauḥ, Āyus, Gauḥ, and Āyus, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, [and] an Atirātra.
Those desirous of cattle should undertake the eighteen-day rite (Aṣṭādaśarātra).
[Its order is:] an Atirātra, an Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, [and] an Atirātra.
By means of the nineteen-day rite (Ekānnaviṃśatirātra) they propagate with offspring and cattle.
By means of the twenty-day rite (Viṃśatirātra) they become endowed with spiritual lustre and eaters of food.

meaning: अतिरात्रो ऽभिप्लवः षडहो ऽभिजिद्विश्वजितौ द्वादशाहस्य दशाहान्यतिरात्रः
text_mt: [Its order is:] an Atirātra, an Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, the Abhijit and Viśvajit, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, [and] an Atirātra.
There are two twenty-one-day rites (Ekaviṃśatirātras).
Whatever desire they desire, that they obtain.
[The first has:] an Atirātra, an Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, an Atirātra, two Abhiplavas, [and] an Atirātra.
Those desirous of spiritual lustre should undertake the second.
A victim dedicated to Soma and Pūṣan is to be seized.
The verses of Manu are the kindling verses (sāmidhenīs).

sanskrit_iast: atirātraḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍahastrayaḥ svarasāmāno divākīrtyamahastrayaḥ svarasāmāna āvṛttaḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tirātraḥ
meaning: अतिरात्रः पृष्ठ्यः षडहस्त्रयः स्वरसामानो दिवाकीर्त्यमहस्त्रयः स्वरसामान आवृत्तः पृष्ठ्यः षडहो ऽतिरात्रः
text_mt: [Its order is:] an Atirātra, a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, three Svarasāmans, the Divākīrtya day, three Svarasāmans, a reversed Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, [and] an Atirātra.
By means of the twenty-two-day rite (Dvāviṃśatirātra) they secure food from the year, from these worlds, and from that sun.

sanskrit_iast: atirātro jyotirgaurāyustryaho 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvratamatirātraśca
meaning: अतिरात्रो ज्योतिर्गौरायुस्त्र्यहो ऽभिप्लवः षडहो द्वादशाहस्य दशाहानि महाव्रतमतिरात्रश्च
text_mt: [Its order is:] an Atirātra, a three-day rite of Jyotis, Gauḥ, and Āyus, an Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.
Those desirous of cattle should undertake the twenty-three-day rite (Trayoviṃśatirātra).

meaning: अतिरात्रो ज्योतिर्गौरायुर्गौरायुःपञ्चाहो ऽभिप्लवः षडहो द्वादशाहस्य दशाहान्यतिरात्रः
text_mt: [Its order is:] an Atirātra, a five-day rite of Jyotis, Gauḥ, Āyus, Gauḥ, and Āyus, an Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, [and] an Atirātra.
There are two twenty-four-day rites (Caturviṃśatirātras).
Whatever desire they desire, that they obtain.
[The first has:] an Atirātra, two Abhiplavas, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, [and] an Atirātra.
By means of the twenty-four-day rite known as the Saṃsad they sit in the heavenly world.

sanskrit_iast: atirātraścaturviṃśa ukthya ārambhaṇīyastrivṛdvā pṛṣṭhyastomaḥ ṣaḍahastrayastriṃśamaharaniruktaṃ trayastriṃśaṃ niruktaṃ triṇavaṃ dve ekaviṃśe triṇavaṃ trayastriṃśamaharniruktaṃ trayastriṃśamaniruktaṃ pṛṣṭhyastomaḥ ṣaḍahaḥ pratyaṅ trivṛdaharaniruktmā jyotiṣṭomo vaiśvānaro 'tirātraḥ
meaning: अतिरात्रश्चतुर्विंश उक्थ्य आरम्भणीयस्त्रिवृद्वा पृष्ठ्यस्तोमः षडहस्त्रयस्त्रिंशमहरनिरुक्तं त्रयस्त्रिंशं निरुक्तं त्रिणवं द्वे एकविंशे त्रिणवं त्रयस्त्रिंशमहर्निरुक्तं त्रयस्त्रिंशमनिरुक्तं पृष्ठ्यस्तोमः षडहः प्रत्यङ् त्रिवृदहरनिरुक्त्मा ज्योतिष्टोमो वैश्वानरो ऽतिरात्रः
text_mt: [Its order is:] an Atirātra, an introductory Ukthya day of twenty-four parts, or [a Trivṛt day], a Pṛṣṭhya-stoma ṣaḍaha, an unexpressed thirty-three-part day, an expressed thirty-three-part day, a twenty-seven-part [day], two twenty-one-part [days], a twenty-seven-part [day], an expressed thirty-three-part day, an unexpressed thirty-three-part day, a Pṛṣṭhya-stoma ṣaḍaha, an unexpressed reverse Trivṛt day, a Jyotiṣṭoma, a Vaiśvānara [day], [and] an Atirātra.
Those desirous of cattle should undertake the twenty-five-day rite (Pañcaviṃśatirātra).
[The twenty-five-night rite consists of:] an Atirātra, two Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.
Those desiring heaven should undertake the twenty-six-night rite.
[It consists of:] an Atirātra, the Go and Āyus days, two Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.
Those desiring proper food should undertake the twenty-seven-night rite.
[It consists of:] an Atirātra, the three-day rite of Jyotis, Go, and Āyus, two Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.
Those desiring cattle should undertake the twenty-eight-night rite.
By means of the twenty-nine-night rite, they win boundless prosperity.
[It consists of:] an Atirātra, the five-day rite of Jyotis, Go, Āyus, Go, and Āyus, two Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.
Those desiring proper food should undertake the thirty-night rite.
[It consists of:] an Atirātra, three Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.
Those desiring proper food should undertake the thirty-one-night rite.
Those desiring firm standing should undertake the thirty-two-night rite.

meaning: अतिरात्रो गोआयुषी त्रयो ऽभिप्लवा द्वादशाहस्य दशाहान्यतिरात्रः
text_mt: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, the Go and Āyus days, three Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.
There are three thirty-three-night rites.
Whatever desire they desire, that they obtain.

sanskrit_iast: atirātrastrayaḥ pañcāhā viśvajidatirātra ekaḥ pañcāho dvādaśāhasya daśāhānyatirātraḥ
meaning: अतिरात्रस्त्रयः पञ्चाहा विश्वजिदतिरात्र एकः पञ्चाहो द्वादशाहस्य दशाहान्यतिरात्रः
text_mt: [The first consists of:] an Atirātra, three five-day rites, a Viśvajit Atirātra, one five-day rite, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.
Those desiring spiritual splendor should undertake the second [thirty-three-night rite].

sanskrit_iast: atirātro 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tirātro 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tirātre 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvratamatirātraśca
meaning: अतिरात्रो ऽभिप्लवः षडहो ऽतिरात्रो ऽभिप्लवः षडहो ऽतिरात्रे ऽभिप्लवः षडहो द्वादशाहस्य दशाहानि महाव्रतमतिरात्रश्च
text_mt: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, an Abhiplava six-day rite, an Atirātra, an Abhiplava six-day rite, an Atirātra, an Abhiplava six-day rite, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.
Those desiring prosperity should undertake the third [thirty-three-night rite].
[It consists of:] an Atirātra, three five-day rites, an Atirātra, three five-day rites, [and] an Atirātra.
Those desiring bodily vigor should undertake the thirty-four-night rite.

meaning: अतिरात्रो ज्योतिर्गौरायुस्त्र्यहस्त्रयो ऽभिप्लवा द्वादशाहस्य दशाहानि महाव्रतमतिरात्रश्च
text_mt: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, the three-day rite of Jyotis, Go, and Āyus, three Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.
Those desiring cattle should undertake the thirty-five-night rite.
[It consists of:] an Atirātra, the five-day rite of Jyotis, Go, Āyus, Go, and Āyus, three Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.
Those desiring heaven should undertake the thirty-six-night rite.
[It consists of:] an Atirātra, four Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.
Those desiring proper food should undertake the thirty-seven-night rite.
Those desiring cattle should undertake the thirty-eight-night rite.

meaning: अतिरात्रो गोआयुषी चत्वारो ऽभिप्लवा द्वादशाहस्य दशाहान्यतिरात्रः
text_mt: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, the Go and Āyus days, four Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.
By means of the thirty-nine-night rite, they win endless prosperity.
[It consists of:] an Atirātra, the three-day rite of Jyotis, Go, and Āyus, four Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.
By means of the forty-night rite, they firmly establish themselves in the supreme Virāj.
There are seven forty-nine-night rites [called] the Vidhṛtis.
By the first, they turn away evil [and] the rival.

sanskrit_iast: atirātrastrayastrivṛto 'gnīṣṭomā atirātro daśa pañcadaśā ukthyāḥ ṣoḍaśimaddaśamamaharatirātro dvādaśa saptadaśā ukthyā atirātraḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tirātro dvādaśaikaviṃśā ukthyā atirātraḥ
meaning: अतिरात्रस्त्रयस्त्रिवृतो ऽग्नीष्टोमा अतिरात्रो दश पञ्चदशा उक्थ्याः षोडशिमद्दशममहरतिरात्रो द्वादश सप्तदशा उक्थ्या अतिरात्रः पृष्ठ्यः षडहो ऽतिरात्रो द्वादशैकविंशा उक्थ्या अतिरात्रः
text_mt: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, three trivṛt Agniṣṭomas, an Atirātra, ten fifteen-verse Ukthyas with the tenth day having the Ṣoḍaśin, an Atirātra, twelve seventeen-verse Ukthyas, an Atirātra, a Pṛṣṭhya six-day rite, an Atirātra, twelve twenty-one-verse Ukthyas, [and] an Atirātra.

sanskrit_iast: yamevaiṣāṃ śrīrbhavati mitraśca varuṇaśca dhātā cāryamā cāṃśaśca bhagaścendraśca vivasvāṃścaitāsāṃ devatānāmṛddhimṛdhnuvanti
meaning: यमेवैषां श्रीर्भवति मित्रश्च वरुणश्च धाता चार्यमा चांशश्च भगश्चेन्द्रश्च विवस्वांश्चैतासां देवतानामृद्धिमृध्नुवन्ति
text_mt: Restrained indeed is their prosperity; Mitra, Varuṇa, Dhātṛ, Aryaman, Aṃśa, Bhaga, Indra, and Vivasvat—they prosper with the prosperity of these deities.

sanskrit_iast: atirātro dvāvabhiplavau goāyuṣī dvāvabhiplavāvabhijidviśvajiccātirātrāveko 'bhiplavaḥ sarvastomo navasapatadaśaścātirātrau dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvratamatirātraśca
meaning: अतिरात्रो द्वावभिप्लवौ गोआयुषी द्वावभिप्लवावभिजिद्विश्वजिच्चातिरात्रावेको ऽभिप्लवः सर्वस्तोमो नवसपतदशश्चातिरात्रौ द्वादशाहस्य दशाहानि महाव्रतमतिरात्रश्च
text_mt: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, two Abhiplavas, the Go and Āyus days, two Abhiplavas, the Abhijit and Viśvajit as Atirātras, one Abhiplava, the Sarvastoma and the seventeen-day rite as Atirātras, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.
The third is the Āñjanābhyañjana.

meaning: यान्न जानीयुर्यदा चाञ्जते ऽभि चाञ्जते जानान्त्येनाम् /
text_mt: [Those] whom they might not know, when they salve and anoint themselves, they know them.
They place beauty in themselves.

sanskrit_iast: gaulgulavena prātaḥsavane saugandhikena mādhyaṃdine pautudraveṇa tṛtīyasavane
meaning: गौल्गुलवेन प्रातःसवने सौगन्धिकेन माध्यंदिने पौतुद्रवेण तृतीयसवने
text_mt: [They salve and anoint] with bdellium ointment at the morning pressing, with sweet-scented ointment at the midday pressing, and with deodar ointment at the third pressing.

meaning: अतिरात्रश्चत्वारो ऽभिप्लवाः सर्वस्तोमो ऽतिरात्रो द्वावभिप्लवौ द्वादशाहस्य दशाहान्यतिरात्रः
text_mt: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, four Abhiplavas, a Sarvastoma Atirātra, two Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.
The fourth is the Saṃvatsarasammita.
They prosper with the prosperity of the year.

sanskrit_iast: atirātraścaturviṃśa ukthya ārambhaṇīyastrivṛdvā trayo 'bhiplavā abhijittrayaḥ svarasāmāno divākīrtyamahastrayaḥ svarasāmāno viśvajideko 'bhiplava āvṛtta āyurgaurdvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvratamatirātraśca
meaning: अतिरात्रश्चतुर्विंश उक्थ्य आरम्भणीयस्त्रिवृद्वा त्रयो ऽभिप्लवा अभिजित्त्रयः स्वरसामानो दिवाकीर्त्यमहस्त्रयः स्वरसामानो विश्वजिदेको ऽभिप्लव आवृत्त आयुर्गौर्द्वादशाहस्य दशाहानि महाव्रतमतिरात्रश्च
text_mt: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, a twenty-four-verse Ukthya introductory day or a trivṛt day, three Abhiplavas, the Abhijit, three Svarasāman days, the Divākīrtya day, three Svarasāman days, the Viśvajit, one reversed Abhiplava, the Āyus and Go days, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.
The fifth is the Savituḥ Kakubhaḥ.
They attain the instigation of all proper food.

sanskrit_iast: atirātro nava trivṛntyahānyagniṣṭomamukhaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tha yāti trīṇyagniṣṭomāvabhita ukthyaṃ madhye tathaiva nava pañcadaśāni tathaiva nava saptadaśāni tatahiva navaikaviṃśāni dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvratamatirātraśca
meaning: अतिरात्रो नव त्रिवृन्त्यहान्यग्निष्टोममुखः षडहो ऽथ याति त्रीण्यग्निष्टोमावभित उक्थ्यं मध्ये तथैव नव पञ्चदशानि तथैव नव सप्तदशानि ततहिव नवैकविंशानि द्वादशाहस्य दशाहानि महाव्रतमतिरात्रश्च
text_mt: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, nine trivṛt days: a six-day rite beginning with an Agniṣṭoma, then it proceeds with three days having Agniṣṭomas on both sides and an Ukthya in the middle; likewise nine fifteen-verse days, likewise nine seventeen-verse days, likewise nine twenty-one-verse days, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.
Those desiring firm standing should undertake the sixth.

meaning: अतिरात्रश्चत्वारो ऽभिप्लवा महाव्रतं द्वावभिप्लवौ द्वादशाहस्य दशाहान्यतिरात्रः
text_mt: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, four Abhiplavas, the Mahāvrata, two Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.
By the seventh, they surpass other creatures [and] become most vigorous.
[It consists of:] an Atirātra, six Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.
Those desiring prosperity should undertake the sixty-one-night rite.

sanskrit_iast: deva varuṇa devayajanaṃ me dehīti devayajanamadhyavasāya juhoti
meaning: देव वरुण देवयजनं मे देहीति देवयजनमध्यवसाय जुहोति
text_mt: Having decided upon the place of sacrificial worship with the formula, 'O divine Varuṇa, grant me the place of sacrificial worship,' he offers an oblation.

sanskrit_iast: atirātraścaturviṃśa ukthya ārambhaṇīyastrivṛdvā pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍahastrayo 'bhiplavā abhijittrayaḥ svarasāmāno divākīrtyamahastrayaḥ svarasāmāno viśvajidāvṛttaḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaha eko 'bhiplava āvṛtta āyurgaurdvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvratamatirātraśca
meaning: अतिरात्रश्चतुर्विंश उक्थ्य आरम्भणीयस्त्रिवृद्वा पृष्ठ्यः षडहस्त्रयो ऽभिप्लवा अभिजित्त्रयः स्वरसामानो दिवाकीर्त्यमहस्त्रयः स्वरसामानो विश्वजिदावृत्तः पृष्ठ्यः षडह एको ऽभिप्लव आवृत्त आयुर्गौर्द्वादशाहस्य दशाहानि महाव्रतमतिरात्रश्च
text_mt: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, a twenty-four-verse Ukthya introductory day or a trivṛt day, a Pṛṣṭhya six-day rite, three Abhiplavas, the Abhijit, three Svarasāman days, the Divākīrtya day, three Svarasāman days, the Viśvajit, a reversed Pṛṣṭhya six-day rite, one reversed Abhiplava, the Āyus and Go days, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.
By means of the Hundred-night sacrifice of the gods they attain full life and become wealthier.
An atirātra, the Jyotis-Gauḥ-Āyus three-day period, fourteen abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day sacrifice, the Mahāvrata, and an atirātra.
They press [the soma] moving forward, or at the same place.

sanskrit_iast: ādityānāmayanena prajātiṃ bhūmānaṃ gacchantyabhi svargaṃ lokaṃ jayantyeṣu lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhanti
meaning: आदित्यानामयनेन प्रजातिं भूमानं गच्छन्त्यभि स्वर्गं लोकं जयन्त्येषु लोकेषु प्रतितिष्ठन्ति
text_mt: By means of the Course of the Ādityas they attain offspring and abundance, conquer heaven, and establish themselves in these worlds.
It is explained by the Course of the Cows.
The months are trivṛt and pañcadaśa, with the pṛṣṭhya in the middle.
In place of the abhijit is the trivṛt Bṛhaspatisava;
in place of the viśvajit is the pañcadaśa ukthya Indrastoma.

sanskrit_iast: tasmādanantaraṃ pṛṣṭhyābhiplavāvupetya dvādaśāhīyasya daśarātrasya vyūḍhā agniṣṭomāstrivṛtaḥ
meaning: तस्मादनन्तरं पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवावुपेत्य द्वादशाहीयस्य दशरात्रस्य व्यूढा अग्निष्टोमास्त्रिवृतः
text_mt: Next after it, having undertaken a pṛṣṭhya and an abhiplava, of the ten-day period belonging to the twelve-day sacrifice, the agniṣṭomas are rearranged as trivṛt.
With the udbhid and valabhid, thus the month deficient by two days is completed.

sanskrit_iast: āyuṣaṃ gāṃ copetya chandomadaśarātraḥ pratyaṅṅaṣṭācatvāriṃśaṃ catuścatvāriṃśaṃ catvāriṃśaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśaṃ dvātriṃśaṃ triṃśaṃ dve aṣṭāviṃśe pañcaviṃśaṃ caturviṃśam
meaning: आयुषं गां चोपेत्य छन्दोमदशरात्रः प्रत्यङ्ङष्टाचत्वारिंशं चतुश्चत्वारिंशं चत्वारिंशं षट्त्रिंशं द्वात्रिंशं त्रिंशं द्वे अष्टाविंशे पञ्चविंशं चतुर्विंशम्
text_mt: And having undertaken the āyus and gauḥ, the Chandoma ten-day period is in reverse order: a forty-eight-versed, a forty-four-versed, a forty-versed, a thirty-six-versed, a thirty-two-versed, a thirty-versed, two twenty-eight-versed, a twenty-five-versed, and a twenty-four-versed.
With the Mahāvrata and the concluding [atirātra], thus the month deficient by two days is completed.
By this, the Course of the Aṅgirases is explained.
The months have the pṛṣṭhyas before, prior to the viṣuvant;
above the viṣuvant, they have the pṛṣṭhyas after, being pañcadaśa.

sanskrit_iast: chandomadaśarātra ūrdhvastomaścaturviṃśaṃ pañcaviṃśaṃ dve aṣṭāviṃśe triṃśaṃ dvātriṃśaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśaṃ catvāriṃśaṃ catuścatvāriṃśamaṣṭācatvāriṃśam
meaning: छन्दोमदशरात्र ऊर्ध्वस्तोमश्चतुर्विंशं पञ्चविंशं द्वे अष्टाविंशे त्रिंशं द्वात्रिंशं षट्त्रिंशं चत्वारिंशं चतुश्चत्वारिंशमष्टाचत्वारिंशम्
text_mt: The Chandoma ten-day period is in ascending order of stomas: a twenty-four-versed, a twenty-five-versed, two twenty-eight-versed, a thirty-versed, a thirty-two-versed, a thirty-six-versed, a forty-versed, a forty-four-versed, and a forty-eight-versed.
With the Mahāvrata and the concluding [atirātra], thus the month deficient by two days is completed.
the pṛṣṭhyas and the ākṣyantis are the Course of the Ādityas, and the abhiplavas and the ākṣyantis are the Course of the Aṅgirases;
whatever is other than the pṛṣṭhyas and abhiplavas, they call those ākṣyantis.
By means of the Course of Dṛti and Vātavant they attain whatever desire they desire.

sanskrit_iast: trivṛtā māsaṃ pñcadaśena māsaṃ saptadaśena māsamekaviṃśena māsaṃ triṇavena māsaṃ trayastriṃśena māsam
meaning: त्रिवृता मासं प्ञ्चदशेन मासं सप्तदशेन मासमेकविंशेन मासं त्रिणवेन मासं त्रयस्त्रिंशेन मासम्
text_mt: A month with trivṛt, a month with pañcadaśa, a month with saptadaśa, a month with ekaviṃśa, a month with triṇava, a month with trayastriṃśa;
then the viṣuvant or the Mahāvrata;
these very same later months begin with trayastriṃśa and end with trivṛt.
In the Course of the Kuṇḍapāyins they remain consecrated for a month.
Having performed the introductory offering and purchased the king [Soma], they tie it up and lay it down.
Having performed twelve upasads, they sacrifice with the haviryajñas.
For a month they offer the agnihotra;

sanskrit_iast: māsaṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajante māsaṃ vaiśvadevena māsaṃ varuṇapraghāsairmāsaṃ sākamedhairmāsaṃ śunāsīrīyeṇa //
meaning: मासं दर्शपूर्णमासाभ्यां यजन्ते मासं वैश्वदेवेन मासं वरुणप्रघासैर्मासं साकमेधैर्मासं शुनासीरीयेण //
text_mt: for a month they sacrifice with the New and Full Moon sacrifices, for a month with the Vaiśvadeva, for a month with the Varuṇapraghāsas, for a month with the Sākamedhas, and for a month with the Śunāsīrīya.

sanskrit_iast: trivṛtā māsaṃ pañcadaśena māsaṃ saptadaśena māsamekaviṃśena māsaṃ triṇavena māsam /
meaning: त्रिवृता मासं पञ्चदशेन मासं सप्तदशेन मासमेकविंशेन मासं त्रिणवेन मासम् /
text_mt: For a month with trivṛt, for a month with pañcadaśa, for a month with saptadaśa, for a month with ekaviṃśa, for a month with triṇava;

sanskrit_iast: aṣṭādaśa trayastriṃśānyahāni dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvratamatirātraśceti dvādaśa māsāḥ
meaning: अष्टादश त्रयस्त्रिंशान्यहानि द्वादशाहस्य दशाहानि महाव्रतमतिरात्रश्चेति द्वादश मासाः
text_mt: eighteen trayastriṃśa days, the ten days of the twelve-day sacrifice, the Mahāvrata, and an atirātra—thus are the twelve months.
They become everything; they prosper with every prosperity.
They partake [of soma] with handleless goblets.

meaning: यो होता सो ऽध्वर्युः स पोता /
text_mt: He who is the hotṛ is the adhvaryu and the potṛ;

meaning: य उद्गाता स नेष्टा सो ऽच्छावाकः /
text_mt: he who is the udgātṛ is the neṣṭṛ and the acchāvāka;

sanskrit_iast: yo maitrāvaruṇaḥ sa brahmā sa pratihartā /
meaning: यो मैत्रावरुणः स ब्रह्मा स प्रतिहर्ता /
text_mt: he who is the maitrāvaruṇa is the brahman and the pratihartṛ;

sanskrit_iast: yaḥ prastotā sa brāhmaṇācchaṃsī sa grāvastut /
meaning: यः प्रस्तोता स ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी स ग्रावस्तुत् /
text_mt: he who is the prastotṛ is the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin and the grāvastut;
he who is the pratiprasthātṛ is the agnīdh and the unnetṛ;
the subrahmaṇya is the subrahmaṇya.
Those desiring heaven should undertake the Course of the Tapaścits.
He offers [libations] for four months each with one upasad mantra.
Following each upasad he piles the fire altar.
Each layer takes two months;
Milk from four teats, from three teats, from two teats, and from one teat—thus are the fast milks for three months each.
By means of the Twelve-Year sacrifice of Prajāpati they prosper with the prosperity of Prajāpati.
Three trivṛt years, three pañcadaśa, three saptadaśa, and three ekaviṃśa.
Those desiring heaven should undertake this very same [course] of the Naimiṣīyas.

sanskrit_iast: nava trivṛtaḥ saṃvatsarā nava pañcadaśā nava saptadaśā navikaviṃśāḥ śāktyānāṃ ṣaṭtriṃśatsaṃvatsaraṃ tarasapuroḍāśaṃ kāpyādhvaryavamāgastyagṛhapatikam
meaning: नव त्रिवृतः संवत्सरा नव पञ्चदशा नव सप्तदशा नविकविंशाः शाक्त्यानां षट्त्रिंशत्संवत्सरं तरसपुरोडाशं काप्याध्वर्यवमागस्त्यगृहपतिकम्
text_mt: Nine trivṛt years, nine pañcadaśa, nine saptadaśa, and nine ekaviṃśa belong to the thirty-six-year sacrifice of the Śāktyas, having flesh cakes, Kāpya as adhvaryu, and Agastya as householder.
As each day concludes, the householder goes hunting.

sanskrit_iast: sa yānmṛgānhanti teṣāṃ tarasāḥ puroḍāśā bhavanti
meaning: स यान्मृगान्हन्ति तेषां तरसाः पुरोडाशा भवन्ति
text_mt: The flesh of the wild beasts he slays becomes the sacrificial cakes.

sanskrit_iast: etena ha vai śāktyo gaurivītistarasapuroḍāśa ārdhnoddevaloke ca manuṣyaloke carddhimṛdhnuvanti
meaning: एतेन ह वै शाक्त्यो गौरिवीतिस्तरसपुरोडाश आर्ध्नोद्देवलोके च मनुष्यलोके चर्द्धिमृध्नुवन्ति
text_mt: By means of this indeed, Gaurīvīti Śāktya prospered with the meat-cake [sacrifice]; and they prosper with prosperity in the world of the gods and in the world of men.

sanskrit_iast: pañcaviṃśatistrivṛtaḥ saṃvatsarāḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ pañcadaśāḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ saptadaśāḥ pañcaviṃśatirekaviṃśāḥ
meaning: पञ्चविंशतिस्त्रिवृतः संवत्सराः पञ्चविंशतिः पञ्चदशाः पञ्चविंशतिः सप्तदशाः पञ्चविंशतिरेकविंशाः
text_mt: There are twenty-five ninefold years, twenty-five fifteenfold, twenty-five seventeenfold, and twenty-five twenty-onefold.

sanskrit_iast: sādhyānāṃ śatasaṃvatsareṇa sagavāḥ sapuruṣāḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ yanti
meaning: साध्यानां शतसंवत्सरेण सगवाः सपुरुषाः स्वर्गं लोकं यन्ति
text_mt: By means of the hundred-year [sacrifice] of the Sādhyas, they go to the heavenly world together with their cattle and with their men.
By means of the thousand-[day]-pressing [sacrifice] of Agni, they attain the production of all food.
There is an Atirātra, a thousand ninefold days, and an Atirātra.
There are three Sarasvatī sacrificial sessions.
The first belongs to Mitra and Varuṇa, the second to Indra and Agni, and the third to Aryaman.
They undergo consecration at the disappearance-place of the Sarasvatī.
Having performed the introductory sacrifice, purchased King [Soma], and tied him up, they deposit [him].
Having performed twelve upasads and undertaken the introductory Atirātra, on that day they keep away the calves.
When the introductory [Atirātra] is completed, they sacrifice with the curd-and-milk oblation.
When that is completed, the adhvaryu hurls the yoke-pin eastward.
Where it falls down, that is the gārhapatya.
From that, he strides thirty-six steps eastward.
The sadas, the havirdhāna [sheds], and the āgnīdhra [shed] have wheels.
The havirdhāna [shed] and the āgnīdhra [shed] are made of aśvattha wood.
The sacrificial post, whose bottom is like a mortar, is dragged along and merely set in the ground.

sanskrit_iast: ta etam āpūryamāṇapakṣam āmāvāsyena haviṣā yānti
meaning: त एतम् आपूर्यमाणपक्षम् आमावास्येन हविषा यान्ति
text_mt: They advance along this waxing half of the month with the new-moon oblation.
On the full moon, they undertake the Goṣṭoma having the Bṛhat sāman.
When that is completed, they sacrifice with the full-moon oblation.
They advance along this waning half of the month with the full-moon oblation.
On the new moon, they undertake the Āyuṣṭoma having the Rathaṃtara sāman.
When that is completed, they sacrifice with the curd-and-milk oblation.

sanskrit_iast: ta evameva vyatyāsaṃ sarasvatyā dakṣiṇena kūlena
meaning: त एवमेव व्यत्यासं सरस्वत्या दक्षिणेन कूलेन
text_mt: In just this way, alternately along the southern bank of the Sarasvatī,
shouting, they advance eastward.
At the confluence of the Dṛṣadvatī, having offered a mess of cooked food to Apāṃ Napāt, they pass beyond.
Among ten cows, [or] among a hundred, they let loose a bull.

sanskrit_iast: yadā daśaśataṃ kurvantyathaikamutthānaṃ yadā vā śataṃ sahasram /
meaning: यदा दशशतं कुर्वन्त्यथैकमुत्थानं यदा वा शतं सहस्रम् /
text_mt: When the ten make a hundred, then is one rising; or when the hundred make a thousand;

sanskrit_iast: yadā vā gṛhapatirmriyeta yadā vā sarvasvaṃ jīyeranyadā vā plākṣaṃ prasravaṇaṃ prāpnuvanti
meaning: यदा वा गृहपतिर्म्रियेत यदा वा सर्वस्वं जीयेरन्यदा वा प्लाक्षं प्रस्रवणं प्राप्नुवन्ति
text_mt:
or when the master of the house dies; or when they are deprived of all property; or when they reach Plakṣaprāsravaṇa.

Having reached Plakṣaprāsravaṇa, they offer a sacrifice to Agni Kāma.

sanskrit_iast: tasyāmaśvāṃ puruṣīṃ ca dhenuke dattvā kārapacavaṃ prati yamunāmavabhṛthamabhyavayanti
meaning: तस्यामश्वां पुरुषीं च धेनुके दत्त्वा कारपचवं प्रति यमुनामवभृथमभ्यवयन्ति
text_mt: At it, having given a mare and a woman as milch animals, they go down to the Yamunā towards Kārapacava for the final purificatory bath.
In the second [session], the Bṛhaspatisava is ninefold, and the Go and Āyus days are the belly of Indra.
They surpass other creatures and become most vigorous.
In the third, the Jyotiḥ, Gauḥ, and Āyus are the course, and the Viśvajit and Abhijit are the belly of Indra.
They ascend the path of Aryaman and go to the world of the gods.
In the [session] along the Dṛṣadvatī, without losing a cow, he should guard the cows of a brahmin for a year.
For a year, he should kindle fire at Vyarṇa Naitandhava.
Having established the fire at Pariṇah, he should cast the yoke-pin along the southern bank of the Dṛṣadvatī with an eight-pot-sherd cake to Agni.
He goes down to the Yamunā towards Triplakṣa for the final purificatory bath.
Then indeed he disappears from men.
By the Turāyaṇa, he prospers with all prosperity.
Without being consecrated, he puts on a black-antelope skin;
he prospers thereby with human prosperity.
By the ascetic heat he performs, [he prospers] with divine [prosperity].
His vow consists of the sacrificial remnants.
For a year, he offers sacrifices arranged according to the pressings:

meaning: आग्नेयो ऽष्टाकपाल ऐन्द्र एकादशकपालो वैश्वदेवो द्वादशकपालः
text_mt: an eight-pot-sherd cake to Agni, an eleven-pot-sherd cake to Indra, and a twelve-pot-sherd cake to the All-gods.
By means of the sacrificial session of the serpents, they ward off old age;
their radiance becomes like that of the Ādityas.
Each year consists of sets of ten [days], the twelfth is the Viṣuvant.
The three-year Gavāmayana belongs to the Ādityas and the Aṅgirases.

sanskrit_iast: prājātiṃ bhūmānaṃ gacchantyabhi svargaṃ lokaṃ jayanatyeṣu lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhanti
meaning: प्राजातिं भूमानं गच्छन्त्यभि स्वर्गं लोकं जयनत्येषु लोकेषु प्रतितिष्ठन्ति
text_mt: They attain offspring and abundance, conquer the heavenly world, and are established in these worlds.
By means of the thousand-year [sacrifice] of Prajāpati, they prosper with the prosperity of Prajāpati.
There is an Atirātra, a thousand ninefold years, and an Atirātra.

sanskrit_iast: pañca pañcāśatastrivṛtaḥ saṃvatsarāḥ pañca pañcāśataḥpañcadaśāḥ pañca pañcāśataḥ saptadaśāḥ pañca pañcāśata ekaviṃśā viśvasṛjāṃ sahasrasaṃvatsaram
meaning: पञ्च पञ्चाशतस्त्रिवृतः संवत्सराः पञ्च पञ्चाशतःपञ्चदशाः पञ्च पञ्चाशतः सप्तदशाः पञ्च पञ्चाशत एकविंशा विश्वसृजां सहस्रसंवत्सरम्
text_mt: There are fifty-five ninefold years, fifty-five fifteenfold, fifty-five seventeenfold, and fifty-five twenty-onefold: this is the thousand-year [sacrifice] of the Viśvasṛjs.
By this, indeed, the Viśvasṛjs created this universe;
because they created the universe (viśva), therefore they are called the Viśvasṛjs.
The universe is propagated after them.

sanskrit_iast: viśvasṛjaḥ prathamāḥ sattramāsata sahasrasamaṃ prasutena yantaḥ /
meaning: विश्वसृजः प्रथमाः सत्त्रमासत सहस्रसमं प्रसुतेन यन्तः /
text_mt: "The universe-creators were the first to sit for a sacrificial session, proceeding for a thousand years with pressed [soma].

sanskrit_iast: tato ha jajñe bhuvanasya gopā hiraṇmayaḥ śakunir brahma nāmeti
meaning: ततो ह जज्ञे भुवनस्य गोपा हिरण्मयः शकुनिर् ब्रह्म नामेति
text_mt: Thence indeed was born the guardian of the world, the golden bird, Brahman by name." [Thus it is said.]

sanskrit_iast: brahmaṇaḥ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etadupayanti ya etadupayanti
meaning: ब्रह्मणः सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतदुपयन्ति य एतदुपयन्ति
text_mt: They attain union with Brahman and common world [with Brahman] who undertake this, who undertake this.
It belongs to the three social classes: the Brahmin, the Rājanya, and the Vaiśya.
It is enjoined by the three Vedas:
by the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, and the Sāmaveda.
The New and Full Moon sacrifices [are enjoined] by the Ṛgveda and the Yajurveda;
the agnihotra by the Yajurveda;
[The ritual acts are] performed loudly with the Ṛgveda and the Sāmaveda;
except in the case of the āśruta, the pratyāśruta, the pravara, dialogues, and ritual calls.
The sāmidhenī verses are to be recited intermediate [between loud and whisper].
In a low tone prior to the two butter portions, and at the morning pressing;
in a middle tone prior to the Sviṣṭakṛt, and at the midday pressing;
in a high tone in the remainder, and at the third pressing.
The continuous flow of voice [is modulated] in the same way.
By explicit rule or in case of conflict, another may perform [the action].
The priestly office belongs to Brahmins.
The fires of all rites are established only once.
When it is enjoined, "he offers," one should understand clarified butter [as the offering substance];
The utensils are maintained from the establishment [of the fires] until the end of life.
Their consecration takes place at each ritual framework.
The mantra and the brāhmaṇa are the authority for the sacrifice.
The name "Veda" applies to mantra and brāhmaṇa.
The brāhmaṇas are injunctions for ritual acts.

meaning: ब्राह्मणशेषो ऽर्थवादो निन्दा प्रशंसा परकृतिः पुराकल्पश्च
text_mt: The remainder of the brāhmaṇa is explanatory statement, censure, praise, the actions of others, and ancient tradition.
Those not handed down [in the Veda] are not mantras, as in the cases of the pravara, the ūha, and the utterance of personal names;
and the sound of a chariot and the sound of a drum.
An occasion of suspension of study applies to the mantras in private study, but not during ritual action, because the purpose is different.
even those consisting of distinct actions involving a number [of repetitions].
And likewise in scratching, sleeping, crossing a river, raining down upon [oneself], and addressing impure things, when they are not separated by time;
in setting out, however, [a single mantra serves] until the purpose is accomplished;
and likewise in actions that are not directly contiguous.
Repetition of the haviṣkṛt-call, the adhrigu-formula, the puronuvākyā, and the manotā-verse [occurs] at different times.
By explicit rule, a single action may have multiple mantras.
One should make the beginnings of actions coincide with the ends of mantras.
In the case of the āghāra libation and the continuous stream, the contact is at the beginning [of the mantra].
One should know the end of the preceding [mantra] by the beginning of the following.
In duties of the hotṛ and duties of the sacrificer, there is combination [of multiple mantras];
option in the case of the yājyā and the anuvākyā;
In purchases, hirings, and consecrations, there is combination of materials.
After performing acts dedicated to Rudra, Rakṣases, Nirṛti, or the ancestors, or acts of cutting, piercing, casting away, or touching one's own body, one should touch water.
The sacred ground has its operations directed from the north.
One should not turn one's back to the fire;
One must not pass a sacrificial implement accompanied by a mantra around oneself.

sanskrit_iast: prāgapavargāṇyudagapavargāṇi vā yajñopavītī pradakṣiṇaṃ daivāni karmāṇi karoti
meaning: प्रागपवर्गाण्युदगपवर्गाणि वा यज्ञोपवीती प्रदक्षिणं दैवानि कर्माणि करोति
text_mt: Wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, moving clockwise, one performs rites for the gods ending towards the east or ending towards the north.
Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder, moving counter-clockwise, rites for the ancestors end towards the south.

sanskrit_iast: yāni śulbāni samāsaṃ gacchanti prasavyaṃ tānyāveṣṭya pradakṣiṇaṃ samasyet
meaning: यानि शुल्बानि समासं गच्छन्ति प्रसव्यं तान्यावेष्ट्य प्रदक्षिणं समस्येत्
text_mt: Regarding cords that are combined together: having twisted them counter-clockwise, one should combine them clockwise.

sanskrit_iast: atha yāni na samasyante pradakṣiṇaṃ tāni
meaning: अथ यानि न समस्यन्ते प्रदक्षिणं तानि
text_mt: Now, those that are not combined are [twisted] clockwise.
One should sacrifice on the new moon day with the New Moon sacrifice,
on the full moon day with the Full Moon sacrifice.
On the day when the full moon rises in the east, on that full moon day one should observe the fast,
The Vājasaneyins recite [the view that it is on] the third, dwarfed [moon].
On the day when it is not seen, that day is the new moon day;
When primary rites are enjoined in a single context, they have the same procedure.
Injunctions are restricted by context.
When there is no specific mention, they are common [to all];
due to specific mention, they are distributed.

meaning: आग्नेयो ऽष्टाकपालो ऽग्नीषोमीय एकादशकपाल उपांशुयाजश्च पौर्णमास्यां प्रधानानि
text_mt: The cake on eight potsherds for Agni, the cake on eleven potsherds for Agni-Soma, and the whisper-offering are the primary rites on the full moon day.

meaning: आग्नेयो ऽष्टाकपाल ऐन्द्राग्न एकादशकपालो द्वादशकपालो वामावास्यायामसोमयाजिनः
text_mt: The cake on eight potsherds for Agni, and a cake on eleven or twelve potsherds for Indra-Agni are [the primary rites] on the new moon day for one who has not performed a soma sacrifice.
The saṃnāyya is the second [primary rite] for one who has performed a soma sacrifice.
For a brahmin who has not performed a soma sacrifice, there is no sacrificial cake for Agni-Soma.
For one offering the saṃnāyya, there is no [cake] for Indra-Agni, without distinction of caste.
The sacrifice to the ancestors should not be an auxiliary rite, because its time is separately enjoined,
because it is enumerated as equivalent,
and because it is seen even when [the main sacrifice] is prohibited.

sanskrit_iast: deśe kāle kartarīti nirdiśyate svaśabdaṃ yat
meaning: देशे काले कर्तरीति निर्दिश्यते स्वशब्दं यत्
text_mt: whatever is expressly designated with regard to place, time, or agent [belongs to both].
or in a series of oblations, having scooped [the oblation] for each oblation,
and there is absence of kindling-stick, except in the agnihotra.
West of the fire, having bent the right knee or without bending it, seated, one offers the ladle-offerings,
Passing to the south behind the āhavanīya, facing north, one offers all oblations,

sanskrit_iast: āśrutapratyāśrute yājyānuvākye avadāneṣu copastaraṇābhighāraṇe caturgṛhītaṃ vaṣaṭkāraścādarvihomānām
meaning: आश्रुतप्रत्याश्रुते याज्यानुवाक्ये अवदानेषु चोपस्तरणाभिघारणे चतुर्गृहीतं वषट्कारश्चादर्विहोमानाम्
text_mt: The call and counter-call, the invitatory and consecratory verses, the under-spreading and dripping [of butter] upon the cut portions, the fourfold scooping, and the vaṣaṭ-call belong to non-ladle-offerings.
At the vaṣaṭ-call, or along with the vaṣaṭ-call, one should make [the oblation] fall into the offerings;
In a group of sacrificial cakes, one should divide off each one with the mantra, 'Divide according to your portions!';
the last two with, 'Divide, you two, according to your portions!'
He designates the deities for those two alone.
In a group of boiled mess and sacrificial cake, he separates what is for the boiled mess and what is for the sacrificial cake before pouring [the grains] out;
he designates them according to their deities.
The word 'idam' ('this') should be the common form,
At the time of placing the potsherds, he places the pot for the boiled mess with the first potsherd-mantra.
He modifies the mantra as 'dhruvo 'si' ('Firm art thou').
At the time of purifying the flour, he purifies the rice grains.
At the time of putting [the potsherds] on the fire, he pours in the rice grains with the putting-on mantra.
Without taking it out [of the pot], he sets down the boiled mess.
There are fifteen kindling verses in the New and Full Moon sacrifices;
seventeen in the animal sacrifices and optional sacrifices wherever they are prescribed.

sanskrit_iast: upāṃśu kāmyā iṣṭayaḥ kriyanta iti tatra yāvatpradhānamupāṃśu
meaning: उपांशु काम्या इष्टयः क्रियन्त इति तत्र यावत्प्रधानमुपांशु
text_mt: Where it is said, 'The optional sacrifices are performed in a whisper,' as much as is primary is [performed] in a whisper.
The New and Full Moon sacrifices are the archetype of the [other] sacrifices.
And [they are the archetype] of the animal [sacrifice] for Agni and Soma.
The savanīya [animal sacrifice is the archetype] of the group of eleven [animal sacrifices].
The group of eleven [animal sacrifices is the archetype] of animal groups.
The Vaiśvadeva [parvan is the archetype] of the Varuṇapraghāsa, Sākamedha, and Śunāsīrīya [parvans].
The single-potsherd [cake] belonging to the Vaiśvadeva is [the archetype] of [all] single-potsherd [cakes].
The curd mixture belonging to the Vaiśvadeva is [the archetype] of curd mixtures.
In that case, the modification should be understood from similarity.
Those [offerings] with a single deity are modifications of the [cake] for Agni.
Those with two deities are modifications of the [cake] for Agni and Soma.
[This applies] when [the deities] are other than the deities of the archetype, as: "a sacrificial cake for Indra, a cooked mess of rice for Soma."
When there is similarity both of the sacrificial substance and of the deity, the sacrificial substance is stronger.
When there is a conflict between substance and consecration, the substance is stronger.
When there is a conflict between purpose and substance, the purpose is stronger.
In the archetype, there is no modification [of mantras].
In an ectypal rite, there is modification according to the purpose, except for an explanatory remark.
An explanatory remark is due to the hearing of another sentence.
In the absence of what has been prescribed, a substitute [is adopted] on the basis of similarity.
If there is a deficiency in quantity, one should complete it with the remainder of that [same substance].
A substitute is excluded in the case of the master [of the sacrifice], the fire, the deity, from the [authoritative] word, and because of a prohibition of the ritual action.
The archetype ceases due to three causes: due to replacement, due to prohibition, and due to cessation of the purpose.
The Agniṣṭoma is the archetype of one-day rites.
The Gavāmayana [is the archetype] of year-long rites.
And of the series [of identical rites], the first [is the archetype].
At the Agniṣṭoma, there is a high altar.
In subsequent sacrifices, there is the piling of the fire;
except in the case of the Sādyaskra rites, the Vājapeya, the Ṣoḍaśin, and the Sārasvata sattra.
At the beginning of a sacrifice, one should desire the desire of the sacrifice.
At the beginning of a subordinate part of the sacrifice, [one should desire] the desire of the subordinate part of the sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast: alpīyāṃso mantrā bhūyāṃsi karmāṇi tatra samaśaḥ prativibhajya pūrvaiḥ pūrvāṇi kārayeduttarairuttarāṇi
meaning: अल्पीयांसो मन्त्रा भूयांसि कर्माणि तत्र समशः प्रतिविभज्य पूर्वैः पूर्वाणि कारयेदुत्तरैरुत्तराणि
text_mt: When there are fewer mantras and more ritual actions, having divided them equally there, one should cause the earlier [actions] to be performed with the earlier [mantras] and the later [actions] with the later [mantras].

sanskrit_iast: alpīyāṃsi karmāṇi bhūyāṃso mantrāstatra pratimantraṃ kuryāt /
meaning: अल्पीयांसि कर्माणि भूयांसो मन्त्रास्तत्र प्रतिमन्त्रं कुर्यात् /
text_mt: When there are fewer ritual actions and more mantras, one should perform [an action] to each mantra;
the remaining ones serve the purpose of option, as [in the case of] the substances for the sacrificial post.
Omission or addition [takes place] from the end.
Because the archetypal [ritual element] is mentioned earlier, the un-archetypal should be at the end.
Because of the sufficiency of the pot, the spit, and the omentum-roasting spit, there should be a common performance.
If there is a difference of species, however, it should be divided, because of the inequality of cooking.

sanskrit_iast: sviṣṭakṛdvikāre vanaspatau yājyāyāṃ devatānigamāḥ syuḥ prakṛtyupabandhāt
meaning: स्विष्टकृद्विकारे वनस्पतौ याज्यायां देवतानिगमाः स्युः प्रकृत्युपबन्धात्
text_mt: In the case of Vanaspati as a modification of Sviṣṭakṛt, the mentions of the deities should occur in the consecratory verse, because of the connection with the archetype.
The initial offering should not occur in an ectypal rite, because it is within the time of the archetypal rite;
Or rather, it should occur, because the time is not an accessory part,
For each distinct purpose, one brings forward the fire.

sanskrit_iast: apavṛtte karmaṇi laukikaḥ saṃpadyate yathā samārūḍhe
meaning: अपवृत्ते कर्मणि लौकिकः संपद्यते यथा समारूढे
text_mt: When the ritual action has ended, it becomes profane, as when it has mounted [the two kindling sticks].
We shall explain the ancestral lineage invocations.
"he does not depart from kinship; furthermore, for continuity," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].
He chooses the ancestral seer lineage neither by gods nor by humans;
"he chooses the ancestral seer lineage only by the seers," so it is known.

sanskrit_iast: ṛṣiṇā hi devāḥ puruṣamanubudhyanta iti vijñāyate
meaning: ऋषिणा हि देवाः पुरुषमनुबुध्यन्त इति विज्ञायते
text_mt: "for by means of the seer the gods recognise a man," so it is known.

sanskrit_iast: yo vā anyaḥ sannathānyasyārṣeyeṇa pravṛṇīte sa vā asya tadṛṣiriṣṭaṃ vītaṃ vṛṅktaṃ iti vijñāyate
meaning: यो वा अन्यः सन्नथान्यस्यार्षेयेण प्रवृणीते स वा अस्य तदृषिरिष्टं वीतं वृङ्क्तं इति विज्ञायते
text_mt: "Whoever, being one person, then chooses [his lineage] with the ancestral seers of another, that seer of his deprives him of what has been sacrificed and what has been given," so it is known.
"according to the seer, he chooses the mantra-makers," so it is known.
he does not choose beyond five—so it is known from the tradition.

meaning: अत ऊर्ध्वानध्वर्युर्वृणीते ऽमुतो ऽर्वाचो होतेति विज्ञायते
text_mt: The adhvaryu chooses them upwards from here; the hotṛ downwards from there—so it is known from the tradition.

sanskrit_iast: purohitasya pravareṇa rājā pravṛṇita iti vijñāyate
meaning: पुरोहितस्य प्रवरेण राजा प्रवृणित इति विज्ञायते
text_mt: A king chooses with the ancestral formula (pravara) of his domestic priest—so it is known from the tradition.
We shall explain [the ancestral invocations] of the Bhṛgus first.
theirs is a five-seer ancestral formula (pravara):
'O descendant of Bhṛgu, of Cyavana, of Apnavāna, of Ūrva, of Jamadagni!'—
'Like Jamadagni, like Ūrva, like Apnavāna, like Cyavana, like Bhṛgu!'
'O descendant of Bhṛgu, of Ūrva, of Jamadagni!'—
'Like Jamadagni, like Ūrva, like Bhṛgu!'
This very one unmodified belongs to the Sāvarṇis, Jīvantis, Jābālis, Aitiśāyanas, Vairohityas, Avaṭas, Maṇḍus, and Prācīnayogyas.
Now for the Ārṣṭiṣeṇas, there is a five-seer ancestral formula:
'O descendant of Bhṛgu, of Cyavana, of Apnavāna, of Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa, of Anūpa!'—
'Like Anūpa, like Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa, like Apnavāna, like Cyavana, like Bhṛgu!'
'O descendant of Bhṛgu, of Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa, of Anūpa!'—
'Like Anūpa, like Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa, like Bhṛgu!'
Now the Vītahavyas: the Yāskas, Vādhūlas, and Maunamaukas:
'O descendant of Bhṛgu, of Vītahavya, of Savedas!'—
'Like Savedas, like Vītahavya, like Bhṛgu!'
Now the Gārtsamadas: the Śunakas:
the adhvaryu says: 'Like Gṛtsamada!'.
Now the Vādhryaśvas: the Mitrāyus:
the adhvaryu says: 'Like Vadhryaśva!'.
'O descendant of Bhṛgu, of Vena, of Pṛthu!'—
'Like Pṛthu, like Vena, like Bhṛgu!'
These Bhṛgus have been explained.
Now then of the Aṅgirases: the Āyāsya Gautamas:
'O descendant of Aṅgiras, of Ayāsya, of Gotama!'
'O descendant of Aṅgiras, of Ucathya, of Gotama!'—
'Like Gotama, like Ucathya, like Aṅgiras!'
'O descendant of Aṅgiras, of Uśij, of Kakṣīvat!'—
'Like Kakṣīvat, like Uśij, like Aṅgiras!'
Now the Vāmadeva Gautamas:
'O descendant of Aṅgiras, of Vāmadeva, of Bṛhaduktha!'—
'Like Bṛhaduktha, like Vāmadeva, like Aṅgiras!'
Now for the Bharadvājas, there is a three-seer ancestral formula:
'O descendant of Aṅgiras, of Bṛhaspati, of Bharadvāja!'—
'Like Bharadvāja, like Bṛhaspati, like Aṅgiras!'
[belongs] to the Kukvas, the Agniveśyas, the Ūrjāyanas, and all those named Stambastamba.
Now, of families of dual lineage (dvyāmuṣyāyaṇa), such as the Śuṅga-Śiśiras:
“O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Bṛhaspati, descendant of Bharadvāja, descendant of Kata, descendant of Atkīla!”
[and in the hotṛ’s formula:] “Like Atkīla, like Kata, like Bharadvāja, like Bṛhaspati, like Aṅgiras!”
“O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Kata, descendant of Atkīla!”
“Like Atkīla, like Kata, like Aṅgiras!”
Now, for the Ṛkṣas, there is a five-seer [pravara]:
“O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Bṛhaspati, descendant of Bharadvāja, descendant of Vandana, descendant of Matavacasa!”
“Like Matavacasa, like Vandana, like Bharadvāja, like Bṛhaspati, like Aṅgiras!”
“O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Vandana, descendant of Matavacasa!”
“Like Matavacasa, like Vandana, like Aṅgiras!”
Now, for the Kapis, there is a three-seer [pravara]:
“O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Āmahīyu, descendant of Urukṣaya!”
“Like Urukṣaya, like Āmahīyu, like Aṅgiras!”
Now, for the Gargas, there is a three-seer [pravara]:
“O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Garga, descendant of Śini!”
“Like Śini, like Garga, like Aṅgiras!”
Some indeed [prescribe] Bharadvāja in place of Aṅgiras:
“O descendant of Bharadvāja, descendant of Garga, descendant of Śini!”
“Like Śini, like Garga, like Bharadvāja!”
Now, for the Haritas, there is a three-seer [pravara]:
“O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Ambarīṣa, descendant of Yuvanāśva!”
“Like Yuvanāśva, like Ambarīṣa, like Aṅgiras!”
Some indeed [prescribe] Māndhātṛ in place of Aṅgiras:
“O descendant of Māndhātṛ, descendant of Ambarīṣa, descendant of Yuvanāśva!”
“Like Yuvanāśva, like Ambarīṣa, like Māndhātṛ!”
Now, for the Kutsas, there is a three-seer [pravara]:
“O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Māndhātṛ, descendant of Kutsa!”
“Like Kutsa, like Māndhātṛ, like Aṅgiras!”
“O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Ajamīḍha, descendant of Kaṇva!”
“Like Kaṇva, like Ajamīḍha, like Aṅgiras!”
Now, the Rathītaras who are Virūpas:
“O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Virūpa, descendant of Pṛṣadaśva!”
“Like Pṛṣadaśva, like Virūpa, like Aṅgiras!”
Some indeed [prescribe] Aṣṭrādaṃṣṭra in place of Aṅgiras:
“O descendant of Aṣṭrādaṃṣṭra, descendant of Virūpa, descendant of Pṛṣadaśva!”
“Like Pṛṣadaśva, like Virūpa, like Aṣṭrādaṃṣṭra!”
Now, for the Mudgalas, there is a three-seer [pravara]:
“O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Bhṛmyaśva, descendant of Mudgala!”
“Like Mudgala, like Bhṛmyaśva, like Aṅgiras!”
Some indeed [prescribe] Tṛkṣa in place of Aṅgiras:
“O descendant of Tṛkṣa, descendant of Bhṛmyaśva, descendant of Mudgala!”
“Like Mudgala, like Bhṛmyaśva, like Tṛkṣa!”
Now, for the Viṣṇuvṛddhas, there is a three-seer [pravara]:
“O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Purukutsa, descendant of Trasadasyu!”
“Like Trasadasyu, like Purukutsa, like Aṅgiras!”
This very same [pravara remains] unmodified for the Śaṭhamarṣaṇas, Bhadraṇas, Madraṇas, Bādarāyaṇas, Aupamanyus, Aupagavis, Sātyakis, Sātyaṃkāmis, Āruṇis, and Nituṇḍis.
Now, for the Atris, there is a three-seer [pravara]:
“O descendant of Atri, descendant of Arcanānas, descendant of Śyāvāśva!”
“Like Śyāvāśva, like Arcanānas, like Atri!”
Now, for the Gaviṣṭhiras, there is a three-seer [pravara]:
“O descendant of Atri, descendant of Arcanānas, descendant of Gaviṣṭhira!”
“Like Gaviṣṭhira, like Arcanānas, like Atri!”
Now, for the Atithis, there are three ancestral seers:
"Ātreya, Ārcanānasa, Ātithya."
[the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Atithi, like Arcanānas, like Atri!'
This very [pravara], unmodified, belongs to the Vāmarathyas, Sumaṅgalas, and Baijavāpis.
Now, among the Viśvāmitras: the Devarātas, Cikitās, Manutantus, Aulakis, Vālukis, Yajñavalkas, Ulūkas, Bṛhadagnis, Babhrus, Gālavas, Śālāvata-Śālaṅkāyanas, and Kālabavas.
[the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, of Devarāta, of Udala!'
[the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Udala, like Devarāta, like Viśvāmitra!'
Now, of the Śraumata-Kāmakāyanas, there is a three-ṛṣi invocation:
[the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, of Devaśravas, of Devataras!'
[the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Devataras, like Devaśravas, like Viśvāmitra!'
Now, of the Ājyas, there is a three-ṛṣi invocation:
[the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, of Madhucchandas, of Aja!'
[the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Aja, like Madhucchandas, like Viśvāmitra!'
Now, the Dhanaṃjayas are indeed descendants of Madhucchandas.
[the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, of Madhucchandas, of Dhanaṃjaya!'
[the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Dhanaṃjaya, like Madhucchandas, like Viśvāmitra!'
[the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Aṣṭaka, like Viśvāmitra!'
Now, the Pūraṇas and Vāridhāpayantas.
[the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, of Pūraṇa!'
[the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Pūraṇa, like Viśvāmitra!'
Now, of the Katas, there is a three-ṛṣi invocation:
[the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, of Kata, of Atkīla!'
[the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Atkīla, like Kata, like Viśvāmitra!'
Now, the Aghamarṣaṇa-Kuśikas.
[the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, of Aghamarṣaṇa, of Kuśika!'
[the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Kuśika, like Aghamarṣaṇa, like Viśvāmitra!'
Now, of the Kaśyapas, there is a three-ṛṣi invocation:
[the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Kaśyapa, of Avatsāra, of Nidhruva!'
[the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Nidhruva, like Avatsāra, like Kaśyapa!'
Now, of the Rebhas, there is a three-ṛṣi invocation:
[the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Kaśyapa, of Avatsāra, of Rebha!'
[the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Rebha, like Avatsāra, like Kaśyapa!'
Now, of the Śaṇḍilas, there is a two-ṛṣi invocation:
[the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Asita, like Devala!'
[the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Kaśyapa, of Devala, of Asita!'
[the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Asita, like Devala, like Kaśyapa!'
By rule, however, they have a two-ṛṣi invocation.
The Vāsiṣṭhas have a one-ṛṣi invocation, except for the Parāśaras:
The hotṛ [says]: 'O descendant of Vasiṣṭha!'; the adhvaryu [says]: 'Like Vasiṣṭha!'
[the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Vasiṣṭha, of Indrapramada, of Ābharadvasu!'
[the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Ābharadvasu, like Indrapramada, like Vasiṣṭha!'
Now, of the Parāśaras, there is a three-ṛṣi invocation:
[the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Vasiṣṭha, of Śakti, of Parāśara!'
[the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Parāśara, like Śakti, like Vasiṣṭha!'
Now, of the Kuṇḍinas, there is a three-ṛṣi invocation:
[the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Vasiṣṭha, of Mitrāvaruṇa, of Kuṇḍina!'
[the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Kuṇḍina, like Mitrāvaruṇa, like Vasiṣṭha!'
Now, of the Saṃkṛtis and Pūtimāṣas, there is a three-ṛṣi invocation:
[the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Śakti, of Saṃkṛti, of Gaurivīti!'
[the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Gaurivīti, like Saṃkṛti, like Śakti!'
Now, of the Agastis, there is a one-ṛṣi invocation:
"Like Agastya," says the adhvaryu.
"O descendant of Agastya, O Dārḍhacyuta, O Idhmavāha," [says the hotṛ];
"like Idhmavāha, like Dṛḍhacyuta, like Agastya," [says the adhvaryu].
If they choose royal sovereignty, there is only one ancestral lineage for them:
"O descendant of Manu, O descendant of Iḍā, O descendant of Purūravas," [says the hotṛ];
"like Purūravas, like Iḍāvat, like Manu," [says the adhvaryu].

sanskrit_iast: atha yeṣāmu ha mantrakṛto na syuḥ sapurohitapravarāste pravṛṇīran
meaning: अथ येषामु ह मन्त्रकृतो न स्युः सपुरोहितप्रवरास्ते प्रवृणीरन्
text_mt: Now, for those who do not have hymn-composers [among their ancestors], they should choose having the ancestral lineage of their purohita.
Now, those who have [hymn-composers among their ancestors] do not have the ancestral lineage of their purohita.
However, by this principle, they [still] have the ancestral lineage of their purohita.
"like Vatsaprī," says the adhvaryu.
Now, one whose lineage is unknown should recite after the lineage of his teacher, [or] he should choose the ancestral lineage of his teacher.
Now the Tāṇḍins prescribe a single ṛṣi belonging to all classes:

sanskrit_iast: mānavyo hi prajā iti hi brāhmaṇamiti hi brāhmaṇam
meaning: मानव्यो हि प्रजा इति हि ब्राह्मणमिति हि ब्राह्मणम्
text_mt: For "creatures are descended from Manu," so indeed says the Brāhmaṇa; so indeed says the Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: purastātsāmidhenīnāṃ hotā hṛdayadeśa ūrdhvaṃ prādeśaṃ dhārayamāṇo japati mayi gṛhṇāmyagre agniṃ yo no agniḥ pitara iti
meaning: पुरस्तात्सामिधेनीनां होता हृदयदेश ऊर्ध्वं प्रादेशं धारयमाणो जपति मयि गृह्णाम्यग्रे अग्निं यो नो अग्निः पितर इति
text_mt: Before the kindling verses, the hotṛ, holding an upright span at the region of his heart, mutters: "In me I take Agni first; he who is our fire, O fathers."

sanskrit_iast: antarāhavanīyamutkaraṃ ca pratīcīnaṃ gacchañjapati kaṃ prapadye taṃ prapadye /
