meaning: अन्तराहवनीयमुत्करं च प्रतीचीनं गच्छञ्जपति कं प्रपद्ये तं प्रपद्ये /
text_mt: Going westward between the āhavanīya and the rubbish heap, he mutters: "Whom do I enter? Him I enter.
That which is your refuge, your meter, O Prajāpati, that do I enter.
As much as I know of you, O Viṣṇu, so much will I do for you.

sanskrit_iast: namo agnaya upadraṣṭre namo vāyava upaśrotre nama ādityāyānukhyātre /
meaning: नमो अग्नय उपद्रष्ट्रे नमो वायव उपश्रोत्रे नम आदित्यायानुख्यात्रे /
text_mt: Homage to Agni, the onlooker! Homage to Vāyu, the overhearer! Homage to Āditya, the overseer!

sanskrit_iast: juṣṭāmadya devebhyo vācamudyāsaṃ svadhāvatīṃ pitṛbhyaḥ śuśrūṣeṇyāṃ manuṣyebhyaḥ /
meaning: जुष्टामद्य देवेभ्यो वाचमुद्यासं स्वधावतीं पितृभ्यः शुश्रूषेण्यां मनुष्येभ्यः /
text_mt: May I speak today speech pleasing to the gods, accompanied by svadhā for the fathers, worthy of being heard by men.

sanskrit_iast: praśāsta ātmanā prajayā paśubhiḥ prajāpatiṃ prapadye /
meaning: प्रशास्त आत्मना प्रजया पशुभिः प्रजापतिं प्रपद्ये /
text_mt: Directing with myself, with offspring, with cattle, I enter Prajāpati.
I will recite what pertains to Prajāpati.
May speech perform the priest's duty; may mind perform the priest's duty.
I enter speech: bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ."
With "I stand in the place of Viṣṇu," he takes his stance.
The right foot is inside the altar ground;

sanskrit_iast: athordhvastiṣṭhanbrahmansāmidhenīranuvakṣyāmīti brahmāṇamāmantrya daśahotāraṃ vyākhyāya vyāhṛtīśca japitvā trirhiṅkṛtottamena hiṅkāreṇārdharcamupasaṃdadhāti
meaning: अथोर्ध्वस्तिष्ठन्ब्रह्मन्सामिधेनीरनुवक्ष्यामीति ब्रह्माणमामन्त्र्य दशहोतारं व्याख्याय व्याहृतीश्च जपित्वा त्रिर्हिङ्कृतोत्तमेन हिङ्कारेणार्धर्चमुपसंदधाति
text_mt: Then, standing upright, having addressed the brahman [priest] with "O brahman, I will recite the kindling verses," having recited the daśahotṛ formula and muttered the mystical utterances, having uttered hiṅ three times, he joins the half-verse with the final hiṅ-sound.
He recites the first [verse] three times, and the last three times.

sanskrit_iast: yaṃ kāmayeta sarvamāyuriyāditi tasya triranavānaṃ prathamottame anubrūyāt
meaning: यं कामयेत सर्वमायुरियादिति तस्य त्रिरनवानं प्रथमोत्तमे अनुब्रूयात्
text_mt: For one of whom he desires that he may attain the full lifespan, he should recite the first and last [verses] three times without taking a breath.
"Continuously connecting each single [verse], he should recite without taking a breath," say some.
He divides the third kindling verse three times.
"He recites continuously," since there is no distinction among the kindling verses.
"From various ṛṣis, indeed, are these kindling verses fashioned.

sanskrit_iast: tā yadasaṃyuktāḥ syuḥ prajayā paśubhiryajamānasya vitiṣṭheran /
meaning: ता यदसंयुक्ताः स्युः प्रजया पशुभिर्यजमानस्य वितिष्ठेरन् /
text_mt: If they were unconnected, they would scatter with the offspring and cattle of the sacrificer.

sanskrit_iast: ardharcau saṃdadhāti saṃyunaktyevainā iti te manyāmahe
meaning: अर्धर्चौ संदधाति संयुनक्त्येवैना इति ते मन्यामहे
text_mt: He joins the two half-verses; he connects them indeed"—so we hold.
He should join the latter [half-verse] of the preceding [verse] and the former [half-verse] of the succeeding [verse].
The teaching that there is no taking of breath during the kindling verses is [from the text] "he recites continuously"; and it is known [from sacred text]:
If he should take breath between two verses, he would place the out-breath in the down-breath.
Passing over the [second] half-verse of the preceding [verse], he takes breath during the [first] half-verse of the succeeding [verse]."
The continuity of half-verses is found through reciting three times, because they have a single ṛṣi.
"You, O Varuṇa" is the concluding verse for the Vasiṣṭhas and the Rājanyas;
"offer!" for other clans.
Narāśaṃsa is the second fore-offering for the Vasiṣṭhas and the Śunakas;
Tanūnapāt for other clans.
Having recited the kindling verses and having spoken the ancestral lineage, he recites the nivids.
Having spoken seven words of them, he takes breath;
then four, then four.

sanskrit_iast: tā anūcya devatā āvāhayati yā yakṣyamāṇo bhavati
meaning: ता अनूच्य देवता आवाहयति या यक्ष्यमाणो भवति
text_mt: Having recited them, he invokes the deities to whom [the sacrificer] is about to sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast: sa vai khalu vājino nāvāhayeddevikā devasuvo yacca kiṃ caitādṛkte manyāmahe
meaning: स वै खलु वाजिनो नावाहयेद्देविका देवसुवो यच्च किं चैतादृक्ते मन्यामहे
text_mt: Indeed, he should not invoke the Vājins, the Devikās, the Devasūs, and whatever else is of such a kind, we consider.
There should be a prohibition of those subordinate to another and separated by another procedure, because the Vedic text indicates that.
For [offerings to] the same deity separated by [offerings to] different deities, the invocation is common, on account of adequacy.

sanskrit_iast: athordhvajñuḥ prādeśena bhūmimabhinidhāya japatīdamahaṃ trivṛtā stomena rathaṃtareṇa sāmaṇ vaṣaṭkāreṇa vajreṇāsyai pṛthivyā asyai pratiṣṭhāyā asmādāyatanādyo 'smāndveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmastaṃ hanmi //
meaning: अथोर्ध्वज्ञुः प्रादेशेन भूमिमभिनिधाय जपतीदमहं त्रिवृता स्तोमेन रथंतरेण सामण् वषट्कारेण वज्रेणास्यै पृथिव्या अस्यै प्रतिष्ठाया अस्मादायतनाद्यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्मस्तं हन्मि //
text_mt: Then, with knee raised, having pressed the ground with a span [of his hand], he murmurs: "Here I strike him who hates us and whom we hate, from this earth, from this firm foundation, from this dwelling, with the trivṛt chant, with the rathaṃtara sāman, with the vaṣaṭ-call as a vajra!"
"If today in the choosing of the hotṛ the eye went astray crookedly,
Agni Jātavedas, who looks upon all men, brought it back!"

sanskrit_iast: vasūnāṃ rātau syāma rudrāṇāmūrmyāyāṃ svādityā aditaye 'nehasaḥ /
meaning: वसूनां रातौ स्याम रुद्राणामूर्म्यायां स्वादित्या अदितये ऽनेहसः /
text_mt: "May we be in the bounty of the Vasus, in the surge of the Rudras, well-Adityas, sinless for Aditi!

sanskrit_iast: cārumadya devebhyo vācamudyāsaṃ cāruṃ brahmabhyaścāruṃ manuṣyebhyaścāruṃ narāśaṃsāyānumatāṃ pitṛbhiḥ /
meaning: चारुमद्य देवेभ्यो वाचमुद्यासं चारुं ब्रह्मभ्यश्चारुं मनुष्येभ्यश्चारुं नराशंसायानुमतां पितृभिः /
text_mt: May I speak pleasant speech today to the gods, pleasant to the Brahmans, pleasant to men, pleasant to Narāśaṃsa, approved by the fathers!

sanskrit_iast: ye te śataṃ varuṇa ye sahasraṃ yajñiyāḥ pāśā vitatāḥ purutrā /
meaning: ये ते शतं वरुण ये सहस्रं यज्ञियाः पाशा वितताः पुरुत्रा /
text_mt: Those hundred, O Varuṇa, those thousand sacrificial snares of yours stretched out far and wide,

sanskrit_iast: tebhyo na indraḥ savitota viṣṇurviśve devā muñcantu marutaḥ svastyeti
meaning: तेभ्यो न इन्द्रः सवितोत विष्णुर्विश्वे देवा मुञ्चन्तु मरुतः स्वस्त्येति
text_mt: from them let Indra, Savitṛ, and Viṣṇu, all the gods, the Maruts release us for well-being!"

sanskrit_iast: atha yadenamāhāsau manuṣa iti tadupotthāya dakṣiṇena pāṇinā dakṣiṇāmadhvaryoraṃsamanvārabhya japati /
meaning: अथ यदेनमाहासौ मनुष इति तदुपोत्थाय दक्षिणेन पाणिना दक्षिणामध्वर्योरंसमन्वारभ्य जपति /
text_mt: Then, when [the adhvaryu] says to him: "Such a one, of human descent!", having stood up towards him, touching the right shoulder of the adhvaryu with his right hand, he murmurs:
with his left [hand], the right [shoulder] of the āgnīdhra.
"Sixty and ninety snares, O adhvaryu, are unfastened between the hotṛ and Agni;

sanskrit_iast: sinanti pākamati dhīra etyṛtasya panthāmanveti hotā //
meaning: सिनन्ति पाकमति धीर एत्यृतस्य पन्थामन्वेति होता //
text_mt: they bind the simpleton; the wise one goes beyond them; the hotṛ follows the path of ṛta."
"We take hold of Agni, who was placed in front at the choosing of the hotṛ,
by whom the divine Aṅgirases went to the highest heaven, the light!"
With "In me are out-breath and in-breath," having withdrawn both hands, he touches the chest region.

sanskrit_iast: ā pṛṇoṣi saṃpṛṇa prajayā mā paśubhirāpṛṇetīdhmasaṃnahanāni mukhaṃ prati vidhūnute
meaning: आ पृणोषि संपृण प्रजया मा पशुभिरापृणेतीध्मसंनहनानि मुखं प्रति विधूनुते
text_mt: With "You fill up, fill [me] up; do fill me up with offspring and cattle," he shakes the firewood-bindings toward his face.

sanskrit_iast: athāpa upaspṛśyāgne naya supathā rāye asmān //
meaning: अथाप उपस्पृश्याग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मान् //
text_mt: Then, having touched water, with "O Agni, lead us along the good path to wealth..."

sanskrit_iast: ehyagna iha hotā ni ṣīdādabdhaḥ su puraetā bhavā naḥ /
meaning: एह्यग्न इह होता नि षीदादब्धः सु पुरएता भवा नः /
text_mt: "Come, O Agni, sit down here as hotṛ; undeceived, be a good leader before us;

sanskrit_iast: avatāṃ mā rodasī viśvaminve yajā mahe saumanasāya devānityete ṛcau japnhotṛṣadanāya pravrajati
meaning: अवतां मा रोदसी विश्वमिन्वे यजा महे सौमनसाय देवानित्येते ऋचौ जप्न्होतृषदनाय प्रव्रजति
text_mt: may the two all-invigorating world-halves protect me; let us sacrifice to the gods for great benevolence!"—murmuring these two verses, he advances to the hotṛ's seat.

sanskrit_iast: jaghanena hotṛṣadanaṃ prāṅmukha upaviśyātha hotṛṣadanamabhimṛśatyahe daidhiṣavyeti
meaning: जघनेन होतृषदनं प्राङ्मुख उपविश्याथ होतृषदनमभिमृशत्यहे दैधिषव्येति
text_mt: Having sat down behind the hotṛ's seat facing east, he touches the hotṛ's seat with: "O Daidhiṣavya..."
Then he tosses away a blade of grass from it;

sanskrit_iast: śuṣkaṃ pracchinnāgraṃ vā nirastaḥ parāgvasuḥ saha pāpmaneti
meaning: शुष्कं प्रच्छिन्नाग्रं वा निरस्तः पराग्वसुः सह पाप्मनेति
text_mt: a dry one, or one whose tip is cut off, with: "Cast away is Parāgvasu together with evil!"

sanskrit_iast: atha hotṛṣadana upaviśati pātaṃ mā dyāvāpṛthivī upastha iti dakṣiṇapūrviṇaṃ savyottariṇaṃ vopasthaṃ kṛtvā
meaning: अथ होतृषदन उपविशति पातं मा द्यावापृथिवी उपस्थ इति दक्षिणपूर्विणं सव्योत्तरिणं वोपस्थं कृत्वा
text_mt: Then he sits down upon the hotṛ's seat, with: "Protect me, Heaven and Earth, in your lap!", having made his lap with the right [foot] first or with the left [foot] above.

sanskrit_iast: atha japati sīda hotarni hotā hotṛṣadana iti dve //
meaning: अथ जपति सीद होतर्नि होता होतृषदन इति द्वे //
text_mt: Then he murmurs the two: "Sit down, O hotṛ..." and "Down the hotṛ in the hotṛ's seat...";
this one: "Please the eager gods, O youngest one!";

sanskrit_iast: veṣi hotramuta potraṃ janānāṃ mandhātāsi draviṇodā ṛtāvā /
meaning: वेषि होत्रमुत पोत्रं जनानां मन्धातासि द्रविणोदा ऋतावा /
text_mt: "You perform the hotṛ's office and the potṛ's office of the people; you are Mandhātṛ, the giver of wealth, the upholder of ṛta;

sanskrit_iast: svāhā vayaṃ kṛṇavāmā havīṃṣi devo devānyajatyagnirarhan //
meaning: स्वाहा वयं कृणवामा हवींषि देवो देवान्यजत्यग्निरर्हन् //
text_mt: svāhā! we would make the oblations; the god Agni, being worthy, sacrifices to the gods!"

sanskrit_iast: viśveṣāṃ hyadhvarāṇāmanīkaṃ citraṃ ketuṃ janitā tvā jajāna /
meaning: विश्वेषां ह्यध्वराणामनीकं चित्रं केतुं जनिता त्वा जजान /
text_mt: "For the creator generated you as the front, the bright beacon of all sacrifices;

sanskrit_iast: sa ā yajasva nṛvatīranu kṣāḥ spārhā iṣaḥ kṣumatīrviśvajanyāḥ //
meaning: स आ यजस्व नृवतीरनु क्षाः स्पार्हा इषः क्षुमतीर्विश्वजन्याः //
text_mt: so offer, along the lands, desirable, rich in cattle, universal refreshments full of heroes!

sanskrit_iast: yaṃ tvā dyāvāpṛthivī yaṃ tvāpastvaṣṭā yaṃ tvā sujanimā jajāna /
meaning: यं त्वा द्यावापृथिवी यं त्वापस्त्वष्टा यं त्वा सुजनिमा जजान /
text_mt: You whom Heaven and Earth, you whom the Waters, you whom Tvaṣṭṛ, good at generating, generated:

sanskrit_iast: panthāmanu pravidvānpitṛyāṇaṃ dyumadagne samidhāno vi bhāhītyetasya sūktasya ṣaṭ sarvaṃ vā //
meaning: पन्थामनु प्रविद्वान्पितृयाणं द्युमदग्ने समिधानो वि भाहीत्येतस्य सूक्तस्य षट् सर्वं वा //
text_mt: knowing well the path traversed by the fathers, O Agni, being kindled, shine brightly!"—six [verses] or the whole of this hymn;

sanskrit_iast: viśve devāḥ śāstana mā yatheha hotā vṛto manavai yanniṣadya /
meaning: विश्वे देवाः शास्तन मा यथेह होता वृतो मनवै यन्निषद्य /
text_mt: "All you gods, instruct me how, chosen as hotṛ here, having sat down, I may think!

sanskrit_iast: pra me brūta bhāgadheyaṃ yathā vo yena pathā havyamā vo vahāni //
meaning: प्र मे ब्रूत भागधेयं यथा वो येन पथा हव्यमा वो वहानि //
text_mt: Declare to me your portion, as it is, along which path I may convey the oblation to you!"
"The one whom I desire with my mind, this very one has arrived, knowing the sacrifice, perceptive of its joints;

sanskrit_iast: sa no yakṣaddevatātā yajīyānni hi ṣatsadantaraḥ pūrvo asmanniṣadya //
meaning: स नो यक्षद्देवताता यजीयान्नि हि षत्सदन्तरः पूर्वो अस्मन्निषद्य //
text_mt: may he, being a better sacrificer, sacrifice for us in the godhead, for he has sat down within, ahead of us, having taken his seat!"

sanskrit_iast: tadadya vācaḥ prathamaṃ masīya yenāsurām̐ abhi devā asāma //
meaning: तदद्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीय येनासुराम्̐ अभि देवा असाम //
text_mt: "Today may I meditate on that first [utterance] of speech whereby we gods may overcome the asuras;

sanskrit_iast: ūrjāda uta yajñiyāsaḥ pañca janā mama hotraṃ juṣadhvam //
meaning: ऊर्जाद उत यज्ञियासः पञ्च जना मम होत्रं जुषध्वम् //
text_mt: eating invigorating food and worthy of sacrifice, O five peoples, enjoy my hotṛ's office!"

sanskrit_iast: namo mahadbhyo namo arbhakebhyo namo yuvabhyo nama āśinebhyaḥ /
meaning: नमो महद्भ्यो नमो अर्भकेभ्यो नमो युवभ्यो नम आशिनेभ्यः /
text_mt: "Homage to the great, homage to the small, homage to the young, homage to the elders!

sanskrit_iast: yajāma devānyadi śaknavāma mā jyāyasaḥ śaṃsamā vṛkṣi devā iti
meaning: यजाम देवान्यदि शक्नवाम मा ज्यायसः शंसमा वृक्षि देवा इति
text_mt: Let us sacrifice to the gods if we are able; let me not, O gods, cut off the praise of the elder!"
Having murmured this, he causes [the adhvaryu and the pratiprasthātṛ] to take up the two ladles.
Everywhere before the consecratory verse, having uttered 'ye yajāmahe', he applies the sacred utterances.
He does not pronounce 'ye yajāmahe' at the after-offerings.
He recites the consecratory verses for the after-offerings without breathing in;
An invitatory verse has its characteristic mark at the beginning;
a consecratory verse has its characteristic mark at the end;
The invitatory verse has its characteristic mark at both ends, and likewise the consecratory verse, say some.
Standing, he recites the invitatory verse;

sanskrit_iast: sā ha tvai samṛddhā puro'nuvākyā yāmabhivyāharandevatāmevāgre 'bhivyāharati /
meaning: सा ह त्वै समृद्धा पुरोऽनुवाक्या यामभिव्याहरन्देवतामेवाग्रे ऽभिव्याहरति /
text_mt: That indeed is an accomplished invitatory verse in reciting which he mentions the deity first;

sanskrit_iast: sā ha tvai samṛddhā yājyā yasyai devatāyā adhi vaṣaṭkaroti
meaning: सा ह त्वै समृद्धा याज्या यस्यै देवताया अधि वषट्करोति
text_mt: that indeed is an accomplished consecratory verse for whose deity he utters the vaṣaṭ-call.
He places the sacred syllable om in the verse, except for the consecratory verse.
Some say it is a modification of the final syllable.
Another [view] is that it should be an additional [syllable].

sanskrit_iast: ṛcamuktvā praṇautyaparāmuktvā praṇautyadhike punaretadupapadyate saṃtatamṛcā vaṣaṭkarotīti ca tadvadyājyāyā adhi vaṣaṭkaroti
meaning: ऋचमुक्त्वा प्रणौत्यपरामुक्त्वा प्रणौत्यधिके पुनरेतदुपपद्यते संततमृचा वषट्करोतीति च तद्वद्याज्याया अधि वषट्करोति
text_mt: “Having spoken a verse, he pronounces the praṇava; having spoken another, he pronounces the praṇava.” But this is possible only if it is additional. And likewise [the text says]: “He utters the vaṣaṭ-call continuously with the verse;” [thus] he utters the vaṣaṭ-call over the consecratory verse.
“Raising the voice, he utters the vaṣaṭ-call”: [this means] loudness of the sound.

sanskrit_iast: yaṃ kāmayeta pramāyukaḥ syāditi tasyoccairapagūrya nikhidanniva vaṣaṭkuryāt /
meaning: यं कामयेत प्रमायुकः स्यादिति तस्योच्चैरपगूर्य निखिदन्निव वषट्कुर्यात् /
text_mt: For one whom he might wish to die soon, he should utter the vaṣaṭ-call having raised [his voice] loudly, as if pressing down.

sanskrit_iast: yaṃ kāmayeta pāpīyānsyāditi nīcaistarāṃ tasya yājyāyā vaṣaṭkuryāt /
meaning: यं कामयेत पापीयान्स्यादिति नीचैस्तरां तस्य याज्याया वषट्कुर्यात् /
text_mt: For one whom he might wish to become worse off, he should utter the vaṣaṭ-call lower than his consecratory verse.

sanskrit_iast: yaṃ kāmayeta vasīyānsyādityuccaistarāṃ tasya yājyāyā vaṣaṭkuryāt /
meaning: यं कामयेत वसीयान्स्यादित्युच्चैस्तरां तस्य याज्याया वषट्कुर्यात् /
text_mt: For one whom he might wish to become better off, he should utter the vaṣaṭ-call higher than his consecratory verse.

sanskrit_iast: na vasīyānna pāpīyāniti samaṃ tasya yājyāyā vaṣaṭkuryāt /
meaning: न वसीयान्न पापीयानिति समं तस्य याज्याया वषट्कुर्यात् /
text_mt: [If he wishes that he be] neither better off nor worse off, he should utter the vaṣaṭ-call at the same level as his consecratory verse.
It is known [from scripture]: “For one desiring heaven, he should utter the vāsaṭ-call loudly, like a krauñca bird.”
Likewise [in the passage]: “He utters the vaṣaṭ-call louder than the verse.”

sanskrit_iast: yaṃ devatāṃ yajettāṃ manasā dhyāyetpurā vaṣaṭkārātsvargakāmasyeti vijñāyate
meaning: यं देवतां यजेत्तां मनसा ध्यायेत्पुरा वषट्कारात्स्वर्गकामस्येति विज्ञायते
text_mt: It is known [from scripture]: “Whichever deity he sacrifices to, he should meditate on that [deity] in his mind before the vaṣaṭ-call, for one who desires heaven.”
Having uttered the vaṣaṭ-call, he should breathe in, breathe out, and blink.
It is known [from scripture]: “He should sustain in-breath with out-breath, and the eye by blinking.”
For one whom he hates, he should utter the vaṣaṭ-call as ‘oṣaṭ’.
Some teach ‘vāsāṭ’;

sanskrit_iast: vaṣaṭkāra mā me pra vāṅmo ahaṃ tvāṃ bṛhatā mana upahvaye /
meaning: वषट्कार मा मे प्र वाङ्मो अहं त्वां बृहता मन उपह्वये /
text_mt: “O vaṣaṭ-call, do not destroy my speech, nor I you; I summon you with the bṛhat metre, O Mind!

sanskrit_iast: na māṃ na me vācaṃ hinasāt /
meaning: न मां न मे वाचं हिनसात् /
text_mt: May it not injure me, nor my speech!

meaning: हव्यं देवेभ्यो ऽभिवहाम्योजः सहः सह ओजः /
text_mt: I carry the oblation to the gods, vigor, strength, strength, vigor!”

sanskrit_iast: vāgvaṣaṭkāra namaste astu mā mā hiṃsīrityetadvaṣaṭkṛte japati /
meaning: वाग्वषट्कार नमस्ते अस्तु मा मा हिंसीरित्येतद्वषट्कृते जपति /
text_mt: “O Speech, O vaṣaṭ-call, homage be to you; do not injure me!”—having uttered the vaṣaṭ-call, he mutters this [formula].

sanskrit_iast: vāgvaṣaṭkāra namaste astu mā mā hiṃsīriti vā
meaning: वाग्वषट्कार नमस्ते अस्तु मा मा हिंसीरिति वा
text_mt: Or [only]: “O Speech, O vaṣaṭ-call, homage be to you; do not injure me!”

sanskrit_iast: aṅgulī muktvā miṣe prāṇāyeti mukhadeśamūrdhvamutkṛṣyorje 'pānāyetyavācīnaṃ niyacchati
meaning: अङ्गुली मुक्त्वा मिषे प्राणायेति मुखदेशमूर्ध्वमुत्कृष्योर्जे ऽपानायेत्यवाचीनं नियच्छति
text_mt: Having unclasped his fingers, having raised [them] upward toward the mouth with [the words]: “For sap, for in-breath,” he directs [them] downward with [the words]: “For vigor, for out-breath.”
Holding the cut-off intermediate iḍā with the fingers, he does not make a fist.
He invokes it facing as if toward his mouth.
It has been said: “For one whom he might wish to be without cattle, [he should invoke] it turned away.”
However, [there is] a prohibition against repetition of words.
And it is known [from scripture]: “ ‘The iḍā is invoked’—that is turned away;

meaning: आध्वर्यव एवातो ऽन्यानि कर्माणि होतुराम्नातानि भवन्ति /
text_mt: Henceforth, other rites prescribed for the hotṛ belong solely to the adhvaryu's duties.
Other [rites are assigned to] other [priests] by express teaching.
